# @kimen/elements — Kimen web components

> Kimen web components (ki-*). Standards-first Stencil components, tokens-only styling, agent-legible by contract.

Install with `pnpm add @kimen/elements @kimen/tokens`.

Register each component before using it. Every component is exported from
`@kimen/elements/<tag>`, the way `ki-button` is here:

```ts
import { defineCustomElement as defineKiButton } from '@kimen/elements/ki-button';
import '@kimen/tokens/css';
import '@kimen/tokens/css/base';

defineKiButton();
```

Load `@kimen/tokens/css` once per page: it is the onmars default theme and
the only stylesheet the components require. It declares every `--ki-*` token
for both schemes together with the `color-scheme` they resolve from, so a
page follows its visitor's light or dark preference with no further setup.
`@kimen/tokens/css/base` — the page contract — is optional: it paints the
page background, text color and body font from those tokens and declares no
color scheme of its own. Without it the page keeps the browser's own canvas
and text color for the active scheme, and every component stays legible on
it.

Human-readable documentation: https://kimen.dev/docs/

## Theming

All themes reassign the same `--ki-*` custom properties, so switching themes
restyles every component with no code changes. Two attributes on the document
root drive selection:

- `data-ki-color-scheme`: `light` or `dark` forces a color scheme for any
  theme, overriding the OS preference. Without it, stylesheets follow
  `prefers-color-scheme`.
- `data-ki-theme`: opts into a non-default theme. Unknown theme names match no
  selector and fall back to onmars through the cascade.

To use the bundled Material 3 reference theme, side-effect import its
stylesheet (exported as `@kimen/tokens/css/material3`) in addition to
`@kimen/tokens/css`, then select it on the document root:

```html
<html data-ki-theme="material3" data-ki-color-scheme="dark">
```

## Agent setup

Coding agents can install the Kimen agent skills (`kimen-components` for
pages built with these components, `kimen-genui` for agent-generated UI) and
connect the `kimen-mcp` server, which lists and describes the catalog,
validates UI specs and renders them. Setup for Claude Code, Claude Desktop,
Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode and other clients:
https://kimen.dev/docs/guides/connect-agents/

## Components

### ki-accordion

A set of native disclosure panels with a shared frame.

When to use: group related FAQ answers, settings or expandable sections.
Enable exclusive when readers benefit from one open section at a time.
When NOT to use: switch between views or make the panels advance a workflow.

Examples:

### Workspace FAQ

Group direct disclosure children. Set `exclusive` when readers should see
one answer at a time.

```html
<ki-accordion exclusive>
  <ki-details open summary="Who can see my workspace?">
    Only people you invite can see it.
  </ki-details>
  <ki-details summary="Can I export my data?">
    Open Settings, then select Data and Export.
  </ki-details>
</ki-accordion>
```

Attributes:
- `exclusive` (boolean, default false): Whether the accordion allows at most one direct member to be open.

Slots:
- (default): Direct ki-details members in reading order.

Parts:
- `group`: The frame around the disclosure rows.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-accordion-divider-width`: Width of the separator between accordion rows.
- `--ki-details-border`: Color of the disclosure frame and accordion separators.
- `--ki-details-border-width`: Width of the disclosure or accordion frame.
- `--ki-details-radius`: Corners of a standalone disclosure or the accordion frame.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-ai-label

A compact provenance mark for AI-generated content, with optional details and a user-initiated request to restore their original text.

When to use: Mark text or a value generated by AI. Include the source in
`explanation` when people can inspect how it was generated. In a `ki-input`,
place the label in the `end` slot to describe the field's provenance.
When NOT to use: Use a status component for active generation or processing,
and an application action for changes that do not restore the person's text.

Examples:

# AI label examples

Mark generated content beside the text it describes.

```html
<header>Weekly summary <ki-ai-label></ki-ai-label></header>
```

Give people a short provenance explanation when they need to assess a result.
The model and generation time are optional.

```html
<ki-ai-label
  explanation="Written from the incident reports of the last 30 days."
  model="Standard"
  generated-at="2026-11-19T10:32"
></ki-ai-label>
```

Use the input's `end` slot to announce the provenance with the field
description. Keep the original in application state and restore it on
`ki-revert`.

```html
<ki-input id="subject" label="Subject" value="Incident summary">
  <ki-ai-label
    slot="end"
    explanation="Suggested from the incident reports."
    revertible
  ></ki-ai-label>
</ki-input>

<script type="module">
  const field = document.querySelector('#subject');
  const label = field.querySelector('ki-ai-label');
  const original = 'Weekly summary';

  label.addEventListener('ki-revert', () => {
    field.value = original;
    label.remove();
    field.focus();
  });
</script>
```

Attributes:
- `explanation` (string | undefined): Plain-text explanation of how the content was generated. Supply a nonblank explanation to offer disclosure. Omit it for a static mark.
- `generated-at` (string | undefined): Optional generation date or time, displayed as supplied.
- `generated-at-label` (string, default 'Generated'): Visible prefix for the generation date or time.
- `label` (string, default 'AI'): Short visible provenance text. Localize it with the trigger name.
- `model` (string | undefined): Optional plain-text model name shown in the explanation.
- `model-label` (string, default 'Model:'): Visible prefix for the model name.
- `popover-label` (string, default 'About this content'): Accessible name of the non-modal explanation panel.
- `revert-label` (string, default 'Revert to my text'): Visible text and accessible name of the revert action.
- `revertible` (boolean, default false): Offer the revert action inside the explanation. Enable it when the application has the original text and handles `ki-revert`.
- `size` ("md" | "sm", default 'sm'): Size of the painted mark. Unknown values use the small metrics.
- `trigger-label` (string, default 'AI-generated: about this content'): Accessible name of the disclosure button. Include the visible label.

Slots: none

Parts:
- `explanation`: Source explanation paragraph.
- `icon`: Decorative sparkles glyph.
- `label`: Tinted mark containing the icon and visible text.
- `metadata`: Optional model and generation time.
- `popover`: Non-modal explanation panel.
- `revert`: Button that requests reversion.
- `trigger`: Disclosure button, available with an explanation.

Events:
- `ki-revert` (CustomEvent<void>): Bubbles when a person requests their original text. Use this request to restore the original from application state.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-ai-label-backdrop-filter`: Complete filter behind the AI provenance mark. Defaults to none.
- `--ki-ai-label-bg`: Fill of the AI provenance mark.
- `--ki-ai-label-bg-image`: Optional image over the AI provenance fill. Defaults to none.
- `--ki-ai-label-border-width`: Border width of the panel and the forced-colors mark.
- `--ki-ai-label-fg`: Text and icon ink of the AI provenance mark.
- `--ki-ai-label-gap`: Gap between the mark and its icon or between provenance metadata items.
- `--ki-ai-label-md-height`: Minimum painted block size of the medium AI mark.
- `--ki-ai-label-md-icon-size`: Sparkles icon size in the medium AI mark.
- `--ki-ai-label-md-padding-inline`: Inline inset of the medium AI mark.
- `--ki-ai-label-popover-backdrop-filter`: Complete filter behind the provenance explanation. Defaults to none.
- `--ki-ai-label-popover-bg`: Raised fill of the provenance explanation.
- `--ki-ai-label-popover-bg-image`: Optional image over the provenance explanation fill. Defaults to none.
- `--ki-ai-label-popover-border`: Hairline color of the explanation panel.
- `--ki-ai-label-popover-fg`: Ink of the provenance explanation and metadata.
- `--ki-ai-label-popover-gap`: Gap between the panel sections and between the panel and trigger.
- `--ki-ai-label-popover-padding`: Inset of the explanation panel.
- `--ki-ai-label-popover-radius`: Corner radius of the explanation panel.
- `--ki-ai-label-popover-shadow`: Elevation of the explanation panel.
- `--ki-ai-label-popover-width`: Preferred inline size of the explanation panel.
- `--ki-ai-label-radius`: Corner radius of the AI provenance mark.
- `--ki-ai-label-sm-height`: Minimum painted block size of the small AI mark.
- `--ki-ai-label-sm-icon-size`: Sparkles icon size in the small AI mark.
- `--ki-ai-label-sm-padding-inline`: Inline inset of the small AI mark.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-para`: semantic dimension for typography line height para.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-2`: semantic dimension for typography size body 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-semibold`: semantic font weight for typography weight body semibold.

### ki-alert

A persistent inline status message with token-backed tone semantics.

When to use: show a persistent inline message about the state of a page or
section, such as a failed save, completed operation, or service notice, that
remains until the condition is resolved or the person dismisses it. Express
severity with `tone`, never custom styling.
When NOT to use: transient confirmations that expire on their own belong to
`ki-toast`, raised into a `ki-toaster`; tiny status descriptors attached to
another element belong to `ki-badge`; blocking decisions belong to
`ki-dialog`; inline field-level validation belongs to the form control.

Assistive technology note: alerts that must be announced should be inserted
dynamically, or re-shown by clearing `dismissed`; alerts present at initial
page load are exposed with their role but platform announcement is not
guaranteed.

Every non-neutral alert draws its tone's glyph in the icon frame (`info`,
`circle-check`, `triangle-alert`, `octagon-alert`) unless an icon is slotted.

Examples:

`tone` sets the token-backed colors and the live-region urgency — `danger` and `warning` expose `role="alert"`, every other value `role="status"`:

```html
<ki-alert tone="success">Your changes were saved.</ki-alert>
<ki-alert tone="danger">Payment failed. Update your billing details.</ki-alert>
```

An optional `heading` adds emphasized text inside the live region; it is a `strong` element, never a document heading:

```html
<ki-alert tone="warning" heading="Storage almost full">
  You are using 92% of your plan.
</ki-alert>
```

`dismissible` renders the alert's only tab stop; user dismissal reflects `dismissed` and fires a composed `ki-dismiss` (programmatic `dismissed` writes stay silent, and clearing the attribute re-shows the alert):

```html
<ki-alert tone="danger" heading="Save failed" dismissible>
  Your changes could not be saved. Retry or copy your work elsewhere.
</ki-alert>
```

`dismiss-label` overrides the dismiss button's accessible name — the default `Dismiss` is the component's only built-in user-visible string, so localize it whenever the document language is not English:

```html
<ki-alert lang="es" tone="info" dismissible dismiss-label="Descartar">
  Mantenimiento programado el sábado desde las 02:00 UTC.
</ki-alert>
```

The `icon` slot takes a decorative glyph, drawn in the tone's colors in a round frame at the top of the card. Without one, every non-neutral tone draws its own Lucide glyph there (`info`, `circle-check`, `triangle-alert`, `octagon-alert`); slot an icon to replace it, or to give a neutral alert one. The `actions` slot takes the responses to the message as `size="sm"` buttons, in a row after the message and outside the live region. An action never dismisses the alert by itself: set `dismissed` when it should go, and focus moves on to the next control:

```html
<ki-alert tone="warning" heading="Session ending" dismissible>
  <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true">
    <path fill="currentColor" d="M10 2a8 8 0 1 0 0 16 8 8 0 0 0 0-16Zm.75 4v4.5h-1.5V6h1.5Zm-.75 8.25a1 1 0 1 1 0-2 1 1 0 0 1 0 2Z" />
  </svg>
  Your session expires in one minute. Choose Stay signed in to keep working.
  <ki-button slot="actions" type="button" variant="secondary" size="sm">Sign out</ki-button>
  <ki-button slot="actions" type="button" variant="primary" size="sm">Stay signed in</ki-button>
</ki-alert>
```

Attributes:
- `dismiss-label` (string, default 'Dismiss'): Accessible name for the dismiss button. Override for localization; the default English string is the component's only built-in user-visible text. When to use: provide a localized action name whenever the document language is not English. When NOT to use: do not put the alert message here; use the default slot.
- `dismissed` (boolean, default false): Reflected dismissed state. User dismissal sets it; applications may also set or clear it. While true, the host remains in the document but renders no alert subtree and leaves the accessibility tree. Clearing it re-shows the alert and creates a dynamic live-region appearance. When to use: persist or restore acknowledgement state from application data. When NOT to use: do not listen for programmatic changes as dismissal events; `ki-dismiss` is only for user activation.
- `dismissible` (boolean, default false): Renders one native dismiss button when true. The button sits outside the live-region boundary, so its accessible name is not announced as part of the alert message. When false, the alert adds no tab stop. When to use: allow a person to acknowledge and clear a persistent message. When NOT to use: do not use dismissible for auto-expiring messages; those belong to `ki-toast`.
- `heading` (string | undefined): Optional emphasized text rendered before the message inside the live region. Empty strings render no heading. The heading is a `strong` element, not a document heading, so it never changes page outline. When to use: add a short label when it helps identify the status message. When NOT to use: do not use heading for page structure; use a real heading outside the alert when the document needs one.
- `tone` ("danger" | "info" | "neutral" | "success" | "warning" | string & {}, default 'neutral'): Semantic intent for visual styling and live-region urgency. `danger` and `warning` expose `role="alert"`; `neutral`, `success`, `info`, absent, and unrecognized values expose `role="status"`. Unknown values keep rendering and fall back to the neutral token matrix by CSS construction. When to use: choose the tone that describes the page or section state. When NOT to use: do not use tone for layout, density, or filled-vs-outlined styling; those are token/theme decisions.

Slots:
- (default): Message body. It lives inside the live-region boundary.
- `actions`: Optional responses to this message, in a row at the bottom of the card, outside the live region. Slot `size="sm"` buttons. The alert never activates them and an action does not dismiss the alert; the application does, by setting `dismissed`. When NOT to use: a response the person cannot skip belongs in `ki-dialog`.
- `icon`: Optional decorative glyph shown in a round frame at the top of the card, in the tone's colors. Hidden from assistive technology: it never carries meaning the heading and message lack. Without one, a non-neutral alert draws its tone's default glyph. When to use: replace the default glyph, or give a neutral alert one. When NOT to use: never as the only cue for the message.

Parts:
- `actions`: Row around the `actions` slot, rendered only when it holds content.
- `alert`: Outer shell around the card: padding, radius, wash and blur.
- `card`: Card holding the icon, text, actions and dismiss control: tone background, border, radius, padding and elevation.
- `dismiss`: Native dismiss button, rendered only when dismissible.
- `heading`: Optional emphasized heading, rendered only when non-empty.
- `icon`: Round frame around the `icon` slot, rendered when it holds content or the tone draws a default glyph.
- `message`: Message body wrapper around the default slot.

Events:
- `ki-dismiss` (CustomEvent<null>): Fired once after the user dismisses the alert — emitted after the alert is hidden and focus has been handed to the next control. `detail` is `null` and the event is not cancelable (the alert is already gone when it runs). When to use: record acknowledgement, or advance an application flow after a user closes the alert. When NOT to use: do not treat it as a veto point, and do not expect it for programmatic `dismissed` changes — it fires only for user activation.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-alert-actions-gap`: dimension used by the alert component for the gap between slotted actions (MarsUI Alert master CTAs gap Space/xl 12px).
- `--ki-alert-border-width`: dimension used by the alert component for the card border width (the MarsUI Alert master card stroke is fully transparent). onmars v2 draws a hairline (spec 011 A2); material3 keeps its 2px border via its override.
- `--ki-alert-card-shadow`: shadow used by the alert component for the card elevation (MarsUI Alert master List_wrap: elevation ramp level e5). An inline alert does not float, so onmars v2 and material3 lay the card flat.
- `--ki-alert-danger-bg`: color used by the alert component for the danger card background (MarsUI Alert master: the List_wrap card is Surface/special/light-s0-dark-s2 in every tone). onmars v2 tints the card with surface.danger-tint so the tone reads on the whole card (spec 011 A2); other themes may tint it per tone here too.
- `--ki-alert-danger-border`: color used by the alert component for the danger card edge (MarsUI draws no tone border on any alert/note/toast surface). onmars v2 draws the outline.danger-low-em hairline around the tinted card (spec 011 A2).
- `--ki-alert-danger-fg`: color used by the alert component for the danger card foreground: heading and message ink (MarsUI Alert master Text/high-em in every tone; the message keeps this 4.5:1 ink instead of the master Text/low-em, spec 011 A1-D8).
- `--ki-alert-danger-icon-bg`: color used by the alert component for the danger icon frame (MarsUI Alert master Feature-icon Surface/danger-base-em-alpha at 12%).
- `--ki-alert-danger-icon-fg`: color used by the alert component for the danger icon glyph (MarsUI Alert master Feature-icon glyph Text/danger-high-em).
- `--ki-alert-dismiss-active-fg`: color used by the alert component for dismiss active foreground.
- `--ki-alert-dismiss-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter behind the alert dismiss button.
- `--ki-alert-dismiss-border-width`: dimension used by the alert component for the dismiss chip outline (MarsUI 24px circle: 1px Outline/secondary_button_top hairline).
- `--ki-alert-dismiss-hover-bg`: color used by the alert component for dismiss hover background (MarsUI hover mechanism: hover-overlay-inverse Black/3 wash).
- `--ki-alert-dismiss-hover-fg`: color used by the alert component for dismiss hover foreground.
- `--ki-alert-dismiss-icon-size`: dimension used by the alert component for dismiss icon size (Figma close glyph box 16px inside the 24px raised circle; repointed from 18px per the fidelity audit).
- `--ki-alert-dismiss-radius`: dimension used by the alert component for the dismiss chip shape (MarsUI Radius/radius_round full circle).
- `--ki-alert-dismiss-rest-fg`: color used by the alert component for dismiss rest foreground.
- `--ki-alert-dismiss-size`: dimension used by the alert component for dismiss size.
- `--ki-alert-focus-ring-color`: color used by the alert component for focus ring color.
- `--ki-alert-focus-ring-offset`: dimension used by the alert component for focus ring offset.
- `--ki-alert-focus-ring-shadow`: shadow used by the alert dismiss control for the focus ring glow (MarsUI Focus/primary: 3px spread ring at 20% — see ki.focus.primary. specs/002-ki-button/design-extraction.md §2.5 recorded 40%, having read the alpha off the Dark canvas mode, same double mechanism as ki-button: glow plus the opaque indicator).
- `--ki-alert-focus-ring-width`: dimension used by the alert component for focus ring width.
- `--ki-alert-font-size`: dimension used by the alert component for font size.
- `--ki-alert-gap`: dimension used by the alert component for the card stack gap between icon, text and actions (MarsUI Alert master List_wrap gap Space/xl 12px).
- `--ki-alert-heading-font-family`: Font family for the alert heading. Override it to give alerts their own heading typeface.
- `--ki-alert-heading-font-size`: dimension used by the alert component for heading font size.
- `--ki-alert-heading-font-weight`: font weight used by the alert component for heading font weight (MarsUI UI/Body 2/medium: weight 600 on the master heading).
- `--ki-alert-icon-glyph-size`: dimension used by the alert component for the icon glyph inside the frame (MarsUI Alert master Feature-icon glyph 20px).
- `--ki-alert-icon-radius`: dimension used by the alert component for the icon frame radius (MarsUI Alert master Feature-icon: a circle).
- `--ki-alert-icon-size`: dimension used by the alert component for the icon frame (MarsUI Alert master Feature-icon size xs: 32px).
- `--ki-alert-info-bg`: color used by the alert component for the info card background (MarsUI Alert master: the List_wrap card is Surface/special/light-s0-dark-s2 in every tone). onmars v2 tints the card with surface.info-tint so the tone reads on the whole card (spec 011 A2); other themes may tint it per tone here too.
- `--ki-alert-info-border`: color used by the alert component for the info card edge (MarsUI draws no tone border on any alert/note/toast surface). onmars v2 draws the outline.info-low-em hairline around the tinted card (spec 011 A2).
- `--ki-alert-info-fg`: color used by the alert component for the info card foreground: heading and message ink (MarsUI Alert master Text/high-em in every tone; the message keeps this 4.5:1 ink instead of the master Text/low-em, spec 011 A1-D8).
- `--ki-alert-info-icon-bg`: color used by the alert component for the info icon frame (MarsUI Alert master Feature-icon Surface/info-base-em-alpha at 12%).
- `--ki-alert-info-icon-fg`: color used by the alert component for the info icon glyph (MarsUI Alert master Feature-icon glyph Text/info-high-em).
- `--ki-alert-line-height`: dimension used by the alert component for line height.
- `--ki-alert-message-line-height`: dimension used by the alert component for message line height (MarsUI description is 13/20 line_height/para; the heading keeps 15/24).
- `--ki-alert-neutral-bg`: color used by the alert component for the neutral card background (MarsUI Alert master: the List_wrap card is Surface/special/light-s0-dark-s2 in every tone). onmars v2 keeps that card for the neutral tone and edges it with a hairline (spec 011 A2).
- `--ki-alert-neutral-border`: color used by the alert component for the neutral card edge. onmars v2 draws it as the outline.low-em hairline of any flat card (spec 011 A2).
- `--ki-alert-neutral-fg`: color used by the alert component for the neutral card foreground: heading and message ink (MarsUI Alert master Text/high-em in every tone; the message keeps this 4.5:1 ink instead of the master Text/low-em, spec 011 A1-D8).
- `--ki-alert-neutral-icon-bg`: color used by the alert component for the neutral icon frame (MarsUI Alert master Feature-icon Surface/primary-base-em-alpha at 12%: the master variable itself, not the heavier primary-tint content fill, so the primary glyph clears 4.5:1 in dark). onmars v2 keeps the accent off it: the frame takes the neutral card surface.
- `--ki-alert-neutral-icon-fg`: color used by the alert component for the neutral icon glyph (MarsUI Alert master Feature-icon glyph Text/primary-high-em). onmars v2 draws it in the neutral text.high-em ink.
- `--ki-alert-padding-block`: dimension used by the alert component for the card padding block (MarsUI Alert master List_wrap card: 12px on all four sides).
- `--ki-alert-padding-inline`: dimension used by the alert component for the card padding inline (MarsUI Alert master List_wrap card: 12px on all four sides).
- `--ki-alert-radius`: dimension used by the alert component for the card radius (MarsUI Alert master List_wrap big_component/radius_xs 16px; the shell around it has its own radius).
- `--ki-alert-shell-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter behind the alert shell.
- `--ki-alert-shell-bg`: color used by the alert component for the shell wash (MarsUI Alert master Inverse-white/alpha-2: the nearest step of the Kimen inverse-white ramp, Black/3 light and White/3 dark). onmars v2 and material3 paint no shell: it is transparent.
- `--ki-alert-shell-padding`: dimension used by the alert component for the shell padding around the card (MarsUI Alert master: 12px on all four sides). onmars v2 and material3 set it to zero, so the alert paints as one flat card (spec 011 A2, S31).
- `--ki-alert-shell-radius`: dimension used by the alert component for the shell radius (MarsUI Alert master big_component/radius_lg 28px). A flat theme gives the shell the card radius.
- `--ki-alert-success-bg`: color used by the alert component for the success card background (MarsUI Alert master: the List_wrap card is Surface/special/light-s0-dark-s2 in every tone). onmars v2 tints the card with surface.success-tint so the tone reads on the whole card (spec 011 A2); other themes may tint it per tone here too.
- `--ki-alert-success-border`: color used by the alert component for the success card edge (MarsUI draws no tone border on any alert/note/toast surface). onmars v2 draws the outline.success-low-em hairline around the tinted card (spec 011 A2).
- `--ki-alert-success-fg`: color used by the alert component for the success card foreground: heading and message ink (MarsUI Alert master Text/high-em in every tone; the message keeps this 4.5:1 ink instead of the master Text/low-em, spec 011 A1-D8).
- `--ki-alert-success-icon-bg`: color used by the alert component for the success icon frame (MarsUI Alert master Feature-icon Surface/success-base-em-alpha at 12%).
- `--ki-alert-success-icon-fg`: color used by the alert component for the success icon glyph (MarsUI Alert master Feature-icon glyph Text/success-high-em).
- `--ki-alert-text-gap`: dimension used by the alert component for the heading-to-message stack gap (MarsUI Text_wrap 4px, decoupled from the outer 12px card gap).
- `--ki-alert-warning-bg`: color used by the alert component for the warning card background (MarsUI Alert master: the List_wrap card is Surface/special/light-s0-dark-s2 in every tone). onmars v2 tints the card with surface.warning-tint so the tone reads on the whole card (spec 011 A2); other themes may tint it per tone here too.
- `--ki-alert-warning-border`: color used by the alert component for the warning card edge (MarsUI draws no tone border on any alert/note/toast surface). onmars v2 draws the outline.warning-low-em hairline around the tinted card (spec 011 A2).
- `--ki-alert-warning-fg`: color used by the alert component for the warning card foreground: heading and message ink (MarsUI Alert master Text/high-em in every tone; the message keeps this 4.5:1 ink instead of the master Text/low-em, spec 011 A1-D8).
- `--ki-alert-warning-icon-bg`: color used by the alert component for the warning icon frame (MarsUI Alert master Feature-icon Surface/warning-base-em-alpha at 12%).
- `--ki-alert-warning-icon-fg`: color used by the alert component for the warning icon glyph (MarsUI Alert master Feature-icon glyph Text/warning-high-em).
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-effect-component-secondary-default-shadow`: MarsUI Component_effect/secondary_default: drop 0/2/1.5/-0.5 plus inner White/3 0/2/3. Pair with --ki-effect-component-backdrop-filter.
- `--ki-motion-distance-sm`: Motion travel distance sm (4px): small slide/settle offsets.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-duration-medium-1`: M3 md.sys.motion.duration.medium1 (250ms). onmars: MarsUI moderate step (240ms, 2x the 120ms base).
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-motion-easing-standard`: Standard interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-outline-secondary-button-top`: semantic color for outline secondary button top.
- `--ki-surface-special-light-s0-dark-s2`: semantic color for surface special light s0 dark s2.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-audio

A recording player with play, pause, a seek timeline, elapsed and total time, playback speed, mute, and an optional transcript link.

When to use: play a voice note, interview, or other prerecorded audio that a person deliberately starts. Provide a title and the equivalent text transcript URL when available.
When NOT to use: show video (use ki-video), play an ambient loop or start playback automatically, or record audio.

Examples:

# Using ki-audio

Offer a voice note or recording with a clear title and an adjacent transcript.

```html
<ki-audio
  src="/ep4.mp3"
  title="Interview, episode 4"
  transcript-href="/ep4/transcript"
></ki-audio>
```

Set the speeds and translate the control labels in the language of the page.
The seek announcement substitutes the formatted elapsed and total times into
the `time-label` template.

```html
<ki-audio
  lang="es"
  src="/notas/7.mp3"
  title="Nota de voz"
  rates="0.75,1,1.5"
  play-label="Reproducir"
  pause-label="Pausar"
  seek-label="Posición"
  time-label="{elapsed} de {duration}"
  speed-label="Velocidad"
  mute-label="Silenciar"
  unmute-label="Activar sonido"
  transcript-href="/notas/7/transcripcion"
  transcript-label="Leer la transcripción"
  error-label="No se pudo reproducir el audio"
></ki-audio>
```

Listen on the player for `play`, `pause`, `timeupdate` and `ended`. For
example, an experiment can observe completion after the listener reaches the
end of a recording.

```js
const player = document.querySelector('ki-audio');
player?.addEventListener('ended', () => {
  document.querySelector('#next-recording')?.removeAttribute('hidden');
});
```

Attributes:
- `title` (string | undefined, default 'Audio player'): Visible title and accessible name of the player.
- `error-label` (string, default 'Audio could not be played'): Message shown if playback cannot start or the recording fails to load.
- `mute-label` (string, default 'Mute'): Accessible name of the mute button.
- `pause-label` (string, default 'Pause'): Accessible name of the pause button.
- `play-label` (string, default 'Play'): Accessible name of the play button.
- `rates` (string, default '0.75,1,1.25,1.5,2'): Comma-separated playback speeds between 0.25 and 4. Normal speed (1) is always available.
- `seek-label` (string, default 'Seek'): Accessible name of the timeline slider.
- `speed-label` (string, default 'Playback speed'): Accessible label for the playback-rate picker.
- `src` (string, required, URL): Source URL for the recording. Use an HTTP(S) URL or a relative URL.
- `time-label` (string | undefined, default '{elapsed} of {duration}'): Accessible time template. Keep the {elapsed} and {duration} placeholders.
- `transcript-href` (string | undefined, URL): URL for the recording's text transcript. Use an HTTP(S) URL or a relative URL.
- `transcript-label` (string, default 'Read the transcript'): Text of the transcript link.
- `unmute-label` (string, default 'Unmute'): Accessible name of the unmute button.

Slots: none

Parts:
- `mute`: Mute and unmute control.
- `play`: Play and pause control.
- `player`: The named group and themed surface.
- `progress`: Played portion of the timeline rail.
- `seek`: Native seek slider.
- `speed`: Native playback-rate picker.
- `status`: Playback failure message.
- `time`: Elapsed and total time readouts.
- `title`: Visible recording title.
- `track`: Timeline rail.
- `transcript`: Transcript link.

Events:
- `ended` (CustomEvent<void>): Forwarded when the recording ends. The catalog can bind a declared action here.
- `pause` (CustomEvent<void>): Forwarded when native playback pauses.
- `play` (CustomEvent<void>): Forwarded when the native playback state switches to playing.
- `timeupdate` (CustomEvent<void>): Forwarded when the native playback position is updated.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-audio-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter applied to the player, off by default.
- `--ki-audio-bg`: Background behind the player and transcript link.
- `--ki-audio-bg-image`: Optional image painted over the player background.
- `--ki-audio-border`: Boundary of the player panel.
- `--ki-audio-fg`: Text on the player background.
- `--ki-audio-progress-bg`: Colour of the elapsed timeline and seek thumb.
- `--ki-audio-radius`: Corner radius of the player panel.
- `--ki-audio-speed-radius`: Corner radius of the playback speed button.
- `--ki-audio-title-family`: Font family of the recording title.
- `--ki-audio-track-bg`: Colour of the inactive timeline.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-disabled-border`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral disabled border.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-hover-border`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral hover border.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-rest-border`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral rest border.
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-disabled-bg`: color used by the button component for primary neutral disabled background. Deliberate deviation: Figma disabled is Surface/disabled_base_em gray.100 with gray.400 text (≈1.4:1); Kimen keeps gray.200 for contrast (precedent 010 D2, pending founder ratification).
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-disabled-border`: color used by the button component for primary neutral disabled border.
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-disabled-fg`: color used by the button component for primary neutral disabled foreground. Deliberate deviation: Figma disabled text is text/base_em gray.400 (≈1.4:1 on gray.100); Kimen keeps text.muted gray.700 for readable disabled text (precedent 010 D2, pending founder ratification).
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-hover-bg`: color used by the button component for primary neutral hover background (MarsUI: rest fill; hover lightening comes from the hover overlay).
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-hover-border`: color used by the button component for primary neutral hover border (MarsUI top/inline edge; none in onmars v2).
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-hover-fg`: color used by the button component for primary neutral hover foreground.
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-rest-bg`: color used by the button component for primary neutral rest background (MarsUI Surface/primary_med_em, brand 500).
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-rest-border`: color used by the button component for primary neutral rest border (MarsUI top/inline edge; none in onmars v2).
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-rest-fg`: color used by the button component for primary neutral rest foreground.
- `--ki-button-quaternary-neutral-disabled-bg`: color used by the button component for quaternary neutral disabled background.
- `--ki-button-quaternary-neutral-disabled-fg`: color used by the button component for quaternary neutral disabled foreground: the disabled ink of every field and selection control (Text/base_em). quaternary has no fill or border, so its ink alone shows the state; ki.text.muted equals its resting ki.text.med-em in onmars.
- `--ki-button-quaternary-neutral-hover-bg`: color used by the button component for quaternary neutral hover background (MarsUI hover mechanism: hover-overlay-inverse Black/3 wash over the transparent rest fill).
- `--ki-button-quaternary-neutral-hover-fg`: color used by the button component for quaternary neutral hover foreground (MarsUI quaternary label text/med_em gray; never the accent).
- `--ki-button-quaternary-neutral-rest-bg`: color used by the button component for quaternary neutral rest background.
- `--ki-button-quaternary-neutral-rest-fg`: color used by the button component for quaternary neutral rest foreground (MarsUI quaternary label text/med_em gray; never the accent).
- `--ki-control-border-width`: Stroke width of the boundary of a compact control.
- `--ki-control-radius-track`: Corner radius of a track containing adjacent controls.
- `--ki-control-size-md`: Medium control track height, 40 CSS px at the default root size.
- `--ki-control-size-sm`: Small control track height, 32 CSS px at the default root size.
- `--ki-corner-activity-mark`: Round corners for rings and typing dots.
- `--ki-corner-inline`: Small radius for an outline around inline content.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-glyph-size-md`: Medium glyph for body content (20px at the default root size).
- `--ki-glyph-size-sm`: Small glyph for dense layouts (16px at the default root size).
- `--ki-media-layout-inline-max`: Maximum inline size of a self-contained media control panel.
- `--ki-scale-control-coarse-target`: Minimum grip target when a value scale has a coarse primary pointer.
- `--ki-scale-control-track-height`: Thickness of the inactive rail of a value scale.
- `--ki-spacing-action-inset`: Interior space at the edge of an action surface or divider.
- `--ki-spacing-block`: Deprecated alias kept for pre-Fase-1 consumers; use ki.space.xl.
- `--ki-spacing-media-caption`: Block spacing between a media frame and its caption.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography line height body 1.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-underline-offset`: Gap between text and its underline.
- `--ki-typography-underline-thickness`: Stroke width of a resting text underline.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-medium`: semantic font weight for typography weight body medium.

### ki-avatar

A static identity visual that shows a person or entity at a glance through a fallback chain: portrait, then initials, then a built-in generic figure.

When to use: a compact identity visual for a person or entity — a comment
author, a contact list item, a project member. Set `label` whenever the
avatar is the only carrier of the identity (no adjacent visible name);
compose several into `ki-avatar-group` for a compact "who is involved"
stack with overflow.
When NOT to use: as a clickable control (compose the avatar inside an
interactive host such as ki-button), for logos or arbitrary illustrations
(plain `img`), or unlabeled when no adjacent text names the identity.
Use the counter slot for a decorative count or presence dot.

Examples:

The fallback chain is content, never a mode switch: a portrait that loads wins, `initials` render verbatim otherwise, and a built-in generic figure covers the rest; `label` exposes the avatar as a named non-interactive image:

```html
<ki-avatar label="Ana García" src="/avatars/ana.png" initials="AG"></ki-avatar>
<ki-avatar label="Sam Bel" initials="SB"></ki-avatar>
<ki-avatar label="Guest"></ki-avatar>
```

Beside a visible name the avatar is decorative — omit `label` so assistive technology hears the name exactly once:

```html
<p><ki-avatar initials="AG" size="sm"></ki-avatar> Ana García</p>
```

`size` steps over the shared scale (`xxs` to `xl`, default `md`); an unrecognized value keeps the medium metrics:

```html
<ki-avatar label="Ana García" initials="AG" size="xs"></ki-avatar>
<ki-avatar label="Ana García" initials="AG"></ki-avatar>
<ki-avatar label="Ana García" initials="AG" size="xl"></ki-avatar>
```

Attributes:
- `initials` (string | undefined): Initials rendered verbatim as the second fallback step — never derived from the label, never truncated (FR-003). Catalog guidance: one to two characters. With a label present the initials are presentational; assistive technology receives the label alone.
- `label` (string | undefined): Accessible name for the identity ("Ana García"). With a label the avatar is exposed as a named non-interactive image (role `img`) in every content mode — the portrait never carries a second alternative text of its own. Without a label the avatar is decorative and contributes nothing to the accessibility tree; the identity must then live in adjacent visible text (FR-002).
- `size` ("lg" | "md" | "sm" | "xl" | "xs" | "xxs", default 'md'): Size step over the shared scale; per-size metrics (box, initials font, figure glyph) are per-theme component tokens, never hardcoded (FR-004). An unrecognized value matches no style selector, so the avatar keeps the default medium metrics (fallback by CSS construction, FR-007).
- `src` (string | undefined, URL): Portrait URL, the first step of the fallback chain. When it fails to load — initially or at runtime — the avatar silently falls back to the initials (or the generic figure) with no error, no layout change and no event (FR-001). Loading policy follows the platform image defaults.

Slots:
- `counter`: Decorative ki-counter. Counts sit at block-start inline-end and dots at block-end inline-end. Include its meaning in the avatar label.

Parts:
- `avatar`: The avatar box: size, shape, surface, border and typography.
- `icon`: The built-in generic person figure of the last fallback step.
- `image`: The portrait image when `src` is set and loads.
- `initials`: The verbatim initials text of the second fallback step.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-avatar-bg`: color used by the avatar component for the initials/figure surface: Surface/primary_med_em, the exact variable behind the Type=text gradient start and the Type=icon solid fill. The Figma text gradient (primary_med_em -> primary_low_em_alpha 20%) is deliberately flattened to its solid start color — the token pipeline models no gradients and the spec defines one family-level bg (declared deviation, specs/019-ki-avatar/design-extraction.md decision 2, pending founder ratification). onmars v2 fills it with the neutral surface.s3, since a list of people is not a list of selected items.
- `--ki-avatar-border-color`: color used by the avatar component for the surface border: Outline/base_em (Black/3 light, White/3 dark), the exact variable on Type=text variants.
- `--ki-avatar-border-width`: dimension used by the avatar component for the surface border (MarsUI 1px hairline on Type=text; applied to the token surface behind initials and figure, dropped under a loaded portrait — design-extraction decision 4).
- `--ki-avatar-fg`: color used by the avatar component for the initials text and the generic-figure glyph (via currentColor): Text/primary_on_primary, the exact variable on every Type=text variant. onmars v2 sets the initials in the text.supporting ink (med-em, stronger under more contrast) on its neutral fill.
- `--ki-avatar-font-family`: font family used by the avatar component for initials: the body family (Instrument Sans in onmars v2).
- `--ki-avatar-font-weight`: font weight used by the avatar component for initials (MarsUI Typeface/weight/body/medium: 600).
- `--ki-avatar-lg-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for lg initials (MarsUI UI/Body 2: 15px).
- `--ki-avatar-lg-icon-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the lg generic-figure glyph (MarsUI Icon/User 24px, Space/7xl).
- `--ki-avatar-lg-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the lg box (48px circle, Figma Space/14xl).
- `--ki-avatar-md-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for md initials (MarsUI UI/Para: body_1 13px).
- `--ki-avatar-md-icon-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the md generic-figure glyph (MarsUI Icon/User 20px, Space/5xl).
- `--ki-avatar-md-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the md box (40px circle, Figma Space/12xl, node 10011:947).
- `--ki-avatar-radius`: dimension used by the avatar component for the shape: Radius/radius_round bound to every avatar variant — the circle is a radius token, never an attribute (002 shape precedent, FR-005).
- `--ki-avatar-sm-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for sm initials (MarsUI UI/Caption 2: 12px).
- `--ki-avatar-sm-icon-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the sm generic-figure glyph (MarsUI Icon/User 18px, Space/4xl).
- `--ki-avatar-sm-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the sm box (32px circle, Figma Space/10xl).
- `--ki-avatar-xl-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for xl initials (MarsUI UI/Title 2: 18px).
- `--ki-avatar-xl-icon-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the xl generic-figure glyph (MarsUI Icon/User 28px, Space/9xl).
- `--ki-avatar-xl-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the xl box (56px circle, Figma Space/16xl).
- `--ki-avatar-xs-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for xs initials (MarsUI UI/Caption 1: 10px, same step as xxs — verified on Type=text Size=xs 10108:6226).
- `--ki-avatar-xs-icon-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the xs generic-figure glyph (MarsUI Icon/User 14px, same step as xxs — NOT the icon-button 16px ramp; verified on 10108:6230).
- `--ki-avatar-xs-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the xs box (24px circle, Figma Space/7xl).
- `--ki-avatar-xxs-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for xxs initials (MarsUI UI/Caption 1: 10px).
- `--ki-avatar-xxs-icon-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the xxs generic-figure glyph (MarsUI Icon/User 14px, Space/2xl).
- `--ki-avatar-xxs-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the xxs box (20px circle, Figma Space/5xl; specs/019-ki-avatar/design-extraction.md).
- `--ki-counter-ring-width`: Thickness of the separating ring.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.

### ki-avatar-group

A token-styled companion container that stacks `ki-avatar` children as one overlapping row with a configurable visible cap and a static "+N" overflow counter.

When to use: a compact "who is involved" stack — the members of a shared
document, project card or event row — where space deserves only the first
few identities and an exact "+N" counter accounts for the rest.
When NOT to use: as a member picker or expandable overflow (future interactive
grouping — the counter is static text, never a button), for a single
identity (use `ki-avatar` alone), or with children other than `ki-avatar`
(foreign markup is unsupported and not repaired, 016 precedent).

Examples:

`max` caps the visible stack; members beyond the cap are neither rendered nor exposed to assistive technology, and a static "+N" counter accounts exactly for the hidden rest:

```html
<ki-avatar-group max="3">
  <ki-avatar label="Ana García" initials="AG"></ki-avatar>
  <ki-avatar label="Sam Bel" initials="SB"></ki-avatar>
  <ki-avatar label="Iris Toma" initials="IT"></ki-avatar>
  <ki-avatar label="Leo Duarte" initials="LD"></ki-avatar>
  <ki-avatar label="Mia Chen" initials="MC"></ki-avatar>
</ki-avatar-group>
<!-- renders Ana, Sam and Iris, then "+2" -->
```

Without `max` — or with a cap that is not a positive whole number — every member renders and no counter appears (never "+0"):

```html
<ki-avatar-group>
  <ki-avatar label="Ana García" initials="AG"></ki-avatar>
  <ki-avatar label="Sam Bel" initials="SB"></ki-avatar>
</ki-avatar-group>
```

The group's `size` governs every visible member and the counter, overriding member-declared sizes so the stack stays uniform:

```html
<ki-avatar-group size="sm" max="2">
  <ki-avatar label="Ana García" initials="AG" size="xl"></ki-avatar>
  <ki-avatar label="Sam Bel" initials="SB"></ki-avatar>
  <ki-avatar label="Iris Toma" initials="IT"></ki-avatar>
</ki-avatar-group>
```

Attributes:
- `max` (number | undefined): Visible cap for the member stack. When the member count exceeds it, the first `max` members render followed by a "+N" counter accounting exactly for the hidden rest. Without it — or when it is not a positive whole number — every member renders and no counter appears; malformed agent-generated markup never breaks the page (FR-009, S14, S15).
- `size` ("lg" | "md" | "sm" | "xl" | "xs" | "xxs", default 'md'): Size step governing the metrics of every visible member and the counter (avatar vocabulary, FR-010). Member-declared sizes are overridden inside a group so the stack stays uniform (S6). An unrecognized value matches no style selector, so the group keeps the default medium metrics (FR-007).

Slots:
- (default): `ki-avatar` members, stacked in source order. Members beyond the visible cap are neither rendered nor exposed to assistive technology.

Parts:
- `counter`: The static "+N" overflow text trailing the stack.
- `group`: The stack row containing the members and the counter.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-avatar-font-family`: font family used by the avatar component for initials: the body family (Instrument Sans in onmars v2).
- `--ki-avatar-font-weight`: font weight used by the avatar component for initials (MarsUI Typeface/weight/body/medium: 600).
- `--ki-avatar-group-counter-bg`: color used by the avatar group component for the +N counter surface: Surface/special/secondary_alpha_base, the exact variable on the secondary-button-styled counter of every capped Avatar_group frame.
- `--ki-avatar-group-counter-border-color`: color used by the avatar group component for the counter border: Outline/secondary_button_top, the exact variable on the counter pill (a hairline in onmars v2).
- `--ki-avatar-group-counter-border-width`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the counter border (MarsUI 1px hairline on the counter pill).
- `--ki-avatar-group-counter-fg`: color used by the avatar group component for the +N counter text: Text/high_em, the exact variable on the counter label.
- `--ki-avatar-group-counter-radius`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the counter shape: Radius/component/radius_* resolves to 1000 in the MarsUI Round mode — the pill is a radius token, never an attribute.
- `--ki-avatar-group-counter-shadow`: shadow used by the avatar group component for the counter effects: the exact Component_effect/secondary_default pair (drop 0/2/1.5/-0.5 Elevation/shadow + inner White/3 0/2/3), flat in onmars v2; no backdrop blur (021 decision 3).
- `--ki-avatar-group-lg-counter-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the lg counter text (body_2 15px on the 48px frame).
- `--ki-avatar-group-lg-counter-padding-inline`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the lg counter inline padding (Space/xl 12px on the 48px frame).
- `--ki-avatar-group-lg-overlap`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the lg member overlap (the exact -12px on the 48px Avatar_group frame 10090:2873).
- `--ki-avatar-group-md-counter-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the md counter text (body_1 13px on the 40px frame).
- `--ki-avatar-group-md-counter-padding-inline`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the md counter inline padding (Space/lg 10px on the 40px frame).
- `--ki-avatar-group-md-overlap`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the md member overlap (the exact -12px on the 40px Avatar_group frame 10087:2701).
- `--ki-avatar-group-ring-color`: color used by the avatar group component for the separating ring: transparent while the onmars ring width is zero (FR-008; a future theme may resolve both).
- `--ki-avatar-group-ring-width`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the separating ring around stacked members: NO Avatar_group frame draws a ring (verified across all five sizes), so onmars resolves the capability to zero — the ring stays a theme decision, never an attribute (FR-008).
- `--ki-avatar-group-sm-counter-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the sm counter text (body_1 13px on the 32px frame — one step above the sm initials, verified).
- `--ki-avatar-group-sm-counter-padding-inline`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the sm counter inline padding (Space/md 8px on the 32px frame).
- `--ki-avatar-group-sm-overlap`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the sm member overlap (the exact -8px on the 32px Avatar_group frame 10087:2601).
- `--ki-avatar-group-xl-counter-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the xl counter text (title_2 18px on the 56px frame).
- `--ki-avatar-group-xl-counter-padding-inline`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the xl counter inline padding (Space/2xl 14px on the 56px frame).
- `--ki-avatar-group-xl-overlap`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the xl member overlap (the exact -12px on the 56px Avatar_group frame 10090:2973).
- `--ki-avatar-group-xs-counter-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the xs counter text (synthesized 24px step following the avatar xs initials size, declared for founder review).
- `--ki-avatar-group-xs-counter-padding-inline`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the xs counter inline padding (synthesized 24px step extending the verified 8/10/12/14 ramp, declared for founder review).
- `--ki-avatar-group-xs-overlap`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the xs member overlap: the 24px group step exists in no Figma frame (five-step set), so it inherits the -8px overlap of the neighboring 20/32px frames (synthesized step, spec 019 Assumptions).
- `--ki-avatar-group-xxs-counter-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the xxs counter text: no counter exists on the 20px frame, so the value follows the avatar xxs initials step (synthesized, declared for founder review).
- `--ki-avatar-group-xxs-counter-padding-inline`: dimension used by the avatar group component for xxs counter padding inline (raised to clear the 8px member tuck so the + glyph is never occluded; the 20px Figma frame ships no counter — synthesized step, founder review pending).
- `--ki-avatar-group-xxs-overlap`: dimension used by the avatar group component for the xxs member overlap (the -8px stack step on the 20px Avatar_group frame — named xs in Figma, the vocabulary skew recorded in spec 019 Assumptions).
- `--ki-avatar-lg-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for lg initials (MarsUI UI/Body 2: 15px).
- `--ki-avatar-lg-icon-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the lg generic-figure glyph (MarsUI Icon/User 24px, Space/7xl).
- `--ki-avatar-lg-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the lg box (48px circle, Figma Space/14xl).
- `--ki-avatar-md-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for md initials (MarsUI UI/Para: body_1 13px).
- `--ki-avatar-md-icon-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the md generic-figure glyph (MarsUI Icon/User 20px, Space/5xl).
- `--ki-avatar-md-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the md box (40px circle, Figma Space/12xl, node 10011:947).
- `--ki-avatar-radius`: dimension used by the avatar component for the shape: Radius/radius_round bound to every avatar variant — the circle is a radius token, never an attribute (002 shape precedent, FR-005).
- `--ki-avatar-sm-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for sm initials (MarsUI UI/Caption 2: 12px).
- `--ki-avatar-sm-icon-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the sm generic-figure glyph (MarsUI Icon/User 18px, Space/4xl).
- `--ki-avatar-sm-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the sm box (32px circle, Figma Space/10xl).
- `--ki-avatar-xl-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for xl initials (MarsUI UI/Title 2: 18px).
- `--ki-avatar-xl-icon-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the xl generic-figure glyph (MarsUI Icon/User 28px, Space/9xl).
- `--ki-avatar-xl-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the xl box (56px circle, Figma Space/16xl).
- `--ki-avatar-xs-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for xs initials (MarsUI UI/Caption 1: 10px, same step as xxs — verified on Type=text Size=xs 10108:6226).
- `--ki-avatar-xs-icon-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the xs generic-figure glyph (MarsUI Icon/User 14px, same step as xxs — NOT the icon-button 16px ramp; verified on 10108:6230).
- `--ki-avatar-xs-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the xs box (24px circle, Figma Space/7xl).
- `--ki-avatar-xxs-font-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for xxs initials (MarsUI UI/Caption 1: 10px).
- `--ki-avatar-xxs-icon-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the xxs generic-figure glyph (MarsUI Icon/User 14px, Space/2xl).
- `--ki-avatar-xxs-size`: dimension used by the avatar component for the xxs box (20px circle, Figma Space/5xl; specs/019-ki-avatar/design-extraction.md).
- `--ki-effect-component-secondary-hover-shadow`: MarsUI Component_effect/secondary_hover: drops as primary_hover plus inner White/8 0/2/3. Pair with --ki-effect-component-backdrop-filter.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-duration-medium-1`: M3 md.sys.motion.duration.medium1 (250ms). onmars: MarsUI moderate step (240ms, 2x the 120ms base).
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-motion-easing-standard`: Standard interaction transition easing curve.

### ki-badge

A static, non-interactive status pill.

When to use: annotate an entity with short status text (a state, a
category) whose meaning is carried by the label itself; the tone color
only reinforces the text, it never replaces it.
When NOT to use: feedback that must be announced (that is
ki-alert's job — the badge has no live region), an interactive
chip, filter or button, empty content (the label IS the meaning), or a
notification-counter overlay (use ki-counter).

Examples:

The slotted label is the sole carrier of meaning; `tone` only reinforces it with the `--ki-badge-{tone}-*` token colors, and an unrecognized value keeps the neutral appearance:

```html
<ki-badge>Draft</ki-badge>
<ki-badge tone="info">Beta</ki-badge>
<ki-badge tone="success">Active</ki-badge>
<ki-badge tone="warning">Trial ends soon</ki-badge>
<ki-badge tone="danger">Suspended</ki-badge>
```

`size` selects the metric scale (`sm` or `md`, default `md`):

```html
<ki-badge tone="success" size="sm">Synced</ki-badge>
```

A typical placement — trailing status on a list entry:

```html
<ki-list>
  <ki-list-item>
    Production deploy
    <ki-badge slot="end" tone="success">Healthy</ki-badge>
  </ki-list-item>
</ki-list>
```

Attributes:
- `size` ("md" | "sm" | "xs", default 'md'): Metric scale (`--ki-badge-{size}-*` tokens): 20, 24 or 28px tall in onmars, with 12px text at every size. An unrecognized value falls back to the `md` metrics the same way.
- `tone` ("danger" | "info" | "neutral" | "success" | "warning", default 'neutral'): Semantic intent, never appearance: each tone resolves its colors from the `--ki-badge-{tone}-*` tokens. An unrecognized value matches no style selector, so the badge keeps the neutral appearance (fallback by CSS construction — no validation code).

Slots:
- (default): The label: short status text, the sole carrier of meaning.

Parts:
- `badge`: The pill: background, foreground, border, radius, metrics and typography.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-badge-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter for the neutral badge surface.
- `--ki-badge-border-width`: dimension used by the badge component for border width (MarsUI tone tags carry width 0 in default state; only the neutral type draws its 1px edge via ki.badge.neutral.border-width. material3 keeps its border via its override).
- `--ki-badge-danger-bg`: color used by the badge component for danger background (MarsUI Surface/danger_base_em_alpha: tone-500 at 12% light — the tint composites over any surface and the dark alias adapts automatically).
- `--ki-badge-danger-border`: color used by the badge component for danger border.
- `--ki-badge-danger-fg`: color used by the badge component for danger foreground.
- `--ki-badge-font-family`: font family used by the badge component for font family.
- `--ki-badge-font-weight`: font weight used by the badge component for font weight.
- `--ki-badge-info-bg`: color used by the badge component for info background (MarsUI Surface/info_base_em_alpha: tone-500 at 12% light — the tint composites over any surface and the dark alias adapts automatically).
- `--ki-badge-info-border`: color used by the badge component for info border.
- `--ki-badge-info-fg`: color used by the badge component for info foreground.
- `--ki-badge-md-font-size`: dimension used by the badge component for md font size (MarsUI UI/Caption 2: 12px at both sm and md; only xs drops to Caption 1).
- `--ki-badge-md-height`: dimension used by the badge component for md height (MarsUI Tag md outer height 28px).
- `--ki-badge-md-line-height`: dimension used by the badge component for md line height (MarsUI caption_2 16px).
- `--ki-badge-md-padding-inline`: dimension used by the badge component for md padding inline (MarsUI total text inset 10px; paired with the border-width 0 + border-box change so the badge does not shrink).
- `--ki-badge-md-radius`: dimension used by the badge component for md radius (MarsUI Tag: Radius/component/radius_sm 8px at both sm and md).
- `--ki-badge-neutral-bg`: color used by the badge component for neutral background (MarsUI secondary Tag: Surface/special/secondary_alpha_base, the same fill as ki-button secondary; opaque white in onmars v2, translucent only where a theme turns that back on. material3 keeps the opaque s2 chip via its override).
- `--ki-badge-neutral-border`: color used by the badge component for neutral border (MarsUI secondary Tag edge: Outline/secondary_button_top; drawn at ki.badge.neutral.border-width).
- `--ki-badge-neutral-border-width`: dimension used by the badge component for the neutral border width: MarsUI draws the 1px edge only on this type.
- `--ki-badge-neutral-fg`: color used by the badge component for neutral foreground.
- `--ki-badge-sm-font-size`: dimension used by the badge component for sm font size.
- `--ki-badge-sm-height`: dimension used by the badge component for sm height.
- `--ki-badge-sm-line-height`: dimension used by the badge component for sm line height.
- `--ki-badge-sm-padding-inline`: dimension used by the badge component for sm padding inline (MarsUI total text inset 8px; paired with the border-width 0 + border-box change).
- `--ki-badge-sm-radius`: dimension used by the badge component for sm radius (MarsUI Tag silhouette is an 8px rounded rect — Radius/component/radius_sm — never a pill).
- `--ki-badge-success-bg`: color used by the badge component for success background (MarsUI Surface/success_base_em_alpha: tone-500 at 12% light — the tint composites over any surface and the dark alias adapts automatically).
- `--ki-badge-success-border`: color used by the badge component for success border.
- `--ki-badge-success-fg`: color used by the badge component for success foreground.
- `--ki-badge-warning-bg`: color used by the badge component for warning background (MarsUI Surface/warning_base_em_alpha: tone-500 at 12% light — the tint composites over any surface and the dark alias adapts automatically).
- `--ki-badge-warning-border`: color used by the badge component for warning border.
- `--ki-badge-warning-fg`: color used by the badge component for warning foreground.
- `--ki-badge-xs-font-size`: dimension used by the badge component for xs font size (Tag 10106:4651 xs). Figma draws caption_1, 10px; caption_2, 12px, is the smallest text the library ships (spec 050 D7).
- `--ki-badge-xs-height`: dimension used by the badge component for xs height (Tag 10106:4651 xs: 20px).
- `--ki-badge-xs-line-height`: dimension used by the badge component for xs line height (caption_2 16px, the same height as caption_1).
- `--ki-badge-xs-padding-inline`: dimension used by the badge component for xs padding inline (Tag 10106:4651 xs: Space/xs plus the Text_wrap Space/xxs, 6px).
- `--ki-badge-xs-radius`: dimension used by the badge component for xs radius (Tag 10106:4651 xs binds Radius/small-component/xs).
- `--ki-effect-component-secondary-default-shadow`: MarsUI Component_effect/secondary_default: drop 0/2/1.5/-0.5 plus inner White/3 0/2/3. Pair with --ki-effect-component-backdrop-filter.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-outline-secondary-button-bottom`: semantic color for outline secondary button bottom.

### ki-breadcrumb

A path of ancestor links ending at the current page, with optional overflow.

When to use: show the current page in a deeper hierarchy using direct ki-breadcrumb-item children ordered from root to current.
When NOT to use: switch between peer routes, toggle peer panels, or display progress through a form.

Examples:

## Show the path to the current page

```html
<ki-breadcrumb label="Project path">
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/workspace">Workspace</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/workspace/projects">Projects</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item current>Settings</ki-breadcrumb-item>
</ki-breadcrumb>
```

## Collapse middle levels

```html
<ki-breadcrumb label="Release path" max-items="4">
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/workspace">Workspace</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/projects">Projects</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/projects/kimen">Kimen</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/projects/kimen/packages">Packages</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/projects/kimen/releases">Releases</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item current>v2.4.0</ki-breadcrumb-item>
</ki-breadcrumb>
```

In this example the overflow has three levels. The trail shows Workspace,
the overflow button, Releases, and v2.4.0.

## Render a guarded breadcrumb

Put breadcrumb items in the default slot and supply plain-text item labels.
The surface's URL policy applies to each destination. Native links have no
custom action binding.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "root": {
    "component": "ki-breadcrumb",
    "props": { "label": "Project path" },
    "slots": {
      "": [
        {
          "component": "ki-breadcrumb-item",
          "props": { "href": "/workspace" },
          "slots": { "": ["Workspace"] }
        },
        {
          "component": "ki-breadcrumb-item",
          "props": { "current": true },
          "slots": { "": ["Settings"] }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Attributes:
- `label` (string, default 'Breadcrumb'): Accessible name of the navigation landmark.
- `max-items` (number | undefined): Optional overflow threshold. Above it, keep the first and last two levels visible. Positive values are rounded down and clamped to four. Omit this prop, or pass a non-positive or non-finite value, to show the full trail.
- `more-label` (string, default 'Show {n} more levels'): Localizable name of the overflow control. Use {n} for the hidden level count.

Slots:
- (default): Direct ki-breadcrumb-item children in hierarchy order.

Parts:
- `current`: The current page label.
- `label`: The label of an ancestor with no destination.
- `link`: A visible native ancestor link.
- `list`: The ordered list of visible levels.
- `list-item`: A list entry for a level or the overflow control.
- `menu`: The anchored menu of collapsed levels.
- `menu-item`: A destination or unavailable level in the overflow menu.
- `more-button`: The overflow menu button.
- `navigation`: The named navigation landmark.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-breadcrumb-bg`: Transparent backing for ancestor text and the overflow trigger.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-current-bg`: Transparent backing for the current level.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-current-fg`: Emphasized foreground of the current level.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-fg`: Medium-emphasis ink for ancestors and the overflow trigger, strengthened in more-contrast mode.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-gap`: Gap between breadcrumb rows, levels and their chevrons.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-glyph-size`: Size of the ellipsis glyph.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-hover-bg`: Backing for the active overflow trigger and highlighted overflow links.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-hover-fg`: Foreground for the active overflow trigger and highlighted overflow links.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-menu-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter of the overflow menu, none by default.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-menu-bg`: Surface behind the overflow menu entries.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-menu-bg-image`: Optional image layered over the overflow menu surface.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-menu-fg`: Text of overflow menu entries.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-menu-max-block-size`: Maximum block size of the scrollable overflow menu.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-menu-padding`: Inset around the overflow menu entries.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-menu-radius`: Outer radius of the overflow menu.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-menu-shadow`: Elevation of the overflow menu above the page.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-padding-block`: Block inset of a level label.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-padding-inline`: Inline inset of a level label.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-radius`: Radius of the overflow trigger and level focus outlines.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-separator`: Foreground of the decorative breadcrumb chevron.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-separator-size`: Edge length of the decorative chevron before rotation.
- `--ki-breadcrumb-separator-stroke`: Stroke width of the decorative chevron.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography line height body 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-underline-offset`: Gap between text and its underline.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-medium`: semantic font weight for typography weight body medium.

### ki-breadcrumb-item

One declarative level in a breadcrumb path.

When to use: declare a direct child of ki-breadcrumb in hierarchy order. Give ancestors an href and use short text labels. The last level is the current page.
When NOT to use: render a standalone link or display an interactive control inside the label.

Examples:

Place each item directly inside a breadcrumb. Use the item's text for its
label and add `href` to link to an ancestor page. A level without
`href` provides context as text. Put the current page last.

```html
<ki-breadcrumb label="Settings path">
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/workspace">Workspace</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item>Administration</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item current>Settings</ki-breadcrumb-item>
</ki-breadcrumb>
```

Attributes:
- `current` (boolean, default false): Explicitly marks the final level as current. The owning breadcrumb treats its final level as current by position, including when this marker is omitted.
- `href` (string | undefined, URL): Native destination for an ancestor level. Leaves the label as text when omitted. The final level never links away from the current page.

Slots:
- (default): Plain-text label mirrored by the owning breadcrumb.

Parts: none

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-button

A token-styled action button with native button semantics.

When to use: trigger the single main action of a view, supporting actions
in descending hierarchy, confirming/destructive actions through tone, or
persistent actions such as Bold with `toggle`.
While the action a button started is in progress, set `loading` on that
button instead of disabling it.
When NOT to use: navigation, icon-only actions, form values, or the
progress of a page or region (use ki-progress).

Examples:

A standalone primary action:

```html
<ki-button variant="primary">Save</ki-button>
```

In momentary mode `type` defaults to `submit`. Use `type="button"` for an independent action inside a form.

```html
<form>
  <ki-button type="button">Cancel</ki-button>
  <ki-button variant="primary">Save changes</ki-button>
</form>
```

Use `toggle` for a persistent action. `selected` sets the starting state and each activation changes `aria-pressed` while keeping the label. Toggle mode acts independently of form submission and reset, regardless of `type`.

```html
<ki-button id="pin" variant="outline" toggle selected>Pin</ki-button>
<script type="module">
  const button = document.getElementById('pin');
  button.addEventListener('ki-change', ({ detail: { selected } }) => {
    console.log('Pinned', selected);
  });
</script>
```

Programmatic writes to `selected` are silent. A parent coordinating several toggles can listen for their bubbling `ki-change` events and update their `selected` values together.

Open a dialog with `command="show-modal"` and its ID in `commandfor`. The
dialog and invoker share a document or shadow root. The command takes
precedence over form submission or reset.

```html
<ki-button commandfor="draft-preview" command="show-modal">Preview draft</ki-button>
<ki-dialog id="draft-preview" heading="Draft preview">
  This draft is visible only to you.
  <ki-button slot="footer" commandfor="draft-preview" command="close">Done</ki-button>
</ki-dialog>
```

Programmatic creation after registration; string attributes and properties are interchangeable:

```ts
import { defineCustomElement } from '@kimen/elements/ki-button';

defineCustomElement();

const saveButton = document.createElement('ki-button');
saveButton.setAttribute('type', 'button');
saveButton.textContent = 'Save';
document.body.append(saveButton);
```

While the action a button started is in progress, set `loading` on it instead of `disabled`: it keeps its width and focus, ignores further activation (it neither submits nor resets its form), draws a spinner in place of its label and announces `loading-label` (default "Loading") as a polite status message. Clear it when the action ends:

```html
<form id="profile">
  <ki-button variant="primary" loading-label="Saving">Save changes</ki-button>
</form>
<script type="module">
  const form = document.getElementById('profile');
  const save = form.querySelector('ki-button');
  form.addEventListener('submit', async (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    save.loading = true;
    try {
      await fetch('/profile', { method: 'POST', body: new FormData(form) });
    } finally {
      save.loading = false;
    }
  });
</script>
```

Attributes:
- `command` ("close" | "request-close" | "show-modal" | undefined): Dialog action to run for `commandfor`. Use `show-modal` to open, `close` for direct dismissal, or `request-close` for guarded dismissal. Choose a command for local dialog control and omit it for other actions.
- `commandfor` (string | undefined): ID of a ki-dialog in the same document or shadow tree as this button. Set it together with `command` to connect a dialog declaratively.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Prevents activation, removes the button from keyboard reach, and exposes the unavailable state through the internal native button. Wins over `loading` when both are set. When NOT to use: do not use disabled for pending/loading semantics; use `loading`.
- `loading` (boolean, default false): Pending state of the action this button started (saving, sending). While set, every activation is blocked (pointer, Enter and Space) and the button neither submits nor resets its form, but it stays focusable, in the Tab order and at its width: the label stays laid out, transparent, and a spinner is drawn in its place. The internal native button is exposed with `aria-disabled="true"` and keeps its name, and `loadingLabel` is announced as a polite status message. `disabled`, and a disabled fieldset, win over it. The application sets it when the action starts and clears it when the action ends. When to use: while the work a click on this button started is running, so a second activation cannot repeat it. When NOT to use: for a button the person cannot use yet (use `disabled`), or for the progress of a page or region (use ki-progress).
