- `loading-label` (string, default 'Loading'): Text of the polite status message announced while `loading` is set. Override for localization; the default English string is the button's only built-in user-visible text. When to use: provide a localized message whenever the document language is not English, or a more specific one ("Saving"). When NOT to use: do not repeat the button's label here; the person already hears it on focus.
- `name` (string | undefined): Form-data key contributed when this button submits its form. When NOT to use: omit when no submitter value should be sent.
- `selected` (boolean, default false): Current press state in toggle mode. Set this to initialize or synchronize the state programmatically without emitting a change.
- `size` ("lg" | "md" | "sm" | "xl" | "xs", default 'md'): Token-backed button size. Every size keeps at least the minimum pointer target; choose the size that matches the density of the surrounding UI. When NOT to use: do not use `ki-button` for icon-only compact controls.
- `toggle` (boolean, default false): Enables persistent press state for an action such as Bold. The native button exposes `aria-pressed` and each activation switches `selected`. Use the same label in both states. A toggle does not submit or reset a form.
- `tone` ("danger" | "neutral" | "success", default 'neutral'): Semantic intent for the action, independent of hierarchy. Use `success` for confirming actions and `danger` for destructive actions. Toggle palettes are specific to the variant. When NOT to use: do not use tone for visual hierarchy; use `variant`.
- `type` ("button" | "reset" | "submit", default 'submit'): Native form action type: `submit` submits the owning form (running constraint validation and contributing `name`/`value` to the form data), `reset` restores field defaults, and `button` leaves the form alone. Toggle mode and configured dialog commands take precedence over form actions. Cancel a submission from the form's `submit` event (`preventDefault()`); unlike a native button, `preventDefault()` on the `click` event does not cancel it. During submission `event.submitter` is a transient native button carrying this element's `name`/`value`, not the `ki-button` host. When NOT to use: use `button` when the action must never submit a form.
- `value` (string | undefined): Form-data value paired with `name` when this button submits its form. When NOT to use: omit when the default empty submitter value is intended.
- `variant` ("ghost" | "outline" | "primary" | "quaternary" | "secondary" | "tertiary", default 'secondary'): Visual hierarchy for the action. Use filled `primary` for the single main action, outlined `secondary` for supporting actions, `quaternary` for neutral text actions, `ghost` for accent text actions and `outline` for an unfilled action with a visible boundary. When NOT to use: do not use variant to signal success or danger; use `tone` for intent.

Slots:
- (default): Label content. This is the accessible name source.
- `end`: Trailing icon or media. Follows writing direction.
- `start`: Leading icon or media. Follows writing direction.

Parts:
- `button`: Internal native button.
- `label`: Label wrapper around the default slot.
- `spinner`: Loading spinner drawn at the center of the button, in the button's foreground ink, rendered only while `loading` is in effect.

Events:
- `ki-change` (CustomEvent<{ selected: boolean }>): Emitted after toggle activation with the new selected state.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-button-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter for button and icon-button variants; none in onmars v2.
- `--ki-button-border-width`: dimension used by the button component for border width (MarsUI outline stroke: 1px).
- `--ki-button-focus-ring-color`: color used by the button component for focus ring color.
- `--ki-button-focus-ring-offset`: dimension used by the button component for focus ring offset.
- `--ki-button-focus-ring-shadow`: shadow used by the button component for the focus ring glow (MarsUI Focus/primary: 3px spread ring).
- `--ki-button-focus-ring-width`: dimension used by the button component for focus ring width.
- `--ki-button-font-family`: font family used by the button component for font family.
- `--ki-button-font-weight`: font weight used by the button component for font weight.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-hover-bg`: color used by the button component for ghost danger hover background.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-hover-border`: color used by the button component for ghost danger hover border.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-hover-fg`: color used by the button component for ghost danger hover foreground.

- `--ki-button-toggle-unselected-fg`: Foreground of unselected filled toggle buttons.

- `--ki-button-xs-font-size`: dimension used by the button component for xs font size: caption_2, 12px, the smallest size the library ships for informative text (spec 002 amendment A1, issue #321). The Figma Button master draws caption_1, 10px.
- `--ki-button-xs-gap`: dimension used by the button component for xs gap (MarsUI effective icon-to-text gap 4px).
- `--ki-button-xs-height`: dimension used by the button component for xs height.
- `--ki-button-xs-icon-size`: dimension used by the button component for xs icon size (MarsUI 14px).
- `--ki-button-xs-line-height`: dimension used by the button component for xs line height (caption_2 16px, the same height as caption_1).
- `--ki-button-xs-min-target`: dimension used by the button component for xs min target.
- `--ki-button-xs-padding-inline`: dimension used by the button component for xs padding inline.
- `--ki-button-xs-radius`: dimension used by the button component for xs radius (Button master 8003:300 binds Radius/small-component/xs, the scale a radius mode reassigns).
- `--ki-button-xs-spinner-size`: dimension used by the button component for the xs loading spinner box (14px, the xs icon size; spec 046 D5: no Figma source, the spinner takes the place of the content).
- `--ki-density-control-offset`: Added to the block size of every scaled control and row (button, icon button, field, select, textarea, option, list item, tab). Components floor the result at ki.size.target-min.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-effect-component-no-backdrop-filter`: An unadorned surface applies no backdrop filter.
- `--ki-elevation-none`: Flat surfaces carry no resting shadow.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-outline-none`: semantic color for outline none.
- `--ki-surface-image-none`: An unadorned surface has no background image.

### ki-button-group

Arranges related actions as a spaced group, attached group, or keyboard toolbar.

When to use: place two to five related actions together, present a primary
action with a menu of alternatives, or give formatting tools one Tab stop.
When NOT to use: for a single-choice setting, unrelated actions, or navigation.
Use a segmented control for a single-choice setting and links for navigation.

Examples:

# Using ki-button-group

## Spaced and attached groups

Use a label that describes what the actions do together. In attached mode the
first button provides the common variant and size. An explicit group size
applies in both modes.

```html
<ki-button-group label="History">
  <ki-button type="button">Undo</ki-button>
  <ki-button type="button">Redo</ki-button>
</ki-button-group>

<ki-button-group label="Clipboard" attached size="sm">
  <ki-button type="button">Copy</ki-button>
  <ki-button type="button">Paste</ki-button>
</ki-button-group>
```

## Formatting toolbar

Import the glyphs used by your page. Give each icon button a tooltip using the
same label. The application sets `pressed` as the formatting state changes. The native button exposes it as `aria-pressed`.

```js
import '@kimen/elements/icons/bold';
import '@kimen/elements/icons/list';
```

```html
<ki-button-group label="Formatting" toolbar size="sm">
  <ki-tooltip label="Bold">
    <ki-icon-button label="Bold" variant="ghost" pressed="true">
      <ki-icon name="bold"></ki-icon>
    </ki-icon-button>
  </ki-tooltip>
  <span role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical"></span>
  <ki-tooltip label="Bulleted list">
    <ki-icon-button label="Bulleted list" variant="ghost">
      <ki-icon name="list"></ki-icon>
    </ki-icon-button>
  </ki-tooltip>
</ki-button-group>
```

## Split button

With a build that includes `ki-menu`, anchor the menu to the chevron action.
Import `@kimen/elements/icons/chevron-down` before mounting the group. Handle the
main button's click and menu selection as separate actions.

```html
<ki-button-group label="Save actions" attached>
  <ki-button type="button" variant="primary">Save</ki-button>
  <ki-tooltip label="More save options">
    <ki-icon-button id="save-options" label="More save options" aria-haspopup="menu" expanded="false">
      <ki-icon name="chevron-down"></ki-icon>
    </ki-icon-button>
  </ki-tooltip>
</ki-button-group>

<ki-menu anchor="save-options">
  <ki-menu-item value="draft">Save as draft</ki-menu-item>
  <ki-menu-item value="copy">Save a copy</ki-menu-item>
</ki-menu>
```

Keep the icon button's `expanded` property in sync with the menu's `open`
state. Its native button exposes that state as `aria-expanded`.

Attributes:
- `attached` (boolean, default false): Joins neighboring actions at their inner edges. Buttons share the first button's variant and use its size when the group has no explicit size. Use for a closely related set of actions or for a split button.
- `label` (string, required): Required accessible name for the group or toolbar (for example, "Text formatting"). Provide a localized name that describes the actions' shared purpose.
- `size` ("lg" | "md" | "sm" | "xl" | "xs" | undefined): Applies one token-backed size to each button while it belongs to the group. Omit it to keep individual sizes in spaced mode.
- `toolbar` (boolean, default false): Gives the group toolbar semantics, a framed surface and one Tab stop. Horizontal arrows, Home and End move between the toolbar's actions.

Slots:
- (default): Related ki-button and ki-icon-button controls, in reading order. Wrap labeled icon actions in ki-tooltip with the same label to show the label on focus and hover. A toolbar can also include vertical separators.

Parts:
- `group`: The named group or toolbar surface.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-button-group-attached-gap`: Gap between joined actions.
- `--ki-button-group-attached-radius`: Radius of the logical corners along a shared button edge.
- `--ki-button-group-backdrop-filter`: Complete optional backdrop filter for the toolbar surface.
- `--ki-button-group-bg`: Toolbar surface colour.
- `--ki-button-group-bg-image`: Optional decorative image over the toolbar surface.
- `--ki-button-group-border-color`: Thin toolbar frame colour.
- `--ki-button-group-border-width`: Thickness of the toolbar frame and divider.
- `--ki-button-group-divider`: Decorative toolbar separator ink.
- `--ki-button-group-divider-size`: Block size of a vertical toolbar separator.
- `--ki-button-group-fg`: Default toolbar foreground on its raised surface.
- `--ki-button-group-gap`: Gap between actions in a spaced group.
- `--ki-button-group-padding`: Toolbar frame inset and divider margin.
- `--ki-button-group-radius`: Logical outside radius of the toolbar frame.
- `--ki-button-group-seam-overlap`: Shared-edge overlap between adjacent attached actions.
- `--ki-button-group-toolbar-gap`: Gap between toolbar actions.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-card

A card surface for grouping related content, with an optional primary link or action.

When to use: group related media, a title, supporting text and actions into
one scannable surface. Set `href` for navigation or `interactive` for a
declared action. Give a clickable card one text heading in the header
slot and place secondary controls in the body or footer.
When NOT to use: as a form field, fieldset, page landmark, section replacement
or nested card. Use a standalone button or link for a control without
supporting content.

Examples:

The four regions — `media`, `header`, default body and `footer`; supply the heading element yourself, because plain text in the `header` slot carries no heading semantics:

```html
<ki-card>
  <img slot="media" src="/telemetry.png" alt="Orbit trajectory plot" />
  <h3 slot="header">Mission telemetry</h3>
  <p>Latest downlink completed at 14:02 UTC. All systems nominal.</p>
  <ki-button slot="footer" type="button" variant="secondary">View details</ki-button>
</ki-card>
```

Any subset of regions works — a text-only card is valid:

```html
<ki-card>
  <h3 slot="header">Storage almost full</h3>
  <p>You are using 92% of your plan. Consider archiving old projects.</p>
</ki-card>
```

Place independent actions in the `footer` slot.

```html
<ki-card>
  <h3 slot="header">Invite your team</h3>
  <p>Collaborators can review specs and approve merges.</p>
  <ki-button slot="footer" type="button" variant="primary">Invite</ki-button>
  <ki-button slot="footer" type="button" variant="ghost">Later</ki-button>
</ki-card>
```

Use `href` for a primary destination. Use `interactive` to emit the
`ki-activate` action event. Supply a single text heading for either option
and keep secondary controls in their own slot content.

```html
<ki-card href="/incidents/42" variant="outlined">
  <h3 slot="header">Search index rebuild</h3>
  <p>Scheduled for midnight.</p>
  <ki-button slot="footer" type="button" variant="secondary">Bookmark</ki-button>
</ki-card>

<ki-card interactive variant="filled">
  <h3 slot="header">Preview monthly report</h3>
  <p>Review the new report before publishing it.</p>
</ki-card>
```

Attributes:
- `href` (string | undefined, URL): Destination for the card's title link. Supply a text heading in the header slot. A nonblank href takes precedence over interactive.
- `interactive` (boolean | undefined, default false): Gives a titled card a primary button that emits ki-activate. Use href for navigation. Keep other actions in separate controls in the card.
- `variant` ("default" | "elevated" | "filled" | "outlined" | undefined, default 'default'): Surface treatment. Choose elevated for a raised panel, filled for a tinted group or outlined for a bordered surface. Use default to follow the theme's existing card treatment.

Slots:
- (default): Body region for supporting text or arbitrary composed content.
- `footer`: Closing region for actions such as `ki-button`; no dedicated actions slot exists in v1.
- `header`: Title region. Supply one nonempty text heading at the surrounding document level for a clickable card.
- `media`: Leading visual region for an image, video or illustration.

Parts:
- `body`: Body region wrapper around the default slot.
- `card`: Card surface: background, border, radius, elevation and region gap.
- `footer`: Footer region wrapper.
- `header`: Header region wrapper.
- `media`: Media region wrapper.
- `trigger`: Native link or action button in a clickable card’s heading.

Events:
- `ki-activate` (CustomEvent<void>): Fires once when the user activates an action card by pointer or keyboard.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-card-backdrop-filter`: Complete card backdrop filter, off by default.
- `--ki-card-bg`: color used by the card component for background (MarsUI Dashboard masters bind Surface/special/light-s0_dark-s1: white light / Dark/900 dark; #f9f9fa is the nested media panel, so the old s1 value inverted the surface hierarchy).
- `--ki-card-bg-image`: Optional decorative image over the card background.
- `--ki-card-body-padding`: dimension used by the card component for body padding.
- `--ki-card-border-color`: color used by the card component for border color (MarsUI Outline/base_em hairline — painted on large Chart cards; Dashboard_info leaves width 0, which stays the default via ki.card.border-width).
- `--ki-card-border-width`: dimension used by the card component for border width.
- `--ki-card-elevated-bg`: Raised card background.
- `--ki-card-elevated-fg`: Text on the elevated card background.
- `--ki-card-elevated-shadow`: Resting shadow for an elevated card.
- `--ki-card-elevation`: Card resting elevation: MarsUI elevation ramp level e1 (brief §5, drop 0/1/1/-0.5 in the scheme shadow color; replaces the migrated M2-era shadow).
- `--ki-card-fg`: color used by the card component for foreground.
- `--ki-card-filled-bg`: Tinted card background.
- `--ki-card-filled-fg`: Text on the filled card background.
- `--ki-card-footer-padding`: dimension used by the card component for footer padding.
- `--ki-card-gap`: dimension used by the card component for gap (MarsUI Dashboard_info/Chart rhythm between regions 12px; material3 keeps zero via its override).
- `--ki-card-header-padding`: dimension used by the card component for header padding.
- `--ki-card-hover-overlay`: Pointer hover state layer on a primary-action card.
- `--ki-card-hover-shadow`: Hover shadow of a primary-action card.
- `--ki-card-media-padding`: dimension used by the card component for media padding (MarsUI Dashboard masters inset media panels 8px inline; material3 keeps full-bleed zero via its override).
- `--ki-card-media-radius`: dimension used by the card component for slotted media corner radius (MarsUI nested media panel Radius/big_component/radius_sm 20px; formalizes the fallback ki-card.css already consumes).
- `--ki-card-outlined-bg`: Page-coloured background for an outlined card.
- `--ki-card-outlined-border`: Boundary colour for an outlined card.
- `--ki-card-outlined-border-width`: Hairline width for an outlined card.
- `--ki-card-outlined-fg`: Text on the outlined card background.
- `--ki-card-padding-block`: dimension used by the card component for the surface block padding (16px carried by the card surface itself so stacked region paddings no longer double to 32px; formalizes the fallback ki-card.css already consumes).
- `--ki-card-radius`: dimension used by the card component for radius (MarsUI card surfaces ride the big_component scale: Dashboard_info 400x128 binds radius_xs 16px; large Chart cards anchor radius_lg 28px).
- `--ki-card-title-family`: Family used for a clickable card title.
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-elevation-e2`: MarsUI Elevation/e2 (cumulative: e1 layers plus 0/3/3/-1.5).
- `--ki-elevation-none`: Flat surfaces carry no resting shadow.
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-motion-distance-sm`: Motion travel distance sm (4px): small slide/settle offsets.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-duration-medium-1`: M3 md.sys.motion.duration.medium1 (250ms). onmars: MarsUI moderate step (240ms, 2x the 120ms base).
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-motion-easing-standard`: Standard interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-title-1`: semantic dimension for typography line height title 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-title-1`: semantic dimension for typography size title 1.

### ki-carousel

An ordered, swipeable sequence with previous and next controls and position feedback.

When to use: show a short set of related highlights, onboarding steps or media panels.
Give the carousel a meaningful label and supply one ki-carousel-item per slide.
When NOT to use: hide essential content behind rotation, replace ordinary page navigation,
or present slides that readers need to compare side by side at the same time.

Examples:

# Carousel examples

```html
<ki-carousel label="Product tour" slides-per-view="2" slides-per-move="2">
  <ki-carousel-item>Discover the tools</ki-carousel-item>
  <ki-carousel-item>Pick a theme</ki-carousel-item>
  <ki-carousel-item>Set up your workspace</ki-carousel-item>
  <ki-carousel-item>Share your first surface</ki-carousel-item>
</ki-carousel>
```

```js
const carousel = document.querySelector('ki-carousel');
carousel.addEventListener('ki-slide-change', ({ detail }) => {
  console.log(detail.index);
});
await carousel.goTo(3);
```

With per-tag imports, define both `ki-carousel` and `ki-carousel-item`.

Attributes:
- `autoplay` (number | undefined, minimum 1, maximum 2147483647): Rotation interval in milliseconds. Omitting it leaves rotation off.
- `carousel-role-description` (string, default 'carousel'): Accessible role description of the region.
- `current` (number, default 1, minimum 1): One-based leading slide. Setting it moves the carousel and clamps the index to the available leading positions.
- `label` (string, required): Required accessible name of the carousel region.
- `layout` ("full-screen" | "hero" | "multi-browse" | "single" | "uncontained", default 'single'): Item arrangement. Full-screen uses a vertical, full-viewport slide.
- `loop` (boolean, default false): Whether navigating past one endpoint wraps to the other.
- `navigation` (boolean, default true): Whether to show the Previous and Next buttons. The viewport stays keyboard-operable.
- `next-label` (string, default 'Next slide'): Accessible label of the Next button.
- `pagination` (boolean, default true): Whether to show the noninteractive slide position indicator.
- `pause-label` (string, default 'Pause'): Visible and accessible label of the Pause button.
- `play-label` (string, default 'Play'): Visible and accessible label of the Play button.
- `position-label` (string, default 'Slide position'): Accessible label of the position indicator.
- `previous-label` (string, default 'Previous slide'): Accessible label of the Previous button.
- `slide-label` (string, default '{index} of {count}'): Spoken slide name and announcement. Use {index} and {count} as placeholders.
- `slide-role-description` (string, default 'slide'): Accessible role description of each slide group.
- `slides-per-move` (number, default 1, minimum 1): Number of positions advanced by Previous, Next and automatic rotation.
- `slides-per-view` (number, default 1, minimum 1): Number of slides visible together in the single layout. Material 3 layouts determine their own item widths.

Slots:
- (default): Direct ki-carousel-item children in reading order.

Parts:
- `announcement`: Visually hidden live region for manual changes.
- `controls`: Row containing slide position and navigation.
- `next`: Next slide button.
- `position`: Position indicator and optional numeric position.
- `previous`: Previous slide button.
- `rotation`: Play or Pause button when automatic rotation is configured.
- `viewport`: Scroll-snap viewport and its keyboard focus outline.

Events:
- `ki-slide-change` (CustomEvent<CarouselSlideChangeDetail>): Reports the one-based index when the leading slide changes.

Methods:
- `goTo(index)` (Promise<void>): Moves to the requested one-based leading position within the available range.
- `next()` (Promise<void>): Advances by slidesPerMove.
- `previous()` (Promise<void>): Moves back by slidesPerMove.

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-carousel-control-backdrop-filter`: Complete optional backdrop filter for the carousel controls.
- `--ki-carousel-control-bg`: Surface of the carousel navigation and rotation controls.
- `--ki-carousel-control-bg-image`: Optional image layered over the carousel control background color.
- `--ki-carousel-control-border`: Visible control boundary against the surrounding surface.
- `--ki-carousel-control-fg`: Text and glyph ink against the carousel control surface.
- `--ki-carousel-control-gap`: Spacing between carousel controls.
- `--ki-carousel-control-icon-size`: Glyph size in the carousel navigation controls.
- `--ki-carousel-control-radius`: Corner radius of the carousel controls.
- `--ki-carousel-control-shadow`: Resting elevation of the carousel controls.
- `--ki-carousel-control-size`: Resting carousel control size before applying the density target floor.
- `--ki-carousel-full-screen-block-size`: Block size of the vertical carousel viewport.
- `--ki-carousel-gap`: Gap between carousel slides and between the viewport and the controls.
- `--ki-carousel-preview-min-inline-size`: Minimum inline size of a decorative carousel preview when space permits.
- `--ki-carousel-radius`: Corner radius shared by the carousel viewport and slide surfaces.
- `--ki-control-border-width`: Stroke width of the boundary of a compact control.
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-carousel-item

A slide in an ordered ki-carousel sequence.

When to use: supply a single slide to a ki-carousel. Put the full slide in the
default slot and optional decorative preview media in the preview slot.
When NOT to use: present a standalone card or a layout container outside a carousel.

Examples:

# Carousel item example

```html
<ki-carousel label="Getting started" layout="hero">
  <ki-carousel-item><a href="/guide">Read the guide</a></ki-carousel-item>
  <ki-carousel-item>
    <img slot="preview" src="/cover.jpg" alt="">
    <a href="/themes">Explore themes</a>
  </ki-carousel-item>
</ki-carousel>
```

Attributes: none

Slots:
- (default): The full slide content, including any links and controls.
- `preview`: Decorative, noninteractive media shown when the item is a reduced preview.

Parts:
- `content`: Surface that holds the full slide.
- `preview`: Decorative surface used in small or partly shown previews.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-carousel-item-backdrop-filter`: Complete optional backdrop filter for the slide surface.
- `--ki-carousel-item-bg`: Surface for carousel slide content and its decorative preview.
- `--ki-carousel-item-bg-image`: Optional image layered over the slide background color.
- `--ki-carousel-item-fg`: Text on the carousel slide surface.
- `--ki-carousel-item-min-block-size`: Minimum block size of a full slide.
- `--ki-carousel-item-padding`: Inset of full slide content.
- `--ki-carousel-radius`: Corner radius shared by the carousel viewport and slide surfaces.
- `--ki-control-border-width`: Stroke width of the boundary of a compact control.
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-checkbox

A form-associated checkbox for selecting independent options. Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`, `setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and `willValidate` synchronously, on the custom-elements build (not on hosts created by the lazy loader).

When to use: selecting one or more independent options that a form submits
later, including a "select all" parent that presents partial selection with
`indeterminate`. Always provide a visible label in the default slot.
When NOT to use: a single mutually exclusive choice, an immediate on/off
effect, triggering an action, unlabeled/icon-only usage, or
`checked="false"` to mean unchecked. Boolean attributes use presence
semantics; omit `checked` to express unchecked.

Examples:

The default slot is the visible label — the accessible name and a native activation surface; when checked, `name` and `value` pair into the submitted form data:

```html
<form>
  <ki-checkbox name="channels" value="email" checked>Email</ki-checkbox>
  <ki-checkbox name="channels" value="sms">SMS</ki-checkbox>
  <ki-button variant="primary">Save preferences</ki-button>
</form>
```

Boolean attributes use presence semantics — omit `checked` to express unchecked, never write `checked="false"`; without `value` a checked box submits `on`, and unchecked boxes contribute no form entry:

```html
<ki-checkbox name="newsletter" checked>Send me the weekly digest</ki-checkbox>
```

`required` blocks submission while unchecked (the invalid appearance appears only after a blocked attempt or an invalidating toggle, never on initial render), and `disabled` removes the checkbox from keyboard reach and form data:

```html
<form>
  <ki-checkbox name="terms" required>I accept the terms of service</ki-checkbox>
  <ki-checkbox name="fax" disabled>Notify me by fax</ki-checkbox>
  <ki-button variant="primary">Create account</ki-button>
</form>
```

`indeterminate` presents the mixed state of a "select all" parent — presentation-only, exposed to assistive technology as mixed, cleared by any user toggle, and never submitted (model data stays binary through `checked`):

```html
<ki-checkbox indeterminate>Select all rows</ki-checkbox>
```

## An error from the application

Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on the submitted
answer. The checkbox is invalid, blocks its form and is announced as invalid
at once. Toggling it withdraws the error. Remove the attribute when a new
attempt starts: setting the same text again while it is still set shows
nothing. Inside a `ki-checkbox-group`, set it on the group.

```html
<ki-checkbox name="newsletter" checked custom-error="Confirm your email address before subscribing.">Send me the newsletter</ki-checkbox>
```

Attributes:
- `checked` (boolean, default false): Live binary selection state. User activation by pointer, slotted label or Space toggles it with native checkbox parity and emits composed `input` before composed `change`. Boolean presence semantics apply: `checked="false"` still renders checked; omit the attribute to express unchecked. Programmatic assignment is silent. When NOT to use: do not treat this reflected attribute as a native `defaultChecked`; reset uses the baseline captured at form association.
- `custom-error` (string | undefined): An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the submitted answer ("This plan needs a signed contract"). While it holds text the checkbox is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help text at once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting when the person toggles the checkbox, or when the form is reset, so it never blocks the corrected answer. It outranks `error-text` and an error set with `setCustomValidity`. When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts. When NOT to use: do not use it for a `required` checkbox left unchecked; `error-text` words that. Inside a `ki-checkbox-group`, set it on the group. Setting the same text again while the prop still holds it shows nothing: remove it first, then set it again.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Prevents activation, removes the checkbox from keyboard reach, exposes the unavailable state, and excludes it from form data. When NOT to use: do not use disabled for validation errors or pending state.
- `error-text` (string | undefined): Message shown in place of the help text once a `required` checkbox is left unchecked, and its `validationMessage`. Say what checking it means ("Accept the terms to continue"). Without it the browser's own message shows, in the browser's language. An error set with `custom-error` or `setCustomValidity` outranks it. When NOT to use: do not use it for server-side or cross-field errors; set `custom-error` or call `setCustomValidity` for those.
- `help-text` (string | undefined): One line of help under the checkbox, read with it as its description: what checking it means or commits to. When NOT to use: do not repeat the label, and do not use it for error messages; use `error-text`.
- `indeterminate` (boolean, default false): Presentation-only mixed state. It renders the dash mark, is forwarded to the internal native input for mixed assistive-technology exposure, and never changes the submitted value. Any user toggle clears it and removes the reflected attribute. When NOT to use: do not submit or persist `indeterminate` as a third value; model data remains binary through `checked`.
- `label-hint` (string | undefined): Short text shown after the slotted label and read with it as part of the checkbox name, so people know before submitting whether they must check it: "(required)" on a consent the form cannot do without, "(optional)" on one it can, in the page's own language. It changes no validation; set `required` for that, and keep the two consistent. When NOT to use: do not put what checking it commits to in it (use `help-text`), errors (use `error-text`), or a repeat of the label.
- `name` (string | undefined): Form-data key contributed when the checkbox is checked. When NOT to use: omit when the checkbox should not submit a value.
- `required` (boolean, default false): Requires the checkbox to be checked before form submission can proceed. The invalid appearance appears after a blocked submission attempt or an invalidating user toggle, never on initial render. When NOT to use: do not use required to express group-level rules; compose those at the form/application layer.
- `size` ("lg" | "md" | "sm", default 'md'): Token-backed size: the box is 18, 20 or 24px in onmars. `sm` also takes the smaller label (13/20, 8px away); `md` and `lg` keep the 15px label. The pointer target never drops under 24px. An unrecognized value matches no style rule and keeps the medium metrics. When to use: match the size of the text and controls around it. When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead, which composes with every size.
- `value` (string | undefined): Form-data value paired with `name` when checked. If omitted, the submitted value is `on`, matching native checkbox behavior. When NOT to use: do not encode the unchecked state here; unchecked checkboxes contribute no form entry.

Slots:
- (default): Visible label content. This is the accessible name source and a native activation surface.

Parts:
- `control`: Visual checkbox box, border, focus ring and currentColor marks.
- `error`: Error line shown in place of the help text while the checkbox is invalid after the person toggled it or submitted; a polite live region, starting with a decorative error symbol.
- `help`: Help line under the checkbox, read as its description.
- `label`: Label wrapper around the default slot.
- `label-hint`: The `label-hint` text after the slotted label, inside the label wrapper and part of the accessible name; rendered only while a hint is set.

Events:
- `change` (Event): Fired once after a user toggle (pointer, slotted label or Space) commits, composed across the shadow boundary; `checked` is already current when listeners run. `click()` from a script, or a page `<label>` for the checkbox, toggles it like a native checkbox: one `input`, then one `change`. When to use: react to the committed selection. When NOT to use: do not expect it for programmatic `checked` writes, which are silent.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-checkbox-border-width`: dimension used by the checkbox component for border width.
- `--ki-checkbox-checked-active-bg`: color used by the checkbox component for checked active background.
- `--ki-checkbox-checked-active-border`: color used by the checkbox component for checked active border.
- `--ki-checkbox-checked-active-fg`: color used by the checkbox component for checked active foreground.
- `--ki-checkbox-checked-disabled-bg`: color used by the checkbox component for checked disabled background (MarsUI Surface/disabled_med_em Gray/300 light / White-18 dark).
- `--ki-checkbox-checked-disabled-border`: color used by the checkbox component for checked disabled border.
- `--ki-checkbox-checked-disabled-fg`: color used by the checkbox component for checked disabled mark (MarsUI Text/base_em Gray/400 light / White-32 dark; retires the deprecated ki.text.muted alias).
- `--ki-checkbox-checked-hover-bg`: color used by the checkbox component for checked hover background.
- `--ki-checkbox-checked-hover-border`: color used by the checkbox component for checked hover border.
- `--ki-checkbox-checked-hover-fg`: color used by the checkbox component for checked hover foreground.
- `--ki-checkbox-checked-rest-bg`: color used by the checkbox component for checked rest background.
- `--ki-checkbox-checked-rest-border`: color used by the checkbox component for checked rest border.
- `--ki-checkbox-checked-rest-fg`: color used by the checkbox component for checked rest foreground.
- `--ki-checkbox-control-size`: dimension used by the checkbox component for control size.
- `--ki-checkbox-focus-ring-color`: color used by the checkbox component for focus ring color.
- `--ki-checkbox-focus-ring-offset`: dimension used by the checkbox component for focus ring offset.
- `--ki-checkbox-focus-ring-shadow`: shadow used by the checkbox component for the focus ring glow (MarsUI Focus/primary: 3px spread ring at 20% — see ki.focus.primary. specs/002-ki-button/design-extraction.md §2.5 recorded 40%, having read the alpha off the Dark canvas mode, same double mechanism as ki-button: glow plus the opaque indicator).
- `--ki-checkbox-focus-ring-width`: dimension used by the checkbox component for focus ring width.
- `--ki-checkbox-gap`: dimension used by the checkbox component for gap (MarsUI md label pairing: Space/xl 12px for the 20px box).
- `--ki-checkbox-indeterminate-active-bg`: color used by the checkbox component for indeterminate active background (MarsUI Surface/primary_low_em_alpha: brand-500 at 20% light / 56% dark; the master defines no indeterminate hover, so every state keeps the tint).
- `--ki-checkbox-indeterminate-active-border`: color used by the checkbox component for indeterminate active border (Figma draws no border on the 20% tint, but the tint alone measures ~1.3:1 against light pages; the opaque brand ring keeps the WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 control boundary — gate-driven declared deviation, same law that pinned ki.outline.control).
- `--ki-checkbox-indeterminate-active-fg`: color used by the checkbox component for indeterminate active dash (Figma binds Text/primary_med_em brand-500, which measures 2.7:1 against the 56% tint in dark; one em step up keeps the 3:1 non-text law in both schemes — gate-driven compliant alternative).
- `--ki-checkbox-indeterminate-disabled-bg`: color used by the checkbox component for indeterminate disabled background (MarsUI Surface/disabled_med_em Gray/300 light / White-18 dark).
- `--ki-checkbox-indeterminate-disabled-border`: color used by the checkbox component for indeterminate disabled border.
- `--ki-checkbox-indeterminate-disabled-fg`: color used by the checkbox component for indeterminate disabled mark (MarsUI Text/base_em Gray/400 light / White-32 dark; retires the deprecated ki.text.muted alias).
- `--ki-checkbox-indeterminate-hover-bg`: color used by the checkbox component for indeterminate hover background (MarsUI Surface/primary_low_em_alpha: brand-500 at 20% light / 56% dark; the master defines no indeterminate hover, so every state keeps the tint).
- `--ki-checkbox-indeterminate-hover-border`: color used by the checkbox component for indeterminate hover border (Figma draws no border on the 20% tint, but the tint alone measures ~1.3:1 against light pages; the opaque brand ring keeps the WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 control boundary — gate-driven declared deviation, same law that pinned ki.outline.control).
- `--ki-checkbox-indeterminate-hover-fg`: color used by the checkbox component for indeterminate hover dash (Figma binds Text/primary_med_em brand-500, which measures 2.7:1 against the 56% tint in dark; one em step up keeps the 3:1 non-text law in both schemes — gate-driven compliant alternative).
- `--ki-checkbox-indeterminate-rest-bg`: color used by the checkbox component for indeterminate rest background (MarsUI Surface/primary_low_em_alpha: brand-500 at 20% light / 56% dark; the master defines no indeterminate hover, so every state keeps the tint).
- `--ki-checkbox-indeterminate-rest-border`: color used by the checkbox component for indeterminate rest border (Figma draws no border on the 20% tint, but the tint alone measures ~1.3:1 against light pages; the opaque brand ring keeps the WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 control boundary — gate-driven declared deviation, same law that pinned ki.outline.control).
- `--ki-checkbox-indeterminate-rest-fg`: color used by the checkbox component for indeterminate rest dash (Figma binds Text/primary_med_em brand-500, which measures 2.7:1 against the 56% tint in dark; one em step up keeps the 3:1 non-text law in both schemes — gate-driven compliant alternative).
- `--ki-checkbox-invalid-bg`: color used by the checkbox component for invalid background.
- `--ki-checkbox-invalid-border`: color used by the checkbox component for invalid border.
- `--ki-checkbox-invalid-fg`: color used by the checkbox component for invalid foreground.
- `--ki-checkbox-label-font-size`: dimension used by the checkbox component for label font size (MarsUI md pairing: body_2 15px for the 20px box).
- `--ki-checkbox-label-font-weight`: font weight used by the checkbox component for label font weight.
- `--ki-checkbox-label-hint-fg`: color used by the checkbox component for the label hint after the label text (spec 047: the supporting-text role, a declared a11y deviation from the MarsUI Input_label support text Text/low_em, which reads 2.8-3.13:1 on the onmars light surfaces; under more contrast it strengthens with every other supporting text).
- `--ki-checkbox-label-hint-gap`: dimension used by the checkbox component for the gap between the label text and the label hint (MarsUI Input_label: Space/xs 4px).
- `--ki-checkbox-label-line-height`: dimension used by the checkbox component for label line height (MarsUI body_2 24px).
- `--ki-checkbox-lg-control-size`: dimension used by the checkbox component for the lg box (Checkbox 10030:982 lg: 24px in a 28px cell).
- `--ki-checkbox-lg-min-target`: dimension used by the checkbox component for the lg min target (Checkbox 10030:982 lg cell: 28px).
- `--ki-checkbox-min-target`: dimension used by the checkbox component for min target.
- `--ki-checkbox-radius`: dimension used by the checkbox component for radius (MarsUI Radius/radius_sm 6px bound on the box; Figma corner smoothing is an accepted rasterization gap).
- `--ki-checkbox-sm-control-size`: dimension used by the checkbox component for the sm box (Checkbox 10030:982 sm: 18px in a 20px cell).
- `--ki-checkbox-sm-gap`: dimension used by the checkbox component for the sm gap between control and label (Checkbox-label 10095:3846 sm binds Space/md, 8px; spec 050 D4).
- `--ki-checkbox-sm-label-font-size`: dimension used by the checkbox component for the sm label font size (Checkbox-label 10095:3846 sm: UI/para 13/20; spec 050 D4).
- `--ki-checkbox-sm-label-line-height`: dimension used by the checkbox component for the sm label line height (Checkbox-label 10095:3846 sm: UI/para 13/20).
- `--ki-checkbox-sm-min-target`: dimension used by the checkbox component for the sm min target: 24px, the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum, above the master's 20px cell.
- `--ki-checkbox-unchecked-active-bg`: color used by the checkbox component for unchecked active background.
- `--ki-checkbox-unchecked-active-border`: color used by the checkbox component for unchecked active border.
- `--ki-checkbox-unchecked-active-fg`: color used by the checkbox component for unchecked active foreground.
- `--ki-checkbox-unchecked-disabled-bg`: color used by the checkbox component for unchecked disabled background (MarsUI Surface/disabled_med_em Gray/300 light / White-18 dark).
- `--ki-checkbox-unchecked-disabled-border`: color used by the checkbox component for unchecked disabled border.
- `--ki-checkbox-unchecked-disabled-fg`: color used by the checkbox component for unchecked disabled mark (MarsUI Text/base_em Gray/400 light / White-32 dark; retires the deprecated ki.text.muted alias).
- `--ki-checkbox-unchecked-hover-bg`: color used by the checkbox component for unchecked hover background.
- `--ki-checkbox-unchecked-hover-border`: color used by the checkbox component for unchecked hover border.
- `--ki-checkbox-unchecked-hover-fg`: color used by the checkbox component for unchecked hover foreground.
- `--ki-checkbox-unchecked-rest-bg`: color used by the checkbox component for unchecked rest background.
- `--ki-checkbox-unchecked-rest-border`: color used by the checkbox component for unchecked rest border.
- `--ki-checkbox-unchecked-rest-fg`: color used by the checkbox component for unchecked rest foreground.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-effect-component-primary-default-shadow`: MarsUI Component_effect/primary_default: drop 0/1/1/-0.5 plus inner White/12 0/3/3. Pair with --ki-effect-component-backdrop-filter — CSS cannot mix backdrop blur into box-shadow.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-easing-emphasized-out`: Expressive exit curve for selected controls. Onmars eases out without overshoot.
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-motion-easing-standard`: Standard interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-surface-special-dark-s0-light-s2`: semantic color for surface special dark s0 light s2.
- `--ki-surface-special-light-s0-dark-s4`: semantic color for surface special light s0 dark s4.
- `--ki-text-danger-high-em`: semantic color for text danger high em.
- `--ki-text-high-em`: semantic color for text high em.
- `--ki-text-supporting`: Supporting text of an enabled control: field labels, placeholders, list secondary lines, quiet button labels and unselected tabs. A role, distinct from the med-em emphasis step it resolves to, so a mode can strengthen enabled supporting text without touching the disabled ink that also draws from med-em (directly, or through text.muted).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-normal`: semantic font weight for typography weight body normal.

### ki-checkbox-group

A form-associated group of independently selectable checkboxes.

When to use: people may select several visible options that share a question,
form field, and optional selection limits.
When NOT to use: mutually exclusive choices (use `ki-radio-group`) or an
immediate on/off setting (use `ki-switch`). Provide a group label.

Examples:

# Checkbox group examples

## Submit several selections

```html
<form id="settings">
  <ki-checkbox-group
    id="regions"
    label="Regions"
    name="regions"
    min="1"
    help-text="Choose the regions you serve."
    error-text="Choose at least one region."
  >
    <ki-checkbox value="eu" checked>Europe</ki-checkbox>
    <ki-checkbox value="am">Americas</ki-checkbox>
    <ki-checkbox value="apac">Asia-Pacific</ki-checkbox>
  </ki-checkbox-group>
  <button type="submit">Save regions</button>
</form>
```

Reading `new FormData(form).getAll('regions')` returns each checked value
in option order. Keep individual option labels visible and give each option
a distinct value when you need to select it independently from JavaScript.

## Read and update selection

```js
import { defineCustomElement as defineCheckbox } from '@kimen/elements/ki-checkbox';
import { defineCustomElement as defineCheckboxGroup } from '@kimen/elements/ki-checkbox-group';

defineCheckbox();
defineCheckboxGroup();

const group = document.querySelector('#regions');
group.value = ['eu', 'apac'];

group.addEventListener('ki-change', (event) => {
  const selectedRegions = event.detail.value;
  console.log(selectedRegions);
});
```

## Horizontal choices

```html
<ki-checkbox-group label="Notifications" orientation="horizontal">
  <ki-checkbox value="mentions">Mentions</ki-checkbox>
  <ki-checkbox value="reviews">Review requests</ki-checkbox>
</ki-checkbox-group>
```

## Name the group from the page

When the question is already written on the page, point the host's
`aria-labelledby` at it and omit `label`. The group takes its accessible name
from the heading, so the question is shown and read once. `label-hidden`
instead keeps a `label` as the name while hiding it from view and from
reading order.

```html
<h2 id="shipping-question">Where do you ship?</h2>
<ki-checkbox-group aria-labelledby="shipping-question" name="regions">
  <ki-checkbox value="eu">Europe</ki-checkbox>
  <ki-checkbox value="am">Americas</ki-checkbox>
</ki-checkbox-group>
```

## An error from the application

Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on the submitted
selection. The group is invalid, blocks its form and is announced as invalid
at once. Toggling any option withdraws the error. Remove the attribute when
a new attempt starts: setting the same text again while it is still set
shows nothing.

```html
<ki-checkbox-group label="Regions" name="regions" custom-error="We do not deliver to the Americas yet.">
  <ki-checkbox value="eu" checked>Europe</ki-checkbox>
  <ki-checkbox value="am" checked>Americas</ki-checkbox>
</ki-checkbox-group>
```

Attributes:
- `custom-error` (string | undefined): An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the submitted selection ("Pick regions we deliver to"). While it holds text the group is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help text at once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting when the person toggles an option, or when the form is reset, so it never blocks the corrected answer. It outranks `error-text` and an error set with `setCustomValidity`. When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts. When NOT to use: do not use it for the `min` and `max` limits the group enforces itself; `error-text` words those. Setting the same text again while the prop still holds it shows nothing: remove it first, then set it again.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Makes the group unavailable and excludes it from form submission.
- `error-text` (string | undefined): Localized message displayed for a failing selection limit.
- `help-text` (string | undefined): One line of guidance displayed under the choices.
- `label` (string, required): Visible legend and accessible name for these choices. When NOT to use: do not omit it unless the host's `aria-labelledby` names the group from the page. Naming from the page: set `aria-labelledby` on the host to the ids of elements in the same document or shadow root, such as the heading that already asks the question. The group then takes its name from them, followed by its own `label` when set. The ids are read when the group renders and whenever the attribute changes. When to use: the question is written on the page above the options; omit `label` so the question is not shown, or read, twice. When NOT to use: do not reference elements inside another component's shadow root, which an id reference cannot reach.
- `label-hidden` (boolean, default false): Hides the legend from view and from reading order while it stays the group's accessible name, so a screen reader announces it once, as the group's name. When to use: the layout already makes the question obvious to sighted people but the group still needs a name of its own. When NOT to use: do not hide a legend that repeats a question already on the page; point `aria-labelledby` at that question instead.
- `max` (number | undefined): Maximum number of checked options, as a nonnegative integer.
- `min` (number | undefined): Minimum number of checked options, as a nonnegative integer.
- `name` (string | undefined): Form-data key repeated for each selected option.
- `orientation` ("horizontal" | "vertical", default 'vertical'): Lays choices out vertically or in a wrapping horizontal row.

Slots:
- (default): Direct `ki-checkbox` options, each with its own visible label and value. Put form naming and constraints on the group.

Parts:
- `error`: Polite error message shown in place of the help.
- `help`: Guidance below the options and the group's accessible description.
- `label`: Legend that names the group.

Events:
- `ki-change` (CustomEvent<KiCheckboxGroupChangeDetail>): Fires once for a committed user toggle with a copy of the current selection.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-checkbox-group-gap`: Space between checkbox options and the group label and messages.
- `--ki-radio-group-label-font-size`: dimension used by the radio group component for label font size.
- `--ki-radio-group-label-font-weight`: font weight used by the radio group component for label font weight.
- `--ki-radio-group-label-line-height`: dimension used by the radio group component for label line height (closest measured analogue: Radio_label sm 13/20; no group-title master exists — low-confidence refinement).
- `--ki-text-danger-high-em`: semantic color for text danger high em.
- `--ki-text-high-em`: semantic color for text high em.
- `--ki-text-med-em`: semantic color for text med em.
- `--ki-text-supporting`: Supporting text of an enabled control: field labels, placeholders, list secondary lines, quiet button labels and unselected tabs. A role, distinct from the med-em emphasis step it resolves to, so a mode can strengthen enabled supporting text without touching the disabled ink that also draws from med-em (directly, or through text.muted).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-normal`: semantic font weight for typography weight body normal.

### ki-chip

A compact filter toggle, removable picked value, or contextual action.

When to use: apply independent filters, represent values selected in an entry
field, or offer a small contextual action alongside content.
When NOT to use: static status (ki-badge), primary actions (ki-button), suggested
prompts, or mutually exclusive choices (ki-radio-group).

Examples:

# Chip examples

Use a filter group for independent toggles. Read `ki-change.detail.selected` to
update the results. The chip's `value` identifies the filter.

```html
<ki-chip-group label="Team" type="filter">
  <ki-chip value="design" selected>Design</ki-chip>
  <ki-chip value="eng">Engineering</ki-chip>
</ki-chip-group>
```

Use an input group for picked values. Link the entry field by ID so focus
returns to it after the last chip. Listen to `ki-remove` to update your
collection. If a framework owns these nodes, cancel the event and let it
apply the DOM change, then focus the next chip or the linked field.

```html
<ki-chip-group label="Recipients" type="input" focus-target="recipient">
  <ki-chip value="ana" removable>
    <ki-avatar slot="start" size="xxs" initials="AG" label="Ana García"></ki-avatar>
    Ana García
  </ki-chip>
  <ki-chip value="luis" removable>Luis</ki-chip>
</ki-chip-group>
<input id="recipient" aria-label="Add recipient">
```

Use assist for a contextual action. Handle `ki-activate` in application code.

```html
<ki-chip type="assist" value="calendar">
  <svg slot="start" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor">
    <rect x="3" y="5" width="18" height="16" rx="2"/>
    <path d="M3 10h18M8 2v6m8-6v6"/>
  </svg>
  Add to calendar
</ki-chip>
```

Attributes:
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Prevents activation, removal and moving the chip.
- `removable` (boolean, default false): Gives an input chip a trailing remove button and keyboard deletion.
- `remove-label` (string, default 'Remove'): Localized action prefix in the remove button's accessible name, followed by the chip label.
- `selected` (boolean, default false): The pressed state of a filter chip. The user can toggle it in place.
- `size` ("md" | "sm", default 'md'): Visual size of the pill, 24 CSS px for sm and 32 CSS px for md at standard text spacing.
- `type` ("assist" | "filter" | "input" | undefined): Chip kind. Inherits the immediate chip group's type when omitted. Standalone chips default to filter.
- `value` (string, default ''): Value sent with removal, contextual activation and reorder events.

Slots:
- (default): The visible text label. Use text or non-interactive markup.
- `start`: One decorative glyph or extra-extra-small avatar. A filter check replaces it when selected. Do not slot controls.

Parts:
- `chip`: The painted pill.
- `drag-handle`: The grip enabled by a reorderable parent group.
- `label`: The text wrapper around the default slot.
- `remove`: The native remove button on a removable input chip.
- `selection-icon`: The selected filter check.
- `start`: The decorative leading content.

Events:
- `ki-activate` (CustomEvent<{
    value: string;
  }>): Emitted by an assist chip when its native button is activated.
- `ki-change` (CustomEvent<{
    selected: boolean;
  }>): Emitted after a filter chip changes its pressed state.
- `ki-remove` (CustomEvent<{ value: string }>): Remove request for an input chip. Cancel it to keep application ownership of the chip.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-chip-assist-icon-fg`: Decorative glyph in an assist chip.
- `--ki-chip-backdrop-filter`: Default compact pill surface leaves the backdrop unfiltered.
- `--ki-chip-bg`: Resting filter and assist surface.
- `--ki-chip-bg-image`: Default compact pill surface uses a solid color.
- `--ki-chip-border`: Outline of an unselected filter or assist chip.
- `--ki-chip-border-width`: Default thickness of a compact pill border.
- `--ki-chip-disabled-border`: Outline of a disabled chip.
- `--ki-chip-disabled-ink`: Label on a disabled chip.
- `--ki-chip-fg`: Resting filter and assist label.
- `--ki-chip-font-family`: Font family for the visible chip label.
- `--ki-chip-font-size`: Default chip label size.
- `--ki-chip-font-size-sm`: Small chip label size.
- `--ki-chip-font-weight`: Weight for a chip label.
- `--ki-chip-gap`: Gap between content in a compact pill.
- `--ki-chip-height`: Default height of a compact pill.
- `--ki-chip-height-sm`: Small height of a compact pill.
- `--ki-chip-hover-bg`: Surface under the hovering pointer.
- `--ki-chip-hover-fg`: Label over the hover surface.
- `--ki-chip-icon-size`: Icon size inside a compact pill.
- `--ki-chip-input-bg`: Surface of a picked value.
- `--ki-chip-input-fg`: Label of a picked value.
- `--ki-chip-inset`: Default inline padding of a compact pill.
- `--ki-chip-inset-action`: Trailing inset beside a pill action.
- `--ki-chip-inset-sm`: Small inline padding of a compact pill.
- `--ki-chip-line-height`: Default line height of the chip label.
- `--ki-chip-line-height-sm`: Small line height of the chip label.
- `--ki-chip-pressed-bg`: Surface while the activation is held.
- `--ki-chip-pressed-fg`: Label while the activation is held.
- `--ki-chip-radius`: Fully rounded compact pill shape.
- `--ki-chip-remove-bg`: Remove button surface inside an input chip.
- `--ki-chip-remove-fg`: Resting remove glyph.
- `--ki-chip-remove-hover-bg`: Remove button hover surface.
- `--ki-chip-remove-hover-fg`: Remove glyph over the hover surface.
- `--ki-chip-selected-bg`: Selected filter surface.
- `--ki-chip-selected-border`: Accessible boundary of a selected filter.
- `--ki-chip-selected-fg`: Selected filter label and check.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.

### ki-chip-group

A named collection of filter, input or assist chips, with optional ordering.

When to use: label related chips or let people change their reading order.
When NOT to use: choose exactly one option or submit a form value.

Examples:

# Chip group examples

A labelled group lets the user reorder direct chips with a drag handle,
two pointer activations on the handles, or Alt+Left/Right. The order is
announced on each move. Listen for `ki-reorder` to persist the new order.

```html
<ki-chip-group label="Recipients" type="input" reorderable focus-target="recipient">
  <ki-chip value="ana" removable>Ana García</ki-chip>
  <ki-chip value="luis" removable>Luis</ki-chip>
</ki-chip-group>
<input id="recipient" aria-label="Add recipient">
```

Attributes:
- `focus-target` (string | undefined, ID of another element of the same spec): ID of the entry field in the same document or shadow root for focus after the last chip.
- `label` (string, default ''): Accessible name for the group or list.
- `reorder-announcement` (string, default '{label} moved to position {position} of {total}.'): Localized polite message using {label}, {position} and {total}. Position is one-based.
- `reorderable` (boolean, default false): Enables dragging, pointer pick-and-place and Alt+Left/Right to move chips.
- `type` ("assist" | "filter" | "input", default 'filter'): Shared chip kind and collection semantics. Input chips are presented as a list.

Slots:
- (default): Direct ki-chip children in reading order.

Parts:
- `group`: The wrapping chip layout.

Events:
- `ki-reorder` (CustomEvent<KiChipReorderDetail>): Emitted after moving a chip. Indices are zero-based positions in the visible chip collection.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-chip-group-font-family`: Font family inherited by chip group content.
- `--ki-chip-group-gap`: Gap between adjacent chips and rows.
- `--ki-chip-height-sm`: Small height of a compact pill.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).

### ki-citation

A numbered inline link from an answer to a source card.

When to use: Next to a claim supported by a `ki-source` in the same document
or shadow root. Repeat the same reference for subsequent mentions.
When NOT to use: To cite a source outside this tree or replace a standalone
link. Use `ki-link` for direct navigation.

Examples:

# Using ki-citation

Place a citation after its claim and set `ref` to the matching source identifier.

```html
<p>The methods account for the difference<ki-citation ref="methods"></ki-citation>.</p>
<ki-sources>
  <ki-source id="methods" title="Study design" href="/methods"></ki-source>
</ki-sources>
```

Use `citationRef` in JSX. Tab to the link for a preview. Escape dismisses the
preview, and Enter opens the list and moves focus to the source link.

Attributes:
- `ref` (string, required): ID or source-id of the source. Use the `ref` attribute in HTML and `citationRef` in JSX so framework refs remain available.
- `label-template` (string, default 'Source {number}: {title}'): Localized link name with `{number}` and `{title}` placeholders.

Slots: none

Parts:
- `link`: Focusable citation link.
- `marker`: Visible citation number.
- `preview`: Anchored title and hostname preview.
- `preview-domain`: Hostname in the preview.
- `preview-title`: Title in the preview.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-citation-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter for a citation marker.
- `--ki-citation-bg`: Background of a citation marker.
- `--ki-citation-bg-image`: Optional decorative image over a citation marker.
- `--ki-citation-fg`: Text on a citation marker.
- `--ki-citation-hover-bg`: Background of a hovered citation marker.
- `--ki-citation-hover-fg`: Text on a hovered citation marker.
- `--ki-citation-padding`: Inline padding of the citation number.
- `--ki-citation-preview-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter for the citation preview.
- `--ki-citation-preview-bg`: Background of the title and hostname preview.
- `--ki-citation-preview-bg-image`: Optional decorative image over the citation preview.
- `--ki-citation-preview-border`: Edge color of the citation preview.
- `--ki-citation-preview-border-width`: Edge width of the citation preview.
- `--ki-citation-preview-fg`: Text on the citation preview.
- `--ki-citation-preview-max-inline-size`: Maximum width of the citation preview.
- `--ki-citation-preview-padding`: Inset around the preview content.
- `--ki-citation-preview-radius`: Corner radius of the citation preview.
- `--ki-citation-preview-shadow`: Elevation of the citation preview.
- `--ki-citation-radius`: Corner radius of a citation marker.
- `--ki-citation-size`: Minimum painted edge of a citation marker.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-semibold`: semantic font weight for typography weight body semibold.

### ki-code-block

Presents source code with a named header, syntax colors, line controls and clipboard feedback.

When to use: display a multiline example, generated code or a tool result that
readers should be able to inspect and copy.
When NOT to use: when the reader should edit the source or when the code belongs
inline in a sentence. Use an editor or a native inline code element.

Examples:

# ki-code-block examples

Display a TypeScript snippet with line numbers and a highlighted line.

```html
<ki-code-block language="ts" filename="main.ts" line-numbers highlight="2">// Load the current sample.
const sample = load(3);</ki-code-block>
```

Use plain text for unsupported syntax. In HTML, escape literal angle
brackets so they remain part of the source.

```html
<ki-code-block language="html" filename="example.html" wrap copyable="false">&lt;p&gt;Hello&lt;/p&gt;</ki-code-block>
```

Color a Gherkin contract in English or Spanish with `language="gherkin"`.
Keywords count only where they open a line.

```html
<ki-code-block language="gherkin" filename="pagos.feature"># language: es
Característica: Pagar el carrito
  Escenario: Pagar con tarjeta
    Dado un carrito con 3 productos y un cupón
    Cuando el cliente paga
    Entonces el recibo muestra el total</ki-code-block>
```

The guarded catalog accepts source strings in the default slot.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "actions": ["sampleCopied"],
  "root": {
    "component": "ki-code-block",
    "props": { "language": "js", "filename": "index.js", "line-numbers": true },
    "slots": { "": ["const sample = load(3);"] },
    "action": "sampleCopied"
  }
}
```

Attributes:
- `copied-label` (string, default 'Copied'): Polite announcement after a successful clipboard write.
- `copy-error-label` (string, default "Couldn't copy"): Polite announcement after a failed clipboard write.
- `copy-label` (string, default 'Copy code'): Accessible name of the copy button.
- `copyable` (boolean, default true): Show the copy control. Set `copyable="false"` in HTML to hide it.
- `filename` (string | undefined): File name shown in the header beside the language.
- `highlight` (string | undefined): Comma-separated lines or inclusive ranges, for example `"3,5-7"`.
- `highlight-label` (string, default 'Highlighted lines'): Localizable prefix for the accessible description of highlighted lines.
- `label` (string | undefined, default 'Code'): Figure and scroll area label when there is no language or filename.
- `language` (string | undefined): Visible language label and syntax grammar. Supports JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON and Gherkin (English and Spanish).
- `line-numbers` (boolean, default false): Show decorative one-based line numbers.
- `wrap` (boolean, default false): Soft-wrap long lines within the available width.

Slots:
- (default): Literal source text. Escape markup in HTML or supply a text node.

Parts:
- `code`: The monospaced source and its optional gutter.
- `figure`: Framed surface around the snippet.
- `header`: Caption containing the language, filename and copy control.
- `scroll`: Focusable native code scroll area.

Events:
- `ki-copy` (CustomEvent<{ value: string }>): CopyButton reports a successful write with the original source text.
- `ki-copy-error` (CustomEvent<void>): CopyButton reports an unsuccessful clipboard write.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-code-backdrop-filter`: Whole backdrop filter for the figure.
- `--ki-code-bg`: Solid backing for the header and source.
- `--ki-code-bg-image`: Optional image layer above the solid backing.
- `--ki-code-border`: Frame and header divider.
- `--ki-code-border-width`: Width of the frame and header divider.
- `--ki-code-comment`: Supporting syntax ink for comments.
- `--ki-code-fg`: Default source ink.
- `--ki-code-focus-color`: Keyboard focus ring of the scroll area.
- `--ki-code-focus-width`: Width of the scroll area's focus ring.
- `--ki-code-font-family`: Typeface for source and line numbers.
- `--ki-code-font-size`: Compact text size for caption and source.
- `--ki-code-function`: Syntax ink for function names.
- `--ki-code-header-fg`: Supporting language and filename ink.
- `--ki-code-header-padding`: Compact header inset and gap.
- `--ki-code-highlight-bg`: Fill of a highlighted line.
- `--ki-code-highlight-marker`: Inline rule identifying a highlighted line.
- `--ki-code-highlight-marker-width`: Width of the highlighted line rule.
- `--ki-code-keyword`: Syntax ink for keywords.
- `--ki-code-line-height`: Line box height for caption and source.
- `--ki-code-line-number`: Ink for the decorative line numbers.
- `--ki-code-number`: Syntax ink for numbers.
- `--ki-code-padding`: Inset of the source and leading caption edge.
- `--ki-code-radius`: Corner radius of the figure.
- `--ki-code-string`: Syntax ink for strings.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-code-input

A form-associated verification field with one native text input and a visual box per character.

When to use: Collect a one-time code of four to eight characters for sign-in or verification.
When NOT to use: Use ki-input for passwords, long codes or free text.

Examples:

# ki-code-input examples

Use `ki-code-input` for fixed one-time codes of four to eight characters. Use
`ki-input` for passwords, longer codes and free text.

## Numeric verification with a resend action

```html
<form id="verification">
  <ki-code-input
    label="Verification code"
    name="otp"
    required
    help-text="We sent a code to ana@example.com. It is valid for ten minutes."
    error-text="Enter all six digits."
  ></ki-code-input>
  <ki-button type="submit">Verify</ki-button>
  <ki-button id="resend-code" type="button" variant="ghost">Resend code</ki-button>
</form>
```

Read `new FormData(form).get('otp')` in the submit handler and send the string
to the verification service. The application knows the expiration time and
owns the resend request. On successful resend, clear the old value and any
custom validity error, update the help text, and focus the field. Offer a
visible and announced status if a request is still pending or fails.

On the custom-elements build, use `field.setCustomValidity(message)` and
`field.reportValidity()` to display a server rejection. Clear the message
with `field.setCustomValidity('')` once the person edits or resends the code.

## Four-character recovery code

```html
<ki-code-input
  label="Recovery code"
  name="recovery"
  type="alphanumeric"
  length="4"
  size="sm"
  help-text="Use the four characters from your verification email."
></ki-code-input>
```

Both `ki-input` and `ki-complete` carry `{ value }`. Listen for
`ki-complete` if filling the last box enables the next step. Leave submission
to the form unless completing the code can safely advance the flow.

## An error from the application

Set `custom-error` to show the server's verdict on the submitted code. The
field is invalid, blocks its form and is announced as invalid at once. The
person's next edit of the code withdraws the error. Remove the attribute when
a new attempt starts: setting the same text again while it is still set
shows nothing.

```html
<ki-code-input label="Verification code" name="code" value="042911" custom-error="This code has expired. Request a new one."></ki-code-input>
```

Attributes:
- `custom-error` (string | undefined): An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the submitted code ("This code has expired"). While it holds text the field is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help text at once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting at the person's next edit of the code, or when the form is reset, so it never blocks the corrected answer. It outranks `error-text` and an error set with `setCustomValidity`. When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts. When NOT to use: do not use it for an incomplete code, which the field reports itself; `error-text` words that. Setting the same text again while the prop still holds it shows nothing: remove it first, then set it again.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Disable editing, sequential focus and form participation.
- `error-text` (string | undefined): Message for a failing code constraint. Omit to use the browser's message. A `custom-error` outranks it.
- `help-text` (string | undefined): Instructions saying where the code was sent and how long it is valid.
- `label` (string, required): Visible accessible name. Supply a label in the language of the form.
- `length` (number, default 6, minimum 4, maximum 8): Number of cells and maximum code length. Unsupported lengths fall back to six.
- `name` (string | undefined): Key for the single value submitted to the enclosing form.
- `required` (boolean, default false): Require a complete code before submitting. An optional field may be empty.
- `size` ("md" | "sm", default 'md'): Medium or small cells. The form region's density adjusts both sizes.
- `type` ("alphanumeric" | "numeric", default 'numeric'): Allowed characters and keyboard hint. Alphanumeric mode preserves ASCII letter case.
- `value` (string, default ''): The current code, including leading zeros. Use the attribute to declare the reset value. Programmatic assignments are normalized and silent.

Slots: none

Parts:
- `cell`: Decorative box for one code character.
- `error`: Polite validation message that replaces the instructions.
- `field`: Enclosure of the native input and its visual boxes.
- `help`: Delivery and validity instructions read with the field.
- `input`: Single native text input, responsible for editing and autofill.
- `label`: Visible label supplying the native input's accessible name.

Events:
- `ki-complete` (CustomEvent<KiCodeInputDetail>): Emitted after the input event when the edited code fills all the cells.
- `ki-input` (CustomEvent<KiCodeInputDetail>): Emitted when a user edit changes the code.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-code-input-active-border`: Focus outline around the active or selected cells.
- `--ki-code-input-backdrop-filter`: Optional compositing filter behind a code cell.
- `--ki-code-input-bg`: Resting code cell fill.
- `--ki-code-input-bg-image`: Optional image painted over the code cell fill.
- `--ki-code-input-blink-duration`: Duration of one code caret blink.
- `--ki-code-input-border`: Resting code cell boundary.
