- `--ki-code-input-cell-size`: Default code cell edge before applying control density.
- `--ki-code-input-cell-size-sm`: Small code cell edge before applying control density.
- `--ki-code-input-disabled-fg`: Code character ink while the field is disabled.
- `--ki-code-input-error-border`: Code cell boundary after failed validation.
- `--ki-code-input-fg`: Resting code character ink.
- `--ki-code-input-font-size`: Code character size.
- `--ki-code-input-gap`: Inline space between code cells.
- `--ki-code-input-radius`: Code cell corner radius.
- `--ki-code-input-selection-bg`: Background of a selected code character.
- `--ki-code-input-selection-fg`: Ink of a selected code character.
- `--ki-code-input-touch-font-size`: Minimum native input text size on a coarse pointer.
- `--ki-control-border-width`: Stroke width of the boundary of a compact control.
- `--ki-density-control-offset`: Added to the block size of every scaled control and row (button, icon button, field, select, textarea, option, list item, tab). Components floor the result at ki.size.target-min.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-xs`: The xs spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-text-danger-high-em`: semantic color for text danger high em.
- `--ki-text-high-em`: semantic color for text high em.
- `--ki-text-supporting`: Supporting text of an enabled control: field labels, placeholders, list secondary lines, quiet button labels and unselected tabs. A role, distinct from the med-em emphasis step it resolves to, so a mode can strengthen enabled supporting text without touching the disabled ink that also draws from med-em (directly, or through text.muted).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-family-mono`: semantic font family for typography family mono.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography line height body 1.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-medium`: semantic font weight for typography weight body medium.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-normal`: semantic font weight for typography weight body normal.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-semibold`: semantic font weight for typography weight body semibold.

### ki-combobox

An editable, form-associated combobox with local or remote filtering, single or multiple selection, and optional free entry.

When to use: choose from a long list of options, let people search an option
source, or allow multiple selections that remain visible as tags.
When NOT to use: use a select-only control for a short closed set or a plain
text field for unrestricted input with no choices.

Examples:

## Search people

When importing custom elements individually, register both
`@kimen/elements/ki-combobox` and `@kimen/elements/ki-option`.

```html
<ki-combobox label="Assignee" name="assignee" placeholder="Search people" required>
  <ki-option value="ana" description="ana@example.com">Ana Ruiz</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="juan" description="juan@example.com">Juan Antón</ki-option>
</ki-combobox>
```

## Pick or create multiple labels

```html
<ki-combobox label="Labels" name="labels" multiple allow-custom value='["bug","search"]'>
  <ki-option>bug</ki-option>
  <ki-option>search</ki-option>
  <ki-option>documentation</ki-option>
</ki-combobox>
```

Assign an array to the JavaScript `value` property to set multiple selections.
Use a JSON array string in HTML or neutral catalog specs. Each selection
submits under the same form name. Read them all with `FormData.getAll`.

## Request server results

Set `filter="none"` to display the options supplied by your application.
Listen for `ki-input` and use `event.detail.value` as the query. Set `loading`
while fetching, replace the field's `ki-option` children with the latest
results, and clear `loading`. Use `change` to respond to a committed selection.

## An error from the application

Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on the committed
choice. The field is invalid, blocks its form and is announced as invalid at
once. Choosing, removing or clearing a choice withdraws the error; typing
filter text does not. Remove the attribute when a new attempt starts:
setting the same text again while it is still set shows nothing.

```html
<ki-combobox label="Assignee" name="assignee" value="ana" custom-error="Ana is on leave this week.">
  <ki-option value="ana">Ana Ruiz</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="juan">Juan Antón</ki-option>
</ki-combobox>
```

Attributes:
- `add-label` (string, default 'Add “{text}”'): Localizable free-entry offer. {text} is replaced by the trimmed query.
- `allow-custom` (boolean, default false): Offers to add trimmed query text when no known or selected choice already matches it.
- `custom-error` (string | undefined): An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the submitted choice ("Ana is on leave this week"). While it holds text the field is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help text at once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting when the person commits another selection (choosing, removing or clearing a choice; typing filter text is not a change), or when the form is reset, so it never blocks the corrected answer. It outranks `error-text`. When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts. When NOT to use: do not use it for a `required` field left without a choice; `error-text` words that. Setting the same text again while the prop still holds it shows nothing: remove it first, then set it again.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Disables editing, navigation and form submission.
- `empty-label` (string, default 'No results'): Localizable status when there are no choices to display.
- `error-text` (string | undefined): Message used when a required selection is missing, in place of the browser's message. A `custom-error` outranks it.
- `filter` ("contains" | "none" | "starts-with", default 'contains'): Filters by label. Set to none when the application provides results from a remote search.
- `help-text` (string | undefined): Guidance shown below the field and read as its description.
- `label` (string, required): Visible label and accessible name. Supply it even when placeholder text is also set.
- `loading` (boolean, default false): Replaces visible options with a loading indicator while a search is pending.
- `loading-label` (string, default 'Loading results'): Localizable status while waiting for a result set.
- `multiple` (boolean, default false): Enables ordered multiple selection and renders selected values as tags.
- `name` (string | undefined): Form-data key. Multiple choices contribute one entry each under this name.
- `placeholder` (string, default ''): Hint shown in the text input when it is empty.
- `remove-label` (string, default 'Remove {label}'): Localizable removal button label. {label} is replaced by the selected label.
- `required` (boolean, default false): Requires a committed choice to submit the form.
- `result-count-label` (string, default '{count} results'): Localizable status for several choices. {count} is replaced by the result count.
- `result-one-label` (string, default '1 result'): Localizable status for one available choice.
- `value` (string | string[], default ''): Committed value. Use a string for single selection and an array of strings for multiple selection. In HTML and catalog specs, encode multiple values as a JSON array string in the value attribute, or supply one literal value. Assign a new array to change multiple selections programmatically.

Slots:
- (default): Declarative ki-option children. Supply unique values and a human-readable label.

Parts:
- `description`: An option's secondary text.
- `error`: Polite error message shown after failed validation.
- `field`: Container for the text input and selected tags.
- `help`: Help below the field.
- `input`: Native text input with the combobox role.
- `label`: Visible label of the field and its listbox.
- `listbox`: Floating listbox surface.
- `option`: A mirrored choice row.
- `remove`: A native button that removes a selected tag.
- `tag`: A selected value in multiple mode.

Events:
- `ki-input` (CustomEvent<{ value: string }>): Reports a raw text edit in `detail.value`. Listen to it to request remote results.
- `change` (Event): Composed event after a user changes the committed selection. Read the committed value from the host.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-combobox-field-bg`: Fill for the editable field.
- `--ki-combobox-field-border`: Outline around the editable field.
- `--ki-combobox-field-fg`: Text on the editable field.
- `--ki-combobox-field-height`: Resting minimum block size of the field.
- `--ki-combobox-icon-size`: Size of search, selection and remove glyphs.
- `--ki-combobox-input-basis`: Preferred text-entry width before a row of tags wraps.
- `--ki-combobox-input-touch-font-size`: Minimum editable text size for coarse-pointer input.
- `--ki-combobox-listbox-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter for the floating listbox.
- `--ki-combobox-listbox-bg`: Fill for the floating listbox.
- `--ki-combobox-listbox-bg-image`: Optional image layered over the floating listbox.
- `--ki-combobox-listbox-border`: Outline around the floating listbox.
- `--ki-combobox-listbox-fg`: Text on the floating listbox.
- `--ki-combobox-listbox-max-block-size`: Maximum listbox block size before options scroll.
- `--ki-combobox-listbox-shadow`: Elevation of the floating listbox.
- `--ki-combobox-match-fg`: Foreground of the first bolded query match.
- `--ki-combobox-option-active-bg`: Fill for the active option.
- `--ki-combobox-option-active-fg`: Text on the active option.
- `--ki-combobox-tag-bg`: Fill for the selected tag.
- `--ki-combobox-tag-fg`: Text on the selected tag.
- `--ki-corner-field-item`: Corner radius for choices and tokens inside an editable field.
- `--ki-corner-field-surface`: Corner radius for an editable field and its floating choice surface.
- `--ki-density-control-offset`: Added to the block size of every scaled control and row (button, icon button, field, select, textarea, option, list item, tab). Components floor the result at ki.size.target-min.
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-md`: The md spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-xs`: The xs spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-xxs`: The xxs spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-outline-danger-high-em`: semantic color for outline danger high em.
- `--ki-outline-hairline-width`: Width of a hairline component surface edge.
- `--ki-text-danger-high-em`: semantic color for text danger high em.
- `--ki-text-high-em`: semantic color for text high em.
- `--ki-text-supporting`: Supporting text of an enabled control: field labels, placeholders, list secondary lines, quiet button labels and unselected tabs. A role, distinct from the med-em emphasis step it resolves to, so a mode can strengthen enabled supporting text without touching the disabled ink that also draws from med-em (directly, or through text.muted).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography line height body 1.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-visually-hidden-size`: Nonzero edge for clipped text available to assistive technology.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-bold`: semantic font weight for typography weight body bold.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-medium`: semantic font weight for typography weight body medium.

### ki-confirmation

An inline prompt for a decision about a proposed assistant action.

When to use: Show the exact action and the details a person needs before
granting permission. A trusted host maps the two decision events to its
declared actions and records the outcome in state.
When NOT to use: Report a completed action without a preceding request, or
block the rest of the interface with a modal decision (use ki-dialog).
The displayed action identifier is text and carries no execution authority.

Examples:

# Confirm an assistant action

```html
<ki-confirmation
  id="send-email-prompt"
  heading="Send this email?"
  action="send_email"
  approve-label="Send email"
  deny-label="Keep draft"
  consequence="Recipients will get the message immediately."
  remember
  remember-label="Allow sending email for the rest of this conversation"
>
  <dl>
    <dt>To</dt><dd>Ana Rivera</dd>
    <dt>Subject</dt><dd>Weekly report</dd>
  </dl>
</ki-confirmation>
```

A guarded UI spec binds each decision to its own action, one per event. A
binding by name alone is rejected, because the component declares two
events. `props.action` carries the visible tool identifier as text, never as
a URL, so the card renders under an origin allowlist too.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "actions": ["approve-send-email", "deny-send-email"],
  "root": {
    "component": "ki-confirmation",
    "props": {
      "heading": "Send this email?",
      "action": "send_email",
      "approve-label": "Send email",
      "deny-label": "Keep draft",
      "consequence": "Recipients will get the message immediately."
    },
    "action": { "ki-approve": "approve-send-email", "ki-deny": "deny-send-email" }
  }
}
```

The action data carries the card's props, not the event's detail. When the
decision needs the conversation preference, map the two events in trusted
host code instead. This MCP Apps example uses a ready `SurfaceBridge` whose
rendered spec declares `approve-send-email` and `deny-send-email` in its
top-level `actions` and leaves the card unbound.

```js
const prompt = document.querySelector('#send-email-prompt');

prompt.addEventListener('ki-approve', (event) => {
  if (event.composedPath()[0] !== prompt) return;
  bridge.dispatch('approve-send-email', {
    tool: 'send_email',
    remember: event.detail?.remember === true,
  });
});

prompt.addEventListener('ki-deny', (event) => {
  if (event.composedPath()[0] !== prompt) return;
  bridge.dispatch('deny-send-email', { tool: 'send_email' });
});
```

The host owns execution, deadlines and any conversation permission. Supply
outcome metadata and set the resolved state after recording the decision.

```js
prompt.resolvedBy = 'You';
prompt.resolvedAt = '10:32';
prompt.state = 'approved';
```

Call `await prompt.focusPrompt()` when the person is waiting for the request.
Keep the proposed inputs stable while the person is deciding. Mount a new
element if another request for the same tool replaces a pending one.

Attributes:
- `action` (string, required): Tool identifier shown to the person and available for reporting by the host.
- `approve-label` (string, required): Verb or short phrase that describes what approval does, such as "Send email".
- `approved-label` (string, default 'Approved'): Localized outcome text when the host marks the request approved.
- `consequence` (string | undefined): Cost or irreversible effect to read before deciding, displayed as a warning note.
- `denied-label` (string, default 'Denied'): Localized outcome text when the host marks the request denied.
- `deny-label` (string, required): Verb or short phrase for refusal, such as "Keep draft".
- `expired-label` (string, default 'Expired'): Localized outcome text when the host marks the request expired.
- `heading` (string, required): Question naming the proposed action. Provide it before asking for a decision.
- `remember` (boolean, default false): Offers an unchecked preference limited to this action in the current conversation.
- `remember-label` (string, default 'Allow this action for the rest of this conversation'): Localized conversation permission label. Name the specific permission when possible.
- `resolved-at` (string | undefined): Display-ready, localized resolution time from the host, if known.
- `resolved-by` (string | undefined): Display-ready name of the person or service that resolved the request, if known.
- `state` ("approved" | "denied" | "expired" | "pending", default 'pending'): Host-controlled outcome. Resolve after recording a decision or expiring the request.
- `tone` ("danger" | "neutral", default 'neutral'): Use danger when approval is destructive. Unknown values use neutral.

Slots:
- (default): Details the person needs to make the decision. Use readable text or semantic markup such as a description list.

Parts:
- `decisions`: The row of decision controls.
- `group`: The painted, labelled prompt or outcome surface.
- `heading`: The pending question.
- `remember`: The label of the conversation preference checkbox.
- `summary`: The resolved row.

Events:
- `ki-approve` (CustomEvent<{ remember: boolean }>): Explicit approval, with the conversation preference at the time of the decision.
- `ki-deny` (CustomEvent<void>): Explicit refusal of the pending request.

Methods:
- `focusPrompt()` (Promise<boolean>): Moves focus to the pending group and reports success. Call only when the host knows the person was waiting for this request. A focused editor keeps its focus, including editors inside open shadow roots.

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-confirmation-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop effect behind the confirmation.
- `--ki-confirmation-bg`: Solid raised background of the confirmation prompt and summary.
- `--ki-confirmation-bg-image`: Optional image painted over the solid confirmation background.
- `--ki-confirmation-border`: Boundary of the confirmation surface.
- `--ki-confirmation-border-width`: Stroke width of the confirmation boundary.
- `--ki-confirmation-fg`: Text on the confirmation surface.
- `--ki-confirmation-gap`: Block separation between confirmation rows.
- `--ki-confirmation-heading-font-family`: Typeface of the pending question.
- `--ki-confirmation-inline-gap`: Space between text and controls in a row.
- `--ki-confirmation-padding`: Space between the prompt's edge and its content.
- `--ki-confirmation-radius`: Corner radius of the confirmation surface.
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-surface-primary-med-em`: semantic color for surface primary med em.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-family-mono`: semantic font family for typography family mono.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-para`: semantic dimension for typography line height para.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-2`: semantic dimension for typography size body 2.
- `--ki-typography-visually-hidden-size`: Nonzero edge for clipped text available to assistive technology.

### ki-conversation

An accessible chat transcript with optional following as messages arrive.

When to use: Display chronological user, assistant and event messages. Give
the host a block-size constraint to keep scrolling within the transcript.
When NOT to use: Collect input, send messages or present a static sequence of
cards. Place the composer outside the transcript.

Examples:

# ki-conversation examples

## Bounded transcript

Set a block size to make the transcript scroll. Enable `stick-to-bottom` to
follow new messages and keep incoming replies in view.

```html
<ki-conversation id="help-chat" label="Component help" stick-to-bottom style="block-size: 20rem">
  <ki-message message-role="user">Which inputs handle form errors?</ki-message>
  <ki-message message-role="event" icon-name="search">Searched the component docs</ki-message>
  <ki-message message-role="assistant">Input, textarea and select show field errors.</ki-message>
</ki-conversation>
<label for="prompt">Message</label>
<textarea id="prompt"></textarea>
```

## Pass application chunks to a message

Call this function with the async iterable supplied by your application.
Keep the composer and any waiting indicator outside the live log.

```js
async function appendReply(conversation, chunks) {
  const reply = document.createElement('ki-message');
  reply.setAttribute('streaming', '');
  conversation.append(reply);
  try {
    for await (const chunk of chunks) {
      reply.append(chunk);
    }
  } finally {
    reply.removeAttribute('streaming');
  }
}
```

## Custom-elements entry points

```ts
import { defineCustomElement as defineConversation } from '@kimen/elements/ki-conversation';
import { defineCustomElement as defineMessage } from '@kimen/elements/ki-message';

defineConversation();
defineMessage();
```

Attributes:
- `jump-label` (string, default 'Jump to latest'): Visible and accessible label for the control that resumes following.
- `label` (string, default 'Conversation'): Accessible name of the transcript. Supply a distinct label when several logs share a page.
- `stick-to-bottom` (boolean, default false): Follow new or growing messages until the reader scrolls away from the end.

Slots:
- (default): The chronological transcript, normally ki-message elements.

Parts:
- `jump`: The Jump to latest button shown while following is paused.
- `log`: The named polite live region and keyboard-focusable scrollport.
- `messages`: The stack of slotted messages inside the scrollport.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-conversation-gap`: Space between messages in the transcript.
- `--ki-conversation-max-width`: Maximum inline size of the transcript.
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-md`: The md spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-copy-button

Copies text to the clipboard and confirms the result in the same button.

When to use: let a person copy a link, identifier, token or code sample. Supply
a direct value or point to a source in the same document or shadow root.
When NOT to use: submit a form, navigate, or trigger an action with no clipboard
write. Use a button or link for those actions.

Examples:

# ki-copy-button examples

## Copy an invite link

```html
<ki-copy-button value="https://kimen.dev/i/4f9a" label="Copy invite link"></ki-copy-button>
```

## Copy what a field currently contains

```html
<ki-input id="token-field" label="Token" value="token-4f9a"></ki-input>
<ki-copy-button from="token-field" variant="secondary">Copy token</ki-copy-button>
```

## Copy a code sample with localized feedback

```html
<pre id="install-command"><code>pnpm add @kimen/elements</code></pre>
<ki-copy-button
  from="install-command"
  copied-label="Copiado"
  copy-error-label="No se pudo copiar"
>Copiar comando</ki-copy-button>
```

Attributes:
- `copied-label` (string, default 'Copied'): Polite announcement after a successful write. Override for localized interfaces.
- `copy-error-label` (string, default "Couldn't copy"): Polite announcement after a failed write or missing source. Override for localized interfaces.
- `feedback-duration` (number, default 1500, minimum 0): Milliseconds to show feedback after a write settles. Zero keeps the outcome visible until the next result. Invalid values use 1500 ms.
- `from` (string | undefined, ID of another element of the same spec): ID of a source in this button's document or shadow root. A nonempty ID takes precedence over `value`. The source's current string value or its text content is read on activation.
- `label` (string, default 'Copy'): Accessible name for the icon-only control. Visible slot text supplies the name when present.
- `size` ("lg" | "md" | "sm" | "xl" | "xs", default 'md'): Token-backed button size. Match the size of adjacent controls.
- `value` (string | undefined): Exact clipboard text, including whitespace. Supply it when the text is known directly.
- `variant` ("ghost" | "outline" | "primary" | "quaternary" | "secondary", default 'ghost'): Button emphasis. Use ghost for compact actions and secondary for a visible supporting action.

Slots:
- (default): Optional visible text, which supplies the accessible name and places the icon at the inline start. Use plain text or non-interactive markup.

Parts:
- `button`: Native copy control with keyboard and pointer activation.
- `icon`: Fixed-size decorative feedback glyph box inside the button.
- `label`: Wrapper around the visible slotted label.

Events:
- `ki-copy` (CustomEvent<{ value: string }>): Fired after a successful clipboard write. The detail carries the exact text copied.
- `ki-copy-error` (CustomEvent<void>): Fired when the source cannot be read or clipboard writing is unavailable or fails.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-button-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter for button and icon-button variants; none in onmars v2.
- `--ki-button-border-width`: dimension used by the button component for border width (MarsUI outline stroke: 1px).
- `--ki-button-focus-ring-color`: color used by the button component for focus ring color.

- `--ki-button-focus-ring-shadow`: shadow used by the button component for the focus ring glow (MarsUI Focus/primary: 3px spread ring).
- `--ki-button-focus-ring-width`: dimension used by the button component for focus ring width.
- `--ki-button-font-family`: font family used by the button component for font family.
- `--ki-button-font-weight`: font weight used by the button component for font weight.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-hover-bg`: color used by the button component for ghost danger hover background.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-hover-border`: color used by the button component for ghost danger hover border.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-hover-fg`: color used by the button component for ghost danger hover foreground.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-rest-bg`: color used by the button component for ghost danger rest background.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-rest-border`: color used by the button component for ghost danger rest border.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-rest-fg`: color used by the button component for ghost danger rest foreground.

- `--ki-button-secondary-neutral-rest-bg`: color used by the button component for secondary neutral rest background (MarsUI Surface/special/secondary_alpha_base: neutral, not a brand tint; white in onmars v2).
- `--ki-button-secondary-neutral-rest-border`: color used by the button component for secondary neutral rest border (MarsUI top/inline edge).
- `--ki-button-secondary-neutral-rest-fg`: color used by the button component for secondary neutral rest foreground (MarsUI text/high_em).
- `--ki-button-secondary-rest-border-bottom`: color used by the button component for the secondary bottom edge (MarsUI Outline/secondary_button_bottom).
- `--ki-button-secondary-rest-shadow`: shadow used by the button component for secondary rest shadow (MarsUI Component_effect/secondary_default).
- `--ki-button-secondary-selected-bg`: Background of the selected secondary button toggle.
- `--ki-button-secondary-selected-fg`: Foreground of the selected secondary button toggle.
- `--ki-button-secondary-success-hover-bg`: color used by the button component for secondary success hover background.
- `--ki-button-secondary-success-hover-border`: color used by the button component for secondary success hover border (MarsUI top/inline edge, variant trait).
- `--ki-button-secondary-success-hover-fg`: color used by the button component for secondary success hover foreground.
- `--ki-button-secondary-success-rest-bg`: color used by the button component for secondary success rest background.
- `--ki-button-secondary-success-rest-border`: color used by the button component for secondary success rest border (MarsUI top/inline edge, variant trait).
- `--ki-button-secondary-success-rest-fg`: color used by the button component for secondary success rest foreground.
- `--ki-button-sm-font-size`: dimension used by the button component for sm font size.
- `--ki-button-sm-gap`: dimension used by the button component for sm gap (Button master 8003:301: root gap Space/xxs 2px + Text_wrap inline padding Space/xs 4px = 6px icon-to-text).
- `--ki-button-sm-height`: dimension used by the button component for sm height.
- `--ki-button-sm-icon-size`: dimension used by the button component for sm icon size.
- `--ki-button-sm-line-height`: dimension used by the button component for sm line height.
- `--ki-button-sm-min-target`: dimension used by the button component for sm min target.
- `--ki-button-sm-padding-inline`: dimension used by the button component for sm padding inline.
- `--ki-button-sm-radius`: dimension used by the button component for sm radius (Button master 8003:300 binds Radius/small-component/sm, the scale a radius mode reassigns).
- `--ki-button-sm-spinner-size`: dimension used by the button component for the sm loading spinner box (16px, the sm icon size; spec 046 D5: no Figma source, the spinner takes the place of the content).
- `--ki-button-spinner-duration`: duration used by the button and icon button components for one turn of the loading spinner (spec 046 D5: the ki-progress indeterminate period). Applied only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- `--ki-button-spinner-stroke-width`: dimension used by the button and icon button components for the loading spinner stroke (spec 046 D5: the circular ki-progress ring, drawn with a non-scaling stroke of this width).
- `--ki-button-tertiary-danger-hover-bg`: Tertiary alias of the secondary danger hover background.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-danger-hover-border`: color used by the button component for tertiary danger hover border (MarsUI secondary top/inline edge — tertiary carries the secondary_button outline pair).
- `--ki-button-tertiary-danger-hover-fg`: color used by the button component for tertiary danger hover foreground.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-danger-rest-bg`: Tertiary alias of the secondary danger rest background.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-danger-rest-border`: color used by the button component for tertiary danger rest border (MarsUI secondary top/inline edge — tertiary carries the secondary_button outline pair).
- `--ki-button-tertiary-danger-rest-fg`: color used by the button component for tertiary danger rest foreground.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-disabled-shadow`: value used by the button component for tertiary disabled shadow.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-hover-overlay`: Hover overlay for neutral tertiary buttons, shared with secondary by default.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-hover-shadow`: shadow used by the button component for tertiary hover shadow (MarsUI Component_effect/secondary_hover).
- `--ki-button-tertiary-neutral-disabled-bg`: color used by the button component for tertiary neutral disabled background.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-neutral-disabled-border`: color used by the button component for tertiary neutral disabled border.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-neutral-disabled-fg`: color used by the button component for tertiary neutral disabled foreground.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-neutral-hover-bg`: Tertiary alias of the secondary neutral hover background.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-neutral-hover-border`: color used by the button component for tertiary neutral hover border (MarsUI secondary top/inline edge — tertiary carries the secondary_button outline pair).
- `--ki-button-tertiary-neutral-hover-fg`: Tertiary alias of the secondary neutral hover foreground.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-neutral-rest-bg`: Tertiary alias of the secondary neutral rest background.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-neutral-rest-border`: color used by the button component for tertiary neutral rest border (MarsUI secondary top/inline edge — tertiary carries the secondary_button outline pair).
- `--ki-button-tertiary-neutral-rest-fg`: Tertiary alias of the secondary neutral rest foreground.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-rest-border-bottom`: color used by the button component for the tertiary bottom edge (MarsUI Outline/secondary_button_bottom, as secondary).
- `--ki-button-tertiary-rest-shadow`: shadow used by the button component for tertiary rest shadow (MarsUI Component_effect/secondary_default — replaces the migrated M2-era stack, which the material3 theme keeps via its own override).
- `--ki-button-tertiary-success-hover-bg`: Tertiary alias of the secondary success hover background.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-success-hover-border`: color used by the button component for tertiary success hover border (MarsUI secondary top/inline edge — tertiary carries the secondary_button outline pair).
- `--ki-button-tertiary-success-hover-fg`: color used by the button component for tertiary success hover foreground.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-success-rest-bg`: Tertiary alias of the secondary success rest background.
- `--ki-button-tertiary-success-rest-border`: color used by the button component for tertiary success rest border (MarsUI secondary top/inline edge — tertiary carries the secondary_button outline pair).
- `--ki-button-tertiary-success-rest-fg`: color used by the button component for tertiary success rest foreground.
- `--ki-button-toggle-radius`: Rounded rectangle shape for an unselected text toggle button.
- `--ki-button-toggle-selected-radius`: Pill shape for a selected text toggle button.
- `--ki-button-xl-font-size`: dimension used by the button component for xl font size.
- `--ki-button-xl-gap`: dimension used by the button component for xl gap (MarsUI effective icon-to-text gap 8px).
- `--ki-button-xl-height`: dimension used by the button component for xl height.
- `--ki-button-xl-icon-size`: dimension used by the button component for xl icon size.
- `--ki-button-xl-line-height`: dimension used by the button component for xl line height.
- `--ki-button-xl-min-target`: dimension used by the button component for xl min target.
- `--ki-button-xl-padding-inline`: dimension used by the button component for xl padding inline (MarsUI 14px).
- `--ki-button-xl-radius`: dimension used by the button component for xl radius (Button master 8003:300 binds Radius/small-component/xl, the scale a radius mode reassigns).
- `--ki-button-xl-spinner-size`: dimension used by the button component for the xl loading spinner box (24px, the xl icon size; spec 046 D5: no Figma source, the spinner takes the place of the content).
- `--ki-button-xs-font-size`: dimension used by the button component for xs font size: caption_2, 12px, the smallest size the library ships for informative text (spec 002 amendment A1, issue #321). The Figma Button master draws caption_1, 10px.
- `--ki-button-xs-gap`: dimension used by the button component for xs gap (MarsUI effective icon-to-text gap 4px).
- `--ki-button-xs-height`: dimension used by the button component for xs height.
- `--ki-button-xs-icon-size`: dimension used by the button component for xs icon size (MarsUI 14px).
- `--ki-button-xs-line-height`: dimension used by the button component for xs line height (caption_2 16px, the same height as caption_1).
- `--ki-button-xs-min-target`: dimension used by the button component for xs min target.
- `--ki-button-xs-padding-inline`: dimension used by the button component for xs padding inline.
- `--ki-button-xs-radius`: dimension used by the button component for xs radius (Button master 8003:300 binds Radius/small-component/xs, the scale a radius mode reassigns).
- `--ki-button-xs-spinner-size`: dimension used by the button component for the xs loading spinner box (14px, the xs icon size; spec 046 D5: no Figma source, the spinner takes the place of the content).
- `--ki-copy-button-error-bg`: Contrast ground for the error glyph on filled primary copy buttons.
- `--ki-copy-button-error-fg`: Copy failure glyph ink.
- `--ki-copy-button-success-bg`: Contrast ground for the success glyph on filled primary copy buttons.
- `--ki-copy-button-success-fg`: Confirmation check ink.
- `--ki-density-control-offset`: Added to the block size of every scaled control and row (button, icon button, field, select, textarea, option, list item, tab). Components floor the result at ki.size.target-min.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-counter

A decorative count or dot over a trigger or avatar.

When to use: mark unread or pending items on a trigger, or presence on an
avatar. Supply the full meaning in the host's accessible name and use a
page-owned polite live region for important updates.
When NOT to use: for an object's status (use ki-badge), a count inside a list
row (use text or ki-badge), or an announcement that needs its own semantics.

Examples:

# Notification count and presence

Provide the actual count or presence in the host's label. The visible counter
is decorative, so a label can expose the full count even if the pill says
`99+`.

```html
<ki-icon-button variant="secondary" label="Notifications, 3 unread">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true" fill="none" stroke="currentColor">
    <path d="M6 17h12l-2-3V9a4 4 0 0 0-8 0v5l-2 3Zm4 3h4" stroke-width="2" />
  </svg>
  <ki-counter slot="counter" value="3"></ki-counter>
</ki-icon-button>

<ki-avatar initials="AG" label="Ana García, online">
  <ki-counter slot="counter" tone="success" dot></ki-counter>
</ki-avatar>
```

The `for` attribute attaches the indicator to a trigger ID in the same
document or shadow root. Set the trigger's accessible name directly.

```html
<a id="inbox-link" href="/inbox" aria-label="Inbox, 120 unread">Inbox</a>
<ki-counter for="inbox-link" value="120" max="99"></ki-counter>
<p id="inbox-updates" role="status"></p>
```

For an important count update, update the trigger name and the counter, then
write one localized announcement to the pre-existing status region.

Attributes:
- `dot` (boolean, default false): Show a dot independently of the count, including when the value is zero.
- `for` (string | undefined, ID of another element of the same spec): Literal ID of a trigger in the same document or shadow root. Places the indicator at its block-start inline-end corner and hides it while the trigger is unavailable. For a named host slot, omit this property.
- `max` (number, default 99): Largest count displayed in full. Higher values display the cap with a plus sign. Fractional caps round down; invalid caps use 99.
- `tone` ("danger" | "neutral" | "primary" | "success", default 'danger'): Semantic palette of the pill or dot. An unknown tone uses danger.
- `value` (number | undefined): Count of unread or pending items. Finite values are rounded down. Values below one and non-finite values hide the count.

Slots: none

Parts:
- `indicator`: Painted pill or dot, including the surrounding ring.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-counter-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter for the indicator.
- `--ki-counter-bg`: Danger notification indicator fill.
- `--ki-counter-bg-image`: Optional image over the notification indicator fill.
- `--ki-counter-dot-size`: Width and height of the presence dot.
- `--ki-counter-fg`: Danger notification count text.
- `--ki-counter-font-family`: Font family for the count.
- `--ki-counter-font-size`: Font size for the count.
- `--ki-counter-font-weight`: Font weight for the count.
- `--ki-counter-neutral-bg`: Neutral notification indicator fill.
- `--ki-counter-neutral-fg`: Neutral notification count text.
- `--ki-counter-padding-inline`: Horizontal padding of a count pill.
- `--ki-counter-primary-bg`: Primary notification indicator fill.
- `--ki-counter-primary-fg`: Primary notification count text.
- `--ki-counter-radius`: Radius of the painted pill or dot.
- `--ki-counter-ring`: Surface-colored ring that separates the indicator from the trigger.
- `--ki-counter-ring-width`: Thickness of the separating ring.
- `--ki-counter-size`: Minimum width and height of a count pill.
- `--ki-counter-success-bg`: Success notification indicator fill.
- `--ki-counter-success-fg`: Success notification count text.

### ki-date-picker

A locale-aware date field with an anchored keyboard-operable calendar.

When to use: Choose a nearby date or date range when the weekday matters, such as
a booking, a deadline or a schedule.
When NOT to use: Enter a known distant date, such as a birth date, or choose a time.

Examples:

# DatePicker examples

## Choose a departure date

```html
<ki-date-picker label="Departure" name="departure" locale="en-GB" required
  help-text="Enter a date in DD/MM/YYYY format." min="2026-11-10">
</ki-date-picker>
```

Typing `20/11/2026` and pressing Enter emits
`ki-change` with `{ "value": "2026-11-20" }`.

## Apply a stay range

```html
<ki-date-picker label="Stay" name="stay" mode="range" confirm
  value="2026-11-12/2026-11-16" locale="en-GB"
  min="2026-11-10" max="2026-11-30">
</ki-date-picker>
```

Pick two endpoints and activate Apply to save the range. The form receives
one `stay` entry with the date pair.

## Text that is not a date

The field keeps text it cannot read as a date within its bounds so the
person can correct it, shows its own message (`error-text`, else
`invalid-date-label`) once the person leaves the field or presses Enter, and
stays invalid, so its form cannot submit it. It fires no `ki-change`, and
`value` keeps the last date it saved. Clearing a saved date is a change: it
fires `ki-change` with `{ "value": "" }`.

## An error from the application

Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on the submitted date,
such as an availability check. The field is invalid, blocks its form and is
announced as invalid at once. The person's next edit of the text or pick of
another date withdraws the error. Remove the attribute when a new attempt
starts: setting the same text again while it is still set shows nothing.

```html
<ki-date-picker label="Departure" name="departure" locale="en-GB" value="2026-12-24"
  custom-error="No flights on that day.">
</ki-date-picker>
```

Attributes:
- `apply-label` (string, default 'Apply'): Localized label of the confirmation button that saves a complete draft.
- `cancel-label` (string, default 'Cancel'): Localized label of the confirmation button that discards a draft.
- `change-label` (string, default 'Change date, {date}'): Localized name of the trigger when a date is saved. Use {date} for the current selection.
- `choose-label` (string, default 'Choose date'): Localized name of the calendar dialog and of the trigger when no date is saved.
- `confirm` (boolean, default false): Require Apply before saving picks made in the calendar.
- `custom-error` (string | undefined): An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the submitted date ("No flights on that day"). While it holds text the field is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help text at once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting at the person's next edit of the text or pick of another date, or when the form is reset, so it never blocks the corrected answer. It outranks `error-text`. When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts. When NOT to use: do not use it for a missing, unreadable or out-of-bounds date, which the field reports itself; `error-text` words those. Setting the same text again while the prop still holds it shows nothing: remove it first, then set it again.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Disables the text entry and calendar button and excludes the field from form data.
- `error-text` (string | undefined): Overrides the message shown when a date is missing, invalid or outside the bounds. A `custom-error` outranks it.
- `first-day-of-week` (number | undefined, minimum 0, maximum 6): First weekday, where Sunday is 0 and Saturday is 6. Defaults to the locale's week start.
- `help-text` (string | undefined): A format hint or explanation read with the field. It is replaced by a visible error.
- `invalid-date-label` (string, default 'Enter a valid date within the allowed range.'): Localized fallback message for an impossible, incomplete or out-of-bounds date.
- `label` (string, required): Visible text and accessible name of the date field. Provide a label for every field.
- `locale` (string | undefined): BCP 47 language tag for localized dates and weekday order. Defaults to the page language.
- `max` (string | undefined): Latest selectable date, inclusive. Use YYYY-MM-DD.
- `min` (string | undefined): Earliest selectable date, inclusive. Use YYYY-MM-DD.
- `mode` ("range" | "single", default 'single'): Select one date or a range with a start and an end date.
- `name` (string | undefined): Form-data key. A range is submitted as a single value.
- `next-month-label` (string, default 'Next month'): Localized accessible name of the next-month button.
- `previous-month-label` (string, default 'Previous month'): Localized accessible name of the previous-month button.
- `required` (boolean, default false): Requires a complete date or pair of dates for native form submission.
- `value` (string, default ''): Current ISO date, ISO start/end pair or empty string. The value attribute is the reset default.

Slots: none

Parts:
- `day`: Date button in the calendar grid.
- `error`: Live constraint message replacing help when the field is invalid.
- `field`: Enclosure of the text field and calendar button.
- `grid`: Calendar grid with localized weekdays and date buttons.
- `help`: Help text associated with the input.
- `input`: Native text entry for a localized date or range.
- `label`: Visible label and accessible name of the text field.
- `month`: Live month and year heading.
- `popup`: Anchored non-modal calendar dialog.
- `trigger`: Button that opens and closes the calendar.

Events:
- `ki-change` (CustomEvent<DatePickerChangeDetail>): Reports a changed, committed value in canonical ISO form. Use this for calendar and typed changes.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-control-border-width`: Stroke width of the boundary of a compact control.
- `--ki-control-radius-track`: Corner radius of a track containing adjacent controls.
- `--ki-control-size-sm`: Small control track height, 32 CSS px at the default root size.
- `--ki-control-size-touch`: Touch target size for controls on a coarse pointer.
- `--ki-date-picker-backdrop-filter`: Complete filter behind the calendar.
- `--ki-date-picker-bg`: Fill of the calendar dialog.
- `--ki-date-picker-bg-image`: Optional image layered over the calendar fill.
- `--ki-date-picker-border`: Calendar surface edge.
- `--ki-date-picker-day-hover-bg`: Hover fill of an available unselected day.
- `--ki-date-picker-day-hover-fg`: Ink on the hover fill.
- `--ki-date-picker-day-radius`: Radius of a day and the ends of a range.
- `--ki-date-picker-day-size`: Default size of a day target.
- `--ki-date-picker-fg`: Default calendar text.
- `--ki-date-picker-field-bg`: Fill of the text field.
- `--ki-date-picker-field-fg`: Text, icon and caret of the field.
- `--ki-date-picker-heading-family`: Family of the calendar month heading.
- `--ki-date-picker-outside-bg`: Fill behind dates in neighboring months.
- `--ki-date-picker-outside-fg`: Ink of dates in neighboring months.
- `--ki-date-picker-radius`: Calendar popup corner radius.
- `--ki-date-picker-range-bg`: Fill of the span between selected endpoints.
- `--ki-date-picker-range-fg`: Text of dates within the span.
- `--ki-date-picker-selected-bg`: Fill of a chosen day or range endpoint.
- `--ki-date-picker-selected-fg`: Text of a chosen day or range endpoint.
- `--ki-date-picker-shadow`: Calendar popup elevation.
- `--ki-date-picker-today-border`: Outline of the current date.
- `--ki-date-picker-weekday-bg`: Fill behind weekday names.
- `--ki-date-picker-weekday-fg`: Ink of weekday names.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-glyph-size-md`: Medium glyph for body content (20px at the default root size).
- `--ki-layout-spacing-3xl`: The 3xl spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-lg`: The lg spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-md`: The md spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-xl`: The xl spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-xs`: The xs spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-outline-control`: The boundary of a control that can be EMPTY — field, checkbox, radio, switch. Such a control carries no label inside its own box, so the box IS what identifies it and must clear WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 against every surface it can sit on (s0-s2). Pinned to an accessibility floor, NOT to a position in the emphasis ramp: rebalancing outline.base/low/med/high must never silently erase a control's edge. MarsUI draws Outline/Black-8 here, but as an edge over a filled cell on a fixed canvas — transcribed literally it measured 1.19:1 against a fill identical to the page (audit 2026-07-25). Declared deviation.
- `--ki-outline-danger-high-em`: semantic color for outline danger high em.
- `--ki-surface-transparent`: Transparent surface backing for a background image that carries its own opacity.
- `--ki-text-danger-high-em`: semantic color for text danger high em.
- `--ki-text-high-em`: semantic color for text high em.
- `--ki-text-supporting`: Supporting text of an enabled control: field labels, placeholders, list secondary lines, quiet button labels and unselected tabs. A role, distinct from the med-em emphasis step it resolves to, so a mode can strengthen enabled supporting text without touching the disabled ink that also draws from med-em (directly, or through text.muted).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography line height body 1.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-medium`: semantic font weight for typography weight body medium.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-semibold`: semantic font weight for typography weight body semibold.

### ki-details

A native disclosure for supporting information that can stay collapsed.

When to use: reveal a short explanation, FAQ answer, settings section or tool
output on demand. Use ki-accordion for related disclosures.
When NOT to use: hide the primary action or information needed to complete a task.
For script-free HTML, author native details and summary directly.

Examples:

### Workspace permissions

Use one disclosure for an explanation the reader can reveal on demand.
Use the plain `summary` prop for text or a heading in the `summary` slot.
The default slot contains the answer.

```html
<ki-details summary="Who can see my workspace?">
  <p>Only people you invite can see it.</p>
</ki-details>
```

Listen for `ki-toggle` on the disclosure to read `event.detail.open`.
In a catalog surface, bind the action to the individual Details node.

Attributes:
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Disables summary activation. The page can still set open.
- `name` (string | undefined): Nonempty name for exclusive disclosures in the same document or shadow root.
- `open` (boolean, default false): Whether the panel is open. Native changes reflect back to this property.
- `summary` (string | undefined): Plain label for the control. Supply the summary slot for a rich label.

Slots:
- (default): Content shown when the disclosure is open.
- `summary`: Rich summary text or an authored heading, replacing the summary prop.

Parts: none

Events:
- `ki-toggle` (CustomEvent<KiDetailsToggleDetail>): Emitted when the native disclosure toggles or an exclusive peer closes it.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-details-backdrop-filter`: Complete filter for the backdrop behind the disclosure surface.
- `--ki-details-bg`: Color of the disclosure surface.
- `--ki-details-bg-image`: Optional image painted over the disclosure surface.
- `--ki-details-body-bg`: Surface color of the disclosure body.
- `--ki-details-body-fg`: Supporting text color of the disclosure body.
- `--ki-details-border`: Color of the disclosure frame and accordion separators.
- `--ki-details-border-width`: Width of the disclosure or accordion frame.
- `--ki-details-disabled-fg`: Text and icon color of a disabled summary.
- `--ki-details-fg`: Text color on the disclosure surface.
- `--ki-details-motion-duration`: Duration of the chevron rotation.
- `--ki-details-motion-easing`: Easing of the chevron rotation.
- `--ki-details-padding`: Inline inset of the summary and inset of the panel body.
- `--ki-details-radius`: Corners of a standalone disclosure or the accordion frame.
- `--ki-details-summary-hover-bg`: Surface color of a hovered summary.
- `--ki-details-summary-hover-fg`: Text and icon color of a hovered summary.
- `--ki-details-summary-padding-block`: Block inset of the summary.
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography line height body 1.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-para`: semantic dimension for typography line height para.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-medium`: semantic font weight for typography weight body medium.

### ki-dialog

A modal dialog for an interrupting decision or a focused task.

When to use: destructive confirmations, blocking choices, and brief
critical input that must be resolved before returning to the page. Always
provide a `heading`, place actions in the `footer` slot, wire each
dismissal to `close()` or a close command, and in destructive confirmations put `autofocus` on
the least destructive action. Use `fullscreen="compact"` for longer tasks
that need the whole window on compact screens.
When NOT to use: non-blocking feedback (`ki-alert`, `ki-toast`),
supplementary hints (`ki-tooltip`), multi-step flows that need their own
page, menus, or pickers.

Examples:

A modal confirmation. `heading` names the dialog and actions go in the `footer`
slot. Each invoker uses the dialog's ID within the same document or shadow root.

```html
<ki-button commandfor="confirm-dialog" command="show-modal" tone="danger">Delete draft</ki-button>
<ki-dialog heading="Delete draft?" id="confirm-dialog">
  <p>This permanently removes the draft.</p>
  <ki-button slot="footer" commandfor="confirm-dialog" command="request-close" autofocus>Cancel</ki-button>
  <ki-button slot="footer" commandfor="confirm-dialog" command="close" tone="danger" variant="primary">Delete</ki-button>
</ki-dialog>
```

`close` dismisses the dialog. `request-close` first gives the dialog a chance
to cancel the request. After an accepted close command, the opening button
regains focus and `ki-close` reports `detail.reason: 'command'`. `show()` and
`close()` remain available for programmatic control.


## Edit a longer form

```html
<ki-button commandfor="event-details" command="show-modal">Add event</ki-button>
<ki-dialog id="event-details" heading="New event" fullscreen="compact"
  confirm-label="Save" close-label="Discard and close">
  <ki-input label="Title"></ki-input>
  <ki-input label="Date"></ki-input>
</ki-dialog>
```

Below 600 CSS pixels the modal fills the window and keeps its heading and
actions visible above the scrollable body. At wider widths `Save` moves to
the centered dialog's footer. Handle `ki-confirm` to save the form and call
`close()` after success. In fullscreen, call `preventDefault()` on
`ki-close` to veto Escape or the header close button while editing.

When importing the dialog directly, register `ki-button` to use the themed
confirmation button. A single-element import still provides a native
confirmation button with the same label and event.

Attributes:
- `close-label` (string, default 'Close'): Accessible name for the fullscreen close button. Localize it or describe the effect of dismissing, for example "Discard and close".
- `close-on-backdrop` (boolean, default false): Opts into backdrop light-dismiss. Omit this attribute for critical confirmations; `close-on-backdrop="false"` still enables it. When to use: low-risk dialogs where an outside click may safely dismiss. When NOT to use: destructive confirmations or decisions that should not be lost to a stray click; omit the attribute entirely rather than setting it to `"false"`.
- `confirm-label` (string | undefined): Label for the optional confirmation button. Use an action verb such as "Save". The button is in the fullscreen header or the centered footer.
- `fullscreen` ("always" | "compact" | "never", default 'never'): Layout for the native modal. Use `compact` to fill windows narrower than 600 CSS pixels, or `always` to fill any window. Use `never` for a centered dialog at every width.
- `heading` (string, required): Visible dialog title and accessible-name source. Always provide a heading; an empty value intentionally leaves the native dialog unnamed. When to use: name the interrupting decision, for example "Delete account?". When NOT to use: do not omit it for production dialogs; APG modal dialogs require an accessible name.
- `open` (boolean, default false): Reflected live modal state. Add it or call `show()` to open; remove it or call `close()` to close. When open, the native dialog enters the top layer and the page behind is inert. When to use: bind application state to the dialog's modal lifecycle. When NOT to use: do not set the internal native `<dialog open>` attribute; the host attribute is the only public source of truth.

Slots:
- (default): Dialog body content.
- `footer`: Dialog actions. Dismiss using an invoker command or `close()`.

Parts:
- `body`: Scrollable body region.
- `dialog`: Internal native dialog surface.
- `footer`: Action row, collapsed when empty.
- `header`: Fullscreen bar with the title and its controls.
- `heading`: Visible h2 title, rendered only when `heading` is non-empty.

Events:
- `ki-close` (CustomEvent<KiDialogCloseDetail>): Requests dismissal on fullscreen Escape or activation of the header close button. Prevent the default on that cancelable event to keep the modal open. The button reports `method` and Escape reports `escape`. Every other dismissal path emits a noncancelable notification after close and focus restoration. Use `open` to observe the modal's live state.
- `ki-confirm` (CustomEvent<void>): The user activated the confirmation button. Handle validation, submission and dismissal in the application.

Methods:
- `close()` (Promise<void>): Closes the dialog and reports `method`. No-op when already closed. Equivalent to removing the host `open` attribute. Footer actions never close automatically; wire them to this method or an invoker command. When to use: resolve footer actions, programmatic dismissals, and application-controlled cancellation. When NOT to use: do not use for Escape or backdrop bookkeeping; those paths set their own close reasons.
- `show()` (Promise<void>): Opens the dialog modally. No-op when already open. Equivalent to adding the host `open` attribute. When to use: call from the invoker that should receive focus again after close. When NOT to use: do not call repeatedly to refresh content; update slotted content directly while open.

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-rest-bg`: color used by the button component for primary neutral rest background (MarsUI Surface/primary_med_em, brand 500).
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-rest-fg`: color used by the button component for primary neutral rest foreground.
- `--ki-control-radius-item`: Corner radius of an individual control inside a track.
- `--ki-control-size-md`: Medium control track height, 40 CSS px at the default root size.
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-dialog-backdrop-bg`: color used by the dialog component for backdrop background.
- `--ki-dialog-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter behind the dialog surface.
- `--ki-dialog-bg`: Base background color of the dialog. Onmars v1 used a transparent backing beneath its translucent image.
- `--ki-dialog-bg-image`: Optional CSS background image layered over the dialog fill. Use none for a solid fill.
- `--ki-dialog-body-padding-block-end`: dimension used by the dialog component for body section padding block end (Modal compact Body: Space/5xl 20px.)
- `--ki-dialog-body-padding-block-start`: dimension used by the dialog component for body section padding block start (Modal compact Body 16414:19668: Space/5xl 20px.)
- `--ki-dialog-body-padding-inline`: dimension used by the dialog component for body section padding inline (Modal compact Body: Space/5xl 20px.)
- `--ki-dialog-border`: border used by the dialog component for border (MarsUI 1px solid Outline/base_em Black/3 light / White/3 dark; retires the migrated Black/5 foundation reference).
- `--ki-dialog-divider-color`: color used by the dialog component for the dividers under the heading and above the footer (Outline/base-em).
- `--ki-dialog-divider-width`: dimension used by the dialog component for the dividers under the heading and above the footer (Modal-header and Modal-actions 1px strokes). Zero removes them.
- `--ki-dialog-fg`: color used by the dialog component for foreground.
- `--ki-dialog-focus-ring-color`: color used by the dialog component for focus ring color.
- `--ki-dialog-focus-ring-offset`: dimension used by the dialog component for focus ring offset.
- `--ki-dialog-focus-ring-width`: dimension used by the dialog component for focus ring width.
- `--ki-dialog-footer-padding-block-end`: dimension used by the dialog component for footer section padding block end (Modal-actions/CTAs: Space/7xl 24px.)
- `--ki-dialog-footer-padding-block-start`: dimension used by the dialog component for footer section padding block start (Modal-actions/CTAs 14158:28302: Space/7xl 24px, below the divider.)
- `--ki-dialog-footer-padding-inline`: dimension used by the dialog component for footer section padding inline (Modal-actions/CTAs: Space/5xl 20px.)
- `--ki-dialog-fullscreen-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter for the fullscreen surface.
- `--ki-dialog-fullscreen-bg`: Solid raised surface for the fullscreen dialog.
- `--ki-dialog-fullscreen-bg-image`: Optional image over the fullscreen fill.
- `--ki-dialog-fullscreen-fg`: Foreground for the fullscreen dialog.
- `--ki-dialog-fullscreen-header-border`: Divider beneath the fullscreen header.
- `--ki-dialog-fullscreen-header-height`: Minimum block size of the fullscreen header.
- `--ki-dialog-gap`: dimension used by the dialog component for the gap between its footer actions (Modal-actions/CTAs 14158:28302: Space/xl 12px).
- `--ki-dialog-heading-font-family`: Font family for the dialog heading. Override it to give dialogs their own heading typeface.
- `--ki-dialog-heading-font-size`: dimension used by the dialog component for heading font size.
- `--ki-dialog-heading-font-weight`: font weight used by the dialog component for heading font weight.
- `--ki-dialog-heading-letter-spacing`: Letter spacing for the dialog heading. Override it to tune tracking for the chosen heading typeface.
- `--ki-dialog-heading-line-height`: dimension used by the dialog component for heading line height.
- `--ki-dialog-heading-padding-block-end`: dimension used by the dialog component for heading section padding block end (Modal-header compact: Space/3xl 16px, above the divider.)
- `--ki-dialog-heading-padding-block-start`: dimension used by the dialog component for heading section padding block start (Modal-header compact 14156:25916: Space/3xl 16px.)
- `--ki-dialog-heading-padding-inline`: dimension used by the dialog component for heading section padding inline (Modal-header compact: Space/5xl 20px.)
- `--ki-dialog-max-width`: dimension used by the dialog component for max width (surface size scale; the former ki.space.26xl reference misused the spacing scale).
- `--ki-dialog-min-width`: dimension used by the dialog component for min width (surface size scale; the former ki.space.25xl reference misused the spacing scale).
- `--ki-dialog-motion-duration`: duration used by the dialog component for the enter transition (MarsUI moderate step 240ms; retires the migrated 0ms token that disabled the @starting-style fade).
- `--ki-dialog-motion-easing`: easing used by the dialog component for the enter transition (MarsUI decelerate curve; retires the migrated linear pair).
- `--ki-dialog-padding`: dimension used by the dialog component for the room it keeps from the viewport edges when its width or height is clamped. Each section pads itself (heading, body and footer padding tokens).
- `--ki-dialog-radius`: dimension used by the dialog component for radius (MarsUI compact Modal master 16414:19665: Radius/big_component/radius_sm 20px; the large variant anchors 24px big_component/radius_md).
- `--ki-dialog-shadow`: Dialog elevation: MarsUI elevation ramp level e4 (brief §5, high modal surface; replaces the migrated approximation). material3 keeps its own e3 override (M3 dialog = level3).
- `--ki-elevation-none`: Flat surfaces carry no resting shadow.
- `--ki-focus-primary`: MarsUI Focus/primary: 3px spread focus ring of Outline/primary_base_em_alpha, read from the Figma master as #845abe33 = brand 500 at 20% (Kimen name: outline.primary-base-em-alpha / brand.500-alpha-2). The previous 40% (outline.primary-low-em-alpha / brand.500-alpha-4) came from specs/002-ki-button/design-extraction.md §2.5, which read the alpha off the Dark canvas mode and recorded it as the Light value; the ring shipped 2x too strong in light and 2.8x in dark across twelve components.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-md`: The md spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-xs`: The xs spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-motion-distance-md`: Motion travel distance md (8px): entrance slide offsets (e.g. dialog rise).
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-motion-easing-standard-accelerate`: Utility exit curve. M3 md.sys.motion.easing.standard-accelerate. onmars: the MarsUI accelerate curve (ki.easing.in).
- `--ki-spacing-action-hairline`: Width of the frame and divider in an action surface.
- `--ki-state-layer-hover`: Hover interaction state layer. M3 md.sys.state.hover.state-layer-opacity: 8% of the on-color. onmars: the hover overlay (White/5 light, Black/5 dark).
- `--ki-state-layer-pressed`: Pressed interaction state layer. M3 md.sys.state.pressed.state-layer-opacity: 12% of the on-color (same as focus). onmars: one step above the hover overlay (White/8 light, Black/8 dark).
- `--ki-surface-transparent`: Transparent surface backing for a background image that carries its own opacity.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-family-heading`: Shared font family for component headings. Reassign it on a theme root to style headings independently of body copy.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-para`: semantic dimension for typography line height para.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-normal`: semantic font weight for typography weight body normal.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-semibold`: semantic font weight for typography weight body semibold.

### ki-divider

A static, decorative rule that visually separates adjacent content.

When to use: visually separate adjacent content when spacing alone is not
enough: grouped settings sections, toolbar action groups, distinct
regions inside a card — horizontal between stacked content, vertical
between side-by-side content.
When NOT to use: between list items (separation is a ki-list theme-token
decision), semantic thematic breaks in running prose (native `<hr>`
carries those semantics — the divider is deliberately decorative and
contributes no role, name or announcement), as a border or outline
substitute (surface/border tokens), or purely decorative flourishes
(prefer white space).

Examples:

A horizontal rule between stacked content; the divider is decorative — no role, no name, no tab stop (semantic thematic breaks belong to native `<hr>`):

```html
<section>Profile</section>
<ki-divider></ki-divider>
<section>Notifications</section>
```

`orientation="vertical"` separates side-by-side content and stretches to the cross size its layout context provides — give the row a height or let flex stretch it:

```html
<div style="display: flex; align-items: stretch">
  <ki-button type="button">Edit</ki-button>
  <ki-divider orientation="vertical"></ki-divider>
  <ki-button type="button">Share</ki-button>
</div>
```

An inset is a per-instance layout decision — use logical margins on the instance; thickness, color, end caps and gutter stay per-theme `--ki-divider-*` tokens, never attributes:

```html
<ki-divider style="margin-inline: 16px"></ki-divider>
```

Attributes:
- `orientation` ("horizontal" | "vertical", default 'horizontal'): Layout axis of the rule: `horizontal` spans the available inline size between stacked content; `vertical` stretches to the cross size its layout context provides, between side-by-side content. A structural axis, never appearance — thickness, color, end caps and gutter are per-theme `--ki-divider-*` tokens. An unrecognized value matches no style selector, so the divider keeps the default horizontal rendering (fallback by CSS construction — no validation code).

Slots: none

Parts:
- `divider`: The rule itself: thickness, color and end-cap radius.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-divider-color`: color used by the divider component for the rule: Outline/base_em (Black/3 light, White/3 dark), the exact variable bound to every Figma divider variant and the same semantic role ki-list uses for item dividers.
- `--ki-divider-radius`: dimension used by the divider component for the end caps: the MarsUI ends axis is a pure-appearance, per-theme choice (FR-006); onmars keeps the rounded hairline (ends=rounded, pill caps).
- `--ki-divider-spacing`: dimension used by the divider component for the reserved gutter: the 8px MarsUI variant frame with the rule centered inside it (FR-007).
- `--ki-divider-thickness`: dimension used by the divider component for the rule thickness: the MarsUI 1px hairline verified on the Divider_horizontal/Divider_vertical sets (specs/020-ki-divider/design-extraction.md).
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-easing-standard-decelerate`: Utility entrance curve. M3 md.sys.motion.easing.standard-decelerate. onmars: the MarsUI decelerate curve (ki.easing.out).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-drawer

An edge-aligned sheet for a focused task that keeps the current page in context.

When to use: Edit an item beside its list or offer a short set of actions in a
bottom sheet. Supply a heading and wire slotted actions in the application.
Use non-modal mode if people need to interact with the page while editing.
When NOT to use: Menus, hover hints, permanent navigation, or work that needs a
full page. For a short interrupting decision in the center, use ki-dialog.

Examples:

## Edit details beside a list

Use `heading` to name the sheet. Open it from a focused trigger so focus can
return there. The app wires its own footer actions.

```html
<ki-button id="edit-incident" type="button">Edit incident</ki-button>
<ki-drawer id="incident-editor" heading="Edit incident" placement="end">
  <ki-input label="Title" value="Search index rebuild"></ki-input>
  <ki-button slot="footer" id="save-incident" type="button" variant="primary">
    Save
  </ki-button>
</ki-drawer>

<script type="module">
  const editor = document.querySelector('#incident-editor');
  document.querySelector('#edit-incident').addEventListener('click', () => editor.show());
  document.querySelector('#save-incident').addEventListener('click', () => {
    // Save the app's changes first.
    editor.close();
  });
  editor.addEventListener('ki-close', (event) => {
    if (editor.hasAttribute('data-unsaved')) event.preventDefault();
  });
</script>
```

## Offer a short list of actions

A bottom sheet has a swipe handle and a keyboard-accessible Close button.
Use `close-label` to translate the button for your audience.

```html
<ki-drawer heading="Share incident" placement="bottom" size="20rem" open>
  <p>Choose how to share the incident.</p>
  <ki-button slot="footer" variant="secondary">Email</ki-button>
  <ki-button slot="footer" variant="primary">Copy link</ki-button>
</ki-drawer>
```

Use `modal="false"` when the page behind the drawer should stay interactive.
`placement="start"` and `placement="end"` follow the inherited direction.

Attributes:
- `close-label` (string | undefined, default 'Close'): Accessible name for the built-in Close button. Translate this for localized interfaces.
- `heading` (string, required): Title and accessible name. Provide a heading whenever the drawer opens.
- `modal` (boolean, default true): Makes the page behind the sheet inert. Set modal="false" for continued page interaction.
- `open` (boolean, default false): Reflected live state. Setting it to false requests dismissal and may be vetoed.
- `placement` ("bottom" | "end" | "start", default 'end'): Logical edge. Use bottom for an action sheet with a swipe handle. Unknown values use end.
- `size` (string | undefined): Optional CSS length. Overrides the 18rem themed width or bottom height cap.

Slots:
- (default): The drawer's content, such as fields or a short list of actions.
- `footer`: Optional actions such as Save. Wire these in the application.
- `header-actions`: Optional actions between the heading and Close button.

Parts:
- `body`: The scrollable content region.
- `close`: The built-in Close button.
- `dialog`: The native sheet surface.
- `footer`: The action row, collapsed when empty.
- `handle`: The decorative bottom-sheet swipe handle.
- `header`: The heading and action layout.
- `heading`: The visible title that names the sheet.

Events:
- `ki-close` (CustomEvent<KiDrawerCloseDetail>): Requests dismissal before the drawer closes. Call preventDefault() to keep it open, for example when edits are unsaved. The event carries the reason in detail.reason.

Methods:
