- `close()` (Promise<void>): Requests dismissal. An application can veto it by canceling ki-close.
- `show()` (Promise<void>): Opens the sheet. A focused invoker receives focus again after modal dismissal.

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-corner-control`: Deprecated alias kept for pre-Fase-1 consumers; use ki.radius.md.
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-dialog-backdrop-bg`: color used by the dialog component for backdrop background.
- `--ki-dialog-divider-width`: dimension used by the dialog component for the dividers under the heading and above the footer (Modal-header and Modal-actions 1px strokes). Zero removes them.
- `--ki-drawer-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter applied behind the drawer surface.
- `--ki-drawer-bg`: Raised surface color of the drawer.
- `--ki-drawer-bg-image`: Optional image layered over the drawer surface.
- `--ki-drawer-close-size`: Preferred size of the Close button before the density minimum.
- `--ki-drawer-fg`: Foreground color on the drawer surface.
- `--ki-drawer-handle-color`: Color of the bottom-sheet handle.
- `--ki-drawer-handle-size`: Inline extent of the bottom-sheet handle.
- `--ki-drawer-handle-thickness`: Thickness of the bottom-sheet handle.
- `--ki-drawer-heading-font-family`: Typeface of the drawer title.
- `--ki-drawer-radius`: Radius of the corners on the inner edge of the drawer.
- `--ki-drawer-shadow`: Resting elevation of the drawer.
- `--ki-drawer-size`: Default inline size of a side sheet and block-size cap of a bottom sheet.
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-2xl`: The 2xl spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-md`: The md spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-xl`: The xl spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-duration-medium-1`: M3 md.sys.motion.duration.medium1 (250ms). onmars: MarsUI moderate step (240ms, 2x the 120ms base).
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-outline-low-em`: semantic color for outline low em.
- `--ki-surface-hover-overlay-inverse`: semantic color for surface hover overlay inverse.
- `--ki-surface-transparent`: Transparent surface backing for a background image that carries its own opacity.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-title-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height title 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-title-2`: semantic dimension for typography size title 2.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-semibold`: semantic font weight for typography weight body semibold.

### ki-empty-state

A short explanation and next step for an empty view.

When to use: explain an empty list, table, search result, or first-run view.
Supply a localized heading that names what is empty and a short next step.
Use announce for results that change after an interaction.
When NOT to use: signal that results are loading or draw attention to an error
that needs acknowledgement. Use ki-spinner or ki-alert for those states.

Examples:

Use EmptyState when a list, table or first-run screen is empty. Name what is
empty, explain why or what to do next, and offer at most one primary action.

```ts
import '@kimen/elements/icons/folder-plus';
```

```html
<ki-empty-state heading="No projects yet" icon-name="folder-plus" tone="primary-light">
  Projects hold your surfaces, catalogs and themes.
  <ki-button slot="actions" variant="primary">New project</ki-button>
</ki-empty-state>
```

Use `announce` for search or filter results. Insert the message when results
become empty. If it remains visible for a subsequent search, update its heading
and description.

```html
<ki-empty-state heading="No results for webhok" heading-level="2" size="sm" announce>
  Check the spelling or remove a filter.
  <ki-button slot="actions" variant="secondary">Clear filters</ki-button>
</ki-empty-state>
```

Put a decorative illustration in `media` to replace the icon.

```html
<ki-empty-state heading="Your inbox is clear">
  <img slot="media" src="/images/empty-inbox.svg" alt="" width="120" height="80">
  New messages will appear here.
</ki-empty-state>
```

Attributes:
- `announce` (boolean, default false): Put the heading and description in a polite status, with actions outside the region. Set before mounting a message that reports changed results.
- `heading` (string, required): Localized heading that identifies the empty view. Blank text omits the heading.
- `heading-level` (number, default 3, minimum 2, maximum 6): Native heading level for the surrounding document outline. Only integers from 2 through 6 are valid; unsupported values use level 3.
- `icon-name` (string | undefined): Optional decorative Lucide glyph. Register it with a per-icon import before mounting. A supplied illustration takes precedence.
- `size` ("md" | "sm", default 'md'): Use small inside a table or narrow panel. Unrecognized sizes use the medium layout.
- `tone` ("danger" | "info" | "neutral" | "primary" | "primary-light" | "success" | "warning", default 'neutral'): FeatureIcon tone. Unrecognized tones use the neutral tile.

Slots:
- (default): Localized supporting text with a reason or recovery advice.
- `actions`: Optional controls for the next step, with at most one primary action. In a guarded surface, bind actions to these controls.
- `media`: Optional decorative illustration in place of the icon. Use an image with empty alt text or a decorative SVG. Keep this slot free of controls.

Parts:
- `actions`: Wrapping row of consumer-supplied controls.
- `container`: Centered layout for the illustration, message and actions.
- `description`: Wrapper for the default slot.
- `heading`: Native heading at the selected document level.
- `media`: Decorative illustration or FeatureIcon tile.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-empty-state-backdrop-filter`: Complete filter applied behind the empty view.
- `--ki-empty-state-bg`: Background behind the empty view.
- `--ki-empty-state-bg-image`: Optional image above the background color.
- `--ki-empty-state-description-bg`: Background layer behind the supporting copy.
- `--ki-empty-state-description-fg`: Supporting text ink, strengthened in contrast-more mode.
- `--ki-empty-state-description-line-height`: Line height of the supporting copy.
- `--ki-empty-state-description-size`: Font size of the supporting copy.
- `--ki-empty-state-fg`: Foreground ink for the heading.
- `--ki-empty-state-gap`: Gap between the decorative media, message and action row.
- `--ki-empty-state-gap-sm`: Gap between regions in a compact empty view.
- `--ki-empty-state-heading-font-family`: Typeface for the native heading.
- `--ki-empty-state-heading-line-height`: Heading line height in a regular empty view.
- `--ki-empty-state-heading-line-height-sm`: Heading line height in a compact empty view.
- `--ki-empty-state-heading-size`: Heading font size in a regular empty view.
- `--ki-empty-state-heading-size-sm`: Heading font size in a compact empty view.
- `--ki-empty-state-heading-weight`: Weight of the heading.
- `--ki-empty-state-max-width`: Maximum inline size of the centered content.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-danger-bg`: Background of the danger decorative tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-danger-fg`: Glyph ink on the danger decorative tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-info-bg`: Background of the info decorative tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-info-fg`: Glyph ink on the info decorative tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-neutral-bg`: Background of the neutral decorative tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-neutral-fg`: Glyph ink on the neutral decorative tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-primary-bg`: Background of the primary decorative tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-primary-fg`: Glyph ink on the primary decorative tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-primary-light-bg`: Background of the primary-light decorative tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-primary-light-fg`: Glyph ink on the primary-light decorative tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-radius`: Corner radius of the regular fallback tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-radius-sm`: Corner radius of the compact fallback tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-size`: Regular FeatureIcon fallback tile size.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-size-sm`: Compact FeatureIcon fallback tile size.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-success-bg`: Background of the success decorative tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-success-fg`: Glyph ink on the success decorative tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-warning-bg`: Background of the warning decorative tile.
- `--ki-empty-state-tile-warning-fg`: Glyph ink on the warning decorative tile.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-fab

The primary action of a screen, as an icon or an extended control with a visible label.

When to use: give a mobile screen one primary action, such as composing a draft or creating a project. Supply a descriptive label and a registered icon or decorative icon slot. Reserve page clearance for fixed placement, and leave the action binding unset for native link navigation.
When NOT to use: for secondary or destructive actions, for multiple actions on the same screen, or on a desktop screen that already has a visible primary ki-button.

Examples:

# Using ki-fab

Use one FAB for the primary action of a screen. Give it a localized `label`
in every layout. Import each Lucide glyph before mounting a FAB that names it.
Use the native `click` event to call your application's action handler.

```js
import '@kimen/elements/icons/pencil';
import { defineCustomElement } from '@kimen/elements/ki-fab';

defineCustomElement();

document.querySelector('#compose')?.addEventListener('click', openComposer);
```

```html
<ki-fab id="compose" label="Compose" icon-name="pencil"></ki-fab>
```

Use `href` when activation takes the user to a destination. To supply a custom
glyph, use the `icon` slot with decorative, noninteractive content.

```html
<ki-fab label="New project" href="/projects/new" variant="primary" extended>
  <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">
    <path d="M5 12h14M12 5v14"></path>
  </svg>
</ki-fab>
```

Place a fixed FAB after the main content so its tab stop follows the page's
controls. Reserve bottom space so the last item can scroll above it. Set
`--ki-fab-mobile-nav-block-size` to the height of the fixed navigation when
present, excluding the safe area.

```html
<main class="compose-page">
  <!-- Page content -->
</main>
<ki-fab label="Compose" icon-name="pencil" position="fixed" extended collapse-on-scroll></ki-fab>
```

```css
:root {
  --ki-fab-mobile-nav-block-size: var(--app-mobile-nav-height, 0px);
  --compose-clearance: calc(
    var(--ki-fab-size) + 2 * var(--ki-fab-offset) +
      var(--ki-fab-mobile-nav-block-size) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)
  );
  scroll-padding-block-end: var(--compose-clearance);
}

.compose-page {
  padding-block-end: var(--compose-clearance);
}
```

The clearance above uses the default `md` size. Adjust it for a larger FAB
and use the actual expanded height if the label wraps. The label hides as the
user scrolls down the document and reappears on upward scroll. The native
control retains its accessible name and focus.

Attributes:
- `collapse-on-scroll` (boolean, default false): Compact an extended FAB on viewport scroll down and restore on scroll up.
- `extended` (boolean, default false): Show the action label next to its icon.
- `href` (string | undefined, URL): A nonempty destination renders an anchor. Relative URLs and fragments retain native resolution.
- `icon-name` (string | undefined): Registered Lucide name. Import the icon module before rendering. The icon slot takes precedence.
- `label` (string, required): Accessible name of the action. Also the visible text in the extended state.
- `position` ("fixed" | "static", default 'static'): Fixed sits at the viewport's block-end inline-end corner. Reserve page clearance there.
- `size` ("lg" | "md" | "xl", default 'md'): Square footprint when icon-only, and minimum size when extended.
- `variant` ("primary" | "secondary" | "surface", default 'secondary'): Surface and ink: strong primary, tinted secondary or raised surface.

Slots:
- `icon`: Decorative, noninteractive icon replacing the named glyph.

Parts:
- `control`: The native button or link, including its surface and focus ring.
- `icon`: Wrapper for the decorative named or slotted glyph.
- `label`: Visible label of an extended FAB.

Events:
- `click` (Event): Native activation click. The page or guarded renderer handles the declared action.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-fab-backdrop-filter`: Complete optional filter behind the FAB.
- `--ki-fab-bg`: Tinted secondary FAB fill.
- `--ki-fab-bg-image`: Optional layer painted over the FAB fill.
- `--ki-fab-collapse-duration`: Duration of the extended FAB footprint change.
- `--ki-fab-collapse-easing`: Easing of the extended FAB footprint change.
- `--ki-fab-fg`: Ink on the tinted secondary FAB.
- `--ki-fab-font-family`: Typeface for FAB labels.
- `--ki-fab-font-size`: Text size for extended FAB labels.
- `--ki-fab-font-weight`: Text weight for extended FAB labels.
- `--ki-fab-forced-colors-border-width`: Boundary width for the FAB in forced colors.
- `--ki-fab-gap`: Space between icon and label in an extended FAB.
- `--ki-fab-hover-shadow`: FAB elevation for a pointer that can hover.
- `--ki-fab-icon-size`: Glyph size of the default FAB.
- `--ki-fab-lg-icon-size`: Glyph size of the medium FAB.
- `--ki-fab-lg-radius`: Corner radius of the medium FAB.
- `--ki-fab-lg-size`: Minimum footprint of the medium FAB.
- `--ki-fab-line-height`: Line height for extended FAB labels.
- `--ki-fab-mobile-nav-block-size`: Height to reserve for mobile navigation, excluding the safe-area inset.
- `--ki-fab-offset`: Fixed FAB gap to the viewport edge or mobile navigation.
- `--ki-fab-padding-inline-end`: Inline end padding of an extended FAB.
- `--ki-fab-padding-inline-start`: Inline start padding of an extended FAB.
- `--ki-fab-primary-bg`: Strong primary FAB fill.
- `--ki-fab-primary-fg`: Ink on the strong primary FAB.
- `--ki-fab-radius`: Corner radius of the default FAB size.
- `--ki-fab-shadow`: Resting FAB elevation.
- `--ki-fab-size`: Minimum FAB footprint in the default size.
- `--ki-fab-surface-bg`: Raised surface FAB fill.
- `--ki-fab-surface-fg`: Ink on the raised surface FAB.
- `--ki-fab-xl-icon-size`: Glyph size of the large FAB.
- `--ki-fab-xl-radius`: Corner radius of the large FAB.
- `--ki-fab-xl-size`: Minimum footprint of the large FAB.
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.

### ki-fab-menu

An icon FAB that opens two to six related actions above its trigger.

When to use: group related creation or screen actions behind one floating button.
When NOT to use: for a single primary action, long lists, or site navigation.

Examples:

# Floating action menu examples

Register optional Lucide glyphs, then register the menu and its item together.

```ts
import '@kimen/elements/icons/calendar';
import '@kimen/elements/icons/pencil';
import { defineCustomElement as defineItem } from '@kimen/elements/ki-fab-menu-item';
import { defineCustomElement as defineMenu } from '@kimen/elements/ki-fab-menu';

defineItem();
defineMenu();
```

```html
<ki-fab-menu label="Create" icon-name="plus" position="fixed">
  <ki-fab-menu-item icon-name="pencil" value="message">New message</ki-fab-menu-item>
  <ki-fab-menu-item icon-name="calendar" href="/events/new">New event</ki-fab-menu-item>
</ki-fab-menu>
```

Listen to `ki-select` on the menu to handle commands. Use the stable `value`
in the event detail. Leave link navigation to the native anchor. In a catalog
spec, bind separate action IDs to command items and supply a stable `value`
for each item. Keep link items unbound.

Use two to six direct items. Fixed placement shares the FAB's safe-area
and navigation clearance tokens. In static placement, leave space above
the trigger for the stack.

Attributes:
- `close-label` (string, default 'Close menu'): Localized accessible name of the trigger when it becomes the close control.
- `icon-name` (string, default 'plus'): Registered Lucide glyph for the closed trigger. The plus glyph ships with the component.
- `label` (string, required): Accessible name of the closed trigger and of the menu.
- `open` (boolean, default false): Whether the action stack is open. Reflected when the user opens or dismisses it.
- `position` ("fixed" | "static", default 'static'): Static anchors to the host. Fixed anchors to the viewport's block-end inline-end corner.
- `scrim` (boolean, default true): Dim the viewport and dismiss on a scrim click. Use the boolean property or scrim="false" to opt out.
- `variant` ("primary" | "secondary" | "surface", default 'secondary'): Closed FAB surface. The open trigger always uses primary.

Slots:
- (default): Two to six direct ki-fab-menu-item children, in top-to-bottom order.

Parts:
- `menu`: The named action list above the trigger.
- `scrim`: The optional pointer-dismissible overlay behind the menu.
- `trigger`: The native floating button that opens and closes the menu.

Events:
- `ki-close` (CustomEvent<void>): Emitted when the action stack closes.
- `ki-open` (CustomEvent<void>): Emitted when the action stack opens.
- `ki-select` (CustomEvent<KiFabMenuSelectDetail>): Emits the selected item's value or its trimmed label. Native links retain their destination.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-fab-backdrop-filter`: Complete optional filter behind the FAB.
- `--ki-fab-bg`: Tinted secondary FAB fill.
- `--ki-fab-bg-image`: Optional layer painted over the FAB fill.
- `--ki-fab-fg`: Ink on the tinted secondary FAB.
- `--ki-fab-font-family`: Typeface for FAB labels.
- `--ki-fab-forced-colors-border-width`: Boundary width for the FAB in forced colors.
- `--ki-fab-hover-shadow`: FAB elevation for a pointer that can hover.
- `--ki-fab-icon-size`: Glyph size of the default FAB.
- `--ki-fab-menu-gap`: Gap between two stacked actions.
- `--ki-fab-menu-scrim-backdrop-filter`: Complete optional filter behind the scrim.
- `--ki-fab-menu-scrim-bg`: Dimming fill behind the open menu and its trigger.
- `--ki-fab-menu-scrim-bg-image`: Optional image painted above the scrim fill.
- `--ki-fab-menu-trigger-bg`: Fill of the closed trigger in the default secondary variant: the secondary FAB's tonal fill, or in onmars v2 the primary FAB ink, so the accent stays on selection, links and focus.
- `--ki-fab-menu-trigger-fg`: Glyph ink on the closed secondary trigger.
- `--ki-fab-menu-trigger-gap`: Gap between the last action and the FAB.
- `--ki-fab-mobile-nav-block-size`: Height to reserve for mobile navigation, excluding the safe-area inset.
- `--ki-fab-offset`: Fixed FAB gap to the viewport edge or mobile navigation.
- `--ki-fab-primary-bg`: Strong primary FAB fill.
- `--ki-fab-primary-fg`: Ink on the strong primary FAB.
- `--ki-fab-radius`: Corner radius of the default FAB size.
- `--ki-fab-shadow`: Resting FAB elevation.
- `--ki-fab-size`: Minimum FAB footprint in the default size.
- `--ki-fab-surface-bg`: Raised surface FAB fill.
- `--ki-fab-surface-fg`: Ink on the raised surface FAB.
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.

### ki-fab-menu-item

A labeled command or native link within a floating action menu.

When to use: as a direct child of ki-fab-menu, with a short, visible action label.
When NOT to use: for a standalone action, a form control, or a container of interactive content.

Examples:

# Floating action menu item examples

Place commands and links directly inside a menu and supply visible labels.

```html
<ki-fab-menu label="Create">
  <ki-fab-menu-item value="message">New message</ki-fab-menu-item>
  <ki-fab-menu-item href="/events/new">New event</ki-fab-menu-item>
</ki-fab-menu>
```

The command reports `message` through the parent menu's `ki-select` event.
The link reports `New event` and follows its native destination.

Attributes:
- `href` (string | undefined, URL): A nonempty destination renders a native link and preserves relative URL resolution.
- `icon-name` (string | undefined): Registered Lucide glyph. Import the desired icon before rendering.
- `value` (string | undefined): Stable selection identifier. When omitted, the menu reports the trimmed visible label.

Slots:
- (default): The visible action label.

Parts:
- `control`: The native action button or link.
- `icon`: The decorative glyph next to the label.

Events:
- `ki-select` (CustomEvent<KiFabMenuSelectDetail>): Local command selection for a direct action binding. Links use native navigation.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-fab-forced-colors-border-width`: Boundary width for the FAB in forced colors.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-backdrop-filter`: Complete optional filter behind the action.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-bg`: Surface of a floating action: a tonal fill, or in onmars v2 the raised surface with a hairline, so the accent stays on selection.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-bg-image`: Optional image painted above the action fill.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-border-color`: Color of the action edge, drawn at border-width.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-border-width`: Width of the action edge. A tonal action draws none; onmars v2 edges its surface actions with a hairline.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-content-gap`: Space between the action glyph and label.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-fg`: Label and icon ink on the action surface.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-font-family`: Typeface for action labels.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-font-size`: Text size for action labels.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-font-weight`: Text weight of an action label.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-height`: Minimum block size and inline target of an action.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-hover-shadow`: Elevation of a hovered action.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-icon-size`: Size of the glyph preceding an action label.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-line-height`: Line height of an action label.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-padding-block`: Block padding for a wrapping action label.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-padding-end`: Inline-end padding of an action.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-padding-start`: Inline-start padding of an action.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-radius`: Pill radius of an action.
- `--ki-fab-menu-item-shadow`: Elevation of a resting action.
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.

### ki-feature-icon

A decorative glyph centered on a tinted tile.

When to use: Place a decorative icon beside the visible heading of a feature,
empty state or settings section. The heading carries the meaning.
When NOT to use: For an action (use ki-icon-button), a status (use ki-badge),
or the sole label of a section.

Examples:

# Using ki-feature-icon

Load the token stylesheet, register each custom element, and import the
Lucide glyph you use. Place one glyph with its default inherited size
in the slot, next to the heading that names the section.

```js
import '@kimen/tokens/css';
import '@kimen/elements/icons/shield-check';
import { defineCustomElement as defineFeatureIcon } from '@kimen/elements/ki-feature-icon';
import { defineCustomElement as defineIcon } from '@kimen/elements/ki-icon';

defineFeatureIcon();
defineIcon();
```

```html
<div style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:var(--ki-space-md)">
  <ki-feature-icon tone="primary-light" size="md">
    <ki-icon name="shield-check"></ki-icon>
  </ki-feature-icon>
  <h2>Security settings</h2>
</div>
```

Choose a circle with `shape="circle"`. For an inline SVG, use `currentColor`
for the glyph's stroke or fill. Keep controls and meaningful labels outside
the tile so they can receive focus and be announced.

A guarded catalog surface supplies the glyph as a `ki-icon` node in the
default slot. The host imports the glyph before rendering the surface.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "root": {
    "component": "div",
    "props": { "direction": "row", "align": "center", "gap": "md" },
    "slots": {
      "": [
        {
          "component": "ki-feature-icon",
          "props": { "tone": "primary-light" },
          "slots": {
            "": [{ "component": "ki-icon", "props": { "name": "shield-check" } }]
          }
        },
        { "component": "h2", "slots": { "": ["Security settings"] } }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Attributes:
- `shape` ("circle" | "square", default 'square'): Rounded square or circle. Unknown values use square.
- `size` ("lg" | "md" | "sm" | "xl" | "xs", default 'md'): Tile size. At a 16px root, the steps are 24, 32, 40, 48 and 64px. Unknown values use md.
- `tone` ("danger" | "info" | "neutral" | "primary" | "primary-light" | "success" | "warning", default 'neutral'): Colour pair for the tile and its glyph. Unknown values use neutral.

Slots:
- (default): One Lucide glyph. Supply an inline SVG using currentColor or a ki-icon with inherited size. Guarded surfaces use a registered ki-icon.

Parts:
- `tile`: The painted tile that centers the glyph.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-feature-icon-backdrop-filter`: Complete filter applied behind the feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-bg`: Background color of a neutral feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-bg-image`: Optional background image painted over the feature icon tile color.
- `--ki-feature-icon-circle-radius`: Corner radius of a circular feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-danger-bg`: Background color of a danger feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-danger-fg`: Glyph color of a danger feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-fg`: Glyph color of a neutral feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-info-bg`: Background color of an info feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-info-fg`: Glyph color of an info feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-lg-radius`: Corner radius of a large square feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-lg-size`: Edge length of a large feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-primary-bg`: Background color of a primary feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-primary-fg`: Glyph color of a primary feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-primary-light-bg`: Background color of a primary-light feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-primary-light-fg`: Glyph color of a primary-light feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-radius`: Default corner radius of a square feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-size`: Default edge length of a feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-sm-radius`: Corner radius of a small square feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-sm-size`: Edge length of a small feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-success-bg`: Background color of a success feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-success-fg`: Glyph color of a success feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-warning-bg`: Background color of a warning feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-warning-fg`: Glyph color of a warning feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-xl-radius`: Corner radius of an extra-large square feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-xl-size`: Edge length of an extra-large feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-xs-radius`: Corner radius of an extra-small square feature icon tile.
- `--ki-feature-icon-xs-size`: Edge length of an extra-small feature icon tile.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-file-upload

A form-associated picker and drop zone with local selection validation and a list of file upload outcomes.

When to use: collect local attachments, media or imports, and optionally show
application-managed upload progress and results.
When NOT to use: transfer files without an application handler, collect a URL,
or use client-side type and size checks as upload authorization.

Examples:

# File upload examples

## Submit attachments with a form

```html
<form action="/attachments" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
  <ki-file-upload
    label="Incident attachments"
    name="attachments"
    accept=".csv,.pdf"
    max-size="10MB"
    max-files="3"
    multiple
    required
  >
    <span slot="help">Choose up to three CSV or PDF files, up to 10 MB each.</span>
  </ki-file-upload>
  <button type="submit">Send attachments</button>
  <button type="reset">Clear attachments</button>
</form>
```

Register the element once with the direct package entry point.

```js
import { defineCustomElement } from '@kimen/elements/ki-file-upload';

defineCustomElement();
```

The form submits each accepted original `File` under `attachments`. A reset
clears the list. Use `error-text` for a form error, such as one returned by
your application, and clear it when the error is resolved.

## Report progress from an application-managed transfer

Use a standalone picker when your application sends files as soon as people
choose them.

```html
<ki-file-upload id="transfer-picker" label="Import CSV files" accept=".csv" multiple>
</ki-file-upload>
```

Here `sendFile` is your application's transfer function. It accepts a
`File`, an abort signal and a progress callback receiving a percentage.

```js
const upload = document.querySelector('#transfer-picker');
const transfers = new Map();

function update(file, changes) {
  upload.files = upload.files.map((entry) =>
    entry.file === file ? { ...entry, ...changes } : entry,
  );
}

async function startUpload(file) {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  transfers.set(file, controller);
  update(file, { status: 'uploading', progress: 0 });

  try {
    await sendFile(file, {
      signal: controller.signal,
      onProgress: (progress) => update(file, { progress }),
    });
    update(file, { status: 'done' });
  } catch {
    const error = controller.signal.aborted ? 'Upload canceled.' : 'Upload failed.';
    update(file, { status: 'error', error });
  } finally {
    transfers.delete(file);
  }
}

upload.addEventListener('ki-files-add', ({ detail }) => {
  for (const { file } of detail.files) {
    void startUpload(file);
  }
});

upload.addEventListener('ki-file-cancel', ({ detail }) => {
  transfers.get(detail.file.file)?.abort();
});
```

Use `ki-file-remove` to update application state when a row is removed.
For previously uploaded attachments, set `files` to rows with metadata and
`status: 'done'`. Only rows carrying an original `File` contribute form
entries.

Attributes:
- `accept` (string | undefined): Comma-separated extensions, MIME types and MIME wildcards allowed in new selections.
- `browse-label` (string, default 'Browse files'): Visible text of the native file picker button.
- `cancel-label` (string, default 'Cancel upload of {file}'): Accessible name template for cancellation. Use {file} for the displayed filename.
- `count-error` (string, default 'Too many files.'): Rejection text for a file beyond selection capacity.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Disables the picker and file actions and excludes the field from submission.
- `done-label` (string, default 'Uploaded'): Status text for a completed upload.
- `drop-label` (string, default 'Drop files here or'): Drop instruction shown just before the Browse button.
- `error-text` (string | undefined): Application validation error. Clear it to allow form submission again.
- `failed-label` (string, default 'Upload failed.'): Fallback status text for a failed upload without a supplied error.
- `help-text` (string | undefined): Guidance for file formats, limits or the purpose of this field.
- `label` (string, default 'Upload files'): Visible label and accessible name of the upload group.
- `list-label` (string, default 'Files'): Accessible name of the list of files.
- `max-files` (number | undefined): Maximum accepted local files as a nonnegative integer. Single-file mode also caps this at one.
- `max-size` (string | undefined): Maximum size per selected file in bytes or decimal B, KB, MB or GB, such as "10MB".
- `multiple` (boolean, default false): Allows a selection of more than one file.
- `name` (string | undefined): Form-data key repeated for each accepted original file.
- `queued-label` (string, default 'Queued'): Status text for an accepted file waiting to upload.
- `remove-label` (string, default 'Remove {file}'): Accessible name template for removal. Use {file} for the displayed filename.
- `required` (boolean, default false): Requires at least one original accepted file to submit the form.
- `required-label` (string, default 'Required'): Visible annotation for a required file field.
- `required-message` (string, default 'Select a file.'): Validation message when the form requires a file and none is selected.
- `size-error` (string, default 'This file is too large.'): Rejection text for a file larger than max-size.
- `type-error` (string, default 'This file type is not allowed.'): Rejection text for a file that does not match accept.
- `uploading-label` (string, default 'Uploading {file}'): Progress indicator name template. Use {file} for the displayed filename.

Slots:
- `help`: Plain-language guidance for the picker, in place of help-text.

Parts:
- `action`: Native button for removal or cancellation.
- `browse`: Native button that opens the file picker.
- `drop-zone`: Surface that receives files dragged from the operating system.
- `error`: Field-level form validation error.
- `file-meta`: Size, outcome or error text for the file.
- `file-name`: Name displayed for the file.
- `help`: Guidance associated with the field.
- `input`: Hidden native file picker.
- `label`: Field label and optional required annotation.
- `list`: List of selected files and rejections.
- `progress`: Progress indicator for an uploading file.
- `row`: A file row, with data-status matching its lifecycle state.

Events:
- `ki-file-cancel` (CustomEvent<KiFileActionDetail>): Requests that the application cancel the identified upload.
- `ki-file-remove` (CustomEvent<KiFileActionDetail>): Reports a row removed by the user, after updating the file list.
- `ki-files-add` (CustomEvent<KiFilesAddDetail>): Reports the accepted rows in one picker or drop batch, each with its original File.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-corner-inline`: Small radius for an outline around inline content.
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-file-upload-active-bg`: Drop zone background while files are dragged over it.
- `--ki-file-upload-active-border`: Drop zone boundary while files are dragged over it.
- `--ki-file-upload-active-fg`: Main drop zone text while files are dragged over it.
- `--ki-file-upload-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter applied behind the drop zone.
- `--ki-file-upload-bg`: Drop zone background at rest.
- `--ki-file-upload-bg-image`: Optional image over the drop zone background.
- `--ki-file-upload-border`: Dashed boundary of the drop zone.
- `--ki-file-upload-border-width`: Outline stroke width for the drop zone and file rows.
- `--ki-file-upload-error-bg`: Background of a file row with an error.
- `--ki-file-upload-error-border`: Boundary of a file row with an error.
- `--ki-file-upload-error-fg`: Text of a file error or field error.
- `--ki-file-upload-fg`: Main drop zone text at rest.
- `--ki-file-upload-radius`: Drop zone corner radius.
- `--ki-file-upload-row-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter applied behind a file row.
- `--ki-file-upload-row-bg`: Background of a file row and the field label.
- `--ki-file-upload-row-bg-image`: Optional image over the file row background.
- `--ki-file-upload-row-border`: Boundary of a file row without an error.
- `--ki-file-upload-row-fg`: File names, row action icons and the field label.
- `--ki-file-upload-row-radius`: File row corner radius.
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-3xl`: The 3xl spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-md`: The md spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-xs`: The xs spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-text-primary-high-em`: semantic color for text primary high em.
- `--ki-text-supporting`: Supporting text of an enabled control: field labels, placeholders, list secondary lines, quiet button labels and unselected tabs. A role, distinct from the med-em emphasis step it resolves to, so a mode can strengthen enabled supporting text without touching the disabled ink that also draws from med-em (directly, or through text.muted).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography line height body 1.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-underline-offset`: Gap between text and its underline.
- `--ki-typography-underline-thickness`: Stroke width of a resting text underline.
- `--ki-typography-underline-thickness-hover`: Stroke width of an emphasized underline on hover.
- `--ki-typography-visually-hidden-size`: Nonzero edge for clipped text available to assistive technology.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-medium`: semantic font weight for typography weight body medium.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-normal`: semantic font weight for typography weight body normal.

### ki-format-date

Displays an ISO date or timestamp in the reader's language.

When to use: For raw date and timestamp values in tables, records and prose.
When NOT to use: For an editable date or an elapsed time that should change as the clock advances.

Examples:

# Format a date

Use a calendar date when the day is the value, and send an offset or `Z` when
the value is a timestamp. Set `lang` on the surrounding document or section.

```html
<section lang="es-ES">
  <ki-format-date date="2026-11-19" date-style="long"></ki-format-date>
  <ki-format-date
    date="2026-11-19T23:41:00Z"
    date-style="long"
    time-style="short"
    time-zone="Europe/Madrid"
  ></ki-format-date>
</section>
```

Attributes:
- `date` (string | undefined): ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO date-time. A timestamp without an offset uses local time.
- `date-style` ("full" | "long" | "medium" | "short" | undefined): Date detail. Defaults to medium when neither date style nor time style is supplied.
- `lang` (string | undefined): Language tag for the formatted date. Inherits the nearest HTML lang declaration when omitted.
- `time-style` ("full" | "long" | "medium" | "short" | undefined): Time detail. Omit to show the date alone.
- `time-zone` (string | undefined): IANA time zone for a timestamp. A calendar date keeps its day in every zone.

Slots: none

Parts: none

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-format-date-font-family`: Default body font family for ki-format-date on a bare page.

### ki-format-number

Displays a raw number using local number conventions and tabular figures.

When to use: For numeric data, currency amounts, ratios and measurements in content.
When NOT to use: For numeric input or values that already include localized formatting.

Examples:

# Format a number

Pass raw numbers and let the nearest `lang` declaration select the separators,
spacing and symbols. A percent takes a ratio.

```html
<section lang="es-ES">
  <ki-format-number value="1284.5"></ki-format-number>
  <ki-format-number value="49" currency="EUR"></ki-format-number>
  <ki-format-number value="0.496" format-style="percent" maximum-fraction-digits="1"></ki-format-number>
  <ki-format-number value="23" format-style="unit" unit="celsius"></ki-format-number>
  <ki-format-number value="59320" notation="compact"></ki-format-number>
</section>
```

Attributes:
- `currency` (string | undefined): ISO 4217 currency code, such as EUR. Selects currency output when format-style is omitted.
- `format-style` ("decimal" | "percent" | "unit" | undefined): Decimal, percent or unit output. Without this option, currency selects currency output and other values use decimal.
- `maximum-fraction-digits` (number | undefined, minimum 0): Maximum number of fraction digits.
- `minimum-fraction-digits` (number | undefined, minimum 0): Minimum number of fraction digits.
- `notation` ("compact" | undefined): Use compact notation for abbreviated large numbers. Omit for standard notation.
- `unit` (string | undefined): Intl unit identifier, such as celsius or kilometer. Use with format-style="unit".
- `value` (number | undefined): Raw finite number. A percent uses a ratio, so 0.49 displays as 49%.

Slots: none

Parts: none

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-format-number-font-family`: Default body font family for ki-format-number on a bare page.

### ki-grid

A passive responsive grid for content items.

When to use: lay out items on responsive tracks with consistent token spacing.
When NOT to use: for page shells, painted grouping (use ki-card), or a data grid.

Examples:

# Grid examples

An automatic grid fills its available space with tracks at least as wide as
`min-column` where room allows. Here the summary takes two tracks when
possible.

```html
<ki-grid min-column="8rem" gap="xl">
  <ki-card data-span="2">Overview</ki-card>
  <ki-card>Orders</ki-card>
  <ki-card>Inventory</ki-card>
  <ki-card>Customers</ki-card>
</ki-grid>
```

For a fixed count, set `columns`. The grid switches to one column when its
own available inline size drops below 30rem.

```html
<ki-grid columns="3" gap="sm">
  <ki-card>Orders</ki-card>
  <ki-card>Inventory</ki-card>
  <ki-card>Customers</ki-card>
</ki-grid>
```

Attributes:
- `columns` (number | undefined, minimum 1): Positive whole track count. Below 30rem of available inline size the fixed grid uses one column. Omit columns for automatic tracks.
- `gap` ("10xl" | "11xl" | "12xl" | "13xl" | "14xl" | "15xl" | "16xl" | "17xl" | "18xl" | "19xl" | "20xl" | "21xl" | "22xl" | "23xl" | "24xl" | "25xl" | "26xl" | "2xl" | "3xl" | "4xl" | "5xl" | "6xl" | "7xl" | "8xl" | "9xl" | "lg" | "md" | "sm" | "xl" | "xs" | "xxs" | "zero", default 'xl'): Kimen spacing step, xl by default. Unsupported values keep the default gap.
- `min-column` (string, default '15rem'): Minimum automatic track size as a CSS length. Defaults to 15rem and is ignored with fixed columns.

Slots:
- (default): The content in reading order. A direct child with data-span="2" spans two tracks when they fit.

Parts:
- `grid`: The grid layout containing the slotted content.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-grid-gap`: Default gap between grid tracks.
- `--ki-grid-min`: Default minimum size of an automatic grid track.
- `--ki-layout-grid-fixed-breakpoint`: Minimum available inline size for a fixed grid to use multiple tracks.
- `--ki-layout-grid-min`: Default minimum inline size of an automatic grid track.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-xl`: The xl spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-icon

A static Lucide glyph selected by name from the application's per-icon imports.

When to use: show a named glyph next to text, or give a standalone meaningful
glyph an accessible label. Import `@kimen/elements/icons/<name>` before
mounting the component or rendering a guarded surface.
When NOT to use: make an icon interactive, accept arbitrary SVG or URLs, or
replace the accessible name of a control. Use the control's own label.

Examples:

# ki-icon examples

Import the exact Lucide names used by your markup before you mount it.

```js
import '@kimen/elements/icons/circle-check';
import '@kimen/elements/icons/triangle-alert';
import { defineCustomElement } from '@kimen/elements/ki-icon';

defineCustomElement();
```

A confirmation has adjacent text, so the glyph is decorative.

```html
<span style="color: var(--ki-text-success-high-em)">
  <ki-icon name="circle-check"></ki-icon> Confirmed
</span>
```

A standalone meaningful glyph takes its accessible name from the label.

```html
<ki-icon name="triangle-alert" size="lg" label="Warning"></ki-icon>
```

For a guarded catalog surface, import the glyph in the host and reference it
by name. The icon has no slots or actions.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "root": {
    "component": "ki-icon",
    "props": { "name": "triangle-alert", "size": "lg", "label": "Warning" }
  }
}
```

Attributes:
- `label` (string | undefined): Accessible name for a meaningful glyph. Omit it when nearby text already conveys the meaning.
- `name` (string, required): Lucide name made available by a per-icon import. An unavailable name draws no glyph.
- `size` ("inherit" | "lg" | "md" | "sm", default 'inherit'): Glyph size. Inherit follows the surrounding text at 1em.

Slots: none

Parts: none

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-icon-size-lg`: Large ki-icon with the surrounding text ink.
- `--ki-icon-size-md`: Medium ki-icon with the surrounding text ink.
- `--ki-icon-size-sm`: Small ki-icon with the surrounding text ink.
- `--ki-icon-stroke-width`: Lucide stroke width in viewBox units, scaled with the glyph.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-icon-button

A token-styled, icon-only action button with native button semantics and a mandatory accessible name.

When to use: a compact, widely understood action where space precludes a
visible label: toolbars, card and dialog corners (close), media transport,
data-row actions. Always supply `label`; usually pair with ki-tooltip for
sighted discoverability. Enable `toggle` for persistent actions such as
Bookmark. While the action it started is in progress, set `loading`.
When NOT to use: whenever a visible label fits (use ki-button),
navigation (use a link), or form
submit/reset (ki-icon-button is not form-associated; use ki-button, whose
visible label communicates the consequence).

Examples:

The default slot holds exactly one decorative icon; the mandatory `label` is the accessible name — the slot never contributes to it:

```html
<ki-icon-button label="Close">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 6l12 12M18 6L6 18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" /></svg>
</ki-icon-button>
```

Visual hierarchy comes from `variant` (default `secondary`). In the original momentary variants, `tone` (default `neutral`) carries semantic intent such as success or danger.

```html
<ki-icon-button variant="primary" label="Play">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M8 5v14l11-7z" fill="currentColor" /></svg>
</ki-icon-button>
<ki-icon-button variant="ghost" tone="danger" label="Delete row">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 7h12M9 7V5h6v2m-8 0l1 12h8l1-12" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" /></svg>
</ki-icon-button>
```

Add `toggle` for an action such as Bookmark that stays pressed until the next activation. `variant="outline"` uses an outline at rest and a fill when selected. Give the pressed version a decorative icon in the `selected` slot.

```html
<ki-icon-button toggle variant="outline" label="Bookmark">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">
    <path d="M6 3h12v18l-6-4-6 4z" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" />
  </svg>
  <svg slot="selected" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true">
    <path d="M6 3h12v18l-6-4-6 4z" />
  </svg>
</ki-icon-button>
```

With an empty `selected` slot, the default inline SVG takes a `currentColor` fill while pressed. Let its paths inherit `fill`. Keep `label` the same in both states. Activating the control emits `ki-change` with `{ selected }`. Set the `selected` attribute for the initial state or write the property to update it silently.

Sizes run `xs` (24px, exactly the WCAG 2.2 pointer-target floor) through `xl`, default `md`; each pairs a square box with its own icon size:

```html
<ki-icon-button size="xs" label="Clear">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 6l12 12M18 6L6 18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" /></svg>
</ki-icon-button>
<ki-icon-button size="xl" variant="primary" label="Record">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="6" fill="currentColor" /></svg>
</ki-icon-button>
```

Pair with `ki-tooltip` for sighted discoverability: the tooltip's `label` becomes the accessible description while the icon button's `label` stays the accessible name:

```html
<ki-tooltip label="Closes the dialog">
  <ki-icon-button label="Close">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 6l12 12M18 6L6 18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" /></svg>
  </ki-icon-button>
</ki-tooltip>
```

An icon button in the dialog footer can dismiss it by ID. The dialog must be
in the same document or shadow root as the icon button.

```html
<ki-icon-button slot="footer" label="Close details" commandfor="details" command="close">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 6l12 12M18 6L6 18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" /></svg>
</ki-icon-button>
```

While the action it started is in progress, set `loading` instead of `disabled`: the icon button keeps its size, its focus and its `label`, ignores further activation, draws a spinner in place of the icon and announces `loading-label` (default "Loading") as a polite status message:

```html
<ki-icon-button label="Refresh" loading loading-label="Refreshing">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M4 12a8 8 0 0 1 14-5l2 2M20 12a8 8 0 0 1-14 5l-2-2" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" /></svg>
</ki-icon-button>
```

Attributes:
- `command` ("close" | "request-close" | "show-modal" | undefined): Dialog action to run for `commandfor`. Use `show-modal` to open, `close` for direct dismissal, or `request-close` for guarded dismissal. Choose a command for local dialog control and omit it for other actions.
- `commandfor` (string | undefined): ID of a ki-dialog in the same document or shadow tree as this button. Set it together with `command` to connect a dialog declaratively.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Prevents activation, removes the icon button from keyboard reach, and exposes the unavailable state through the internal native button. Wins over `loading` when both are set. When NOT to use: do not use disabled for pending/loading semantics; use `loading`.
- `expanded` (boolean | undefined): Application-owned disclosure state for a trigger that opens a popup. The native icon button exposes this as `aria-expanded`. Use with `aria-haspopup="menu"` for a menu trigger. Omit for other actions.
- `label` (string, required): Accessible name of the internal focusable button ("Close", "Play"). Required in the catalog. When slotted as a trailing list control, the row text supplies a fallback through the host aria-label. Use ki-button when the action has a visible label.
- `loading` (boolean, default false): Pending state of the action this icon button started (refreshing, sending). While set, every activation is blocked (pointer, Enter and Space), but the icon button stays focusable, in the Tab order and at its size: the icon stays laid out, transparent, and a spinner is drawn in its place. The internal native button is exposed with `aria-disabled="true"` and keeps its `label`, and `loadingLabel` is announced as a polite status message. `disabled` wins over it. The application sets it when the action starts and clears it when the action ends. When to use: while the work a click on this icon button started is running, so a second activation cannot repeat it. When NOT to use: for an icon button the person cannot use yet (use `disabled`), or for the progress of a page or region (use ki-progress).
- `loading-label` (string, default 'Loading'): Text of the polite status message announced while `loading` is set. Override for localization; the default English string is the icon button's only built-in user-visible text. When to use: provide a localized message whenever the document language is not English, or a more specific one ("Refreshing"). When NOT to use: do not repeat `label` here; the person already hears it on focus.
- `pressed` (boolean | undefined): Application-owned toggle state. The native icon button exposes this as `aria-pressed` when `toggle` is off. Omit for a momentary action.
- `selected` (boolean, default false): Current press state in toggle mode. Set this to initialize or synchronize the state programmatically without emitting a change.
- `size` ("lg" | "md" | "sm" | "xl" | "xs", default 'md'): Token-backed square size. Every size keeps at least the 24×24 minimum pointer target (`xs` sits exactly on it); choose the size that matches the density of the surrounding UI. When NOT to use: do not shrink below `xs` through tokens; no theme may go under the WCAG 2.2 pointer-target floor.
- `toggle` (boolean, default false): Enables persistent press state for an action such as Bookmark. The native button exposes `aria-pressed` and each activation switches `selected`. Keep the same accessible label in both states.
- `tone` ("danger" | "neutral" | "success", default 'neutral'): Semantic intent for the action, independent of hierarchy. Use `success` for confirming actions and `danger` for destructive actions. Toggle palettes are specific to the variant. When NOT to use: do not use tone for visual hierarchy; use `variant`.
- `variant` ("ghost" | "outline" | "primary" | "quaternary" | "secondary" | "tertiary", default 'secondary'): Visual hierarchy for the action. Use filled `primary` for the single main action, outlined `secondary` for supporting actions, `quaternary` for neutral icon actions, `ghost` for accent icon actions and `outline` for an unfilled action with a visible boundary. When NOT to use: do not use variant to signal success or danger; use `tone` for intent.

Slots:
- (default): Exactly one decorative icon. The slot is presentational: its content is hidden from assistive technology and never contributes to the accessible name. Supply `label` or use a named trailing list control.
- `counter`: Decorative ki-counter in the block-start inline-end corner. Include its meaning in the button label.
- `selected`: Optional decorative icon shown when the toggle is selected. If omitted, the default icon stays visible and an inline SVG takes a current-colour fill.

Parts:
- `button`: Internal native button.
- `icon`: Icon wrapper around the default slot.
- `spinner`: Loading spinner drawn in place of the icon, in the button's foreground ink, rendered only while `loading` is in effect.

Events:
- `ki-change` (CustomEvent<{ selected: boolean }>): Emitted after toggle activation with the new selected state.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-button-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter for button and icon-button variants; none in onmars v2.
- `--ki-button-border-width`: dimension used by the button component for border width (MarsUI outline stroke: 1px).
- `--ki-button-focus-ring-color`: color used by the button component for focus ring color.
- `--ki-button-focus-ring-offset`: dimension used by the button component for focus ring offset.
- `--ki-button-focus-ring-shadow`: shadow used by the button component for the focus ring glow (MarsUI Focus/primary: 3px spread ring).
- `--ki-button-focus-ring-width`: dimension used by the button component for focus ring width.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-hover-bg`: color used by the button component for ghost danger hover background.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-hover-border`: color used by the button component for ghost danger hover border.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-hover-fg`: color used by the button component for ghost danger hover foreground.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-rest-bg`: color used by the button component for ghost danger rest background.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-rest-border`: color used by the button component for ghost danger rest border.
- `--ki-button-ghost-danger-rest-fg`: color used by the button component for ghost danger rest foreground.
- `--ki-button-ghost-disabled-shadow`: value used by the button component for ghost disabled shadow.
- `--ki-button-ghost-hover-shadow`: value used by the button component for ghost hover shadow.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-disabled-bg`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral disabled background.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-disabled-border`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral disabled border.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-disabled-fg`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral disabled foreground.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-hover-bg`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral hover background.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-hover-border`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral hover border.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-hover-fg`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral hover foreground.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-rest-bg`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral rest background.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-rest-border`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral rest border.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-rest-fg`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral rest foreground.
- `--ki-button-ghost-rest-shadow`: value used by the button component for ghost rest shadow.
- `--ki-button-ghost-success-hover-bg`: color used by the button component for ghost success hover background.
- `--ki-button-ghost-success-hover-border`: color used by the button component for ghost success hover border.
- `--ki-button-ghost-success-hover-fg`: color used by the button component for ghost success hover foreground.
- `--ki-button-ghost-success-rest-bg`: color used by the button component for ghost success rest background.
- `--ki-button-ghost-success-rest-border`: color used by the button component for ghost success rest border.
- `--ki-button-ghost-success-rest-fg`: color used by the button component for ghost success rest foreground.
- `--ki-button-lg-radius`: dimension used by the button component for lg radius (Button master 8003:300 binds Radius/small-component/lg, the scale a radius mode reassigns).
- `--ki-button-md-radius`: dimension used by the button component for md radius (Button master 8003:300 binds Radius/small-component/md, the scale a radius mode reassigns).

### ki-image

Displays one accessible image in a reserved frame, with an optional caption and a fallback if the source is refused or fails to load.

When to use: to show a photo, illustration, or diagram with a predictable
layout. Supply task-relevant alt text, or mark purely decorative media as
decorative. Set an explicit ratio when the layout must stay fixed.
When NOT to use: for a background decoration, a video, or an interactive
control. Use a separate control to open or otherwise act on an image.

Examples:

# Using ki-image

Give an informative image alt text that describes the detail the reader needs.
An explicit ratio reserves the same frame while the image loads and when the
fallback appears. Add supporting context in the caption slot.

```html
<ki-image src="/hills.jpg" alt="Low green hills under a pale sky" ratio="16:9">
  <span slot="caption">View from the ridge</span>
</ki-image>
```

Use `contain` when the whole image must stay visible. The fallback for this
example is named `Image unavailable: Office floor plan` if the source fails.

```html
<ki-image src="/floor-plan.png" alt="Office floor plan" ratio="4:3" fit="contain"></ki-image>
```

Use `decorative` for ornamentation. The image and fallback stay out of the
accessibility tree.

```html
<ki-image src="/divider.svg" decorative radius="none"></ki-image>
```

Attributes:
- `alt` (string | undefined): Describe what the image shows for the task at hand. Required and nonblank for an informative image. Omit it for a decorative image.
- `decorative` (boolean, default false): Hide the media from assistive technology when it conveys no information.
- `fallback-label` (string, default 'Image unavailable'): Localizable fallback label. An informative fallback appends the image's description, when available, to this label.
- `fit` ("contain" | "cover", default 'cover'): Cover fills the frame. Contain preserves the whole image in it.
- `loading` ("eager" | "lazy", default 'lazy'): Native loading hint. Use eager for a critical image above the fold.
- `radius` ("lg" | "md" | "none", default 'lg'): Corner radius of the media frame.
- `ratio` ("16:9" | "1:1" | "3:2" | "4:3" | "auto", default 'auto'): An explicit ratio reserves the same frame before load and on failure. Auto reserves 16:9 first and uses the intrinsic ratio after load.
- `src` (string, required, URL): Relative or HTTP(S) image URL. Refused sources are left unloaded.

Slots:
- `caption`: Optional visible context displayed below the media in a figcaption.

Parts:
- `caption`: The figcaption carrying the slotted caption.
- `fallback`: The unavailable-image indicator inside the frame.
- `figure`: The figure containing the frame and optional caption.
- `frame`: The reserved media box and its shape and backing surface.
- `image`: The native image and its fit within the frame.

Events:
- `ki-error` (CustomEvent<void>): Reports a load failure or rejected URL once per source attempt. Bubbles and crosses shadow boundaries so consumers can observe it on a surface.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-image-caption-fg`: Text colour of the visible caption.
- `--ki-image-caption-font-family`: Typeface of the visible caption.
- `--ki-image-caption-font-size`: Type size of the visible caption.
- `--ki-image-caption-gap`: Space between the image frame and its caption.
- `--ki-image-caption-line-height`: Line height of the visible caption.
- `--ki-image-fallback-backdrop-filter`: Complete filter applied behind the media surface.
- `--ki-image-fallback-bg`: Solid fill behind the image and fallback symbol.
- `--ki-image-fallback-bg-image`: Optional background image over the media fill.
- `--ki-image-fallback-fg`: Foreground of the fallback symbol.
- `--ki-image-fallback-icon-size`: Inline and block size of the unavailable-image symbol.
- `--ki-image-fallback-icon-stroke-width`: Stroke width of the unavailable-image symbol.
- `--ki-image-radius`: Corner radius of the default media frame.
- `--ki-image-radius-md`: Corner radius of the medium media frame.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-indicator

A non-interactive page-position indicator: one dot per position of a bounded sequence, exactly one highlighted as current.

When to use: show the current position within a bounded, sequential set of
peer views whose navigation lives elsewhere: carousel slides, unlabeled
onboarding steps, gallery pages. Wire `count` and `current` (1-based) to
the sequence the consumer renders and give it a `label` (required
authoring: assistive technology reads one graphic named
"<label>, <current> / <count>"). Below two positions an indicator carries
no information.
When NOT to use: section navigation (ki-tabs), task completion or loading
(ki-progress), labeled step flows (a stepper is a separate roadmap item),
interactive pagination (a future feature — the indicator takes no focus
and no input; navigation belongs to the composing carousel's own
controls), or conveying quantity without a current position. Position
changes are never announced by the indicator itself (no live region): the
composing carousel owns announcements.

Examples:

Two integers determine everything — one dot per `count` position with the 1-based `current` highlighted — and `label` names the sequence (the exposed name reads "&lt;label&gt;, &lt;current&gt; / &lt;count&gt;"):

```html
<ki-indicator label="Slide position" count="5" current="2"></ki-indicator>
```

Malformed declarations never break the row: `current` above `count` clamps to the last position, a non-numeric one falls back to the first, and an invalid `count` renders zero dots (an authoring mistake, not an error state):

```html
<ki-indicator label="Slide position" count="5" current="9"></ki-indicator>
<!-- fifth dot current -->
```

Drive it from the composing carousel by updating `current` (1-based); the highlight and exposed text follow immediately, and the indicator never announces changes (no live region) — announcements belong to the carousel:

```html
<ki-indicator id="gallery-position" label="Photo position" count="4" current="1"></ki-indicator>

<script type="module">
  const indicator = document.getElementById('gallery-position');
  indicator.current = 3;
</script>
```

Attributes:
- `count` (number | undefined, minimum 0, maximum 20): Number of positions (non-negative integer): one dot renders per position, in position order. A missing, non-numeric or negative value renders zero dots — an authoring mistake by catalog guidance, never an error state or a rendering failure (FR-002; empty ki-list precedent). At most 20 positions render, and the catalog accepts no more: the indicator serves a short sequence of peer views, 20 dots are the longest row that fits a 320 CSS px viewport (the WCAG reflow width) in both shipped themes, and one dot renders per position, so the bound also caps the work a single node can demand. A larger value renders 20.
- `current` (number | undefined, minimum 1, maximum 20): The current position, 1-based to match the exposed position text ("2 / 5"). Exactly one dot presents the current appearance whenever `count` >= 1: values above `count` clamp to the last position, values below 1 and non-numeric values fall back to the first (FR-003). Updates re-render in place — the highlight and the exposed text follow immediately, re-applying the normalization (FR-004). The catalog accepts 1 to 20, the positions a bounded `count` can have.
- `label` (string, required): Accessible name of the sequence ("Slide position"). The exposed name combines it with the wordless numeric position — "<label>, <current> / <count>" — on a single non-interactive graphic; without a label the name degrades to the bare position text (documented as required authoring, FR-005). The label is never rendered visually and position changes are never announced (no live region, FR-006).

Slots: none

Parts:
- `dot`: Every dot: size, shape and color.
- `dot-current`: Additionally on the current dot: the highlight treatment.
- `indicator`: The row container: layout and the token-driven gap.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-indicator-dot-block-size`: dimension used by the indicator component for the resting dot block size: the 8px circle diameter measured in the State=inactive vector (the 16px frame height is row alignment, carried by the current dot).
- `--ki-indicator-dot-color`: color used by the indicator component for the resting dot fill: Inverse_white/alpha_48 (Black/48 light, White/48 dark) — a declared a11y deviation from the MarsUI binding Inverse_white/alpha_18, which reads 1.53:1 light and 1.64:1 dark against the page; alpha_48 is the first step of the same ramp that clears the 3:1 FR-012 and WCAG 1.4.11 ask. The scheme flip rides the semantic layer.
- `--ki-indicator-dot-current-block-size`: dimension used by the indicator component for the current dot block size: Space/3xl, the exact variable bound as the 16px height of the State=active pill (the full row line; declared family extension, design-extraction §Decisiones).
- `--ki-indicator-dot-current-color`: color used by the indicator component for the current dot treatment: Inverse_white/alpha_48, the same step as the resting dots — the MarsUI State=active ring vector binds the variable of the resting fill, and its alpha_18 reads 1.53-1.64:1 against the page (declared a11y deviation, FR-012). Painted as the pill ring in onmars, where elongation carries the state; as the solid dot in themes that zero the hole.
- `--ki-indicator-dot-current-hole-block-size`: dimension used by the indicator component for the block size of the transparent hole cut from the current pill: the 6px cutout height measured in the State=active vector; the ring width derives by construction as (current block size − hole block size) / 2 and a theme resolves it to zero for a solid dot (declared family extension, design-extraction §Decisiones).
- `--ki-indicator-dot-current-inline-size`: dimension used by the indicator component for the current dot inline size: Space/10xl, the exact variable bound as the 32px width of the State=active pill — the MarsUI elongation lives here, never in an attribute (FR-007).
- `--ki-indicator-dot-current-radius`: dimension used by the indicator component for the current dot shape: Radius/radius_round bound in Figma — the pill is a radius token, never an attribute (002 shape precedent).
- `--ki-indicator-dot-inline-size`: dimension used by the indicator component for the resting dot inline size: Space/md, the exact variable bound as the 8px width of the State=inactive symbol; the painted circle is 8x8 centered in the 16px row line.
- `--ki-indicator-dot-radius`: dimension used by the indicator component for the resting dot shape: Radius/radius_round bound in Figma — the round dot is a radius token, never an attribute (002 shape precedent).
- `--ki-indicator-gap`: dimension used by the indicator component for the space between dots: Space/sm, the exact variable bound as the 6px gap of the composed Nav_indicator row (node 14195:5866, specs/024-ki-indicator/design-extraction.md).
- `--ki-indicator-motion-duration`: duration used by the indicator component for the highlight transfer between dots: the Figma set documents no motion, so onmars resolves the single transition to the fast semantic duration (FR-008; disabled under reduced motion by construction).
- `--ki-indicator-motion-easing`: easing used by the indicator component for the highlight-transfer transition (MarsUI standard curve; previously the UA default ease applied).
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-easing-standard-decelerate`: Utility entrance curve. M3 md.sys.motion.easing.standard-decelerate. onmars: the MarsUI decelerate curve (ki.easing.out).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-input

A token-styled single-line text field with native input semantics. Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`, `setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and `willValidate` synchronously, on the custom-elements build (not on hosts created by the lazy loader).

When to use: collect one line of free text from a person, always with a
visible `label`; choose the `type` and `autocomplete` that match the entry
purpose.
When NOT to use: multiline text, predefined choices, boolean state, numeric
stepper entry, or placeholder-only labeling.

Examples:

A labeled field participating in native form submission (`label` is mandatory; it is the accessible name):

```html
<form>
  <ki-input label="Work email" name="email" type="email" required></ki-input>
  <ki-button variant="primary">Subscribe</ki-button>
</form>
```

Place a one-field form's only submit action inside the field.

```html
<form role="search">
  <ki-input type="search" name="q" label="Search docs" placeholder="Components, tokens…">
    <ki-button slot="action" size="sm" variant="secondary" type="submit">Search</ki-button>
  </ki-input>
</form>
```

The action has a separate tab stop. Enter in the entry also submits the form.
For an icon-only action, give `ki-icon-button size="sm"` a `label` and call
`form.requestSubmit()` from its click handler.

Read-only and disabled are distinct states — read-only stays focusable and is submitted, disabled is neither:

```html
<ki-input label="Plan" value="Pro" readonly></ki-input>
<ki-input label="Legacy ID" value="A-1042" disabled></ki-input>
```

## Appearance and character limits

Set `appearance` to `outlined` for a full border or `filled` for a
tinted surface with a bottom indicator. Both keep the label above the field.
The default appearance follows the theme.

Set `minlength` and `maxlength` to use the native input limits. With
a maximum, `show-count` adds the current length to the field description
and announces when the user reaches the limit.

```html
<ki-input label="Workspace name" appearance="outlined" minlength="3" maxlength="30" show-count help-text="Shown to members" value="Kimen design"></ki-input>
<ki-input label="Price" appearance="filled" value="49.00"><span slot="start">EUR</span><span slot="end">/ month</span></ki-input>
```

## An error from the application

Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on a submitted answer,
such as a server-side check. The field is invalid, blocks its form and is
announced as invalid at once. The person's next keystroke withdraws the
error. Remove the attribute when a new attempt starts: setting the same text
again while it is still set shows nothing.

```html
<ki-input label="Work email" name="email" type="email" value="ana@example.com" custom-error="This email is already registered."></ki-input>
```

Attributes:
- `ai-suggestion-text` (string, default 'Suggested by AI'): Localized provenance description read alongside help or an error when the end slot contains an AI label. Use this to translate the description.
- `appearance` ("default" | "filled" | "outlined" | undefined, default 'default'): Field appearance. `default` uses the current theme, `outlined` draws a full border, and `filled` uses a tinted surface and bottom indicator. The visible label stays above the field. When to use: set an explicit appearance when fields must share a shape across themes.
- `autocomplete` (string | undefined): Native autocomplete detail token forwarded to the internal input. When NOT to use: omit when no autofill entry purpose is known.
- `custom-error` (string | undefined): An error of the application's own, such as a server-side or cross-field verdict on the submitted answer ("Already registered"). While it holds text the field is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help text at once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting at the person's next change of the answer, or when the form is reset, so it never blocks the corrected answer. It outranks `error-text` and an error set with `setCustomValidity`. When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts. When NOT to use: do not use it for `required` or other constraints the field enforces itself; `error-text` words those. Setting the same text again while the prop still holds it shows nothing: remove it first, then set it again.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Prevents editing, removes the field from keyboard reach and exposes the unavailable state through the internal native input. When NOT to use: do not use disabled for readonly reference values.
- `error-text` (string | undefined): Message shown in place of the help text once the person's answer fails a constraint (`required`, `type` or a length limit), and the field's `validationMessage`. Say how to fix the answer ("Enter an email address like name@example.com"). Without it the browser's own message shows, in the browser's language. An error set with `custom-error` or `setCustomValidity` outranks it. When NOT to use: do not use it for server-side or cross-field errors; set `custom-error` or call `setCustomValidity` for those.
- `help-text` (string | undefined): One line of help under the field, read with it as its description: the format expected, or why the answer is asked. While an error shows, the error takes its place. When NOT to use: do not repeat the label, and do not use it for error messages; use `error-text`.
- `label` (string, required): Visible label rendered next to the entry area and used as the accessible name. This is mandatory for valid usage. When NOT to use: never use `placeholder` as a label substitute.
