Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on the submitted
number, such as a stock check. The field is invalid, blocks its form and is
announced as invalid at once. The person's next edit or step withdraws the
error. Remove the attribute when a new attempt starts: setting the same text
again while it is still set shows nothing.

```html
<ki-number-input label="Seats" name="seats" value="42" min="1" custom-error="Only 40 seats left."></ki-number-input>
```

## Custom-elements entry point

```ts
import { defineCustomElement } from '@kimen/elements/ki-number-input';

defineCustomElement();
const discount = document.querySelector('ki-number-input[name="discount"]');
if (discount) {
  discount.format = { style: 'percent', maximumFractionDigits: 1 };
}
```

Attributes:
- `custom-error` (string | undefined): An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the submitted number ("Only 40 seats left"). While it holds text the field is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help text at once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting at the person's next edit or step of the number, or when the form is reset, so it never blocks the corrected answer. It outranks `error-text`. When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts. When NOT to use: do not use it for `required`, the bounds or unreadable text, which the field reports itself; `error-text` words those. Setting the same text again while the prop still holds it shows nothing: remove it first, then set it again.
- `decrease-label` (string, default 'Decrease {label}'): Stepper's accessible name. The field label replaces {label}.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Prevents editing and excludes the control from form submission.
- `error-text` (string | undefined): Validation hint to show when the entry fails a constraint. A `custom-error` outranks it.
- `format` (string): Intl.NumberFormat options for display. In HTML or a catalog spec, supply these options as JSON text. The form value retains its original precision.
- `help-text` (string | undefined): Context or instructions displayed beneath the field when it has no visible error.
- `increase-label` (string, default 'Increase {label}'): Stepper's accessible name. The field label replaces {label}.
- `invalid-number-message` (string, default 'Enter a number.'): Default validation message for text that cannot be read as a number.
- `label` (string, required): Visible accessible name. Supply a meaningful label in the page language.
- `max` (number | undefined): Maximum permitted numeric value. Omit for an unbounded maximum.
- `maximum-message` (string, default 'Value adjusted to the maximum of {value}.'): Polite adjustment message after exceeding the maximum. The formatted bound replaces {value}.
- `min` (number | undefined): Minimum permitted numeric value. Omit for an unbounded minimum.
- `minimum-message` (string, default 'Value adjusted to the minimum of {value}.'): Polite adjustment message after falling below the minimum. The formatted bound replaces {value}.
- `name` (string | undefined): Form-data key for the plain numeric value.
- `required` (boolean, default false): Whether the user must enter a number before submitting the form.
- `step` (number, default 1): Positive increment for arrows and buttons. Page keys and Shift+arrows move ten increments.
- `steppers` (boolean, default false): Shows named decrease and increase buttons inside the field.
- `unit` (string | undefined): Visible suffix such as seconds or seats, included in the accessible description.
- `value` (number | undefined): Current numeric value, or undefined when empty or unparseable. Use the attribute for the form reset value. Property assignments are silent.

Slots: none

Parts:
- `decrease`: Button that subtracts one step.
- `error`: Polite validation feedback associated with the spinbutton.
- `field`: Enclosure around the editor, unit and stepper buttons.
- `help`: Help message associated with the spinbutton.
- `increase`: Button that adds one step.
- `input`: Native text editor carrying the spinbutton role.
- `label`: Visible name of the spinbutton.
- `status`: Polite feedback explaining a value adjustment.
- `unit`: Visible unit referenced by the spinbutton's description.

Events:
- `change` (Event): Composed event fired when the person commits an edited or stepped value. Read the host's numeric value. Listen to native input for live edits.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-control-offset`: Added to the block size of every scaled control and row (button, icon button, field, select, textarea, option, list item, tab). Components floor the result at ki.size.target-min.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-number-input-border-block-end-width`: Field border width at block end.
- `--ki-number-input-border-block-start-width`: Field border width at block start.
- `--ki-number-input-border-inline-width`: Field border width at either inline edge.
- `--ki-number-input-field-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter behind the field.
- `--ki-number-input-field-bg`: Resting NumberInput field fill.
- `--ki-number-input-field-bg-image`: Optional theme image layered over the field fill.
- `--ki-number-input-field-border`: Resting NumberInput field boundary.
- `--ki-number-input-field-disabled-bg`: Field fill when disabled.
- `--ki-number-input-field-disabled-border`: Boundary when the entire field is disabled.
- `--ki-number-input-field-disabled-fg`: Numeric entry ink when disabled.
- `--ki-number-input-field-fg`: Foreground of the numeric entry.
- `--ki-number-input-field-focus-bg`: Field fill while focused.
- `--ki-number-input-field-focus-fg`: Numeric entry ink while focused.
- `--ki-number-input-field-invalid-border`: Field boundary when a validation message is visible.
- `--ki-number-input-font-size`: Font size of the numeric entry and its suffix.
- `--ki-number-input-font-size-touch`: Minimum input font size under a coarse pointer.
- `--ki-number-input-height`: Medium field height before applying regional density.
- `--ki-number-input-label-font-size`: Field label font size.
- `--ki-number-input-label-font-weight`: Field label font weight.
- `--ki-number-input-label-gap`: Gap between the label, field and supporting messages.
- `--ki-number-input-label-line-height`: Line height of the field label.
- `--ki-number-input-line-height`: Line height of the numeric entry and its suffix.
- `--ki-number-input-padding-inline`: Inline padding for the plain field and unit suffix.
- `--ki-number-input-radius`: Field corners.
- `--ki-number-input-stepper-bg`: Resting stepper button fill.
- `--ki-number-input-stepper-disabled-fg`: Stepper icon ink when disabled.
- `--ki-number-input-stepper-fg`: Resting stepper icon ink.
- `--ki-number-input-stepper-hover-bg`: Stepper fill when hovered.
- `--ki-number-input-stepper-hover-fg`: Stepper icon ink when hovered.
- `--ki-number-input-stepper-padding-inline`: Editor inline padding between the steppers.
- `--ki-number-input-unit-bg`: Backing of the unit suffix within the field.
- `--ki-number-input-unit-fg`: Unit suffix ink. Medium emphasis in the standard contrast setting.
- `--ki-text-danger-high-em`: semantic color for text danger high em.
- `--ki-text-high-em`: semantic color for text high em.
- `--ki-text-supporting`: Supporting text of an enabled control: field labels, placeholders, list secondary lines, quiet button labels and unselected tabs. A role, distinct from the med-em emphasis step it resolves to, so a mode can strengthen enabled supporting text without touching the disabled ink that also draws from med-em (directly, or through text.muted).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-normal`: semantic font weight for typography weight body normal.

### ki-option

A declarative data option rendered by its owning `ki-select` or `ki-combobox`.

When to use: declare one choice inside a `ki-select` or `ki-combobox`; its text is the
human-facing label and its `value` is the submitted value.
When NOT to use: `ki-option` standalone, authoring selection
on an option, or expecting it to paint its own row.

Examples:

An option is meaningful only inside `ki-select`: it does not paint itself — the trimmed text is the visible label the select mirrors into its popup listbox, and `value` is what the form submits:

```html
<ki-select label="Language" name="language" placeholder="Choose a language">
  <ki-option value="en">English</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="es">Spanish</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="pt">Portuguese</ki-option>
</ki-select>
```

Omitting `value` submits the trimmed option text (native `<option>` parity); `disabled` options cannot be selected, are skipped by keyboard highlight, and are exposed unavailable by the select:

```html
<ki-select label="Priority" name="priority">
  <ki-option>Low</ki-option>
  <ki-option>Medium</ki-option>
  <ki-option disabled>Urgent</ki-option>
</ki-select>
```

Never author selection on the option — assign `ki-select.value` and the first matching option is selected silently:

```html
<ki-select id="language" label="Language" name="language">
  <ki-option value="en">English</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="es">Spanish</ki-option>
</ki-select>

<script type="module">
  document.getElementById('language').value = 'es';
</script>
```

Attributes:
- `description` (string | undefined): Secondary text shown below the label in a combobox choice row.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Makes this option unavailable. Disabled options cannot be selected, are skipped by keyboard highlight, and are exposed unavailable by the select.
- `value` (string | undefined): Submission and selection value for this option. When omitted, the value falls back to the trimmed option text, matching native `<option>` parity. When NOT to use: do not use this as selection state; set `ki-select.value`.

Slots:
- (default): Text label mirrored by the owning choice field.
- `start`: Decorative content shown before the label in a combobox row.

Parts: none

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties: none

### ki-pagination

Controls for moving among pages of results or appending the next batch.

When to use: paged tables, search results or long lists. Use compact for
a previous/next stepper and load-more to append results in place.
When NOT to use: short lists that fit in one view or the steps of a task.

Examples:

# Pagination examples

Import `@kimen/tokens/css` and register the element with
`defineCustomElement` from `@kimen/elements/components/ki-pagination.js`.

## Replace a results page

```html
<h2 id="results-heading" tabindex="-1">Results page 1</h2>
<ul id="results"><li>Mercury</li><li>Venus</li></ul>
<ki-pagination id="results-pages" page="1" pages="2" label="Planet results pages"></ki-pagination>

<script type="module">
  const pages = [['Mercury', 'Venus'], ['Earth', 'Mars']];
  const pager = document.getElementById('results-pages');
  const heading = document.getElementById('results-heading');
  const results = document.getElementById('results');

  pager.addEventListener('ki-page-change', ({ detail: { page } }) => {
    const items = pages[page - 1].map((name) => {
      const item = document.createElement('li');
      item.textContent = name;
      return item;
    });
    results.replaceChildren(...items);
    heading.textContent = `Results page ${page}`;
    pager.page = page;
    heading.focus();
  });
</script>
```

When fetching asynchronously, update `page` and move focus after the
requested results render. Keep the heading programmatically focusable.

## Let the server render each page

```html
<ki-pagination page="5" pages="12" href-template="?page={page}"
  label="Search results pages"></ki-pagination>
```

Place `{page}` in the path, query, or fragment of a relative or HTTP(S) URL.
The generated anchors support browser link actions. The catalog applies
its URL policy. For a guarded page action, use numbered or compact pagination
in button mode.

## Append results and announce the count

```html
<ul id="recent-results"><li>Mercury</li><li>Venus</li></ul>
<ki-pagination id="recent-pagination" variant="load-more" shown="2" total="4"
  label="More planets"></ki-pagination>

<script type="module">
  const pager = document.getElementById('recent-pagination');
  const results = document.getElementById('recent-results');

  pager.addEventListener('ki-load-more', () => {
    const items = ['Earth', 'Mars'].map((name) => {
      const item = document.createElement('li');
      item.textContent = name;
      return item;
    });
    results.append(...items);
    pager.shown = results.childElementCount;
  });
</script>
```

The last update keeps the same button in place and announces the final
count. Set `previous-label`, `next-label`, and `load-more-label` for
translated controls. Use `page-label`, `compact-label`, and `status-label`
with the named placeholders to translate the generated text.

Attributes:
- `boundaries` (number, default 1, minimum 0, maximum 10): Number of pages to display at each end of the numbered list.
- `compact-label` (string, default 'Page {page} of {pages}'): Localized stepper label template. Include {page} and {pages}.
- `href-template` (string | undefined, URL): Relative or HTTP(S) URL template for native navigation. Place {page} in the path, query or fragment, for example "?page={page}".
- `label` (string, default 'Pagination'): Accessible name of the navigation landmark. Distinguish multiple result sets.
- `load-more-label` (string, default 'Load more'): Localized visible label for the button that appends results.
- `next-label` (string, default 'Next page'): Localized accessible name of the control that requests the next page.
- `page` (number, default 1, minimum 1): Current 1-based page. Update it when the requested results are ready.
- `page-label` (string, default 'Page {page}'): Localized accessible name template for numbered controls. Include {page}.
- `pages` (number | undefined, minimum 0): Total number of result pages. Omit it until a page count is available.
- `previous-label` (string, default 'Previous page'): Localized accessible name of the control that requests the previous page.
- `shown` (number | undefined, minimum 0): Displayed result count in load-more mode. Update it after appending results.
- `siblings` (number, default 1, minimum 0, maximum 10): Number of pages to display on each side of the current page.
- `status-label` (string, default 'Showing {shown} of {total} results'): Localized polite count template. Include {shown} and {total}.
- `total` (number | undefined, minimum 0): Total result count in load-more mode. Required with shown for the count.
- `variant` ("compact" | "load-more" | "pages", default 'pages'): Numbered pages, a previous/next stepper, or a button to append results. Numbered pages switch to the stepper below 480 CSS pixels of available width.

Slots: none

Parts:
- `compact`: Current page and page count in the stepper.
- `gap`: Decorative marker for omitted pages.
- `list`: Ordered list of pages in the numbered variant.
- `load-more`: Button that requests another batch.
- `navigation`: Named navigation landmark.
- `next`: Next-page control.
- `page`: Numbered button or link.
- `previous`: Previous-page control.
- `status`: Polite result-count announcement.

Events:
- `ki-load-more` (CustomEvent<void>): Requests another batch. Append results in place and update shown.
- `ki-page-change` (CustomEvent<{
    page: number;
  }>): Requests a different page. Update results and move focus to their heading when they are ready. Cancelling the event also cancels a plain link click.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-pagination-compact-gap`: Gap between the compact count and direction controls.
- `--ki-pagination-current-bg`: Background of the current page control.
- `--ki-pagination-current-fg`: Ink for the current page control.
- `--ki-pagination-gap`: Gap between numbered page controls.
- `--ki-pagination-item-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter for the page control.
- `--ki-pagination-item-bg`: Resting background of a numbered page control.
- `--ki-pagination-item-bg-image`: Optional image above the page control background color.
- `--ki-pagination-item-fg`: Resting ink for page labels and status text.
- `--ki-pagination-item-hover-bg`: Background of a hovered page control.
- `--ki-pagination-item-hover-fg`: Ink for a hovered page control.
- `--ki-pagination-item-radius`: Corner radius of numbered page controls and direction links.
- `--ki-pagination-item-size`: Minimum size of a numbered page control at standard density.
- `--ki-pagination-more-gap`: Gap between the load-more button and the count.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-medium`: semantic font weight for typography weight body medium.

### ki-popover

A non-modal popover anchored to a button.

When to use: Show filters, details, a small form, or an explanation opened by click. Use a rich toggletip for a short explanation with actions.
When NOT to use: Use ki-dialog for required decisions and ki-tooltip for hover or focus hints.

Examples:

Use a named dialog popover for interactive filters. The host supplies the trigger in the same document or shadow tree.

```html
<ki-button id="filters" type="button" variant="secondary">Filters</ki-button>
<ki-popover for="filters" label="Incident filters" placement="bottom-start">
  <ki-checkbox checked>Open incidents</ki-checkbox>
</ki-popover>
```

Use a toggletip to announce supplementary text and keep focus on the trigger.

```html
<ki-button id="retention" type="button" variant="ghost">About retention</ki-button>
<ki-popover for="retention" kind="toggletip" arrow="false">
  Logs are kept for 30 days.
</ki-popover>
```

Use a rich toggletip for an explanation with actions. Opening the panel
moves focus inside, and Escape restores it to the trigger.

```html
<ki-button id="contrast-mode" type="button" variant="ghost">Contrast mode</ki-button>
<ki-popover for="contrast-mode" kind="toggletip" appearance="rich" label="About contrast mode" arrow="false">
  <strong>Contrast mode</strong>
  <p>Kimen follows the system setting.</p>
  <ki-button type="button" size="sm" variant="ghost">Learn more</ki-button>
</ki-popover>
```

Use `open` to drive visibility and listen for `ki-open` and `ki-close` to observe it. In guarded catalog markup, bind actions to slotted controls. A trusted host can listen to the popover's two lifecycle events through the DOM.

Attributes:
- `appearance` ("default" | "rich" | undefined, default 'default'): Rich shares the tooltip's raised surface, body and heading styles. With `kind="toggletip"` it enables actions and moves focus inside on open.
- `arrow` (boolean, default true): Shows the arrow toward the trigger.
- `for` (string | undefined, ID of another element of the same spec): ID of the button in the same document or shadow tree.
- `kind` ("dialog" | "toggletip", default 'dialog'): Use dialog for controls or toggletip for supplemental information. Rich toggletips can contain actions.
- `label` (string | undefined, default 'Popover'): Accessible name of a dialog popover.
- `open` (boolean, default false): Visibility. Reflects activation and native dismissal.
- `placement` ("bottom" | "bottom-end" | "bottom-start" | "end" | "end-end" | "end-start" | "start" | "start-end" | "start-start" | "top" | "top-end" | "top-start", default 'bottom-start'): Preferred side and logical alignment. Flips when room is limited.

Slots:
- (default): Dialog content or toggletip text. A rich toggletip also accepts actions.

Parts:
- `arrow`: The decorative arrow.
- `surface`: The popover panel.

Events:
- `ki-close` (CustomEvent<void>): Emitted when the popover closes.
- `ki-open` (CustomEvent<void>): Emitted when the popover opens.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-popover-arrow-size`: Side length of an anchored surface pointer before rotation.
- `--ki-popover-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter behind an anchored surface.
- `--ki-popover-bg`: Raised popover surface colour.
- `--ki-popover-bg-image`: Optional image layer over an anchored surface colour.
- `--ki-popover-border`: Popover outline colour.
- `--ki-popover-border-width`: Outline thickness for a small anchored surface.
- `--ki-popover-fg`: Popover content ink.
- `--ki-popover-gap`: Space between a floating surface and its trigger.
- `--ki-popover-max-width`: Maximum inline size of a small anchored surface.
- `--ki-popover-padding`: Interior padding for a small anchored surface.
- `--ki-popover-radius`: Corner radius for a small anchored surface.
- `--ki-popover-shadow`: Popover elevation.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-bg`: Fill of the rich tooltip or rich popover.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-bg-image`: Optional image layer over the rich surface fill.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-border-color`: Outline ink of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-border-width`: Outline thickness of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-fg`: Ink of the rich surface body text.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-font-size`: Body text size of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-font-weight`: Body text weight of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-heading-family`: Typeface of the rich surface heading.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-heading-fg`: Ink of the rich surface heading over the shared fill.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-heading-gap`: Distance between the rich heading and its body.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-heading-size`: Text size of the rich surface heading.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-heading-weight`: Text weight of the rich surface heading.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-line-height`: Body text line height of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-max-width`: Maximum inline size of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-padding-block`: Block-axis inset of the rich surface, before density scaling.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-padding-inline`: Inline-axis inset of the rich surface, before density scaling.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-radius`: Corner radius of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-shadow`: Raised elevation of the rich surface.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-para`: semantic dimension for typography line height para.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.

### ki-progress

A token-styled, non-interactive progress indicator for known or unknown duration work.

When to use: communicate advancement of an ongoing task such as upload,
download, installation or multi-step processing. Use `value`/`max` when
the completed fraction is known; use `indeterminate` when work is ongoing
but its duration cannot be measured, including loading-indicator use cases.
Choose `linear` in page flows and lists, and `circular` in compact or
centered placements. Always set `label` to what is progressing.
When NOT to use: static measurements within a known range such as disk
usage or scores (gauge/meter), step-by-step wizard navigation (stepper),
skeleton placeholders while content loads, or operations that finish in
under about one second.

Examples:

A determinate task; `label` names what is progressing (without it the progressbar exposes no accessible name) and `value` is clamped to `0..max` for both presentation and ARIA:

```html
<ki-progress label="Uploading report.pdf" value="42"></ki-progress>
```

When the total is not 100, set `max`; non-finite, zero or negative totals normalize to `100`:

```html
<ki-progress label="Installing dependencies" value="3" max="8"></ki-progress>
```

Unknown-duration work sets `indeterminate` instead of a fabricated `value` (which is ignored while it is set); the motion is declared only when reduced motion is not requested:

```html
<ki-progress label="Contacting server" indeterminate></ki-progress>
```

`shape="circular"` fits compact or centered placements; unknown shape values render linear:

```html
<ki-progress label="Export progress" shape="circular" value="80"></ki-progress>
```

Attributes:
- `indeterminate` (boolean, default false): Unknown-duration mode. When set, no completed fraction or current value is exposed. Its motion is declared only when reduced motion is not requested. When to use: show ongoing work whose duration or total cannot be measured. When NOT to use: do not use for known fractions; use `value` and `max`.
- `label` (string, required): Accessible name applied to the internal progressbar. Always set this to what is progressing, such as "Uploading report.pdf". Without it the element renders but exposes no accessible name, so the catalog contract requires it. When NOT to use: do not use a generic label such as "Loading" when the task can be named more specifically.
- `max` (number, default 100): Total amount. Non-finite, zero or negative values normalize to `100` for presentation and ARIA. When to use: set when a determinate task's total is not 100. When NOT to use: omit for conventional percentage-style progress.
- `shape` ("circular" | "linear", default 'linear'): Structural presentation. Use `linear` in page flows and lists; use `circular` in compact or centered placements. Unknown values render linear. When NOT to use: do not use shape to encode semantic status or task intent.
- `value` (number, default 0): Completed amount. Presentation and ARIA clamp this value to `0..max`; malformed values fall back to `0`. Ignored while `indeterminate` is set. When to use: set with `max` for determinate task advancement. When NOT to use: do not set a fabricated value for unknown-duration work; set `indeterminate` instead.

Slots: none

Parts:
- `indicator`: The advancing fill or arc: indicator ink and indeterminate animation.
- `track`: The full channel or ring: track ink and radius/stroke geometry.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-duration-medium-2`: M3 md.sys.motion.duration.medium2 (300ms). onmars: MarsUI moderate step (240ms).
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-motion-easing-standard`: Standard interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-progress-circular-size`: dimension used by the progress component for circular size.
- `--ki-progress-circular-track-width`: dimension used by the progress component for circular track width.
- `--ki-progress-indeterminate-duration`: duration used by the progress component for progress indeterminate duration.
- `--ki-progress-indicator-color`: MarsUI fills components with the med-em (500) tone of the ramp (marsui-design-dna.md §1; specs/002-ki-button/design-extraction.md §§2.1-2.4 delta 500-vs-high-em): progress indicator uses surface.primary-med-em.
- `--ki-progress-linear-radius`: dimension used by the progress component for linear radius.
- `--ki-progress-linear-thickness`: dimension used by the progress component for linear thickness.
- `--ki-progress-track-color`: color used by the progress component for track color.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-prompt-input

A multiline assistant composer with local file attachments and send and stop requests.

When to use: Compose a message to an assistant, optionally attach local files, and let people interrupt the assistant's response.
When NOT to use: Ordinary multiline form input without a send or stop interaction (`ki-textarea`), file uploads, or rich text editing.

Examples:

# PromptInput examples

Use a composer when a person can send a message to an assistant and stop its response. Provide a `label` even when there is a placeholder.

## Text and attachments

```html
<ki-prompt-input
  label="Message Kimen Assistant"
  placeholder="Ask anything, or drop a file"
  accept=".csv,.pdf,image/*"
  max-files="5"
  max-size="5000000"
></ki-prompt-input>
```

The file picker, drop area and clipboard share the same checks. `max-size` is the number of bytes allowed per file. An empty `accept` hides the attachment UI. The host receives a `ki-submit` event with `detail.text` and `detail.files`.

## Model selection and keyboard shortcuts

```html
<ki-prompt-input label="Message assistant" submit-on="mod-enter">
  <select slot="tools" aria-label="Assistant model">
    <option value="standard">Standard</option>
    <option value="careful">Careful</option>
  </select>
</ki-prompt-input>
```

In modifier mode, Control+Enter and Command+Enter send. Shift+Enter always inserts a newline. A model picker built with a menu can use the same slot. Read model selection from that control when handling `ki-submit`.

The application sets `status` to `submitted` while awaiting a response and to `streaming` when output begins. It handles `ki-stop` and sets `status` to `idle` when the response ends or stops.

Attributes:
- `accept` (string | undefined, default ''): Comma-separated extensions or MIME types. Empty hides the attachment surface.
- `attach-label` (string, default 'Attach files'): Accessible name of the file picker button.
- `attachments-label` (string, default 'Attachments'): Accessible name of the attachment list.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Excludes the composer from interaction and native form data.
- `file-count-message` (string, default '{name} exceeds the maximum number of attachments.'): Localized count rejection. The {name} marker is replaced with the file name.
- `file-size-message` (string, default '{name} exceeds the file size limit.'): Localized size rejection. The {name} marker is replaced with the file name.
- `file-type-message` (string, default '{name} has an unsupported file type.'): Localized type rejection. The {name} marker is replaced with the file name.
- `label` (string, required): Required accessible name of the text field. Supply it even with a placeholder.
- `max-files` (number | undefined): Maximum count of attached files. Omit for no count limit.
- `max-size` (number | undefined): Maximum attachment size in bytes per file. Omit for no size limit.
- `name` (string | undefined): Optional key for the text in native form data. Files are carried by ki-submit.
- `placeholder` (string | undefined): Hint displayed while the text field is empty.
- `remove-label` (string, default 'Remove'): Prefix of an attachment's remove button name, followed by the file name.
- `send-label` (string, default 'Send'): Accessible name of the Send button.
- `status` ("idle" | "streaming" | "submitted" | undefined, default 'idle'): Application-owned request state. Only idle can send; streaming exposes Stop.
- `stop-label` (string, default 'Stop generating'): Accessible name of the Stop button.
- `submit-on` ("enter" | "mod-enter", default 'enter'): Send with Enter or with Control/Command+Enter. Shift+Enter always adds a line.
- `value` (string | undefined, default ''): Current draft text; the value attribute provides the form reset default.
- `writing-message` (string, default 'Writing…'): Visible polite status while the assistant streams.

Slots:
- `attachments`: Supplemental list items, visible when accept is set. Composer-managed files appear in the same list and alone contribute to ki-submit.
- `tools`: Application-owned toolbar controls, such as a model-picker trigger. Use non-submitting controls.

Parts:
- `actions`: The toolbar with attachment, tool and message actions.
- `attach`: The native file-picker button.
- `attachments`: The labelled attachment list.
- `feedback`: The polite announcement for rejected attachments.
- `field`: The painted composer enclosure.
- `send`: The native Send button.
- `status`: The polite announcement for the streaming state.
- `stop`: The native Stop button, visible while streaming.
- `textarea`: The native growing text control.
- `tools`: The container for the tools slot.

Events:
- `ki-stop` (CustomEvent<void>): Requests that the application stop its streaming response.
- `ki-submit` (CustomEvent<KiPromptInputSubmitDetail>): Requests a send with original text and a snapshot of accepted local files.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-hover-bg`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral hover background.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-hover-fg`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral hover foreground.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-rest-bg`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral rest background.
- `--ki-button-ghost-neutral-rest-fg`: color used by the button component for ghost neutral rest foreground.
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-disabled-bg`: color used by the button component for primary neutral disabled background. Deliberate deviation: Figma disabled is Surface/disabled_base_em gray.100 with gray.400 text (≈1.4:1); Kimen keeps gray.200 for contrast (precedent 010 D2, pending founder ratification).
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-disabled-border`: color used by the button component for primary neutral disabled border.
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-disabled-fg`: color used by the button component for primary neutral disabled foreground. Deliberate deviation: Figma disabled text is text/base_em gray.400 (≈1.4:1 on gray.100); Kimen keeps text.muted gray.700 for readable disabled text (precedent 010 D2, pending founder ratification).
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-rest-bg`: color used by the button component for primary neutral rest background (MarsUI Surface/primary_med_em, brand 500).
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-rest-border`: color used by the button component for primary neutral rest border (MarsUI top/inline edge; none in onmars v2).
- `--ki-button-primary-neutral-rest-fg`: color used by the button component for primary neutral rest foreground.
- `--ki-button-secondary-neutral-rest-bg`: color used by the button component for secondary neutral rest background (MarsUI Surface/special/secondary_alpha_base: neutral, not a brand tint; white in onmars v2).
- `--ki-button-secondary-neutral-rest-border`: color used by the button component for secondary neutral rest border (MarsUI top/inline edge).
- `--ki-button-secondary-neutral-rest-fg`: color used by the button component for secondary neutral rest foreground (MarsUI text/high_em).
- `--ki-button-sm-radius`: dimension used by the button component for sm radius (Button master 8003:300 binds Radius/small-component/sm, the scale a radius mode reassigns).
- `--ki-control-size-sm`: Small control track height, 32 CSS px at the default root size.
- `--ki-density-control-offset`: Added to the block size of every scaled control and row (button, icon button, field, select, textarea, option, list item, tab). Components floor the result at ki.size.target-min.
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-icon-button-sm-icon-size`: dimension used by the icon button component for sm icon size (MarsUI Placeholder_sm 18px).
- `--ki-prompt-input-action-gap`: Default spacing between attachments and toolbar controls.
- `--ki-prompt-input-backdrop-filter`: Optional whole backdrop filter behind the composer.
- `--ki-prompt-input-bg`: Raised surface behind the prompt composer.
- `--ki-prompt-input-bg-image`: Optional background image painted above the composer surface.
- `--ki-prompt-input-border`: Outline around the composer.
- `--ki-prompt-input-border-width`: Outline thickness around the composer.
- `--ki-prompt-input-editor-padding-block`: Block inset for the native text field and its sizer.
- `--ki-prompt-input-editor-padding-inline`: Inline inset for the native text field and its sizer.
- `--ki-prompt-input-feedback-bg`: Surface immediately behind attachment rejection text.
- `--ki-prompt-input-feedback-fg`: Attachment rejection text on the composer surface.
- `--ki-prompt-input-fg`: Draft text on the composer surface.
- `--ki-prompt-input-max-height`: Maximum height of the draft before the textarea scrolls.
- `--ki-prompt-input-min-height`: Minimum height of the editable draft.
- `--ki-prompt-input-padding`: Inset and spacing between rows in the composer.
- `--ki-prompt-input-placeholder-fg`: Placeholder and writing status on the composer surface.
- `--ki-prompt-input-radius`: Corner radius of the composer surface.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-body-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height body 2.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-2`: semantic dimension for typography size body 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.

### ki-qr

A machine-scannable QR code that hands a declared value — a link, a pairing payload — from the screen to a nearby camera, encoded locally and restyled entirely through tokens.

When to use: hand a URL or machine-readable payload from the screen to a
nearby camera device: login pairing, tickets and passes, "continue on
mobile" links, Wi-Fi sharing. Declare `value` (encoded verbatim, always
locally) and a purpose-stating `label` ("Open onmars.dev on your phone"),
and always offer the same payload through an accessible alternative next
to the code — a visible link or copyable text — because a QR code is only
useful to someone who can point a second device's camera at the screen.
When NOT to use: data the person must read on this same screen (render text
or a link), one-dimensional barcodes (out of scope), anything interactive
(a QR code is not a button — pair it with a real control instead), secret
values (anyone who can photograph the screen can decode them), or as the
sole carrier of the payload (the accessible alternative is mandatory
guidance). An always-empty ki-qr and a value beyond the ~2,331-byte
capacity are authoring mistakes: both render nothing, silently.

Examples:

A scannable link with a purpose-stating `label` (the accessible name) and the same payload offered as a visible link next to the code — the accessible alternative is mandatory, the code never travels alone:

```html
<ki-qr value="https://onmars.dev" label="Open onmars.dev on your phone"></ki-qr>
<a href="https://onmars.dev">onmars.dev</a>
```

`value` is data, never behavior: it is encoded locally byte-for-byte and never interpreted, resolved, navigated to or fetched; non-ASCII text round-trips exactly:

```html
<ki-qr value="Reunión mañana — Zúrich" label="Add the meeting to your phone"></ki-qr>
```

Malformed declarations never break a page: with no `value` (or one beyond the ~2,331-byte capacity) nothing renders and nothing errors:

```html
<ki-qr label="Nothing to encode"></ki-qr>
```

Attributes:
- `label` (string | undefined): Accessible name stating the code's purpose ("Open onmars.dev on your phone"). The component exposes exactly one non-interactive image named by it, falling back to the encoded value when absent (FR-005) — never an unnamed graphic. The label is never rendered visually, and naming the purpose is what tells assistive-technology users to look for the accessible alternative carrying the same payload (documented catalog guidance, FR-013).
- `value` (string | undefined): The exact text the code encodes — the single source of the content, encoded locally as one UTF-8 byte segment at error-correction level M (non-ASCII text additionally carries the UTF-8 ECI designator, so real scanners decode the declared string rather than an ISO-8859-1 misreading), so an independent decoder recovers it byte-for-byte, including non-ASCII text (FR-001), and no network request is ever made — the value is data, never behavior: the component never interprets, resolves, navigates to or fetches it (FR-002). Changes re-encode in place. When absent, empty or beyond the capacity of the densest symbol (~2,331 bytes at level M), nothing renders and nothing errors (FR-003).

Slots: none

Parts:
- `code`: The code tile: size, tile background and corners, quiet zone, module and finder shape/color.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-duration-medium-1`: M3 md.sys.motion.duration.medium1 (250ms). onmars: MarsUI moderate step (240ms, 2x the 120ms base).
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-motion-easing-standard-decelerate`: Utility entrance curve. M3 md.sys.motion.easing.standard-decelerate. onmars: the MarsUI decelerate curve (ki.easing.out).
- `--ki-qr-background`: color used by the qr component for the light tile behind the modules: the Figma symbol is transparent over the showcase card's Surface/s0 white, but a scannable code owns its tile — the scheme-stable white keeps dark-on-light module contrast in both schemes (FR-010, a documented theme obligation).
- `--ki-qr-color`: color used by the qr component for module/finder ink (the master binds Text/high_em, whose light-scheme hue is Gray/950 #0a0c11; referenced as the scheme-stable primitive because FR-010 keeps QR ink from flipping in dark — 18.9:1 on white).
- `--ki-qr-finder-radius`: dimension used by the qr component for the corner radius of the three finder rings, applied to the ring's midline in the code's internal coordinate space of 8px per module: Type=square renders square concentric finders (radius 0); the documented round value is {ki.radius.2xl} (14px midline = 18px outer edge, the 2.25-module radius measured on Type=round); the inner-edge and center radii derive by construction (stroke geometry and a 3/7 scale — design-extraction §5).
- `--ki-qr-module-radius`: dimension used by the qr component for the corner radius of every data module, in the code's internal coordinate space of 8px per module: Type=square (the set default) renders pure squares (radius 0); the documented round value is {ki.radius.xs} (4px = half a module, the MarsUI Type=round dot carried as a token value, never an attribute — FR-007, 002 shape precedent).
- `--ki-qr-quiet-zone`: dimension used by the qr component for the light quiet zone around the modules: the 8px band measured on both 128px variants (about two modules of the sample matrices), painted as tile padding and preserved at any token-driven size (FR-008).
- `--ki-qr-radius`: dimension used by the qr component for the tile corners: the QR_code frames are square with no own radius (the rounded showcase card beneath is framing, not anatomy — design-extraction §1).
- `--ki-qr-size`: dimension used by the qr component for size (MarsUI 128x128 symbol frame via the dedicated ki.size.qr surface size; replaces the 120px space-scale approximation).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-radio

One option in a token-styled radio group.

When to use: place inside `ki-radio-group` when a person must choose
exactly one of a small visible set.
When NOT to use: `ki-radio` standalone, multiple selection,
or authored selection state; set the parent group's `value` instead.

Examples:

Each option is a `ki-radio` child of a `ki-radio-group`; the slotted text is the option's accessible name and activation surface, and `value` is what the group submits when the option is selected:

```html
<ki-radio-group label="Delivery speed" name="delivery">
  <ki-radio value="standard">Standard (3–5 days)</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="express">Express (1–2 days)</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

A disabled option cannot be selected or focused, and group arrow navigation skips it:

```html
<ki-radio-group label="Plan" name="plan" value="pro">
  <ki-radio value="free">Free</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="pro">Pro</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="enterprise" disabled>Enterprise (contact sales)</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

Selection is never authored on the option — the parent group's `value` selects the matching option:

```html
<ki-radio-group label="Theme" name="theme" value="dark">
  <ki-radio value="light">Light</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="dark">Dark</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="system">Match system</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

Attributes:
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Prevents this option from being selected or focused. Disabled options are skipped by group arrow navigation and omitted from form submission when selected before becoming disabled. When NOT to use: do not use disabled as a temporary loading state.
- `value` (string, default 'on'): Submission value projected by the parent `ki-radio-group` when this option is selected. Omit for native radio parity with value `"on"`. When NOT to use: do not use `value` to author selection; set the group's `value` property or attribute.

Slots:
- (default): Option label. This is the accessible name and activation surface.

Parts:
- `control`: Visual ring and selected dot.
- `label`: Wrapper around the option label.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-effect-component-primary-default-shadow`: MarsUI Component_effect/primary_default: drop 0/1/1/-0.5 plus inner White/12 0/3/3. Pair with --ki-effect-component-backdrop-filter — CSS cannot mix backdrop blur into box-shadow.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-easing-emphasized-out`: Expressive exit curve for selected controls. Onmars eases out without overshoot.
- `--ki-motion-easing-standard`: Standard interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-radio-border-width`: dimension used by the radio component for border width.
- `--ki-radio-control-radius`: dimension used by the radio component for control radius.
- `--ki-radio-control-size`: dimension used by the radio component for control size.
- `--ki-radio-dot-shadow`: shadow used by the radio component for the selected dot (MarsUI Small_dark_shadow: drop 0/2/3/-1.5 Elevation/shadow_dark, the lifted-dot look of the master).
- `--ki-radio-dot-size`: dimension used by the radio component for dot size.
- `--ki-radio-focus-ring-color`: color used by the radio component for focus ring color.
- `--ki-radio-focus-ring-offset`: dimension used by the radio component for focus ring offset.
- `--ki-radio-focus-ring-shadow`: shadow used by the radio component for the focus ring glow (MarsUI Focus/primary: 3px spread ring at 20% — see ki.focus.primary. specs/002-ki-button/design-extraction.md §2.5 recorded 40%, having read the alpha off the Dark canvas mode, same double mechanism as ki-button: glow plus the opaque indicator).
- `--ki-radio-focus-ring-width`: dimension used by the radio component for focus ring width.
- `--ki-radio-gap`: dimension used by the radio component for gap (MarsUI md label pairing: Space/xl 12px for the 20px circle / 24px target geometry).
- `--ki-radio-label-font-size`: dimension used by the radio component for label font size (MarsUI md pairing: body_2 15px; line-height stays 24 and weight 500).
- `--ki-radio-label-font-weight`: font weight used by the radio component for label font weight.
- `--ki-radio-label-line-height`: dimension used by the radio component for label line height.
- `--ki-radio-min-target`: dimension used by the radio component for min target.
- `--ki-radio-selected-active-bg`: color used by the radio component for selected active background (MarsUI defines no pressed state; mirrors rest).
- `--ki-radio-selected-active-border`: color used by the radio component for selected active border (same as the fill: borderless look).
- `--ki-radio-selected-active-fg`: color used by the radio component for selected active foreground.
- `--ki-radio-selected-active-overlay`: color used by the radio component for the selected pressed wash (ki-button active/overlay precedent). MarsUI defines no pressed fill and the brand ramp has no darker rung that survives the dark scheme, so the press composites the pressed state layer over the rest fill — a keyboard hold shows a real paint delta even under reduced motion, where the transform compress is gated off (bare-page state-delta contract).
- `--ki-radio-selected-disabled-bg`: color used by the radio component for selected disabled background (MarsUI Surface/disabled_med_em Gray/300).
- `--ki-radio-selected-disabled-border`: color used by the radio component for selected disabled border (same as the fill: borderless look).
- `--ki-radio-selected-disabled-fg`: color used by the radio component for selected disabled dot (MarsUI Surface/disabled_base_em Gray/100 — a light dot one quiet value step above the gray donut, not a dark dot).
- `--ki-radio-selected-hover-bg`: color used by the radio component for selected hover background (the master has no selected-hover variant; mirrors ki-checkbox checked hover: a real delta in both schemes).
- `--ki-radio-selected-hover-border`: color used by the radio component for selected hover border (same as the fill: borderless look).
- `--ki-radio-selected-hover-fg`: color used by the radio component for selected hover foreground.
- `--ki-radio-selected-rest-bg`: color used by the radio component for selected rest background (MarsUI active radio is a solid Surface/primary_med_em #845abe circle — the filled donut with a white dot is the signature, mirroring ki-checkbox checked).
- `--ki-radio-selected-rest-border`: color used by the radio component for selected rest border (same as the fill: the selected circle is borderless in the master).
- `--ki-radio-selected-rest-fg`: color used by the radio component for selected rest dot (MarsUI Text/primary_on_primary white 8px dot).
- `--ki-radio-unselected-active-bg`: color used by the radio component for unselected active background. Brief §1: neutral surface em ramp one step above hover (s1→s2), matching ki-checkbox unchecked active; the primary-tinted alpha stays in radio.material3.
- `--ki-radio-unselected-active-border`: color used by the radio component for unselected active border.
- `--ki-radio-unselected-active-fg`: color used by the radio component for unselected active foreground.
- `--ki-radio-unselected-disabled-bg`: color used by the radio component for unselected disabled background (MarsUI Surface/disabled_med_em Gray/300).
- `--ki-radio-unselected-disabled-border`: color used by the radio component for unselected disabled border (same as the fill: borderless look in the master).
- `--ki-radio-unselected-disabled-fg`: color used by the radio component for unselected disabled dot color (dot is hidden unselected; kept coherent with the disabled ladder, retiring the deprecated ki.text.muted alias).
- `--ki-radio-unselected-hover-bg`: color used by the radio component for unselected hover background. Brief §1: onmars hover is neutral (hover overlay / surface em ramp), matching ki-checkbox unchecked hover (s1); the former primary-tinted alpha is the M3 state-layer pattern and stays in radio.material3.
- `--ki-radio-unselected-hover-border`: color used by the radio component for unselected hover border.
- `--ki-radio-unselected-hover-fg`: color used by the radio component for unselected hover foreground.
- `--ki-radio-unselected-rest-bg`: color used by the radio component for unselected rest background.
- `--ki-radio-unselected-rest-border`: color used by the radio component for unselected rest border.
- `--ki-radio-unselected-rest-fg`: color used by the radio component for unselected rest foreground.
- `--ki-surface-special-dark-s0-light-s2`: semantic color for surface special dark s0 light s2.
- `--ki-surface-special-light-s0-dark-s4`: semantic color for surface special light s0 dark s4.
- `--ki-text-high-em`: semantic color for text high em.
- `--ki-text-med-em`: semantic color for text med em.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-radio-group

A token-styled radio group that owns selection, keyboard coordination and form participation for slotted `ki-radio` options. Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`, `setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and `willValidate` synchronously, on the custom-elements build (not on hosts created by the lazy loader).

When to use: a person must choose exactly one of a small set of mutually
exclusive options that should all be visible at once.
When NOT to use: many options or tight space (use `ki-select`), independent
on/off settings (use `ki-checkbox` or `ki-switch`), multiple selection, or
authored selection on options; set this group's `value` instead.

Examples:

The group owns the `label` (mandatory; the radiogroup's accessible name), the form `name` and the selected `value`; user selection dispatches a composed `change` event, while programmatic `value` writes stay silent:

```html
<ki-radio-group label="Delivery speed" name="delivery" value="standard">
  <ki-radio value="standard">Standard (3–5 days)</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="express">Express (1–2 days)</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="overnight">Overnight</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

Without an initial `value` the group renders unselected and operable; `required` blocks form submission through the platform `valueMissing` validity until an option is chosen:

```html
<form>
  <ki-radio-group label="Billing cycle" name="cycle" required>
    <ki-radio value="monthly">Monthly</ki-radio>
    <ki-radio value="yearly">Yearly</ki-radio>
  </ki-radio-group>
  <ki-button variant="primary">Continue</ki-button>
</form>
```

A `disabled` group is skipped in Tab order and contributes no form entry; do not use it for pending or loading semantics:

```html
<ki-radio-group label="Region" name="region" value="eu" disabled>
  <ki-radio value="eu">Europe</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="us">United States</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

When the question is already written on the page, name the group from it with `aria-labelledby` on the host and omit `label`, so the question is shown and read once:

```html
<h2 id="plan-question">Which plan suits you?</h2>
<ki-radio-group aria-labelledby="plan-question" name="plan">
  <ki-radio value="basic">Basic</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="pro">Pro</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

When the layout makes the question obvious but the group still needs its own name, `label-hidden` hides the label from view and from reading order; it stays the group's accessible name and is announced once:

```html
<ki-radio-group label="Your answer" label-hidden name="answer">
  <ki-radio value="yes">Yes</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="no">No</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

## An error from the application

Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on the submitted
choice. The group is invalid, blocks its form and is announced as invalid at
once. Choosing another option withdraws the error. Remove the attribute when
a new attempt starts: setting the same text again while it is still set
shows nothing.

```html
<ki-radio-group label="Plan" name="plan" value="team" custom-error="The Team plan is sold out this month.">
  <ki-radio value="solo">Solo</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="team">Team</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

Attributes:
- `custom-error` (string | undefined): An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the submitted choice ("This plan is sold out"). While it holds text the group is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help text at once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting when the person chooses another option, or when the form is reset, so it never blocks the corrected answer. It outranks `error-text` and an error set with `setCustomValidity`. When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts. When NOT to use: do not use it for a `required` group left without a choice; `error-text` words that. Setting the same text again while the prop still holds it shows nothing: remove it first, then set it again.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Makes the whole group unavailable, skips it in Tab order and removes its form entry. When NOT to use: do not use disabled for pending/loading semantics.
- `error-text` (string | undefined): Message shown in place of the help text once a `required` group is left without a choice, and its `validationMessage` ("Choose a plan"). Without it the browser's own message shows, in the browser's language. An error set with `custom-error` or `setCustomValidity` outranks it. When NOT to use: do not use it for server-side or cross-field errors; set `custom-error` or call `setCustomValidity` for those.
- `help-text` (string | undefined): One line of help under the options, read with the group as its description: what the choice decides. While an error shows, the error takes its place. When NOT to use: do not repeat the label, and do not use it for error messages; use `error-text`.
- `label` (string, required): Visible label and accessible-name source for the radiogroup. When NOT to use: do not omit it unless the host's `aria-labelledby` names the group from the page; a group with neither fails accessibility gates. Naming from the page: set `aria-labelledby` on the host to the ids of elements in the same document or shadow root, such as the heading that already asks the question. The group then takes its name from them, followed by its own `label` and `label-hint` when set. The ids are read when the group renders and whenever the attribute changes. When to use: the question is written on the page above the options; omit `label` so the question is not shown, or read, twice. When NOT to use: do not reference elements inside another component's shadow root, which an id reference cannot reach.
- `label-hidden` (boolean, default false): Hides the `label` (and its hint) from view and from reading order while it stays the radiogroup's accessible name, so a screen reader announces it once, as the group's name. When to use: the layout already makes the question obvious to sighted people (a heading in a card, an icon row) but the group still needs a name of its own. When NOT to use: do not hide a label that repeats a question already on the page; point `aria-labelledby` at that question instead. Do not hide the only description of what a choice decides; that is `help-text`.
- `label-hint` (string | undefined): Short text shown after the group label and read with it as part of the radiogroup name, so people know before submitting whether to choose: "(optional)" on the few optional questions of a mostly required form, or "(required)" the other way round, in the page's own language. It changes no validation; set `required` for that, and keep the two consistent. When NOT to use: do not put what the choice decides in it (use `help-text`), errors (use `error-text`), or a repeat of the label.
- `name` (string | undefined): Form-data key for the selected option's value. Omit when the group should not contribute a form entry. When NOT to use: do not put `name` on `ki-radio` options; their internal native inputs are intentionally unnamed.
- `required` (boolean, default false): Requires one selected option for form submission. The group uses platform `valueMissing` from its internal native radio inputs. When NOT to use: do not use required when no answer is acceptable.
- `size` ("md" | "sm", default 'md'): Token-backed size of every `ki-radio` the group holds: the circle is 18 or 20px in onmars, and `sm` takes the smaller option label (13/20, 8px away). The group decides for all its options; the group's own label, help and error keep their size. An unrecognized value matches no style rule and keeps the medium metrics. When to use: match the size of the text and controls around the group. When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead, which composes with every size.
- `value` (string, default ''): Projection of the current selection. The initial attribute selects the first matching option; unmatched values leave the group unselected and operable. Assigning the property updates selection silently. When NOT to use: never author selection on `ki-radio`; set this value.

Slots:
- (default): `ki-radio` options. Document order is navigation order.

Parts:
- `error`: Error line shown in place of the help text while the group is invalid after the person submitted; a polite live region, starting with a decorative error symbol.
- `help`: Help line under the options, read as the radiogroup description.
- `label`: Visible group label and accessible-name source.
- `label-hint`: The `label-hint` text after the group label text, inside the label and part of the radiogroup's accessible name; rendered only while a hint is set.

Events:
- `change` (Event): Fired once after the user selects a different radio, composed across the shadow boundary; `value` is already current when listeners run. `click()` on a `ki-radio` from a script selects it like a native radio: one `input`, then one `change`. When to use: react to the committed choice. When NOT to use: do not expect it for programmatic `value` writes, which are silent.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-radio-group-gap`: dimension used by the radio group component for gap.
- `--ki-radio-group-label-font-size`: dimension used by the radio group component for label font size.
- `--ki-radio-group-label-font-weight`: font weight used by the radio group component for label font weight.
- `--ki-radio-group-label-hint-fg`: color used by the radio group component for the label hint after the label text (spec 047: the supporting-text role, a declared a11y deviation from the MarsUI Input_label support text Text/low_em, which reads 2.8-3.13:1 on the onmars light surfaces; under more contrast it strengthens with every other supporting text).
- `--ki-radio-group-label-hint-gap`: dimension used by the radio group component for the gap between the label text and the label hint (MarsUI Input_label: Space/xs 4px).
- `--ki-radio-group-label-line-height`: dimension used by the radio group component for label line height (closest measured analogue: Radio_label sm 13/20; no group-title master exists — low-confidence refinement).
- `--ki-radio-sm-control-size`: dimension used by the radio component for the sm circle (Radio 10053:1943 sm: 18px in a 20px cell).
- `--ki-radio-sm-dot-size`: dimension used by the radio component for the sm dot (Radio 10053:1943 sm: 8px, as at md).
- `--ki-radio-sm-gap`: dimension used by the radio component for the sm gap between control and label (Radio-label 10100:3931 sm binds Space/md, 8px; spec 050 D4).
- `--ki-radio-sm-label-font-size`: dimension used by the radio component for the sm label font size (Radio-label 10100:3931 sm: UI/para 13/20; spec 050 D4).
- `--ki-radio-sm-label-line-height`: dimension used by the radio component for the sm label line height (Radio-label 10100:3931 sm: UI/para 13/20).
- `--ki-radio-sm-min-target`: dimension used by the radio component for the sm min target: 24px, the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum, above the master's 20px cell.
- `--ki-text-danger-high-em`: semantic color for text danger high em.
- `--ki-text-high-em`: semantic color for text high em.
- `--ki-text-med-em`: semantic color for text med em.
- `--ki-text-supporting`: Supporting text of an enabled control: field labels, placeholders, list secondary lines, quiet button labels and unselected tabs. A role, distinct from the med-em emphasis step it resolves to, so a mode can strengthen enabled supporting text without touching the disabled ink that also draws from med-em (directly, or through text.muted).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-normal`: semantic font weight for typography weight body normal.

### ki-rating

Displays a score or collects one choice on a small rating scale.

When to use: Show an average review score in readonly mode or ask people to rate
an answer, experience, or product on a small scale.
When NOT to use: Use message actions for yes/no feedback and a slider for a
continuous or large numeric range.

Examples:

# Rating usage

## Display a review average

```html
<ki-rating readonly label="Average review score" value="4.3"></ki-rating>
```

The text reads 4.3. The glyphs fill to 4.5 and assistive technology receives one image named “Rated 4.3 out of 5”.

## Collect answer feedback

```html
<form>
  <ki-rating
    label="How useful was this answer?"
    name="usefulness"
    precision="0.5"
    required
  ></ki-rating>
  <button>Submit feedback</button>
</form>
```

A choice of 2.5 submits as `usefulness=2.5`. A form reset restores the starting value. Subscribe to `ki-change` for a user's changed choice and read its numeric `detail.value`.

## Use a different glyph

```js
import '@kimen/elements/icons/heart';
```

```html
<ki-rating
  label="How much did you enjoy the experience?"
  icon-name="heart"
  option-singular-label="{value} heart"
  option-label="{value} hearts"
></ki-rating>
```

Attributes:
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Makes an editable rating unavailable and excludes it from form submission.
- `icon-name` (string, default 'star'): Lucide icon name. Import custom names before mounting. Unavailable names use star.
- `label` (string, required): Visible question in input mode and accessible context in read-only mode. Always supply it.
- `max` (number, default 5, minimum 1, maximum 10): Highest score and number of glyphs. Use a whole number from 1 to 10.
- `name` (string | undefined): Form field name for a selected editable score.
- `option-label` (string, default '{value} stars'): Accessible name pattern for the other choices. Use {value} for the choice.
- `option-singular-label` (string, default '{value} star'): Accessible name pattern for the one-star choice. Use {value} for the choice.
- `precision` (number, default 1): Choose 1 for whole steps or 0.5 for half steps. Other inputs use whole steps.
- `rated-label` (string, default 'Rated {value} out of {max}'): Accessible name pattern for the read-only image. Use {value} and {max} for the scores.
- `readonly` (boolean, default false): Displays a score without editing or submitting it.
- `required` (boolean, default false): Requires an editable score before the form can be submitted.
- `required-message` (string, default 'Select a rating.'): Validation message for an unanswered required rating.
- `score-label` (string, default '{value} of {max}'): Visible score pattern in input mode. Use {value} and {max} for the scores.
- `value` (number, default 0, minimum 0, maximum 10): Current score. Zero means unanswered in input mode. Editable scores use the nearest allowed step. Read-only scores retain their decimal precision.

Slots: none

Parts:
- `choice`: Native radio target for one selectable score.
- `glyph`: Decorative artwork for one rating step.
- `label`: Visible question above the editable scale.
- `scale`: Read-only score image or editable radio group.
- `score`: Visible numeric score.

Events:
- `ki-change` (CustomEvent<{ value: number }>): Fires once when a person changes the selection. The detail contains the numeric value.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-rating-disabled-fg`: Glyph ink while the rating is unavailable.
- `--ki-rating-gap`: Space between rating glyphs or targets.
- `--ki-rating-hover-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter for the hovered choice.
- `--ki-rating-hover-bg`: Surface of the choice under the pointer.
- `--ki-rating-hover-bg-image`: Optional image over the hovered choice surface.
- `--ki-rating-label-bg`: Backdrop of the visible question.
- `--ki-rating-label-fg`: Ink of the visible question.
- `--ki-rating-label-gap`: Space between the question and scale.
- `--ki-rating-off-bg`: Backdrop of an outlined glyph.
- `--ki-rating-off-fg`: Ink of an outlined glyph.
- `--ki-rating-on-bg`: Backdrop of a filled glyph.
- `--ki-rating-on-fg`: Ink of a filled glyph.
- `--ki-rating-score-bg`: Backdrop of the visible score.
- `--ki-rating-score-fg`: Ink of the visible score.
- `--ki-rating-score-gap`: Space between the glyphs and visible score.
- `--ki-rating-size`: Size of a rating glyph.
- `--ki-rating-target-radius`: Corners of the interactive target.
- `--ki-rating-target-size`: Default whole-step target size.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography line height body 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-medium`: semantic font weight for typography weight body medium.

### ki-reasoning

A disclosure for the assistant's progress or plan, with a localized summary.

When to use: present assistant-supplied steps, progress or a completed plan alongside the answer.
When NOT to use: hide the answer or controls the user needs to complete a task. Use a general disclosure for unrelated content.

Examples:

# Using ki-reasoning

## Show a plan while it develops

```html
<ki-reasoning open>
  <ol>
    <li>Check the inputs.</li>
  </ol>
</ki-reasoning>
```

Add subsequent list items as the assistant produces them. The default state is
collapsed. Set `open` to show the steps immediately.

## Show the elapsed time after completion

```html
<ki-reasoning status="done" duration="12000">
  <ol>
    <li>Check the inputs.</li>
    <li>Compare the available outcomes.</li>
  </ol>
</ki-reasoning>
```

The summary reads “Thought for 12 seconds.” Omit `duration` if it is unavailable.

## Localize the summary

```html
<ki-reasoning
  lang="es"
  status="done"
  duration="1000"
  thinking-label="Pensando…"
  done-label="Listo"
  singular-duration-label="Pensó durante {seconds} segundo"
  duration-label="Pensó durante {seconds} segundos"
>
  <ol>
    <li>Revisar los datos de entrada.</li>
  </ol>
</ki-reasoning>
```

## Report disclosure changes in a guarded surface

Declare the action in the surface and reference it on the disclosure. The
renderer binds it to the catalog's `ki-toggle` event.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "actions": ["record-plan-toggle"],
  "root": {
    "component": "ki-reasoning",
    "props": { "status": "done", "duration": 12000 },
    "action": "record-plan-toggle",
    "slots": { "": ["Check the inputs and compare the outcomes."] }
  }
}
```

## Custom-elements entry point

```ts
import { defineCustomElement } from '@kimen/elements/ki-reasoning';

defineCustomElement();
```

Attributes:
- `done-label` (string, default 'Thought'): Summary text when done and elapsed time is unavailable.
- `duration` (number | undefined): Optional elapsed milliseconds. Done displays finite, nonnegative values rounded to seconds.
- `duration-label` (string, default 'Thought for {seconds} seconds'): Summary template for zero or multiple elapsed seconds. The {seconds} placeholder receives the rounded time.
- `open` (boolean, default false): Whether the disclosure shows its steps. Native toggles update this reflected property.
- `singular-duration-label` (string, default 'Thought for {seconds} second'): Summary template for one elapsed second. The {seconds} placeholder receives the rounded time.
- `status` ("done" | "thinking", default 'thinking'): Use thinking while steps arrive and done once the assistant finishes.
- `thinking-label` (string, default 'Thinking…'): Summary text while the assistant is thinking.

Slots:
- (default): Supporting content shown when expanded, such as an ordered list of steps supplied by the application.

Parts:
- `body`: The slotted content area with the inline-start rule.
- `summary`: The native disclosure control that shows the current status.

Events:
- `ki-toggle` (CustomEvent<KiReasoningToggleDetail>): Emitted after a native disclosure toggle. Setting open from the application is silent.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-easing-standard`: Standard interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-reasoning-backdrop-filter`: Complete filter behind the disclosure. None keeps the backdrop clear.
- `--ki-reasoning-bg`: Fill behind the disclosure summary and its steps.
- `--ki-reasoning-bg-image`: Optional image painted over the disclosure fill.
- `--ki-reasoning-body-gap`: Block spacing between the summary and the step content.
- `--ki-reasoning-body-indent`: Inline spacing between the rule and the content.
- `--ki-reasoning-border`: Ink of the decorative rule at the inline start of the steps.
- `--ki-reasoning-border-width`: Width of the steps rule.
- `--ki-reasoning-fg`: Medium-emphasis ink for the disclosure summary and its steps.
- `--ki-reasoning-list-indent`: Inline space for markers on a slotted list.
- `--ki-reasoning-shimmer-duration`: Period of the thinking shimmer.
- `--ki-reasoning-shimmer-easing`: Easing into and out of the thinking highlight.
- `--ki-reasoning-shimmer-fg`: Readable highlight at the midpoint of the thinking shimmer.
- `--ki-reasoning-summary-gap`: Space between the summary text and glyphs and between separate step blocks.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-para`: semantic dimension for typography line height para.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-visually-hidden-size`: Nonzero edge for clipped text available to assistive technology.

### ki-relative-time

Displays the elapsed or remaining time for a timestamp in the reader's language.

When to use: For timestamps whose distance from the present matters, such as timeline entries or recent changes.
When NOT to use: For an interactive countdown or a date that should always show an absolute value.

Examples:

# Format a relative timestamp

Use `sync` to update the visible wording as time passes. A threshold of
86,400 seconds switches to the formatted timestamp at one day's distance.
Assistive technology and the tooltip expose the absolute timestamp throughout.

```html
<ki-relative-time date="2026-11-19T08:41:00Z" sync threshold="86400"></ki-relative-time>
```

Attributes:
- `date` (string | undefined): ISO calendar date or date-time. A timestamp without an offset uses local time.
- `numeric` ("always" | "auto", default 'auto'): Auto can show words such as yesterday. Always uses a number.
- `sync` (boolean, default false): Refresh the visible wording as the clock crosses a formatting boundary.
- `threshold` (number | undefined, minimum 0): Display an absolute timestamp when the distance reaches this many seconds. Omit to keep relative wording at any distance.

Slots: none

Parts: none

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-relative-time-font-family`: Default body font family for ki-relative-time on a bare page.

### ki-scroller
