```html
<ki-textarea label="Accepted policy" value="Version 2.1, accepted 2026-05-02." readonly></ki-textarea>
<ki-textarea label="Legacy notes" value="Migrated from v1." disabled></ki-textarea>
```

## Appearance and character limits

Set `appearance` to `outlined` for a full border or `filled` for a
tinted surface with a bottom indicator. Both keep the label above the field.
The default appearance follows the theme.

`minlength` uses native minimum-length validation. The textarea keeps edits
past `maxlength` and blocks submission until the value fits. With a maximum,
`show-count` adds the current length to the field description and announces
when the user reaches or exceeds the limit. Use `maxlength-error-text` to
localize the default length error.

```html
<ki-textarea label="Bio" appearance="outlined" minlength="3" maxlength="24" show-count help-text="Keep it short" value="Designer and front-end developer"></ki-textarea>
<ki-textarea label="Short bio" appearance="filled" maxlength="12" show-count help-text="Keep it short" value="Designs generative interfaces."></ki-textarea>
```

## An error from the application

Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on the submitted text,
such as a moderation check. The field is invalid, blocks its form and is
announced as invalid at once. The person's next keystroke withdraws the
error. Remove the attribute when a new attempt starts: setting the same text
again while it is still set shows nothing.

```html
<ki-textarea label="Bio" name="bio" value="Call me at 555-0100" custom-error="Remove the phone number from your bio."></ki-textarea>
```

Attributes:
- `appearance` ("default" | "filled" | "outlined" | undefined, default 'default'): Field appearance. `default` uses the current theme, `outlined` draws a full border, and `filled` uses a tinted surface and bottom indicator. The visible label stays above the field. When to use: set an explicit appearance when fields must share a shape across themes.
- `autocomplete` (string | undefined): Autofill detail token forwarded to the native textarea. When to use: expose entry purpose such as `street-address` when available. When NOT to use: omit when no valid autofill purpose applies.
- `custom-error` (string | undefined): An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the submitted text ("This title is taken"). While it holds text the field is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help text at once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting at the person's next change of the text, or when the form is reset, so it never blocks the corrected answer. It outranks `error-text` and an error set with `setCustomValidity`. When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts. When NOT to use: do not use it for `required` or a length limit the field enforces itself; `error-text` words those. Setting the same text again while the prop still holds it shows nothing: remove it first, then set it again.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Disables editing, focus, validation and form-data contribution. When to use: make a field temporarily unavailable. When NOT to use: do not use disabled for readonly review text that should submit.
- `error-text` (string | undefined): Message shown in place of the help text once the person's answer fails a constraint (`required` or a length limit), and the field's `validationMessage`. Say how to fix the answer. Without it the browser's own message shows, in the browser's language. An error set with `custom-error` or `setCustomValidity` outranks it. When NOT to use: do not use it for server-side or cross-field errors; set `custom-error` or call `setCustomValidity` for those.
- `help-text` (string | undefined): One line of help under the field, read with it as its description: what to write, or how long. While an error shows, the error takes its place. When NOT to use: do not repeat the label, and do not use it for error messages; use `error-text`.
- `label` (string, required): Visible label rendered by the component and used as the accessible name. When to use: always provide a concise label for the requested long-form text. When NOT to use: do not substitute placeholder text for the label.
- `label-hint` (string | undefined): Short text shown after the label and read with it as part of the field's name, so people know before submitting whether to answer: "(optional)" on the few optional fields of a mostly required form, or "(required)" the other way round, in the page's own language. It changes no validation; set `required` for that, and keep the two consistent. When NOT to use: do not put instructions or length limits in it (use `help-text`), errors (use `error-text`), or a repeat of the label.
- `maxlength` (number | undefined, minimum 0, maximum 2147483647): Soft maximum in UTF-16 code units. Longer user edits and assigned values are preserved and fail form validation with `validity.tooLong`. When to use: let people revise an over-limit draft without losing text.
- `maxlength-error-text` (string | undefined, default 'Shorten the text to fit the character limit.'): Localized message for an over-limit value. `error-text` and `setCustomValidity()` take precedence. When to use: translate the soft maximum message for the page language.
- `minlength` (number | undefined, minimum 0, maximum 2147483647): Native minimum length in UTF-16 code units for a nonempty user edit. When to use: require a minimum number of characters in an answer.
- `name` (string | undefined): Form-data key used when the textarea submits with a form. When to use: provide for fields whose text must be included in FormData. When NOT to use: omit for display-only or client-only fields.
- `placeholder` (string | undefined): Hint shown while the textarea is empty. When to use: add an example or short formatting hint. When NOT to use: do not use placeholder as the accessible name or required instruction.
- `readonly` (boolean, default false): Makes the textarea focusable and selectable while rejecting edits. When to use: show submitted or policy text that should still be included in form data. When NOT to use: do not use readonly to remove a field from submission; use disabled.
- `required` (boolean, default false): Requires a non-empty value before form submission. When to use: mark mandatory long-form text. When NOT to use: do not pair with `readonly` expecting it to block; readonly fields are validation exempt like native textareas.
- `rows` (number, default 2): Visible line count. Invalid, non-numeric, zero, or negative values fall back to 2; no auto-grow or user resize handle exists in v1. When to use: set the stable multiline height needed by the layout. When NOT to use: do not use rows as a responsive size axis.
- `show-count` (boolean | undefined, default false): Shows the current count and maximum next to the help or error text and announces reaching or exceeding the limit. Requires `maxlength`. When to use: give people feedback while writing to a limit.
- `size` ("lg" | "md" | "sm" | "xl" | "xs", default 'md'): Token-backed field size (`--ki-textarea-{size}-*` tokens): padding, radius and text; the label and help text follow in three steps. The height stays `rows` lines. An unrecognized value matches no style rule and keeps the medium metrics. When to use: match the size of the fields around it. When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead, which composes with every size.
- `value` (string, default ''): Live current text. The `value` attribute declares the reset default; element text content is ignored. Programmatic assignments replace the display and emit no events. When to use: preload or read free-form text, line breaks included. When NOT to use: do not put initial text between the element tags.

Slots: none

Parts:
- `count`: Current character count and maximum at the end of the field message row.
- `error`: Error line shown in place of the help text while the field is invalid after the person answered or submitted; a polite live region, starting with a decorative error symbol.
- `field`: The enclosure wrapper.
- `help`: Help line under the field, read as the field's description.
- `label`: Rendered visible label and accessible-name source.
- `label-hint`: The `label-hint` text after the label text, inside the label and part of the accessible name; rendered only while a hint is set.
- `textarea`: Internal native multiline control.

Events:
- `change` (Event): Fired when the user commits an edited value (on blur, with native textarea timing), composed across the shadow boundary; `value` is already current when listeners run. When to use: react to a committed value. When NOT to use: do not use it for per-keystroke updates; the native `input` event carries those.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-control-offset`: Added to the block size of every scaled control and row (button, icon button, field, select, textarea, option, list item, tab). Components floor the result at ki.size.target-min.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-input-appearance-border-width`: Resting stroke width of both explicit text field appearances.
- `--ki-input-count-bg`: Resting character count surface over the surrounding page.
- `--ki-input-count-fg`: Character count when the value fits the maximum.
- `--ki-input-count-over-bg`: Over-limit character count surface over the surrounding page.
- `--ki-input-count-over-fg`: Character count when the value exceeds the maximum.
- `--ki-input-filled-backdrop-filter`: Optional backdrop filter of a filled field.
- `--ki-input-filled-bg`: Surface of a filled text field.
- `--ki-input-filled-bg-image`: Optional background image of a filled field.
- `--ki-input-filled-fg`: Entered text on a filled field.
- `--ki-input-filled-focus-width`: Stroke width of the block-end indicator while focused.
- `--ki-input-filled-indicator`: Continuous block-end edge of an enabled filled text field.
- `--ki-input-filled-placeholder-fg`: Placeholder on a filled field.
- `--ki-input-filled-radius`: Block-start corner radius of a filled text field.
- `--ki-input-label-gap`: dimension used by the input component for label gap.
- `--ki-input-outlined-bg`: Surface of an outlined text field.
- `--ki-input-outlined-border`: Full outline of an enabled outlined text field.
- `--ki-input-outlined-fg`: Entered text on an outlined field.
- `--ki-input-outlined-placeholder-fg`: Placeholder on an outlined field.
- `--ki-input-outlined-radius`: Corner radius of an outlined text field.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-text-danger-high-em`: semantic color for text danger high em.
- `--ki-text-supporting`: Supporting text of an enabled control: field labels, placeholders, list secondary lines, quiet button labels and unselected tabs. A role, distinct from the med-em emphasis step it resolves to, so a mode can strengthen enabled supporting text without touching the disabled ink that also draws from med-em (directly, or through text.muted).
- `--ki-textarea-border-block-end-width`: dimension used by the textarea component for border block end width.
- `--ki-textarea-border-block-start-width`: dimension used by the textarea component for border block start width.
- `--ki-textarea-border-inline-end-width`: dimension used by the textarea component for border inline end width.
- `--ki-textarea-border-inline-start-width`: dimension used by the textarea component for border inline start width.
- `--ki-textarea-disabled-bg`: color used by the textarea component for disabled background (MarsUI Surface/disabled_base_em Gray/100; aligned with ki-input).
- `--ki-textarea-disabled-border`: color used by the textarea component for disabled border.
- `--ki-textarea-disabled-fg`: color used by the textarea component for disabled foreground.
- `--ki-textarea-disabled-label-fg`: color used by the textarea component for disabled label foreground.
- `--ki-textarea-disabled-placeholder-fg`: color used by the textarea component for disabled placeholder foreground.
- `--ki-textarea-focus-bg`: color used by the textarea component for focus background (MarsUI active fill switches to white / dark s2 — modeled with the scheme ladder s0).
- `--ki-textarea-focus-fg`: color used by the textarea component for focus foreground.
- `--ki-textarea-focus-label-fg`: color used by the textarea component for focus label foreground (MarsUI label is Text/med_em in every non-disabled state; matches ki-input).
- `--ki-textarea-focus-placeholder-fg`: color used by the textarea component for focus placeholder foreground (Text/med_em — a declared a11y deviation from the MarsUI placeholder binding Text/low_em, which reads 2.66-3.13:1 on the light field fills; a placeholder is not the accessible name but it is still text, so the contrast gate holds it to 4.5:1).
- `--ki-textarea-focus-ring-color`: color used by the textarea component for focus ring color.
- `--ki-textarea-focus-ring-offset`: dimension used by the textarea component for focus ring offset.
- `--ki-textarea-focus-ring-shadow`: shadow used by the textarea component for the focus ring glow (MarsUI Focus/primary: 3px spread ring at 20% — see ki.focus.primary. specs/002-ki-button/design-extraction.md §2.5 recorded 40%, having read the alpha off the Dark canvas mode, same double mechanism as ki-button: glow plus the opaque indicator).
- `--ki-textarea-focus-ring-width`: dimension used by the textarea component for focus ring width.
- `--ki-textarea-font-size`: dimension used by the textarea component for font size.
- `--ki-textarea-font-size-touch`: dimension used by the textarea component for the text a person types under a coarse primary pointer: 16px, under which Safari on iOS zooms the page into the focused field (spec 048). The onmars type scale has no 16px step.
- `--ki-textarea-font-weight`: font weight used by the textarea component for font weight.
- `--ki-textarea-hover-bg`: color used by the textarea component for hover background (MarsUI hover = s2 + Black/3 overlay; s3 is the nearest token).
- `--ki-textarea-hover-border`: color used by the textarea component for hover border.
- `--ki-textarea-hover-fg`: color used by the textarea component for hover foreground.
- `--ki-textarea-hover-label-fg`: color used by the textarea component for hover label foreground (MarsUI label is Text/med_em in every non-disabled state; matches ki-input).
- `--ki-textarea-hover-placeholder-fg`: color used by the textarea component for hover placeholder foreground (Text/med_em — a declared a11y deviation from the MarsUI placeholder binding Text/low_em, which reads 2.66-3.13:1 on the light field fills; a placeholder is not the accessible name but it is still text, so the contrast gate holds it to 4.5:1).
- `--ki-textarea-invalid-bg`: color used by the textarea component for invalid background (MarsUI danger keeps the white active fill — no tinted slab; ring and hint carry the signal).
- `--ki-textarea-invalid-border`: color used by the textarea component for invalid border.
- `--ki-textarea-invalid-fg`: color used by the textarea component for invalid foreground.
- `--ki-textarea-invalid-label-fg`: color used by the textarea component for invalid label foreground (MarsUI label is Text/med_em in every non-disabled state; matches ki-input).
- `--ki-textarea-invalid-placeholder-fg`: color used by the textarea component for invalid placeholder foreground (Text/med_em — a declared a11y deviation from the MarsUI placeholder binding Text/low_em, which reads 2.66-3.13:1 on the light field fills; a placeholder is not the accessible name but it is still text, so the contrast gate holds it to 4.5:1).
- `--ki-textarea-invalid-ring`: shadow used by the textarea component for the persistent invalid ring (MarsUI Focus/danger: 3px danger-500 alpha spread; applied as box-shadow while :state(user-invalid)).
- `--ki-textarea-label-font-size`: dimension used by the textarea component for label font size (MarsUI UI/Para/medium: body_1 13px).
- `--ki-textarea-label-font-weight`: font weight used by the textarea component for label font weight.
- `--ki-textarea-label-gap`: dimension used by the textarea component for label gap.
- `--ki-textarea-label-hint-fg`: color used by the textarea component for the label hint after the label text (spec 047: the supporting-text role, a declared a11y deviation from the MarsUI Input_label support text Text/low_em, which reads 2.8-3.13:1 on the onmars light surfaces; under more contrast it strengthens with every other supporting text).
- `--ki-textarea-label-hint-gap`: dimension used by the textarea component for the gap between the label text and the label hint (MarsUI Input_label: Space/xs 4px).
- `--ki-textarea-label-line-height`: dimension used by the textarea component for label line height (MarsUI line_height/para 20px).
- `--ki-textarea-label-padding-inline`: dimension used by the textarea component for label padding inline (MarsUI Input_label row 2px inset aligning the label ink with the cell radius; matches ki-input).
- `--ki-textarea-lg-font-size`: dimension used by the textarea component for lg font size: body-2 (Input-cell 8016:286 Type=textarea lg).
- `--ki-textarea-lg-label-font-size`: dimension used by the textarea component for the lg label font size: the Input-label 12021:6068 lg step, body-2 (spec 050 D4).
- `--ki-textarea-lg-label-line-height`: dimension used by the textarea component for the lg label line height (body-2, Input-label lg; spec 050 D4).
- `--ki-textarea-lg-line-height`: dimension used by the textarea component for lg line height (body-2, Input-cell 8016:286 Type=textarea lg).
- `--ki-textarea-lg-padding-block`: dimension used by the textarea component for lg padding block (Input-cell 8016:286 Type=textarea lg binds Space/lg, 10px).
- `--ki-textarea-lg-padding-inline`: dimension used by the textarea component for lg padding inline (Input-cell 8016:286 Type=textarea lg binds Space/xl, 12px).
- `--ki-textarea-lg-radius`: dimension used by the textarea component for lg radius (Input-cell 8016:286 Type=textarea lg binds Radius/small-component/lg).
- `--ki-textarea-line-height`: dimension used by the textarea component for line height.
- `--ki-textarea-min-target`: dimension used by the textarea component for min target.
- `--ki-textarea-padding-block`: dimension used by the textarea component for padding block (Input-cell textarea md 8018:176: Space/md 8px).
- `--ki-textarea-padding-inline`: dimension used by the textarea component for padding inline (MarsUI 96px md textarea: 12px ink inset).
- `--ki-textarea-radius`: dimension used by the textarea component for radius (MarsUI Radius/component/radius_md 10px for the md size; component ramp so personality modes reach it).
- `--ki-textarea-readonly-bg`: color used by the textarea component for readonly background.
- `--ki-textarea-readonly-border`: color used by the textarea component for readonly border.
- `--ki-textarea-readonly-fg`: color used by the textarea component for readonly foreground.

- `--ki-textarea-readonly-placeholder-fg`: color used by the textarea component for readonly placeholder foreground (Text/med_em — a declared a11y deviation from the MarsUI placeholder binding Text/low_em, which reads 2.66-3.13:1 on the light field fills; a placeholder is not the accessible name but it is still text, so the contrast gate holds it to 4.5:1).

### ki-time-input

A time-of-day field with locale-aware typing and suggested slots. The shadow root keeps the combobox and listbox in the same accessibility ID scope. The host owns native form participation.

When to use: collect an exact time of day or offer regular appointment slots.
Provide a visible label and set bounding times when the schedule is limited.
When NOT to use: durations, dates or timestamps. Pair with a date field when
the day matters. Timezone conversion belongs to the application.

Examples:

Display 12-hour time for a US English form and keep the value in canonical
24-hour form. The person can type any time from 08:00 through 18:00, including
minutes between the half-hour suggestions.

```html
<ki-time-input
  lang="en-US"
  label="Pickup time"
  name="pickup"
  required
  value="09:30"
  min="08:00"
  max="18:00"
  step="30"
  help-text="Store hours"
  time-zone="America/New_York"
  error-text="Choose a pickup time between 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM."
></ki-time-input>
```

Set the language on a surrounding element to localize the time, and pass
translated labels for the suggestion controls. Touch density increases the
field and suggestion hit areas.

```html
<div lang="es-ES" data-ki-density="touch">
  <ki-time-input
    label="Hora de la cita"
    picker-label="Elige una hora"
    list-label="Horas sugeridas"
    error-text="Introduce una hora válida."
  ></ki-time-input>
</div>
```

## An error from the application

Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on the submitted time,
such as a booking check. The field is invalid, blocks its form and is
announced as invalid at once. The person's next edit or pick of a time
withdraws the error. Remove the attribute when a new attempt starts: setting
the same text again while it is still set shows nothing.

```html
<ki-time-input label="Start time" name="start" lang="en-GB" value="09:30" custom-error="That slot was just booked."></ki-time-input>
```

Attributes:
- `custom-error` (string | undefined): An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the submitted time ("That slot was just booked"). While it holds text the field is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help text at once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting at the person's next edit or pick of a time, or when the form is reset, so it never blocks the corrected answer. It outranks `error-text` and an error set with `setCustomValidity`. When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts. When NOT to use: do not use it for `required`, the bounds or unreadable text, which the field reports itself; `error-text` words those. Setting the same text again while the prop still holds it shows nothing: remove it first, then set it again.
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Disables typing, suggestions and form participation.
- `error-text` (string | undefined): Validation message to show after blur or a blocked form submission. A `custom-error` outranks it.
- `help-text` (string | undefined): Guidance read with the field until a validation error replaces it.
- `invalid-time-text` (string, default 'Enter a valid time within the allowed range.'): Fallback validation message for invalid time syntax or bounds.
- `label` (string, required): Visible text naming the time field. Provide it for every use.
- `list-label` (string, default 'Suggested times'): Accessible name of the suggestion listbox.
- `max` (string | undefined): Latest allowed wall-clock time in HH:mm, inclusive.
- `min` (string | undefined): Earliest allowed wall-clock time in HH:mm, inclusive.
- `name` (string | undefined): Name under which the canonical time is submitted.
- `picker-label` (string, default 'Choose time'): Accessible name of the button that opens suggestions.
- `required` (boolean, default false): Empty values block form submission when true.
- `step` (number, default 30): Suggested slot interval in whole minutes. Typed times keep their exact minutes.
- `time-zone` (string | undefined): IANA timezone shown alongside help. Does not change wall-clock values.
- `value` (string, default ''): Committed wall-clock time in HH:mm, or empty. The attribute sets the form reset value.

Slots:
- `start`: Optional leading adornment, outside the input's accessible name.

Parts:
- `error`: Polite validation message that replaces help.
- `field`: Field enclosure and anchor for the suggestions.
- `help`: Help and timezone describing the field.
- `input`: Editable text combobox.
- `label`: Visible label naming the editable combobox.
- `listbox`: Scrollable list of suggested times.
- `option`: Individual suggested time.
- `trigger`: Button that opens suggested times.

Events:
- `ki-change` (CustomEvent<KiTimeInputChangeDetail>): Emitted when a person commits a different canonical time or clears it.
- `change` (Event): Native-style composed event for a changed user commit.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-control-offset`: Added to the block size of every scaled control and row (button, icon button, field, select, textarea, option, list item, tab). Components floor the result at ki.size.target-min.
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-input-border-block-end-width`: dimension used by the input component for border block end width.
- `--ki-input-border-block-start-width`: dimension used by the input component for border block start width.
- `--ki-input-border-inline-end-width`: dimension used by the input component for border inline end width.
- `--ki-input-border-inline-start-width`: dimension used by the input component for border inline start width.
- `--ki-input-disabled-bg`: color used by the input component for disabled background.
- `--ki-input-disabled-border`: color used by the input component for disabled border.
- `--ki-input-disabled-fg`: color used by the input component for disabled foreground (MarsUI disabled text Text/base_em; disabled cells are exempt from the contrast sweep).
- `--ki-input-disabled-label-fg`: color used by the input component for disabled label foreground.
- `--ki-input-focus-bg`: color used by the input component for focus background (MarsUI active state switches the fill to Surface/Special white / dark s2 — modeled with the scheme ladder s0).
- `--ki-input-focus-fg`: color used by the input component for focus foreground.
- `--ki-input-focus-label-fg`: color used by the input component for focus label foreground (MarsUI label is Text/med_em in every non-disabled state — active and danger included; the danger signal lives in the hint).
- `--ki-input-focus-ring-color`: color used by the input component for focus ring color.
- `--ki-input-focus-ring-offset`: dimension used by the input component for focus ring offset.
- `--ki-input-focus-ring-shadow`: shadow used by the input component for the focus ring glow (MarsUI Focus/primary: 3px spread ring at 20% — see ki.focus.primary. specs/002-ki-button/design-extraction.md §2.5 recorded 40%, having read the alpha off the Dark canvas mode, same double mechanism as ki-button: glow plus the opaque indicator).
- `--ki-input-focus-ring-width`: dimension used by the input component for focus ring width.
- `--ki-input-font-size`: dimension used by the input component for font size.
- `--ki-input-font-size-touch`: dimension used by the input component for the text a person types under a coarse primary pointer: 16px, under which Safari on iOS zooms the page into the focused field (spec 048). The onmars type scale has no 16px step.
- `--ki-input-font-weight`: font weight used by the input component for font weight.
- `--ki-input-gap`: dimension used by the input component for gap.
- `--ki-input-height`: dimension used by the input component for height (MarsUI Input_field md cell: min-height 40px; consume as min-block-size so the field can grow).
- `--ki-input-hover-bg`: color used by the input component for hover background (MarsUI hover = s2 + Black/3 overlay; s3 is the nearest token).
- `--ki-input-hover-border`: color used by the input component for hover border.
- `--ki-input-hover-fg`: color used by the input component for hover foreground.
- `--ki-input-hover-label-fg`: color used by the input component for hover label foreground (MarsUI label is Text/med_em in every non-disabled state — active and danger included; the danger signal lives in the hint).
- `--ki-input-icon-size`: dimension used by the input component for icon size.
- `--ki-input-invalid-bg`: color used by the input component for invalid background (MarsUI danger state keeps the white active fill; the ring and hint carry the signal).
- `--ki-input-invalid-border`: color used by the input component for invalid border.
- `--ki-input-invalid-fg`: color used by the input component for invalid foreground.
- `--ki-input-invalid-label-fg`: color used by the input component for invalid label foreground (MarsUI label is Text/med_em in every non-disabled state — active and danger included; the danger signal lives in the hint).
- `--ki-input-invalid-ring`: shadow used by the input component for the persistent invalid ring (MarsUI Focus/danger: 3px danger-500 alpha spread; applied as box-shadow while :state(user-invalid)).
- `--ki-input-label-font-size`: dimension used by the input component for label font size (MarsUI UI/Para/medium: body_1 13px).
- `--ki-input-label-font-weight`: font weight used by the input component for label font weight.
- `--ki-input-label-gap`: dimension used by the input component for label gap.
- `--ki-input-label-line-height`: dimension used by the input component for label line height (MarsUI line_height/para 20px).
- `--ki-input-label-padding-inline`: dimension used by the input component for label padding inline (MarsUI Input_label row 2px inset aligning the label ink with the cell radius).
- `--ki-input-line-height`: dimension used by the input component for line height.
- `--ki-input-padding-inline`: dimension used by the input component for padding inline.
- `--ki-input-radius`: dimension used by the input component for radius (MarsUI Radius/component/radius_md 10px, the md Input_cell binding; component ramp so personality modes reach it).
- `--ki-input-rest-bg`: color used by the input component for rest background (MarsUI Input_field rest fill Surface/s2: the fill identifies the field, not the outline).
- `--ki-input-rest-border`: color used by the input component for rest border.
- `--ki-input-rest-fg`: color used by the input component for rest foreground.
- `--ki-input-rest-label-fg`: color used by the input component for rest label foreground (MarsUI label is Text/med_em in every non-disabled state — active and danger included; the danger signal lives in the hint).
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-text-danger-high-em`: semantic color for text danger high em.
- `--ki-text-supporting`: Supporting text of an enabled control: field labels, placeholders, list secondary lines, quiet button labels and unselected tabs. A role, distinct from the med-em emphasis step it resolves to, so a mode can strengthen enabled supporting text without touching the disabled ink that also draws from med-em (directly, or through text.muted).
- `--ki-time-input-field-backdrop-filter`: Complete filter applied behind the surface.
- `--ki-time-input-field-bg-image`: Image painted over the surface background.
- `--ki-time-input-list-backdrop-filter`: Complete filter applied behind the surface.
- `--ki-time-input-list-bg`: Background of the suggested times list.
- `--ki-time-input-list-bg-image`: Image painted over the surface background.
- `--ki-time-input-list-border-color`: Border colour of the suggested times list.
- `--ki-time-input-list-border-width`: Border width of the suggested times list.
- `--ki-time-input-list-fg`: Text colour of the suggested times list.
- `--ki-time-input-list-max-height`: Maximum block size of the scrolling suggestions.
- `--ki-time-input-list-padding`: Padding on the inside edge of the suggested times list.
- `--ki-time-input-list-radius`: Corner radius of the suggested times list.
- `--ki-time-input-list-shadow`: Elevation of the suggested times list.
- `--ki-time-input-option-height`: Minimum block size of a suggestion at standard density.
- `--ki-time-input-option-hover-bg`: Background of a hovered suggestion.
- `--ki-time-input-option-hover-fg`: Text colour of a hovered suggestion.
- `--ki-time-input-option-padding-inline`: Inline padding of a suggestion.
- `--ki-time-input-option-radius`: Corner radius of a suggestion.
- `--ki-time-input-selected-bg`: Background of the committed suggestion.
- `--ki-time-input-selected-fg`: Text and check mark of the committed suggestion.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography line height body 1.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-normal`: semantic font weight for typography weight body normal.

### ki-timeline

A chronological list of activity, audit records, or steps from a run.

When to use: present chronological events with independently readable summaries,
optional times and details, including new entries in a live feed.
When NOT to use: offer a selectable command list, control the current step of a
task, or represent progress toward completion.

Examples:

# ki-timeline examples

## Show deployment activity

```html
<ki-timeline id="activity" label="Deployment activity">
  <ki-timeline-item icon-name="git-merge" tone="primary" datetime="2024-11-19T10:41:00Z">
    Luis Perez merged fix/search-index
  </ki-timeline-item>
  <ki-timeline-item icon-name="circle-alert" tone="danger" datetime="2024-11-19T10:20:00Z">
    Preview deploy failed
  </ki-timeline-item>
</ki-timeline>
```

```js
import '@kimen/elements/icons/circle-alert';
import '@kimen/elements/icons/git-merge';
import { defineCustomElement as defineTimeline } from '@kimen/elements/ki-timeline';
import { defineCustomElement as defineTimelineItem } from '@kimen/elements/ki-timeline-item';

defineTimeline();
defineTimelineItem();
```

Give the list a short name, and describe each event in words. The timeline
sorts its direct items by `datetime`. The default is newest first. Set
`order="oldest-first"` for a history that starts at the beginning.

## Add an event to a live feed

```js
const activity = document.querySelector('#activity');
const item = document.createElement('ki-timeline-item');
item.setAttribute('datetime', new Date().toISOString());
item.textContent = 'Preview deployment completed';
activity.append(item);
```

The list updates its order and announces nearby additions together. The
message comes from the event's default slot.

Attributes:
- `label` (string | undefined): Accessible name of the ordered list.
- `order` ("newest-first" | "oldest-first", default 'newest-first'): Chronological order of valid dates. Ties and undated entries retain source order. Undated entries follow valid dates in either direction.

Slots:
- (default): Direct ki-timeline-item children.

Parts:
- `announcements`: Polite region for batches of new event summaries.
- `item`: Native list entry including the connector to the next event.
- `list`: Named native ordered list.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-timeline-dot-size`: Diameter of the timeline marker.
- `--ki-timeline-gap`: Space between marker and text and between timeline entries.
- `--ki-timeline-item-fg`: Text color of the event summary and details.
- `--ki-timeline-line`: Color of the decorative line connecting timeline markers.
- `--ki-timeline-line-width`: Hairline width of the timeline connector.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-visually-hidden-size`: Nonzero edge for clipped text available to assistive technology.

### ki-timeline-item

One event in a timeline, with an optional time and details disclosure.

When to use: describe an activity, audit, or run event inside a ki-timeline.
When NOT to use: convey the outcome only through marker colour, or use the marker
as a control. Put actions in the event content or details.

Examples:

# ki-timeline-item examples

## Add an avatar and expandable details

```html
<ki-timeline label="Order updates" order="oldest-first">
  <ki-timeline-item datetime="2024-11-19">
    <ki-avatar slot="start" initials="ML" size="xs"></ki-avatar>
    Mina Lee packed the order
  </ki-timeline-item>
  <ki-timeline-item datetime="2024-11-20T11:45:00Z" details-label="Carrier details">
    Dispatch confirmed
    <div slot="details">The parcel is with the carrier.</div>
  </ki-timeline-item>
</ki-timeline>
```

Keep identity and status in the event text. Use the decorative `start`
slot for an avatar or use `icon-name` with an imported Lucide glyph. If you
use direct imports, register `ki-avatar` when you use it in the slot.

Use `details-label` to localize or describe the disclosure. The control
appears only when the event supplies details. The main event text stays
visible while details are collapsed.

Attributes:
- `datetime` (string | undefined): ISO date or date-time. Invalid or missing dates have no time label.
- `details-label` (string | undefined, default 'Details'): Label of the details control when the details slot is populated.
- `icon-name` (string | undefined): Decorative Lucide icon name, registered by the caller's per-icon import.
- `tone` ("danger" | "neutral" | "primary" | "success" | "warning", default 'neutral'): Marker tone. The event text carries the meaning. Without an icon, a non-neutral tone draws a solid dot in its ink.

Slots:
- (default): Event summary. Include important status information in the text.
- `details`: Additional event information in a native details disclosure.
- `start`: Decorative avatar or other noninteractive marker in place of the icon.

Parts:
- `content`: Event summary, time and disclosure container.
- `details`: Native details disclosure.
- `dot`: Decorative event marker.
- `summary`: Keyboard-accessible details control.
- `time`: Native time element for a valid ISO date.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-md`: The md spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-xs`: The xs spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-xxs`: The xxs spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter behind a timeline marker, off by default.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-bg`: Fill of the neutral timeline marker.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-bg-image`: Optional decorative image over the timeline marker fill.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-danger-bg`: Fill of the danger timeline marker.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-danger-fg`: Glyph color on the danger timeline marker.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-fg`: Glyph color on the neutral timeline marker.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-icon-size`: Size of the decorative glyph inside the timeline marker.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-primary-bg`: Fill of the primary timeline marker.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-primary-fg`: Glyph color on the primary timeline marker.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-radius`: Round corners of the timeline marker.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-size`: Diameter of the timeline marker.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-success-bg`: Fill of the success timeline marker.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-success-fg`: Glyph color on the success timeline marker.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-warning-bg`: Fill of the warning timeline marker.
- `--ki-timeline-dot-warning-fg`: Glyph color on the warning timeline marker.
- `--ki-timeline-gap`: Space between marker and text and between timeline entries.
- `--ki-timeline-item-fg`: Text color of the event summary and details.
- `--ki-timeline-line-width`: Hairline width of the timeline connector.
- `--ki-timeline-time-bg`: The timestamp shows the surrounding surface through its transparent background.
- `--ki-timeline-time-fg`: Text color of the timeline timestamp.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height caption 2.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-para`: semantic dimension for typography line height para.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-caption-2`: semantic dimension for typography size caption 2.

### ki-toast

A short, transient message about something the person just did, shown without blocking the page. It leaves on its own after its time, which stops while the person points at the toaster, works inside it or is away from the page; a toast with an action, or reporting an error, waits for the person.

When to use: confirm an action that happened elsewhere on screen ("Changes
saved", "Link copied"), report a background result ("Export ready"), or
offer a quick undo. Raise it into a `ki-toaster`, in markup or with its
`show()` method; express urgency with `tone`.
When NOT to use: anything the person must read or act on to continue belongs
to `ki-dialog`; form validation belongs to the field's error text; a lasting
condition of the page belongs to `ki-alert`, which stays inline.

Assistive technology note: a toast announces as it appears, so append it
when the event happens; a toast present at initial page load is exposed with
its role but its announcement is not guaranteed. The heading and the message
are the whole announcement: the icon, the action and the dismiss button
stay outside the live region.

Examples:

Put a toast in a `ki-toaster` when something happens; it announces itself as it appears and leaves on its own after 5 seconds. `tone` picks the icon and its ink and the live-region urgency: `danger` exposes `role="alert"`, every other value `role="status"`:

```html
<ki-toaster>
  <ki-toast tone="success" heading="Changes saved">Workspace settings are up to date.</ki-toast>
</ki-toaster>
```

`duration` (milliseconds) changes the time; `0` keeps the toast until it is dismissed. A toast in the `danger` tone, or holding an action, never leaves on its own, whatever its `duration`. The time stops while the pointer rests on the toaster, while focus is inside it, or while the page is hidden:

```html
<ki-toast duration="8000">The export is ready in your downloads.</ki-toast>
<ki-toast tone="danger" heading="Upload failed">The file is larger than 20 MB.</ki-toast>
```

The `action` slot takes one ghost `ki-button size="sm"`. Its own click handler runs, then the toast leaves:

```html
<ki-toast heading="Message archived">
  The conversation moved to your archive.
  <ki-button slot="action" variant="ghost" size="sm">Undo</ki-button>
</ki-toast>
```

`ki-dismiss` says why the toast left: `detail.reason` is `"timeout"`, `"button"`, `"escape"` or `"action"`. `dismissible="false"` drops the dismiss button (Escape still works on a focused toast); `dismiss-label` is the component's only built-in word, so localize it whenever the document language is not English:

```html
<ki-toast lang="es" dismiss-label="Descartar">Borrador guardado.</ki-toast>
```

Attributes:
- `dismiss-label` (string, default 'Dismiss'): Accessible name of the dismiss button. Override for localization; the default English word is the component's only built-in text. When to use: whenever the document language is not English. When NOT to use: do not put the message here; use the default slot.
- `dismissed` (boolean, default false): Reflected state: true once the toast has left. The timer, the dismiss button, Escape and the action set it; the page may set or clear it. While true the host stays in the document but renders nothing and leaves the accessibility tree. Clearing it shows the toast again with its full time. When to use: show a toast again, or close it from the page. When NOT to use: do not read programmatic changes as dismissals; `ki-dismiss` reports only the timer and the person.
- `dismissible` (boolean, default true): Shows the dismiss button, a ghost `ki-icon-button` named by `dismiss-label`. Escape still dismisses a focused toast without it. When to use: keep it on unless the toast leaves on its own and the page offers no other way to read it again. When NOT to use: do not turn it off on a toast that waits for the person.
- `duration` (number | undefined, minimum 0): How long the toast stays, in milliseconds, before it leaves on its own; `0` keeps it until it is dismissed. Ignored (treated as `0`) when the toast holds an action or its tone is `danger`. Unset, or not a finite number of zero or more, it is 5000. The time stops while the pointer rests on the toaster, while focus is inside it, or while the page is hidden, and continues with what was left. Changing it restarts the time. When to use: give a longer message more time. When NOT to use: do not shorten it below what a person needs to read the message.
- `heading` (string | undefined): Optional bold first line, inside the live region. Empty strings render no heading. It is a `strong` element, never a document heading. When to use: a short label for the event ("Changes saved"). When NOT to use: do not use it for page structure.
- `queued` (boolean, default false): Output-only state written by an enclosing `ki-toaster`: true while the toast waits for a place. A queued toast renders nothing, is absent from the accessibility tree and its time does not run. Authors do not set it; the toaster overwrites it.
- `tone` ("danger" | "info" | "neutral" | "success" | "warning" | string & {}, default 'neutral'): Picks the icon and its ink, and the live-region urgency: `danger` exposes `role="alert"` and never leaves on its own; `neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, absent and unrecognized values expose `role="status"`. The surface and the text look the same in every tone. Unknown values render neutral. When to use: choose the tone that describes what happened. When NOT to use: do not use tone for emphasis; a lasting failure belongs in `ki-alert`.

Slots:
- (default): Message text. It lives inside the live-region boundary.
- `action`: At most one action, as a `ki-button size="sm" variant="ghost"`. Its own click handler runs, then the toast leaves (`reason: "action"`). A toast holding an action never leaves on its own. When NOT to use: a response the person cannot skip belongs in `ki-dialog`.

Parts:
- `action`: Wrapper around the `action` slot, rendered only when it holds content.
- `dismiss`: The dismiss `ki-icon-button`, rendered only when `dismissible`.
- `heading`: Optional bold first line, rendered only when non-empty.
- `icon`: The tone icon, drawn by the component in the tone's ink.
- `message`: Message wrapper around the default slot.
- `toast`: The flat surface: fill, image, edge, radius, padding, elevation and backdrop filter.

Events:
- `ki-dismiss` (CustomEvent<KiToastDismissDetail>): Fired once when the toast leaves because its time ran out (`reason: "timeout"`), the person used the dismiss button (`"button"`), pressed Escape inside it (`"escape"`) or activated its action (`"action"`), after it is hidden and focus has been handed on. Not cancelable. When to use: remove the element, or record that the message was seen. When NOT to use: do not expect it for programmatic `dismissed` changes.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-motion-distance-sm`: Motion travel distance sm (4px): small slide/settle offsets.
- `--ki-motion-duration-medium-1`: M3 md.sys.motion.duration.medium1 (250ms). onmars: MarsUI moderate step (240ms, 2x the 120ms base).
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-toast-backdrop-filter`: filter used by the toast component behind its surface, taken whole: none by default; a theme may blur here (document 2, rule 6; issue #342).
- `--ki-toast-bg`: color used by the toast component for its flat raised surface (issue #353: surface-raised, the deprecated alias of surface.s1, so the step itself).
- `--ki-toast-bg-image`: image used by the toast component over its background color: none by default; a theme may paint a gradient here (document 2, rule 6).
- `--ki-toast-border`: color used by the toast component for its hairline edge (issue #353).
- `--ki-toast-border-width`: dimension used by the toast component for its hairline edge.
- `--ki-toast-danger-icon`: color used by the toast component for the danger tone icon: the tone lives in the icon alone (issue #353).
- `--ki-toast-fg`: color used by the toast component for the heading ink (issue #353).
- `--ki-toast-gap`: dimension used by the toast component between icon, text, action and dismiss button (issue #353: 12px).
- `--ki-toast-heading-font-family`: Font family for the toast heading (document 2, rule 6; issue #347). Override it to give toasts their own heading typeface.
- `--ki-toast-icon-size`: dimension used by the toast component for the tone icon.
- `--ki-toast-info-icon`: color used by the toast component for the info tone icon: the tone lives in the icon alone (issue #353).
- `--ki-toast-message-fg`: color used by the toast component for the message ink (issue #353).
- `--ki-toast-neutral-icon`: color used by the toast component for the neutral tone icon: the tone lives in the icon alone (issue #353).
- `--ki-toast-padding`: dimension used by the toast component for its padding (issue #353: 12px).
- `--ki-toast-radius`: dimension used by the toast component for its corners (issue #353: 16px).
- `--ki-toast-shadow`: shadow used by the toast component for its elevation (issue #353: e4). The only theme-controlled shadow in the toast's box-shadow (document 2, rule 6).
- `--ki-toast-success-icon`: color used by the toast component for the success tone icon: the tone lives in the icon alone (issue #353).
- `--ki-toast-warning-icon`: color used by the toast component for the warning tone icon: the tone lives in the icon alone (issue #353).
- `--ki-toast-width`: dimension used by the toast component for the widest a toast gets (issue #353: 22.5rem).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-body-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height body 2.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-para`: semantic dimension for typography line height para.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-2`: semantic dimension for typography size body 2.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-semibold`: semantic font weight for typography weight body semibold.

### ki-toaster

The one place toasts appear: it paints its `ki-toast` children in the top layer at a corner of the viewport, stacks them in arrival order, shows the newest few and queues the older ones, without covering the page beside them.

When to use: once per page (or once inside a modal `ki-dialog`), as the place
every `ki-toast` of the application appears in: append toasts to it, or call
`show()`. Choose the corner with `placement`.
When NOT to use: do not put anything but `ki-toast` elements in it; do not use
it for persistent content, which belongs in the page or in `ki-alert`.

Assistive technology note: while it shows toasts the toaster is a group
named by `label`, never a landmark; F6 moves focus into it and Escape on a
toast returns focus to where it was. An empty toaster exposes nothing and
covers nothing.

Examples:

Place one toaster per page (or one inside a modal `ki-dialog`). It paints its stack in the top layer, stacks toasts from the top down in arrival order and shows the newest three; older ones wait their turn:

```html
<ki-toaster></ki-toaster>
<script>
  document.querySelector('ki-toaster').show({
    tone: 'success',
    title: 'Changes saved',
    message: 'Workspace settings are up to date.',
    action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: undo },
  });
</script>
```

`show()` creates the toast, appends it, and removes it once it has left; its action renders as a ghost `ki-button size="sm"`. The toaster does not bundle either element, so define `ki-toast` and `ki-button` too. Toasts can also be written in markup inside the toaster; those stay the page's own and are never removed.

`placement` picks the corner — `top-center`, `top-end`, `bottom-center` or `bottom-end` (the default); `end` follows the writing direction, and a narrow touch screen always uses the bottom center. `max` sets how many toasts show at once:

```html
<ki-toaster placement="top-center" max="2"></ki-toaster>
```

While it shows toasts the toaster is a group named by `label` (`Notifications` by default); F6 moves focus into it, and Escape on a toast returns focus to where it was. Localize the name whenever the document language is not English:

```html
<ki-toaster lang="es" label="Avisos"></ki-toaster>
```

The distance from the viewport edges and the gap between toasts are tokens:

```css
:root {
  --ki-toaster-inset-block: 24px;
  --ki-toaster-inset-inline: 24px;
}
```

Attributes:
- `label` (string, default 'Notifications'): Accessible name of the group the toaster exposes while it shows toasts. Override for localization. When to use: provide the name in the document language. When NOT to use: do not put a message here.
- `max` (number, default 3, minimum 1): How many toasts show at once: the newest ones. Older toasts wait, and come back with their full time as shown ones leave. A toast holding focus keeps its place until focus leaves the toaster; the oldest other one waits instead. A value below 1 or not a whole number shows 3. When to use: lower it on small screens or busy applications. When NOT to use: do not raise it to show every toast; a tall stack covers the page.
- `placement` ("bottom-center" | "bottom-end" | "top-center" | "top-end" | string & {}, default 'bottom-end'): Corner or edge of the viewport the stack sits against; `end` follows the writing direction. On a coarse pointer and a viewport narrower than 40rem the stack always sits at the bottom center. Unknown values place the stack at the bottom end. When to use: keep toasts away from where the page's own controls live. When NOT to use: do not change it per toast; one toaster keeps one place.

Slots:
- (default): The `ki-toast` elements, in arrival order. Other children are not counted, queued or placed.

Parts:
- `stack`: The stack in the top layer: placement, edge distance, gap between toasts and width.

Events: none

Methods:
- `show(options)` (Promise<HTMLElement>): Raises a toast: creates a `ki-toast` from `tone`, `title` (its heading), `message`, `duration`, `dismissible` and `action` (a ghost `ki-button size="sm"` in its `action` slot that calls `onClick`), appends it to the toaster and resolves with it. Once the toast has left it is removed from the page. The toaster does not bundle `ki-toast` or `ki-button`: define them, as for toasts written in markup. When to use: raise a toast from script without writing its markup. When NOT to use: a toast written in markup stays the page's own: append it instead, and it is never removed.

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-toast-width`: dimension used by the toast component for the widest a toast gets (issue #353: 22.5rem).
- `--ki-toaster-gap`: dimension used by the toaster component for the gap between stacked toasts (spec 049 FR-014).
- `--ki-toaster-inset-block`: dimension used by the toaster component for the distance between the stack and the top or bottom edge of the viewport (spec 049 FR-014).
- `--ki-toaster-inset-inline`: dimension used by the toaster component for the distance between the stack and the end edge of the viewport (spec 049 FR-014).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-tool-call

A disclosure for one assistant tool call, with a status and optional payloads.

When to use: show which tool ran, its state and duration, and let the reader
inspect the supplied input, output or error. Use a conversation log for status updates.
When NOT to use: collecting approval, running or configuring tools. Pair with a
separate confirmation control for an approval decision.

Examples:

# ToolCall examples

## Inspect a completed tool call

```html
<ki-tool-call name="search_docs" title="Search docs" status="done" duration="1200">
  <ki-code-block slot="input" language="json" filename="search-input.json" wrap>{"query": "Forms"}</ki-code-block>
  <ki-code-block slot="output" language="json" filename="search-output.json" wrap>["Field help"]</ki-code-block>
</ki-tool-call>
```

## Handle a failed call

```html
<ki-tool-call name="build_preview" status="failed" retryable>
  <p slot="error">The build was interrupted.</p>
</ki-tool-call>
```

Listen for `ki-tool-retry` to let the application handle the request. In
a guarded surface, set the node's `action` to a declared retry action.
A consumer-owned control in the error slot can declare its own action.

## Record a transition in the conversation

```html
<div id="tool-updates" role="log" aria-label="Tool updates"></div>
<ki-tool-call id="call" name="run_tests" status="running"></ki-tool-call>
<script type="module">
  const log = document.querySelector('#tool-updates');
  const call = document.querySelector('#call');
  call.addEventListener('ki-tool-status-change', ({ detail: { name, label } }) => {
    const entry = document.createElement('p');
    entry.textContent = [name, label].join(': ');
    log.append(entry);
  });
</script>
```

Attributes:
- `approval-label` (string, default 'Needs approval'): Status text for a call waiting on an approval decision.
- `done-label` (string, default 'Done'): Status text for a successful call.
- `duration` (number | undefined, minimum 0): Non-negative elapsed time in milliseconds. Displayed only for Done.
- `error-label` (string, default 'Error'): Caption for the error slot.
- `failed-label` (string, default 'Failed'): Status text for a failed call.
- `input-label` (string, default 'Input'): Caption for the input slot.
- `locale` (string, default 'en'): Language tag used to format the completed duration. Defaults to English.
- `name` (string, required): Tool identifier, such as search_docs, displayed in monospace.
- `open` (boolean | undefined): Override the disclosure state. Without an override, failed calls are open and other calls are closed. Set open="false" for an explicit collapse. Using the summary sets the property to the reader's choice.
- `output-label` (string, default 'Output'): Caption for the output slot.
- `pending-label` (string, default 'Pending'): Status text for a call waiting to run.
- `retry-label` (string, default 'Retry'): Visible and accessible label for the built-in retry control.
- `retryable` (boolean, default false): Offer the built-in Retry button when the call fails.
- `running-label` (string, default 'Running'): Status text for a call in progress.
- `status` ("approval" | "done" | "failed" | "pending" | "running", default 'pending'): Lifecycle status. Unknown values display Pending.
- `title` (string | undefined): Optional human-readable label displayed beside the identifier.

Slots:
- `error`: A failure message or a consumer-owned retry control, visible on failed calls.
- `input`: Arguments supplied to the tool. Use ki-code-block for structured text.
- `output`: Result returned by the tool. Use ki-code-block for structured text.

Parts:
- `body`: Content disclosed by opening the call.
- `disclosure`: Native details surface.
- `error`: Error section for failed calls.
- `input`: Input section with its caption and payload.
- `name`: Monospaced tool identifier.
- `output`: Output section with its caption and payload.
- `payload`: Surface for the input and output content.
- `retry`: Opt-in action button for failed calls.
- `status`: Badge that contains the status text and completed duration.
- `summary`: Native disclosure control and its status row.

Events:
- `ki-tool-retry` (CustomEvent<{ name: string }>): A request to retry this tool call. Bind a declared surface action to handle it.
- `ki-tool-status-change` (CustomEvent<{ name: string; status: string; label: string }>): Once per status transition after initialization. Append one entry to the conversation log.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-badge-sm-height`: dimension used by the badge component for sm height.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-tool-call-backdrop-filter`: Whole filter behind the call.
- `--ki-tool-call-bg`: Solid background of the call disclosure.
- `--ki-tool-call-bg-image`: Optional image over the solid background.
- `--ki-tool-call-border`: Border ink around the call.
- `--ki-tool-call-border-width`: Width of the disclosure frame.
- `--ki-tool-call-caption-size`: Size of captions and the tool identifier.
- `--ki-tool-call-code-bg`: Background for input and output payloads.
- `--ki-tool-call-code-fg`: Plain text ink on the payload surface.
- `--ki-tool-call-code-radius`: Corners of the plain payload surface.
- `--ki-tool-call-fg`: Text ink on the call surface.
- `--ki-tool-call-font-size`: Body text size.
- `--ki-tool-call-gap`: Gap between summary items and body sections.
- `--ki-tool-call-icon`: Ink of the decorative icons.
- `--ki-tool-call-icon-size`: Size of the wrench and chevron.
- `--ki-tool-call-inline-gap`: Gap between status items and after each caption.
- `--ki-tool-call-line-height`: Body text line height.
- `--ki-tool-call-mono-family`: Typeface of the tool identifier.
- `--ki-tool-call-padding`: Horizontal inset and space after the body.
- `--ki-tool-call-radius`: Corners of the disclosure surface.
- `--ki-tool-call-transition-duration`: Duration of the disclosure chevron rotation.
- `--ki-tool-call-transition-easing`: Easing of the disclosure chevron rotation.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-toolbar

Brings frequent page actions together in a floating pill or docked surface.

When to use: group a small set of related page actions, such as text
formatting or the commands on a compact message screen.
When NOT to use: for site navigation, mutually exclusive choices, or a docked
bar on a screen already using MobileNav.

Examples:

# Toolbar examples

## Formatting controls

```html
<ki-toolbar label="Formatting">
  <ki-button variant="ghost">Bold</ki-button>
  <ki-divider orientation="vertical"></ki-divider>
  <ki-button variant="ghost">Insert link</ki-button>
</ki-toolbar>
```

Give icon-only actions their own label. With ToggleIconButton available, a
`ki-icon-button` with `toggle`, `selected` and `label="Bold"` owns the
pressed state and activation of the Bold command.

## Docked message actions

```html
<ki-toolbar label="Message actions" variant="docked" tone="vibrant" hide-on-scroll>
  <ki-button variant="ghost">Archive</ki-button>
  <ki-button variant="ghost">Mark unread</ki-button>
</ki-toolbar>
```

Reserve the bottom edge for the toolbar and leave space for its minimum
height plus `env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)` below page content. Use this
variant on compact pages without MobileNav.

## Floating with a FAB

When `ki-fab` is available, register it alongside the toolbar and buttons
when using direct imports. Give the FAB a label and use its named slot.

```html
<ki-toolbar label="Message actions" tone="vibrant">
  <ki-button variant="ghost">Archive</ki-button>
  <ki-fab slot="fab" label="Reply"></ki-fab>
</ki-toolbar>
```

This companion action follows the pill in the Tab sequence. Handle actions
on the slotted controls. The toolbar coordinates navigation and placement.

Attributes:
- `hide-on-scroll` (boolean, default false): Hides on downward page scroll and reveals on upward scroll or when an action receives focus. Use for secondary actions where content needs room.
- `label` (string, required): Accessible name for the group, such as "Formatting". Supply it in the page's language.
- `orientation` ("horizontal" | "vertical", default 'horizontal'): Layout and keyboard axis. Set vertical for a floating column. Docked is always horizontal.
- `tone` ("standard" | "vibrant", default 'standard'): Surface palette. Use vibrant to emphasize the toolbar with an accent tint.
- `variant` ("docked" | "floating", default 'floating'): Floating leaves placement to the page. Docked fixes the surface to the viewport's bottom edge. Reserve space below the content when docking.

Slots:
- (default): Direct ki-button, ki-icon-button (including toggles), native button and ki-divider children. Give every icon-only action an accessible name.
- `fab`: A companion ki-fab for the floating variant. It follows the toolbar and has its own Tab stop.

Parts:
- `toolbar`: The named surface containing the grouped actions.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-toolbar-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter behind the surface.
- `--ki-toolbar-bg`: Background of the standard toolbar.
- `--ki-toolbar-bg-image`: Optional image above the solid surface color.
- `--ki-toolbar-docked-padding-inline`: Inline insets for docked actions.
- `--ki-toolbar-docked-radius`: Corner radius of the docked toolbar.
- `--ki-toolbar-fab-gap`: Gap between a floating pill and its companion FAB.
- `--ki-toolbar-fg`: Foreground of the standard toolbar.
- `--ki-toolbar-gap`: Gap between toolbar actions.
- `--ki-toolbar-height`: Minimum height of the docked toolbar before its safe area.
- `--ki-toolbar-padding`: Toolbar surface padding.
- `--ki-toolbar-radius`: Radius of the floating pill.
- `--ki-toolbar-scroll-duration`: Duration of the scroll visibility transition.
- `--ki-toolbar-scroll-easing`: Easing of the scroll visibility transition.
- `--ki-toolbar-shadow`: Resting elevation of the floating pill.
- `--ki-toolbar-vibrant-bg`: Accent background of the vibrant toolbar.
- `--ki-toolbar-vibrant-fg`: Foreground on the vibrant toolbar.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-tooltip

A transient, text-only hint with an optional heading.

When to use: add a brief clarifying hint for an icon-only, abbreviated, or
otherwise ambiguous control when the same information is discoverable
elsewhere in the interface.
When NOT to use: essential or unique information in a tooltip; interactive
content in a tooltip; form validation messages, disabled controls, or
touch-primary flows. Use visible layout text or a rich `ki-popover` with
`kind="toggletip"` when the content includes actions.

Examples:

`label` is the entire plain tooltip content, reflected to the slotted trigger's accessible description; the trigger must already carry its own accessible name:

```html
<ki-tooltip label="Copies a shareable link to the clipboard">
  <ki-button type="button">Copy link</ki-button>
</ki-tooltip>
```

`placement` (default `top`; also `bottom`, `start`, `end`) is a preference — the component flips or clamps it to keep the bubble inside the viewport:

```html
<ki-tooltip label="Downloads the report as PDF" placement="bottom">
  <ki-button type="button">Export</ki-button>
</ki-tooltip>
```

An empty or whitespace-only `label` renders no tooltip and exposes no description — useful for conditional hints; never put essential or unique information in a tooltip:

```html
<ki-tooltip label="">
  <ki-button type="button">No hint here</ki-button>
</ki-tooltip>
```

Use a heading and direct text when the explanation needs more structure.
The external trigger must be in the same document or shadow tree.

```html
<button id="retention-info" type="button">Retention</button>
<ki-tooltip for="retention-info" heading="Grace period">
  Deleted projects stay restorable for 30 days.
</ki-tooltip>
```

For an explanation with controls, use `ki-popover` with
`kind="toggletip"` and `appearance="rich"`.

Attributes:
- `for` (string | undefined, ID of another element of the same spec): ID of the rich tooltip's external trigger in the same document or shadow tree.
- `heading` (string | undefined): Rich tooltip heading. Pair it with `for` and optional direct text in the default slot.
- `label` (string, default ''): The entire plain tooltip content. The string is reflected to the slotted trigger's accessible description without changing its name. Empty or whitespace-only labels render no tooltip and expose no description. When to use: a short hint that clarifies the slotted trigger. When NOT to use: never use `label` for essential information, rich content, interactive content, validation messages, or information attached to disabled controls; put that content in visible UI or a popover.
- `placement` ("bottom" | "end" | "start" | "top", default 'top'): Preferred placement for the tooltip. The component may flip or clamp the rendered placement to keep the bubble inside the viewport; unknown runtime values fall back to `top`. When NOT to use: do not depend on placement for meaning or reading order.

Slots:
- (default): One trigger for a plain tooltip, or direct explanatory text when `for` and `heading` are provided. Rich tooltips accept text only.

Parts:
- `tooltip`: The non-focusable tooltip bubble.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-effect-component-secondary-default-shadow`: MarsUI Component_effect/secondary_default: drop 0/2/1.5/-0.5 plus inner White/3 0/2/3. Pair with --ki-effect-component-backdrop-filter.
- `--ki-motion-distance-sm`: Motion travel distance sm (4px): small slide/settle offsets.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-duration-instant`: Zero-duration step: transitions that must complete immediately (reduced-motion fallbacks, instant handoffs).
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-motion-easing-standard-accelerate`: Utility exit curve. M3 md.sys.motion.easing.standard-accelerate. onmars: the MarsUI accelerate curve (ki.easing.in).
- `--ki-surface-image-tooltip-arrow-end`: End-edge arrow color for a themed tooltip surface.
- `--ki-surface-image-tooltip-arrow-start`: Start-edge arrow color for a themed tooltip surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-arrow-radius`: dimension used by the tooltip component for the rounding of the arrow tip (Tooltip master pointer: 1.5px, nearest radius step).
- `--ki-tooltip-arrow-size`: dimension used by the tooltip component for the depth of the arrow that points at the trigger; it is twice as wide (Tooltip master 12089:7621 pointer: 16x8). Zero removes it. Equal to offset, so the tip meets the trigger.
- `--ki-tooltip-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter behind the tooltip bubble.
- `--ki-tooltip-bg`: Base background color of the tooltip. Onmars v1 used a transparent backing beneath its translucent image.
- `--ki-tooltip-bg-image`: Optional CSS background image layered over the tooltip fill. Use none for a solid fill.
- `--ki-tooltip-border-color`: color used by the tooltip component for its edge (MarsUI hairline, Outline/secondary_button_top); one token so a mode or a theme can strengthen it.
- `--ki-tooltip-border-width`: dimension used by the tooltip component for the outline width (MarsUI card 1px Outline/secondary_button_top stroke; replaces the 1px literal ki-tooltip.css shipped while the token was pending).
- `--ki-tooltip-fg`: color used by the tooltip component for foreground (MarsUI title row Text/high_em; onmars v2 sets the inverse tooltip ink).
- `--ki-tooltip-font-size`: dimension used by the tooltip component for font size (MarsUI Heading_top style UI/Para/medium: body_1 13px).
- `--ki-tooltip-font-weight`: font weight used by the tooltip component for font weight.
- `--ki-tooltip-line-height`: dimension used by the tooltip component for line height (MarsUI line_height/para 20px).
- `--ki-tooltip-max-inline-size`: dimension used by the tooltip component for max inline size (288px; the master card is fixed 280px wide in its rich variants — the 8px divergence is a documented text-only reduction).
- `--ki-tooltip-offset`: dimension used by the tooltip component for offset (MarsUI caret depth 8px with zero extra gap = trigger-to-card distance).
- `--ki-tooltip-padding-block`: dimension used by the tooltip component for padding block (MarsUI card padding Space/xl 12px on all sides).
- `--ki-tooltip-padding-inline`: dimension used by the tooltip component for padding inline (MarsUI card padding Space/xl 12px on all sides).
- `--ki-tooltip-radius`: dimension used by the tooltip component for radius (MarsUI Tooltip master 12089:7621 List_wrap: Radius/big_component/radius_xs 16px).
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-bg`: Fill of the rich tooltip or rich popover.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-bg-image`: Optional image layer over the rich surface fill.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-border-color`: Outline ink of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-border-width`: Outline thickness of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-fg`: Ink of the rich surface body text.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-font-size`: Body text size of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-font-weight`: Body text weight of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-heading-family`: Typeface of the rich surface heading.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-heading-fg`: Ink of the rich surface heading over the shared fill.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-heading-gap`: Distance between the rich heading and its body.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-heading-size`: Text size of the rich surface heading.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-heading-weight`: Text weight of the rich surface heading.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-line-height`: Body text line height of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-max-width`: Maximum inline size of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-padding-block`: Block-axis inset of the rich surface, before density scaling.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-padding-inline`: Inline-axis inset of the rich surface, before density scaling.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-radius`: Corner radius of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-rich-shadow`: Raised elevation of the rich surface.
- `--ki-tooltip-shadow`: shadow used by the tooltip component for shadow (MarsUI Elevation/e4 on the master wrap).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.

### ki-top-nav

Application navigation with responsive primary links, or a per-screen app bar with a real heading, optional search, and overflow actions.

When to use: group a brand, up to five primary sections and global controls,
or set a screen title, leading control and screen actions in app-bar mode.
When NOT to use: more than five sections or a deep navigation tree (use a
sidebar), or switches between in-page views (use ki-tabs).

Examples:

# Using TopNav

## Application header

Use direct anchors for primary sections and keep the page's skip link before
the header. Import `@kimen/elements/icons/bell` for the notification glyph.

```html
<a href="#content" class="skip-link">Skip to content</a>
<ki-top-nav label="Primary" collapse-at="48rem" sticky>
  <a slot="brand" href="/">Kimen</a>
  <a href="/overview" aria-current="page">Overview</a>
  <a href="/projects">Projects</a>
  <ki-icon-button slot="actions" variant="ghost" label="Notifications, 3 unread">
    <ki-icon name="bell"></ki-icon>
    <ki-counter slot="counter" value="3"></ki-counter>
  </ki-icon-button>
</ki-top-nav>
<main id="content" tabindex="-1">Workspace</main>
```

## Per-screen bar with search

Use the native `title` attribute in HTML and `screenTitle` for the framework
prop. The leading button and search control keep their names and behavior.
The screen heading remains accessible when search occupies its visual space.

```html
<ki-top-nav variant="app-bar" title="Projects" heading-level="2">
  <button type="button" slot="leading">Back</button>
  <input slot="search" type="search" aria-label="Search projects">
  <button type="button" slot="actions">Filters</button>
</ki-top-nav>
```

When an app bar has more than three actions, slot the named controls directly.
Attach handlers to those controls. TopNav uses their existing activation
handlers in the overflow menu. Keep application-specific account menus and
navigation destinations in the consuming app.

Attributes:
- `collapse-at` (string, default '48rem'): CSS length below which navigation collapses and single-row app bars can center their title.
- `heading-level` (number, default 1): Native heading level for the screen title. Use 1 through 6 to fit the page outline.
- `label` (string, default 'Main'): Accessible name of the header's primary navigation landmark. Override for localization.
