- `navigation-label` (string, default 'Open navigation'): Accessible name for the compact navigation button and menu. Override for localization.
- `overflow-label` (string, default 'More actions'): Accessible name for the app-bar overflow button and menu. Override for localization.
- `title` (string, default ''): Screen heading, set with the HTML title attribute or the screenTitle property.
- `scroll-behavior` ("collapse" | "elevate" | "none", default 'elevate'): Tint on scroll with elevate, also shrink tall bars with collapse, or opt out with none.
- `size` ("lg" | "md" | "sm" | "xl", default 'md'): Bar size. Only app-bar mode has large and extra-large two-row sizes.
- `sticky` (boolean, default false): Keep the bar at the block start of the scroll container and draw a bottom border.
- `subtitle` (string, default ''): Supporting text displayed under the screen heading.
- `title-align` ("center" | "start", default 'start'): Center a compact single-row title when the app bar has at most one action.
- `variant` ("app-bar" | "header", default 'header'): Header for primary navigation, or app-bar for the current screen. Defaults to header.

Slots:
- (default): Header mode: up to five direct native anchors; mark the current one with aria-current="page". They stay the page's own anchors, so the page's link rules reach them and outrank the bar's link styles (CSS Scoping gives the page's styles precedence over a component's `::slotted()` rules, whatever their specificity). `a { color: inherit }` is safe: the links then take the bar's item ink. A rule that sets `color`, `text-decoration`, `font-*` or `padding` on every `a` restyles them too: scope it away from the bar, for example `:where(main, footer) a` or `a:not(ki-top-nav > a)`, and restyle the bar's links with the `--ki-top-nav-item-*` tokens.
- `actions`: Header: global actions. App bar: up to three inline; additional direct named buttons or links go into overflow.
- `brand`: Header mode: the brand link or wordmark. Page link rules reach it as they reach the primary links.
- `leading`: App bar: a named Back or Open navigation control.
- `search`: App bar: an accessible search control that can shrink inside its row.

Parts:
- `actions`: Wrapper for the trailing actions.
- `bar`: Painted header or app-bar surface.
- `brand`: Wrapper for the header brand.
- `heading`: The native screen heading.
- `leading`: Wrapper for the app-bar leading control.
- `links`: Wrapper for the primary links, including when displayed as a menu.
- `menu`: Anchored navigation or overflow menu surface.
- `menu-item`: Generated screen action in the overflow menu.
- `menu-trigger`: Native button opening collapsed navigation or overflow.
- `navigation`: The named primary navigation landmark.
- `search`: Wrapper for the app-bar search control.
- `subtitle`: Supporting text below the screen heading.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-app-bar-backdrop-filter`: Filter applied to the entire app-bar backdrop.
- `--ki-app-bar-bg`: Resting app-bar fill.
- `--ki-app-bar-bg-image`: Optional image above the app-bar fill.
- `--ki-app-bar-fg`: Resting app-bar title and control ink.
- `--ki-app-bar-height`: Height of a normal or collapsed app bar.
- `--ki-app-bar-lg-height`: Expanded height of a large app bar.
- `--ki-app-bar-lg-title-size`: Expanded two-row app-bar title size.
- `--ki-app-bar-scrolled-bg`: App-bar fill when its container scrolls.
- `--ki-app-bar-scrolled-fg`: App-bar title and control ink when its container scrolls.
- `--ki-app-bar-scrolled-subtitle-fg`: App-bar subtitle ink when its container scrolls.
- `--ki-app-bar-subtitle-fg`: Resting app-bar subtitle ink.
- `--ki-app-bar-title-font-family`: Screen heading typeface.
- `--ki-app-bar-title-size`: One-row app-bar title size.
- `--ki-app-bar-xl-height`: Expanded height of an extra-large app bar.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-elevation-e3`: MarsUI Elevation/e3 (cumulative: e2 layers plus 0/20/20/-12).
- `--ki-focus-ring-color`: Colour of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws: 3:1 or more against the page in every theme and scheme.
- `--ki-focus-ring-offset`: Gap between a focusable component and its keyboard focus ring.
- `--ki-focus-ring-width`: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring every focusable component draws (its outline). One token instead of one per component, so a mode or a theme changes every ring at once.
- `--ki-layout-border-width`: Hairline edge on a structural surface.
- `--ki-layout-indicator-width`: Thickness of the line identifying a selected navigation destination.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-12xl`: The 12xl spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-7xl`: The 7xl spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-xl`: The xl spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-spacing-xs`: The xs spacing step for a stack or grid gap.
- `--ki-layout-touch-target`: Minimum target dimension for navigation controls on a coarse pointer.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-duration-medium-1`: M3 md.sys.motion.duration.medium1 (250ms). onmars: MarsUI moderate step (240ms, 2x the 120ms base).
- `--ki-motion-easing-standard`: Standard interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-text-low-em`: semantic color for text low em. Not an ink for body text: under 4.5:1 on the light surfaces (s0-s2). Use it for large text (24px, or 18.66px bold), icons and decoration; body text takes the high-em ink of the tone.
- `--ki-top-nav-backdrop-filter`: Filter applied to the entire header backdrop.
- `--ki-top-nav-bg`: Application header fill.
- `--ki-top-nav-bg-image`: Optional image above the header fill.
- `--ki-top-nav-border`: Edge color for sticky bars and menus.
- `--ki-top-nav-fg`: Application header brand and control ink.
- `--ki-top-nav-height`: Height of a normal application header.
- `--ki-top-nav-height-compact`: Height of a small application header.
- `--ki-top-nav-indicator`: Bar marking the current primary destination.
- `--ki-top-nav-item-bg`: Primary navigation item resting surface.
- `--ki-top-nav-item-current-bg`: Current navigation destination surface.
- `--ki-top-nav-item-current-fg`: Current navigation destination ink.
- `--ki-top-nav-item-fg`: Primary navigation item resting ink.
- `--ki-top-nav-item-hover-bg`: Hovered control or highlighted menu item surface.
- `--ki-top-nav-item-hover-fg`: Hovered control or highlighted menu item ink.
- `--ki-top-nav-menu-radius`: Menu and trigger corner radius.
- `--ki-top-nav-padding-inline`: Padding at the inline edges of both bars.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography line height body 1.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-heading-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height heading 2.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-title-2`: semantic dimension for typography line height title 2.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-title-2`: semantic dimension for typography size title 2.
- `--ki-typography-visually-hidden-size`: Nonzero edge for clipped text available to assistive technology.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-medium`: semantic font weight for typography weight body medium.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-semibold`: semantic font weight for typography weight body semibold.
- `--ki-typography-weight-display-semibold`: semantic font weight for typography weight display semibold.

### ki-tree

A named hierarchy with collapsible branches and independent keyboard focus.

When to use: browse nested files, categories or an outline, select items in
a hierarchy, or navigate through linked destinations.
When NOT to use: flat lists of peers, menus of commands, or submitted form values.

Examples:

# Tree examples

Give the tree a label and put the item text before any nested items. Set
`expanded` to show a branch's children and `selected` to mark the initial
selection. The tree defaults to single selection.

```html
<ki-tree label="Project files">
  <ki-tree-item expanded>
    src
    <ki-tree-item selected>ki-dialog.ts</ki-tree-item>
    <ki-tree-item>ki-menu.ts</ki-tree-item>
  </ki-tree-item>
  <ki-tree-item>README.md</ki-tree-item>
</ki-tree>
```

Set `selection="multiple"` to show checkboxes. The Reports branch starts
mixed because Summary is the only checked child. Toggling Reports also
updates its enabled descendants. The `ki-selection-change` event reports
the committed selection in `detail.selectedItems`, including fully checked
branches.

```html
<ki-tree label="Export files" selection="multiple">
  <ki-tree-item expanded>
    Reports
    <ki-tree-item selected>Summary</ki-tree-item>
    <ki-tree-item>Appendix</ki-tree-item>
    <ki-tree-item disabled>Draft</ki-tree-item>
  </ki-tree-item>
</ki-tree>
```

Use `selection="none"` with `href` to build a navigation tree.

```html
<ki-tree label="Documentation" selection="none">
  <ki-tree-item expanded>
    Guides
    <ki-tree-item href="./quick-start/">Quick start</ki-tree-item>
    <ki-tree-item href="./theming/">Theming</ki-tree-item>
  </ki-tree-item>
</ki-tree>
```

A lazy branch emits `ki-load` the first time it opens. Append its child
items to `event.detail.item` to replace the spinner. Set `item.lazy = false`
to finish the wait if there are no children.

```html
<ki-tree label="Project files">
  <ki-tree-item lazy loading-label="Loading tokens">tokens</ki-tree-item>
</ki-tree>
```

```js
document.querySelector('ki-tree')?.addEventListener('ki-load', ({ detail: { item } }) => {
  const child = document.createElement('ki-tree-item');
  child.textContent = 'palette.tokens.json';
  item.append(child);
});
```

Attributes:
- `label` (string, default 'Tree'): Accessible name of the hierarchy. Localize it and make it distinct among nearby trees.
- `selection` ("multiple" | "none" | "single", default 'single'): Use none for navigation, single for one selected item, or multiple for checkable branches.

Slots:
- (default): Direct ki-tree-item children in reading order.

Parts:
- `base`: The surface around the hierarchy.

Events:
- `ki-selection-change` (CustomEvent<{ selectedItems: HTMLKiTreeItemElement[] }>): Emitted after a user selection changes. Selected items are in tree order.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-space-scale`: Multiplies every scaled container padding and gap (card, dialog, alert, list, list item, select listbox, tab panel, tooltip).
- `--ki-tree-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter behind the surface.
- `--ki-tree-bg`: Base surface of the hierarchy.
- `--ki-tree-bg-image`: Optional image layered over the tree surface.
- `--ki-tree-edge`: Perimeter color of the hierarchy surface.
- `--ki-tree-edge-width`: Width of the surface and checkbox outlines.
- `--ki-tree-fg`: Text on the base surface.
- `--ki-tree-padding`: Interior padding of the hierarchy surface.
- `--ki-tree-radius`: Rounding of the hierarchy surface.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-line-height-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography line height body 1.
- `--ki-typography-size-body-1`: semantic dimension for typography size body 1.

### ki-tree-item

An item or expandable branch inside a ki-tree.

When to use: label a file, category or destination in a hierarchy. Nest more
ki-tree-item children for a branch.
When NOT to use: standalone controls, form checkboxes, or a row with other
interactive descendants.

Examples:

# Tree item examples

Place each item directly in a `ki-tree` or another `ki-tree-item`. Put the
label text before the child items. A disabled item stays in the tree's
arrow-key sequence and cannot be activated.

```html
<ki-tree label="Project files">
  <ki-tree-item expanded>
    src
    <ki-tree-item selected>ki-dialog.ts</ki-tree-item>
    <ki-tree-item disabled>Archived code</ki-tree-item>
  </ki-tree-item>
</ki-tree>
```

Import the decorative glyph before the tree mounts if you set `icon-name`.

```js
import '@kimen/elements/icons/file-code';
```

```html
<ki-tree label="Project files">
  <ki-tree-item icon-name="file-code">ki-dialog.ts</ki-tree-item>
</ki-tree>
```

Attributes:
- `disabled` (boolean, default false): Keep the row discoverable by keyboard while preventing user activation.
- `expanded` (boolean, default false): Whether a branch reveals its children. Has no visible effect on a leaf.
- `href` (string | undefined, URL): Native destination of the row. Prefer selection="none" for navigation trees.
- `icon-name` (string | undefined): Optional decorative icon. Import the named Kimen glyph before mounting the tree.
- `lazy` (boolean, default false): Request children on the first empty expansion. Clear it to finish an empty load.
- `loading-label` (string, default 'Loading'): Localized text for the spinner status during an outstanding lazy request.
- `selected` (boolean, default false): Selected state. The tree keeps it in sync with single selection or fully checked branches.

Slots:
- (default): The row label and directly nested ki-tree-item children.

Parts:
- `checkbox`: Check-state indicator and hit area in multiple selection.
- `disclosure`: Leading hit area and direction indicator of a branch.
- `group`: The region containing the expanded child items.
- `label`: Visible row text or native destination link.
- `row`: The painted and focus-highlighted item row.

Events:
- `ki-collapse` (CustomEvent<{ item: HTMLKiTreeItemElement }>): Emitted when an existing branch collapses.
- `ki-expand` (CustomEvent<{ item: HTMLKiTreeItemElement }>): Emitted when an existing branch expands.
- `ki-load` (CustomEvent<{ item: HTMLKiTreeItemElement }>): Emitted once when an empty lazy branch first opens. The listener supplies the children.

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-density-control-offset`: Added to the block size of every scaled control and row (button, icon button, field, select, textarea, option, list item, tab). Components floor the result at ki.size.target-min.
- `--ki-density-target-min`: The smallest pointer target any density may produce: 24 x 24 CSS px by default and in compact (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), 44 x 44 in touch (WCAG 2.5.5). It floors a shrinking control but never lifts what a control paints: a control painted smaller extends its target to it, invisibly; rows and tabs grow to it (spec 045 A1).
- `--ki-tree-disclosure-duration`: Disclosure turn duration.
- `--ki-tree-disclosure-easing`: Disclosure turn easing.
- `--ki-tree-edge-width`: Width of the surface and checkbox outlines.
- `--ki-tree-focus-ring-color`: Ink of the focused row outline.
- `--ki-tree-focus-ring-width`: Width of the focused row outline.
- `--ki-tree-hover-bg`: Fill of an unselected row hovered by a fine pointer.
- `--ki-tree-hover-fg`: Text of an unselected row hovered by a fine pointer.
- `--ki-tree-icon-fg`: Default ink of the decorative row icons.
- `--ki-tree-indent`: Inline indentation per hierarchy level.
- `--ki-tree-item-box-radius`: Rounding of the visual checkbox indicator.
- `--ki-tree-item-box-size`: Size of the visual checkbox indicator.
- `--ki-tree-item-gap`: Space between an optional item icon and its label.
- `--ki-tree-item-padding`: Inline-end inset of an item row.
- `--ki-tree-item-radius`: Rounding of a highlighted item row.
- `--ki-tree-item-target`: Minimum inline target of a disclosure or checkbox.
- `--ki-tree-row-height`: Minimum block size before density adjustment.
- `--ki-tree-selected-bg`: Fill of a selected or checked row.
- `--ki-tree-selected-fg`: Text and glyph ink on a selected row.
- `--ki-tree-touch-row-min`: Minimum row block size on a coarse pointer.
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-typography-weight-body-medium`: semantic font weight for typography weight body medium.

### ki-video

A themed video surface: a calm poster facade with exactly one accessible play control over a slotted native `<video>` element. From the first activation on, playback, scrubbing, volume, captions and fullscreen belong to the native player — Kimen ships no custom chrome.

When to use: playable content the person deliberately chooses to watch —
product tours, talks, tutorials, announcements — presented as a poster
with one play control. Slot exactly one native `<video>` carrying its own
`poster`, sources and `<track>` captions, omit `controls` (the component
enables the native chrome the moment the facade yields, FR-002), and give
the control a `label` (required: the accessible name of the play button).
When NOT to use: decorative background or ambient loops (plain CSS and
`<video>` are the tool), audio-only recordings (use ki-audio),
embeds from streaming platforms that ship their own player chrome (use
their embed), or static imagery (use an image, not a video). `autoplay`
on the slotted media is unsupported: the facade's contract is that
playback begins only by explicit user activation — never on scroll,
hover or visibility — so preexisting `autoplay` and `controls` on the
slotted media are cleared when it arrives, and any playback already
running is paused (FR-003; the native chrome returns at activation).

Examples:

Slot exactly one native `<video>` carrying its own poster, sources and `<track>` captions; `label` names the play control (required — never rendered visually) and the native chrome returns the moment the facade yields:

```html
<ki-video label="Play the product tour">
  <video muted playsinline width="1280" height="720" poster="tour.jpg">
    <source src="tour.webm" type="video/webm" />
    <track kind="captions" srclang="en" label="English" src="tour.en.vtt" />
  </video>
</ki-video>
```

Everything on the media element passes through untouched — offer format fallbacks through multiple `<source>` children, and the native media events (`play`, `pause`, `ended`) keep firing on the element you own; ki-video emits no events of its own:

```html
<ki-video label="Play the setup walkthrough">
  <video width="1280" height="720" poster="walkthrough.jpg">
    <source src="walkthrough.webm" type="video/webm" />
    <source src="walkthrough.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
    <track kind="captions" srclang="en" label="English" src="walkthrough.en.vtt" />
  </video>
</ki-video>
```

The frame fills its container's inline size and the media keeps the intrinsic aspect ratio declared by `width`/`height` (16:9 is a demonstration, not a constraint); `autoplay` and `controls` on arriving media are cleared — playback begins only from the play control:

```html
<ki-video label="Play the workshop recording">
  <video width="800" height="600" poster="workshop.jpg">
    <source src="workshop.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
    <track kind="captions" srclang="en" label="English" src="workshop.en.vtt" />
  </video>
</ki-video>
```

Attributes:
- `label` (string, required): Accessible name of the play control ("Play the product tour"). The control is a real button exposing role button with exactly this name; the frame contributes no role, name or state of its own (FR-004, FR-005). Documented as required: no default human-language string is baked in, and an unlabeled control renders but fails the accessibility audit (015-ki-progress precedent). The label is never rendered visually.

Slots:
- (default): Exactly one native `<video>` element carrying its own poster, sources and `<track>` captions.

Parts:
- `frame`: The media frame: radius, clipping, the themed surface.
- `play`: The play control: overlay scrim, glass container and glyph.

Events: none

Methods: none

CSS custom properties:
- `--ki-effect-component-primary-default-shadow`: MarsUI Component_effect/primary_default: drop 0/1/1/-0.5 plus inner White/12 0/3/3. Pair with --ki-effect-component-backdrop-filter — CSS cannot mix backdrop blur into box-shadow.
- `--ki-effect-component-primary-hover-shadow`: MarsUI Component_effect/primary_hover: drops 0/20/20/-12 + 0/3/3/-1.5 + 0/1/1/-0.5 plus inner White/18 0/3/3. Pair with --ki-effect-component-backdrop-filter.
- `--ki-effect-video-hover-opacity`: Opacity of the added play-container shadow on hover. onmars shows the full primary hover effect over the resting shadow.
- `--ki-motion-duration-fast`: Fast interaction transition duration.
- `--ki-motion-duration-medium-1`: M3 md.sys.motion.duration.medium1 (250ms). onmars: MarsUI moderate step (240ms, 2x the 120ms base).
- `--ki-motion-easing-out`: Decelerating interaction transition easing curve.
- `--ki-motion-easing-standard-accelerate`: Utility exit curve. M3 md.sys.motion.easing.standard-accelerate. onmars: the MarsUI accelerate curve (ki.easing.in).
- `--ki-typography-family-body`: semantic font family for typography family body.
- `--ki-video-backdrop-filter`: Complete backdrop filter behind the video play scrim and control.
- `--ki-video-focus-ring-color`: color used by the video component for the play control focus ring: the keyboard-reachable facade control (FR-004, S6) adopts the ki-dialog/ki-icon-button focus-ring pair verbatim.
- `--ki-video-focus-ring-offset`: dimension used by the video component for the play control focus ring offset (ki-dialog precedent).
- `--ki-video-focus-ring-width`: dimension used by the video component for the play control focus ring width (ki-dialog precedent).
- `--ki-video-frame-radius`: dimension used by the video component for the frame corners: Radius/big_component/radius_xs, the exact variable bound to the Size=md Video frame (node 12089:6570, specs/025-ki-video/design-extraction.md) — the sm frame's radius_md is the scale demo, not a second API value.
- `--ki-video-motion-duration`: duration used by the video component for the facade dismissal fade: the Figma set documents no motion, so onmars resolves the single transition to the fast semantic duration (FR-013; disabled under reduced motion by construction, 024 precedent).
- `--ki-video-play-bg`: color used by the video component for the play container surface: Surface/inverse_white, the exact variable bound to the Icon_button fill (black over light, white over dark) — the control carries its own surface so glyph contrast never depends on the poster imagery (FR-008).
- `--ki-video-play-border-color`: color used by the video component for the play container edge: Outline/primary_button_top, the exact variable bound to the Icon_button stroke (as ki-button; none in onmars v2).
- `--ki-video-play-border-width`: dimension used by the video component for the play container edge width (MarsUI hairline stroke, ki-icon-button precedent).
- `--ki-video-play-fg`: color used by the video component for the play glyph: Text/inverse_black, the counterpart of the inverse container surface (white over light, black over dark) — the glyph inherits it via currentColor; the -bg/-fg pair is swept by the contrast gate (FR-008).
- `--ki-video-play-icon-size`: dimension used by the video component for the play glyph: the 28px Icon/Placeholder_xl slot measured inside the Size=md play container (the ki-icon-button xl icon size).
- `--ki-video-play-radius`: dimension used by the video component for the play container shape: Radius/component/radius_xl, the exact variable bound to the Size=md Icon_button instance (14px, the ki-icon-button xl radius).
- `--ki-video-play-shadow`: shadow used by the video component for the play control (MarsUI stacks Elevation/e6 on the button_wrap beneath the Component_effect/primary_default inner White/12 highlight — the measured master stack).
- `--ki-video-play-size`: dimension used by the video component for the play container box: the 56px Icon_button instance of the Size=md Video (the ki-icon-button xl box; the sm variant's 40px box is the scale demo).
- `--ki-video-scrim-color`: color used by the video component for the overlay scrim behind the play control: Inverse_white/alpha_6, the exact variable bound to the Play halo on both Video variants (Black/5 light, White/5 dark) — the scheme flip rides the semantic layer.
- `--ki-video-scrim-padding`: dimension used by the video component for the scrim clearance around the play container: Space/3xl, the exact variable bound as the Size=md Play halo padding (16px on every side).
- `--ki-video-scrim-radius`: dimension used by the video component for the overlay scrim shape: Radius/component/radius_6xl, the exact variable bound to the Size=md Play halo (28px pill-cornered square).

## GenUI layer

Above the components sits Kimen's GenUI layer: agents emit JSON UI specs
(data, never code), the neutral catalog validates them against the
published component surface, and the guarded renderer turns accepted
specs into DOM. Protocol adapters translate external vocabularies into
that neutral core and are disposable by design; the catalog and the
ki-* elements are the durable assets. These packages live in this
repository next to @kimen/elements.

### @kimen/catalog

Kimen neutral catalog and guardrail boundary: schema-constrained specs rendered from a closed component catalog. The durable asset (constitution Art. VIII).

When to use: Any boundary where agent-emitted JSON must become Kimen UI: validate specs standalone, render them with the guardrail enforced, stream them progressively, or keep a long-lived surface current with id-addressed batches. Both protocol adapters and any custom transport build on it.
When NOT to use: Hand-authored pages that never render agent output — use @kimen/elements directly.

Entry points:
- `validateUiSpec(input, options?) => ValidationReport`: Accepts or rejects an agent-emitted UI spec against the catalog in use — the built-in generated catalog, or a registered one passed as options.catalog — before anything renders. The report lists every issue with a code (unknown-component, unknown-prop, invalid-prop-type, missing-required-prop, prop-out-of-range, unknown-slot, undeclared-action, undeclared-event, invalid-child, action-not-allowed, collect-without-action, collect-unknown-node, collect-no-value, collect-key-conflict, collect-budget, url-scheme, url-origin, invalid-id, duplicate-id, forbidden-key, size-budget, depth-budget, malformed-spec), a path into the spec document and the offending value.
- `renderUiSpec(input, options) => RenderResult`: Validates and renders a spec into options.surface through the guarded renderer: only components of the catalog in use render (options.catalog selects it; absent, the built-in catalog applies) plus the native primitives it carries, only actions declared in the spec dispatch, by name or one per declared event (delivered as data to options.onAction, with the live values of the fields a node collects once each of them is valid), unknown props are rejected and no code path executes from spec data. Failures come back as diagnostics naming rule, path and value; nothing attaches on failure.
- `preflightUiSpec(input, options?) => RenderResult`: The guarded renderer's verdict without a DOM: runs exactly the preparation renderUiSpec runs before its first attach (purity wall, version gate, payload budget, catalog validation, then the depth, node-count, tag, activation and prop-name guards) and renders nothing. Use it at a DOM-less boundary — an MCP server, a service that checks specs before forwarding them — so that "valid" means "the renderer will paint it"; validateUiSpec alone accepts specs the renderer's tighter budgets refuse.
- `createStreamingRenderer(options) => StreamingRenderer`: Progressive rendering over a streamed spec: each push(node) validates one top-level subtree and attaches it only when fully valid; an invalid node fails closed while previously attached content remains, and the render budgets bind the accumulated stream. The catalog in use is fixed at creation via options.catalog.
- `createLiveSurface(options) => LiveSurface`: A long-lived surface changed through atomic batches of insert, set, text, remove, replace and reset ops addressed by stable node ids: apply(batch) validates the whole batch and the state it would produce (purity wall, per-batch budgets, optional ifRevision, catalog, guards, state budgets) before any DOM write, rejects it whole with diagnostics while the surface stays live, and otherwise touches only the attributes, text and subtrees it names so focus, typed values and scroll survive. A rejection is the return value, never a throw, and leaves earlier batches applied: several batches are not one change. The five limits (64 ops and 65,536 bytes per batch; 512 nodes, 32 levels and 262,144 bytes of state) are host options at creation, lower or higher than the defaults. A batch may name a focus node: if the batch leaves keyboard focus nowhere, it goes there; focus that is somewhere never moves. No set, replace or remove overwrites or discards checked/open/selected/value the user changed unless forced and allowed by the host; a dialog the person closed is reopened with open: false, then open: true in a later batch. A reset op returns a control to its spec value, or empties it, without force or host permission, only once what it holds left in an action; input no action carried is kept and the batch is rejected as unsent-user-input. Action events carry id, current path, revision and live data; snapshot() returns deep-frozen plain data. The batch and op shapes are exported as the LiveBatch and LiveOp types.
- `createCatalog(definition, options?) => CatalogCreationResult`: Registers your own components behind a data-only JSON facade — the exact entry shape of the generated catalog (tag, usage guidance, typed prop constraints, slots, events) — and returns a deeply frozen catalog that validateUiSpec and both renderers accept via options.catalog. The definition is untrusted input: it crosses the same purity wall as UI specs, tags must be conservative custom-element names, collisions with the extended catalog fail closed, usage guidance is mandatory, and every rejection is a RegistrationIssue naming code, path and offender. Pass { extend: catalogData } to compose with the built-in components, or omit it for a standalone catalog.
- `DEFAULT_RENDER_BUDGETS`: The declared render budgets (maxDepth 32, maxNodes 512, maxBytes 262144). A spec exactly at a budget passes; one beyond it is rejected before any node attaches. Hosts may lower or raise them via options.budgets; the renderer never renders past the ones in force. Standalone validation has its own ceilings, VALIDATION_MAX_BYTES (262144 UTF-8 bytes, overridable per call with maxBytes) and VALIDATION_MAX_DEPTH (256).
- `catalogData`: The generated catalog document itself: one entry per opted-in ki-* element and per native primitive with typed props, events, slots and when-to-use guidance, plus the elements version it derives from. Its schema version is exported as CATALOG_SCHEMA_VERSION.
- `NATIVE_PRIMITIVE_TAGS`: The closed set of native HTML elements a spec may carry next to catalog components: h2, h3, h4, p, strong and em for text, img for images, div for layout, and table, caption, thead, tbody, tr, th and td for read-only tables. They take the host page's typography, carry only their declared attributes (img: src under the URL policy, alt that is a description or exactly empty for decoration, width, height; div: direction, gap on the --ki-space-* steps, align, justify, wrap; th: scope col or row), keep a content model (a table part sits only in its own parent), never bind an action, and lay out through the CSSOM so a CSP without unsafe-inline styles holds. They come with the built-in catalog and with catalogs that extend it; a consumer definition can never declare one.

### @kimen/emitter

Kimen emitter kit: model-agnostic guidance artifacts (prompt, catalog-specialized JSON Schema with provider lowerings, tool definition) plus emission ingest helpers, derived deterministically from the neutral catalog. Advisory reliability tooling — validation and the guarded renderer remain the only enforcement points (spec 033).

When to use: Configure ANY LLM to emit valid Kimen UI specs: derive a system prompt, a catalog-specialized JSON Schema (with provider-strict lowerings) or a tool definition from the catalog in use — built-in or registered — and close the reliability loop with normalization and a single-round repair message.
When NOT to use: Enforcement: the artifacts are advisory. Validation and rendering stay in @kimen/catalog; hosts that already emit valid specs need nothing from this package.

Entry points:
- `catalogPrompt(catalog, options?) => Derivation<string>`: Model-facing prompt: format rules, every component's when-to-use and when-NOT-to-use guidance verbatim, props with enums inline, and one example spec that validates against the same catalog. The universal fallback — works with any model, no structured-output support required.
- `uiSpecJsonSchema(catalog, options?) => Derivation<JsonSchema>`: The neutral UI-spec format specialized to the catalog as a JSON Schema document: one branch per component, closed props and enums, closed objects everywhere. Targets: draft-2020-12 (default) and openai-strict (all-required closed objects, recursion via $ref, only the keywords the provider documents, its published limits enforced with named offenders). Deterministic and version-stamped; fail-closed on skew, bad subsets and exceeded limits — never a silent truncation.
- `uiSpecTool(catalog, options?) => Derivation<UiSpecTool>`: Provider-neutral tool definition { name: 'emit_ui', description, inputSchema } wrapping exactly the lowered schema for the same options; maps mechanically onto any provider's tool or function surface.
- `normalizeEmission(value) => unknown`: Strips the placeholders strict-mode all-required schemas force a model to emit (null-valued props, null action bindings, empty props containers) and touches nothing else. Pure cleanup over a fresh clone; output is untrusted until validateUiSpec passes.
- `repairPrompt(report) => string | null`: Formats a failed ValidationReport into ONE corrective message naming every issue's code, path and offender, or null when the report is ok. The single-round-then-fail-closed policy is fixed.

### @kimen/adapter-a2ui

Kimen adapter for A2UI: disposable by design (constitution Art. VIII). Translates declarative A2UI messages into the neutral catalog and renders them only through the guarded renderer. Supported protocol versions live in COMPAT.md, versioned with the adapter.

When to use: Your agent runtime speaks the A2UI protocol and its surfaces should render as Kimen components with the guardrail enforced.
When NOT to use: The agent can emit neutral Kimen UI specs directly (use @kimen/catalog alone), or the host is an MCP Apps client (use @kimen/adapter-mcp-apps).

Entry points:
- `createA2uiAdapter(options) => A2uiAdapter`: Creates the translation boundary: adapter.apply(message) turns A2UI 1.0 and v0.9.1 messages (createSurface, updateComponents, updateDataModel, deleteSurface) into neutral UI specs rendered only through the guarded renderer, resolving the surface data model inside the adapter. Each message is validated against the version its envelope declares, and a surface accepts only the version that created it. User interactions return through options.onAction as A2UI action events in the surface's version, rejected messages through options.onError as VALIDATION_FAILED errors; unmapped basic-catalog types degrade to a fixed fallback reported through options.onDegradation, and every A2UI 1.0 callRendererFunction is refused through options.onFunctionResponse.
- `SUPPORTED_A2UI_VERSIONS`: The exact A2UI envelope versions this adapter accepts: 1.0 (preferred) plus v0.9.1 and v0.9 (one payload-compatible family), each pinned to an upstream commit in A2UI_PROTOCOLS and versioned with the adapter in COMPAT.md.
- `A2UI_COVERAGE`: Machine-readable coverage table declaring how each A2UI 0.9.1 basic-catalog component type is handled: mapped to catalog components, rendered inline, degraded as unmapped, or forbidden. A2UI_V1_COVERAGE is the A2UI 1.0 counterpart.
- `A2UI_RENDERER_CAPABILITIES`: The renderer capabilities a host transport attaches for each supported A2UI version, preferred version (1.0) first: the metadata key (a2uiRendererCapabilities or a2uiClientCapabilities) and its value naming the basic catalog of that version.

### @kimen/adapter-mcp-apps

Kimen adapter for MCP Apps (SEP-1865): disposable by design (constitution Art. VIII). Exposes Kimen surfaces to MCP Apps hosts as predeclared, self-contained ui:// resources rendered only through the guarded renderer. Supported protocol versions live in COMPAT.md, versioned with the adapter.

When to use: You ship an MCP server and want tool results to render as interactive Kimen surfaces in MCP Apps (SEP-1865) hosts.
When NOT to use: The host is not an MCP Apps client, or you control the rendering surface directly — render neutral specs with @kimen/catalog instead.

Entry points:
- `declareToolSurface(name?) => { ui: { resourceUri } }`: Declares in an MCP tool's _meta that its results render in a predeclared ui:// surface.
- `createKimenSurfaceResource(name?) => KimenSurfaceResource`: The self-contained ui:// resource the server serves: one HTML document with every script and style inline, a no-network content policy, and the guarded renderer as its only render path.
- `surfaceToolResult(spec, textFallback, update?) => SurfaceToolResult`: Wraps a neutral UI spec plus a plain-text fallback as an MCP CallToolResult (spec in structuredContent.kimenSurface, text in content), so hosts without interactive surfaces still get text. The optional update { baseRevision, batch } is a live batch computed on the revision an action call carried: the surface applies it, keeping what the person is typing, only on that revision and when the live surface accepts it, and otherwise paints the full spec.
- `declareActionTool(name?) => KimenActionTool`: The app-only MCP tool (kimen_surface_action, _meta.ui.visibility ["app"]) that receives the surface's declared actions as tools/call { action, data, revision, id? } (the page revision the person acted on and the bound node's id; both optional in its schema); register it on the same server and validate the action.
- `acknowledgeSurfaceAction(action, options?) => SurfaceActionAcknowledgment`: The action tool's answer for an action your server accepts. With { relay: true } the surface relays that exact action to the model as one ui/message, if the host advertises text messages: one line, kimen-surface-action followed by { action, data } as escaped JSON, at most 8192 bytes, built by the surface from what it sent, never from this result. Relay when the person's choice needs the model; leave it off for UI-only actions such as a refresh.
- `createSurfaceBridge(options) => SurfaceBridge`: Runs inside the surface document and speaks the MCP Apps 2026-01-26 lifecycle: sends ui/initialize, refuses an undeclared negotiated version, renders ui/notifications/tool-result specs through the guarded renderer and its live surface only after the handshake (applying a result's update when it was computed on the current page revision), answers ui/resource-teardown and ping, and dispatches only declared actions as tools/call; when the server acknowledges one for relay and the host advertises text messages, relays it once as ui/message. Non-protocol messages are ignored with no state change.
- `MCP_APPS_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS`: The exact MCP Apps protocol revisions this adapter supports, versioned with the adapter in COMPAT.md.
